values.title: Accept or pass on a ranked record
values.job: Turn a person's accept or pass on one suggestion in a review list into the request that keeps it as their stand, in their own words
values.description: Give the same descriptor and the one record, the id of the action the person took (the descriptor says which stance each action keeps: accept is agree, pass is disagree) and what the person said. Returns the request for the keep-where-you-stand tool, with the stand on the row's own view and answered_by person. Writes nothing; run the returned tool with the returned input only (the other fields are for you): skip it if unchanged is true (the stands you gave already say this) or if you have already run this idempotency_ref, since running it twice makes two versions of the stance record. A record the descriptor leaves out, an unknown or disabled action, or a copy rule that sets anything but why, by or at is refused with the reason.

values.title: Act on a page in my browser
values.job: Click, type, press keys, scroll and choose on a page in the person's own browser, signed in as they are, and read the page again after
values.description: Opens the page at url in a window of its own that is not brought forward, validates steps (page-actions.json), does them in order, reads the page again and answers what each step did with the page after. dry_run only locates every target and acts on none. Refused in words when no browser is connected to this computer.

values.title: Add a customer
values.job: Add a customer or contact to my customer list, with their name, how to reach them and where they came from
values.description: Builds the customer record and returns it with its id (contact_id, contact_record); it keeps nothing, so your AI writes the record to your store. The id is what record-a-customer-step and see-where-each-customer-is use. Give contact_id to change a customer you already added.

values.title: Add a shared situation to the pool
values.job: Keep one situation a person made safe to show strangers, with its meaning, so others can learn how similar decisions turned out
values.description: Keeps nothing. Checks one shared situation and answers the row for the caller to keep in the pooled situations list: { entry, embedding, day }, under a new random id. The entry is the rewrite the person's side already checked (tool:share-a-decision); the plain privacy pass runs on it again here with no private terms, and words that still carry an address, a handle, a long number, an amount of money, a key, the removed mark or a name inside a sentence are refused. embedding is the meaning of the entry's situation, at most 4096 numbers. The row holds no account and no contributor.

values.title: Add an email sending domain
values.job: Add a domain my email-sending account should send from, and see the DNS records it needs
values.description: Asks the person's email-sending account (Resend), with the key they connected, to add a domain to send from, and answers the domain's id, status and the DNS records its owner must add (each record's kind, name, type, value and priority). Nothing is added to DNS here; tool:check-an-email-sending-domain asks the account to look again once the records are in.

values.title: Add captions to a video from its transcript
values.job: Burn captions into a video from its transcript, in a caption style: plain subtitles, large captions, or words that light up as they are said
values.description: Takes timed words (the speech-to-text tool's output, or a list of {text, start, end}) and burns captions into the whole video in the style you name (see style), words gathered into short lines the way that style reads best. Saves the new video in your files.

values.title: Add evidence to a decision
values.job: Add evidence to a decision I am making, at any time, so that its answers can cite it, or bring it in from another of my decisions
values.description: Adds evidence rows to a decision in the person's own records: each { ref, claim }, or { ref, from: { decision_id, ref } } to bring in another of the person's decisions' evidence as it stood. Each row is kept with when it came in. Rows can be added at any time, also after a decision is made; an answer may cite them at once. The same rows again replay; a ref that already says something else in the decision is refused. Returns the rows added and how many evidence rows the decision has.

values.title: Add or update reviewed videos in my video-packaging ledger without touching any other row (runs on your computer)
values.job: Record the titles, thumbnails, thumbnail words and opening hooks of a channel's videos I reviewed in one ledger, keeping every earlier row exactly as it was
values.description: Writes rows into a video-packaging ledger (JSON Lines, one row per video) from what the person explicitly admitted: an intake manifest (which videos, each with its metadata and caption file), the channel's catalog and a review record (thumbnail words, composition, how the title and thumbnail relate, caption event locators for the opening and internal hooks). A video counts only when it is in all three. Every file it relies on is pinned by BLAKE3 identity and size, and caption text is never copied: a hook is a caption file, an event index and its time span. Modes: a new source key; --append-new for a later batch under an existing key (only bytes are added at the end); --update-existing for reviewing rows that were unreviewed; --direct-review-batch, --identity-only-update, --hook-enrichment and --source-reconciliation each take a pinned contract file and check the ledger matches --expected-ledger-blake3 first; the identity-only, hook and source modes write a preimage of every line they change, and the hook and source modes stage a --prospective-ledger until --apply. Every other line stays byte for byte. It also updates the coverage and source-coverage summaries and writes a read-back.

values.title: Add to Notion
values.job: Add a page to a Notion database from a note, or anything picked
values.description: Makes a page in the Notion database you name (database: its id, the 32 letters and numbers in its address), titled title (else the first thing's name), holding your note and a link to what was sent. Uses your Notion connection, so connect Notion first. Returns what Notion answered.

values.title: Add up revenue
values.job: Add up revenue, refunds, net revenue and active recurring revenue from a list of payments, by plan or any other group
values.description: Reads any payment provider's events: you say which field holds the amount, which holds the recurring amount, which event kinds add revenue and which subtract it (refunds), and optionally which field groups payments (a plan, an offer, a month). Returns gross, refunds, net and active recurring revenue in cents, totals by group and by role, and the payments that need a look (missing or negative amounts, duplicates, the same payment twice with different amounts).

values.title: Add a requested item to a work tree
values.job: Add a requested item to a work tree, keeping who asked for it and in which message, without adding it twice
values.description: Adds one item someone asked for to a work tree, under a branch or at the top, with the checks that will show it is done. Each item keeps where it was asked (a conversation and the message's number), so sending the same request again changes nothing, a later message can refine an existing item (attach_to) or correct it (correction: true), and the same message can never become two items. Returns the whole tree with the item in it, whether it changed, and the item as recorded.

values.title: Admit the files sent with a message
values.job: Decide how many of the files sent with a message are accepted, and which limit stopped the rest, in words to show the person
values.description: Give files ([{ name, size }] in the order offered), and when wanted limits ({ per_turn_cap, absolute_bytes, max_bytes, binding_words }; defaults from src/attachment-admission.json), daily ({ remaining, resets_at } when the plan keeps a daily count) and now (milliseconds). A file over the size ceiling is left out; the first files that fit min(per-turn cap, remaining daily count) are accepted in order. Returns accepted (indexes), left_out ([{ index, because }]), binding (size, per_turn, daily or null), banner (the words naming the limit) and blocked. A null limit does not bind. Pure: reads no clock, plan or network.

values.title: Adopt a reviewed window of evidence into my library (runs on your computer)
values.job: Take a saved, reviewed set of intervals or evidence and adopt it into my library of records, refusing anything that does not match
values.description: Reads a saved adoption input the person gives (its schema member picks intervals or evidence-only) and adopts it into the library under the profile the library's schema declares, checking membership against the declared table first. Which tables, fields and rules apply comes from the schema.

values.title: Run a community's matchmaker clock: start or close a round, introduce, follow up
values.job: Pair a community's members on its cadence without anyone asking: start a round when it is due, close it at its deadline, make introductions everyone said yes to, and follow up the ones nobody acted on
values.description: The wake target of a community's matchmaker; a person declares it as their own wake (a wake-declaration record with tool tool:advance-a-community-matchmaker, a time repeat, and input { community_id }). Reads the community's settings (a match-community record, checked by tool:check-community-matching-settings), its members, rounds, matches and answers. When no round is open and the cadence (every_days after the last round) has come, it starts one: each opted-in member whose answers are incomplete gets a profile job for their own AI, and each complete member gets a bounded shortlist (an inverted index over categories and words, at most shortlist_size candidates, never every pair) and a score job asking their AI to score each candidate on the contract's factors with cited claims. Nothing here runs a model. At the deadline it forms groups from the grounded scores only (exact product of the factors, every factor cited), proposes each and hands each person's AI a consent job. It makes the one-to-one group of any match whose yeses all hold and hands topic jobs; it hands follow-up tasks at the community's follow_up_hours until the members talk. Tasks are calendar-task records assigned to their person, once per request key. Returns round (what started or closed, or null), next_at (when the clock next has something to do) and written; a community without usable settings returns ok false and its error. This tool reads and keeps no records: the caller's AI reads the community's records from a store and hands them in as `records`, and puts the answer's `write` (each changed record with the value it expected, null for a new one) in a store.

values.title: Allow my AI command line some tools in one folder (runs on your computer)
values.job: Keep, read or clear the tools I allow my own AI command line in one workspace folder, passed as that command line's own allow-list flag
values.description: Keeps the person's list of allowed tools for one existing folder in this computer's settings file (`workspace_tools`), reads one folder's list or all of them, and clears one. Nothing widens permissions by default: a folder with no list runs with the command line's own permission rules, and a command line with no allow-list flag (its row has no `allowed_tools`) is answered as not applying.

values.title: Answer the yes or no questions my checks ask, with a small model on my computer (runs on your computer)
values.job: Answer the questions a check of my writing asks a model, one line at a time, with the small model, adapter or hosted model each of my check rows names, keeping every answer so a line is never asked twice
values.description: Give settings_record (the person's setting row for this tool, record:setting:ask-a-small-model-for-a-verdict~<scope_kind>~<scope_id>, as the person's store gives it), asks, the questions tool:check-against-a-persons-rules-and-verdicts lists: each { question, options, text } with the row's adapter ({ name, blake3 }: decider-2b with that LoRA adapter, its folder the setting's adapters[name], checked by BLAKE3 before loading), model ({ mlx: repo id } a downloaded MLX chat model at its one snapshot, { consult: name } a hosted model through the consult-model route, or { stand_in } fixed answers), examples ({ items: <set>, bad_for }: the person's ruled lines of that set, shown first and never the judged line) and line_rows (the person's labelled-line check rows of the sets the examples name, read by the caller's AI from list:checks) and context (where the line sits in its film). mode live asks a model for what the answer cache lacks; cache answers only from it. Answers one { option: probability } or null per ask, in order.

values.title: Answer a community's matchmaker: profile, scores, yes or no, topics, wrote
values.job: Give a community's matchmaker what it asked for: a member's answers and on/off switch, an AI's cited scores for its shortlist, a person's yes or no to an introduction, first topics, or that they wrote in the one-to-one
values.description: One answer from one person (person), then the community's clock. kind profile: { on?, answers: { question_id: answer }, categories? }, refused when a question is not one the community asks or an answer holds the community's contact pattern. kind scores: { round_id, scores: [{ candidate_ref, factors: { factor: { score in (0, 1], reason, you: [claim_ref], them: [claim_ref] } } }] }; answers which candidates were grounded and why not, and the round closes once every asked AI answered. kind answer: { match_id, yes, consent }: a yes counts only when the run's task carries the community's person stamp (consent.yes_needs, a task fact the engine sets on a run the person started on their own page, which no input can set) and the consent the person was shown (read-my-community-matches gives it); an AI's yes is refused with the screen to open; a no, from the person or their AI, passes the match for everyone. Once every member's yes holds, the one-to-one group (group:introduction) is made and each AI is asked for first topics. kind topics: { match_id, topics: [line] }. kind wrote: { match_id }: once every member wrote, the match has talked. kind run-round: the community's owner closes the open round and starts the next. Returns outcome ({ ok: true, ... } or { ok: false, error, status, next_call?, changed?, consent? }), round, next_at and written. This tool reads and keeps no records: the caller's AI reads the community's records from a store and hands them in as `records`, and puts the answer's `write` (each changed record with the value it expected, null for a new one) in a store.

values.title: Answer several typed questions about one thing in one request (runs on your computer)
values.job: Ask a model several questions about one piece of state at once and get one answer for each, in the type I asked for, or a refusal if any is missing or the wrong type
values.description: Give state (any JSON), questions ({<id>: {type: choice | score | noul, instructions, criteria?}}: choice answers with one of the names in criteria, or any text without criteria; score answers with a number; noul is yes or no answered as the likelihood of yes, 0 to 1), endpoint (a model server on your computer), model and timeout_seconds (no default). The state and the questions are written into the prompt and the answer schema names every question id, so the reply cannot use keys of its own. Returns answers keyed by question id. A server that answers with an error status, is unreachable or too slow, or sends a body that is not JSON, and a model reply that is not JSON, leaves a question out, or answers one in the wrong type, are each refused with a sentence saying which, rather than repaired. A noul answer is the likelihood of yes, a number from 0 to 1, checked as such (the old package accepted any text for it). This is an uncalibrated read of the state; for a decision, use tool:ask-a-small-model-for-a-verdict.

values.title: Answer the same questions about many states, in bulk, on this Mac
values.job: Ask the same set of questions about every one of these lines or records, all at once, with my classifier model
values.description: Takes the model's value, the question set, the settings and the states in the request, and asks every state every question on this Mac: the questions run once as a cached prefix and the states batched against them on Apple's GPU through MLX. The answer for each state and question is the classifier's probabilities over its options (choice: each option; score: each level, with the expected level; noul: the probability of yes). The answer returns them all: {status, states_done, states, classifier_answers_as, seconds, answers: [{index, id?, answers: {question id: answer}}]}. The caller reads the inputs from the person's lists and puts the answers wherever it wants them; nothing is written to the person's records, and nothing is kept on this Mac: the states go to the classifier program on a pipe and its answers come back on one.

values.title: Answer the calendar page routes
values.job: Answer the page's calendar routes (GET /work/api/calendar, GET and POST /work/api/calendar/tasks, and the task proposal and date-shift routes) from the calendar rows handed in
values.description: The page's calendar routes, run by the engine for the page's account (workshop-routes): the request's { path, method, query, body, browser, records } in, { status, body, keep } out. Each read is answered by old trillion's own calendar owner (src/native-calendar-owner.mjs calendar:request) over the calendar rows the caller hands in as `records` ([{id, type, value}]); this run reads no store of its own. A read may answer in `keep` the starting calendar list definitions it finds missing, rows for the caller to keep where the person keeps them, conditional on the rows it read. GET /calendar reads every source; the person's tasks are read here, and a source only another route or a connected calendar tool can read is said unread in the calendar's own words. A POST to the task, proposal or date-shift routes answers 405: keeping those is workflow:keep-my-calendar-tasks-and-proposals. /calendar/actions and /calendar/availability are not answered here (404).

values.title: Answer the page that says how this device stands
values.job: Answer the Trillion page route POST /work/api/catch-up/here: keep how this device stands and answer the page as old Trillion did
values.description: A page route tool: the engine runs it for the page's account with { path, method, query, body, browser } and answers the page with { status, body }. POST /catch-up/here with { device_id, state, waiting?, at?, title?, kind?, copy_id? } keeps that device's row in setting:catch_up_devices (written only when what the person sees changed, or its last catch-up moved by more than an hour; newest 40 kept) and answers 200 { device, written }. A refused report answers 400 { error }; any other path or method answers 404 { error: "Not found" }. The write stands on the rows it read; rows another device changed meanwhile are read again.

values.title: Answer the saved configurations routes
values.job: Answer the saved configurations routes: list, read, save, remove and copy my saved configurations
values.description: The /configurations routes, as the old account owner answered them (tools/query-and-change-list-rows/src/configurations.mjs): GET /configurations?target=&limit=&before= lists this account's own configurations, newest id first, with next_before; GET /configurations/<id> reads one (404 configuration_not_found); POST /configurations saves one ({ label, target, settings, aspects, field_ids, format, open_path }); POST /configurations/<id> updates it at expected_revision (409 configuration_conflict when stale) or removes it with { remove: true, expected_revision }; POST /configurations/<id>/duplicate copies it. Each is one record:configuration record, and the Saved configurations list record is made with the first. Configurations shared with this account by link or offer, and the time-bound context, answer 503 configuration_unavailable: they are reached through record sharing, which this run does not reach. Answers { status, body, keep }.

values.title: Answer the Formats page
values.job: Answer the Formats page: list my content formats, list what can fill them, shape a thought into them and follow a script
values.description: The Formats page's routes, as the old account owner answered them: GET /content-formats (the saved formats handed in as `saved` first, then the starters, with removed_starters and example_kinds); POST /content-formats { formats } checks their own list whole and answers the list it would keep (a refused list is 400); nothing is stored here, the caller stores the answer; GET /content-formats/sources (their recordings and notes from their files and the `pursuits` rows handed in, newest first); POST /content-formats/shape { thought?, source?, format_ids? } (each format's script, with before_writing); POST /content-formats/follow { format_id | script, heard, said? }. Answers { status, body }.

values.title: Answer the Decisions page
values.job: Answer the Trillion page route GET /work/api/decisions: the Decisions screen's rows, as old Trillion answered them
values.description: A page route tool: the engine runs it for the page's account with { path, method, query, body, browser } and answers the page with { status, body }. GET /decisions answers 200 with the Decisions screen's rows, the same read as tool:see-my-decisions with no input: { free, summaries, pursuits, space_pursuits, plans, access, allowance, pursuits_words, helped }. Any other path or method answers 404 { error: "Not found" }. It changes nothing.

values.title: Answer the Media page's saved edits
values.job: Answer the Media page: check an edit of my recordings and answer it
values.description: The Media page's routes, answered by old trillion's src/work-media.mjs handleWorkMedia: GET /media/edit?id= answers the `edit` handed in (null when none); POST /media/edit { id, title, clips, ratio?, captions?, textOverlays?, edl?, panels?, file? } checks the edit as the old route did (400 with words when a clip has no source or valid times), answers it as { edit } for the caller to store, and answers each clip it used as file_uses ({ file, kind: edited }) for the caller to keep on Recent, where the person's files program records file uses. Nothing else is kept here. An edit in a shared project (space_id), and the page's library, next-edit, render, transcribe and editor routes, need what this run cannot reach, and answer 503 with words naming it. Answers { status, body }.

values.title: Answer the web chat message routes
values.job: Answer the web chat's message routes (GET /work/api/messages, /messages/threads and /messages/thread, POST /work/api/messages/send and /messages/send-all) and keep each message the person sends as a message row in my own records, and wake the AI it is for
values.description: The web chat's message routes, run by the engine for the page's account (workshop-routes): the request's { path, method, query, body } in, { status, body } out. GET /messages and /messages/threads answer the person's conversations newest first ({conversations, next_before}); GET /messages/thread answers one conversation's messages (app and conversation_id). POST /messages/send keeps the person's words to one AI (app, conversation_id, text, client_id?) and POST /messages/send-all keeps them once in the shared Trillion conversation, each as one `message` row, given back in `keep` for the caller to write as new rows: the route holds no database, so it reads only the rows the caller gives as `stored` and writes nothing. The same client_id sent again is the message already kept. POST /messages/correct replaces the words of one of the person's own messages (message_id, text, client_id?) in its row, keeping the words before it in corrected_from; that one row is given back in `keep` with replaces: true, to be updated in place, and the same client_id sent again keeps nothing. Files ride by reference (each must be one of the person's own, linked in the message). An AI is woken the way the person's AIs take work: a To do calendar-task row kept in the same write (send with agent_id: for that AI; send-all: for any AI, or for the AIs @-mentioned). The answer says the message is kept and read on the AI's next connection; it never says delivered.

values.title: Answer the page that shows the one thing that holds me
values.job: Answer the Trillion page routes GET and POST /work/api/needs-you-hold: the one thing held for me now, and setting it aside, handing it back, choosing a stake, asking off or turning it on
values.description: A page route tool: the engine runs it for the page's account with { path, method, query, body, browser, stored } and answers the page with { status, body }; it reads and writes no store: stored.records are the person's records it works from, and it answers the rows to keep (keep) and the device runs to start (runs). GET /needs-you-hold answers 200 with the hold over the person's Waiting on you rows (record:waiting-on-you), their hold setting (setting:needs_you_hold) and their hold rules (setting:needs_you_hold_rules): { on, held, ranked, ..., said, words }; a read that fails answers 503 { error, busy: true }. POST /needs-you-hold with { op, key?, title?, reason?, way?, stake?, values? } (op: read, seen, aside, hand_back, stake, off or on) changes the hold setting on condition of what was read (409 when the store refuses the kept setting), keeps each task the change hands to the person's AIs as a calendar-task record once, and answers the change with the read after it; seen marks read the notices the held thing's own device runs told, on this page's surface. Every read keeps the held thing as setting:needs_you_held when it changed; a refused change answers 400 { error }. Any other path or method answers 404.

values.title: Answer the page's pursuits
values.job: List what I am pursuing now, and keep a goal I add or change from the page
values.description: The page route /pursuits: GET answers { pursuits } (every pursuit that is not ended or archived); PUT { pursuits: [{ title, now, after, ... }], replace_all? } adds or updates each pursuit by its id (made from its id or title), and with replace_all ends every current pursuit left out except one with a room, then answers every current pursuit. Each pursuit is one pursuit record. A pursuit missing its title, now or after is refused 400 with { error }, as old trillion's DecisionEngine refused it; any other route answers 404.

values.title: Answer the Saved examples page
values.job: Answer the Saved examples page: list my saved examples, save one from its link, remove one
values.description: The Saved examples page's routes (GET /saved-examples lists every example newest first with its count; POST /saved-examples saves one from { url, title?, words?, pictures?, why_it_worked?, collection?, added_from? }, filling what was not given from the public link itself the first time; POST /saved-examples/remove { id } removes one). Each example is one saved-example record. The records it reads are the ones handed in as stored.records; the records it makes are handed back in keep (a removed example as a null value), and the run writes nothing itself. Answers { status, body } as the old account route did: a refused save is 400 with { error }, and the example stays as it was.

values.title: Answer the search page route
values.job: Answer the page's one search (GET /work/api/search) over every list, record and file name I keep
values.description: GET /work/api/search for the account: calls the same searchEverything as tool:search-everything-with-one-question, including said, seen, name and written. Query q, places, sources, matches and limit retain the page contract. Returns status and body; unavailable and pending remain visible.

values.title: Answer the page that lists what Trillion told me
values.job: Answer the Trillion page route GET /work/api/tell/notices: the notices the open page shows, or what one channel's devices read, as old Trillion did
values.description: A page route tool: the engine runs it for the page's account with { path, method, query, body, browser } and answers the page with { status, body }. GET /tell/notices answers 200 { notices }: the newest notices the open Trillion page carried (its own channel), newest first, each with its read mark, the surface it was read on, how far each way got, its state, chips and buttons. With query channel (and after, a notice number) it answers what that channel's devices read after it, oldest first; a channel that does not exist answers 400 { error }. Any other path or method answers 404. It reads only the told-the-person records given to it as `records` and writes nothing.

values.title: Answer which page builds may keep working
values.job: Say which builds of the Trillion page may keep working, so an open tab the store moved past shows a reload screen
values.description: The page route GET /client-version: answers { minimum_generation, lock_out_before } from the minimum-version DATA this tool carries (src/client-version.json), as old trillion's Worker answered it. A tab whose build is below minimum_generation, or that was opened before lock_out_before, covers itself with a reload screen. Any other route or method answers 404 { error: 'Not found' }. It reads and changes nothing.

values.title: Apply a device's message to a recording session
values.job: Update a multi-camera recording session when one device (a camera, a watch, a remote control) joins, leaves, reports its state or hands over the primary role
values.description: Give session ({ id, states, primary?, devices? }: states are the states a device can report, the first being where a joining device starts; leave out primary and devices for a new session) and message ({ session, device, type }): type join (role primary or secondary, default secondary), leave, state (state: one of the session's states) or handover (from: the current primary, device: the one taking over). Returns the session after the message. A message for another session, with no device, from a device that never joined, joining twice, taking a primary that is held, handing over from a device that is not primary, naming an unknown state or type, changes nothing and returns the session as it was with ignored { reason, message }. Exactly one device is primary; the primary leaving leaves none. Nothing is kept: hand the returned session in with the next message.

values.title: Rebuild an answer from its changes
values.job: Rebuild the answer a screen should show from the answer it holds and the changes it was sent
values.description: Give answer (what tool:make-a-view-patch returned: whole with text, or with patch) and previous, the JSON text the screen holds. Returns { text, held } where held is { identity, text } to keep for the next ask, or { stale: true } when the patch was made against a different answer, cannot be applied, or does not rebuild its stated identity, so the screen should read the whole answer again.

values.title: Put new titles into my video plans and the cards that name them (runs on your computer)
values.job: Change the titles of my video plans to the ones in my titles list, and fix every card that points to an old title
values.description: Reads the person's titles list (one row per plan id, with its new title and any fields to copy) and applies it to every plan in a folder: the new title, the fields the request names, and every card segment whose text is an old title or a prefix the request names plus an old title. A title that is one of the request's placeholder words keeps the withdrawn title under its own field and leaves its cards as they are. A row may name the old title of a plan that is gone, so cards pointing at it are renamed too. Also: titles-table, the titles list as a Markdown table (id, title with each placeholder in bold, and the columns the request names), to show the person before or after the change.

values.title: Approve a pairing code
values.job: Let a waiting sender's messages through by approving the pairing code they were given
values.description: Give code (case and spaces do not matter) and, optionally, source_id. A code works once, only before it expires, and only for the source it was issued for. Returns source_id, sender and said; an unknown, used or expired code is refused with what to do. It reaches no database: give the pairing facts the person keeps as facts, and keep what the answer's keep lists.

values.title: Approve a post
values.job: Check a drafted post is approved exactly as it was reviewed and answer the approved post row to keep
values.description: Give post_id and expected_values (the complete approval_values of the post as it was reviewed); expected_values is required, and approval is refused when its words, file, destinations or time changed since. A post going nowhere yet is refused. approved_by names who approved it. Returns post, said and the approved post row to store under `keep`. Give records: the post. Give database to approve in that pursuit database: the post and the person's approval setting are read there and the answer is kept there, so no caller can carry an auto setting in.

values.title: Approve words to show
values.job: Work out the approval, decline or withdrawal of one row of words exactly as it was reviewed, so only approved words are ever shown
values.description: decision approve needs reviewed_words equal to the words now in the row, a received row, and a consent that allows showing: then the row to keep is approved and pinned to the speaker, the words and the consent together. decline marks a received row declined. withdraw (the person took their consent back, or the owner took the words down) works on any row and stops it showing at once. The row is found among the `rows` handed in. Nothing is written by this tool: `keep` holds the records the caller's AI keeps in its store, conditional on the row as handed in, so a store refuses it when the row changed since. Returns row_id, status and keep.

values.title: Arrange videos side by side
values.job: Put two or more videos side by side, stacked, or in a grid in one frame, such as a swing next to a pro's
values.description: Plays the videos together in one frame: side by side (h), stacked (v) or a grid, with their sound mixed. Saves the new video in your files.

values.title: Ask a command-line MCP server one request
values.job: Ask a command-line MCP server one request the way the web gateway answers a caller with no session: start it in a working folder of its own, initialize it, ask, and stop it
values.description: Makes the gateway (do-work/gateway.mjs createGateway) for the one stdio MCP server the input names (cli, args, env) and hands it one POST /<app>/mcp with no session id, in this process: no port is opened. The gateway starts the server as a child process in a fresh empty working folder with only PATH, HOME, TMPDIR and LANG (plus env), sends initialize (protocol_version, 2025-06-18 when left out) and notifications/initialized, writes the request (one JSON-RPC message per line), waits at most timeout_seconds (30 when left out), answers a request the server asks back with method not found, then kills the server and removes its folder. An arg that starts with ./ or ../ names a file in the run's working folder (the tool folder) and is made absolute first. Answers the HTTP status the gateway gave (200, or 502 when the server would not start or initialize) and the JSON-RPC reply. The server runs whatever command cli names inside the run's container, with no internet; this run reads and writes nothing else and keeps nothing. Refuses a missing cli, args that are not text, an app name the gateway's path would not take, a request with no method, and initialize as the request. The hosted gateway (do-work/serve.mjs) also keeps sessions open between requests (Mcp-Session-Id), streams a server's notifications, caps and reaps idle sessions and serves on a port for the web; this run does only the one-off flow.

values.title: Ask a model
values.job: Ask a model served on the person's own computer (a local model, free to run) a conversation, a yes-or-no question about some words, or for vectors that compare words by meaning, instead of a service billed per word
values.description: Runs on the person's computer with the models it serves (read-data/models-on-this-computer.json: Ollama for conversations, a small classifier for yes-or-no questions). messages asks a conversation and answers in the chat-completions shape; job picks a job row (which models, how many words, what answer format); tools optionally supplies the functions it may call, whose calls are returned for the caller to execute through its normal permissions; parts true also returns the answer as keyed parts. state and questions ask the classifier and answer its probabilities. texts answers one vector per text from the embedding model its job names (meaning when it names none), with that model's name, since vectors compare only with vectors from the same model. Answers error in words, with each model tried and why it did not answer, when no model on the computer is running.

values.title: Ask a small model a question about some text, and trust it only if it got my known cases right (runs on your computer)
values.job: Ask a small model one question about some text (yes or no, which of a list, or how much on a scale) and get its answer with how sure it is, but only after that model got my already-answered cases right
values.description: Give rubric (your question, answer_shape {kind: true-or-false | one-of with options | score with levels, and for a score score_tolerance: how many levels away still counts as right}, calibration cases [{content, expect}] with at least two different answers, optional confidence_bands [{at_least, then}], accept_when_answer_in) or rubrics_file plus rubric_id, the content, and providers (the models you can ask: {via: locally-served, endpoint} for a model server on your computer, or {via: hosted-classifier, endpoint, model, key_file} for a hosted classifier whose key is in a file you name). A rubric with no cases, or whose cases all expect the same answer, is refused, and so is a model that gets a case wrong, so a yes-man never becomes your judge. Returns the answer, accepted (does your rubric accept it), confidence, the whole spread, the band your rubric drew for that confidence, who answered and the scoreboard of who was tried. Content longer than a provider row's accepts_characters is refused, never cut; a row that declares no limit is sent the whole content, so declare one for any model with a smaller reading window. remember_file keeps the calibration so later questions are one call; log_file (with excerpt_characters, how much text to keep) keeps each verdict with an excerpt so a wrong one can be turned into a known case with tool:tell-it-when-it-was-wrong.

values.title: Ask a web address, or give me the last answer it gave
values.job: Ask a web address for its answer; when the address cannot answer, give back the last answer it gave, so a feed or service that is down does not leave the person with nothing
values.description: Give address (a web address that starts with http:// or https://) and key (a short name for this answer: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, so the last answer can be found again); wait_seconds (1 to 120, default 20) is how long to wait for the address; last_answer is the answer given back last time (the to_keep record this tool returned, or its value), which the person's own write kept. The answer is JSON when the address says it is JSON and text otherwise, up to 256 KiB. When the address answers, the answer is returned with origin from-the-source, the time, and to_keep, the one record that keeps it under the key; the tool keeps nothing itself. When it fails (an error status, no answer in time, an unreadable or too large body) or answers with nothing, last_answer is returned with origin from-what-was-kept and when it was kept; an empty answer never replaces a good one. With no last_answer the origin is nothing-to-give and the answer is null. Failures are returned in words (source_failure), never raised. When the address answers 429 or 503 with a Retry-After header, retry_after_seconds says how long it asked to be left alone (seconds or a date, held to a day); the tool itself never waits or asks again. The engine keeps this to public web addresses.

values.title: Ask people for their words
values.job: Ask people, each after their own good word, to say in their own words how it went: the asked row to keep for each person for a case, and their draft
values.description: For each person who may be asked, answers the asked row to keep in the list and the person's draft ({to, subject, body}) from the words the list's gathers.ask holds, with {name} filled in. Sends nothing and keeps nothing: the draft goes out through a sending tool the person chose, and the caller's AI keeps the `keep` rows in its store. A person is asked once for a case (the same person and case, found among the `rows` handed in, is skipped as already_asked), and only with `win`, a reference to the person's own positive word that made this the time to ask (otherwise skipped as no_win). The address is in the draft only, never in the row to keep. Returns asked ({row_id, person, draft}), skipped ({person, reason}) and keep.

values.title: What was said since this conversation last asked
values.job: Tell me what was said in a listening since I last asked
values.description: Answers the turns of a listening (`heard`) after `cursor` (what this conversation was last given), with the captions' corrections applied (`captions`), and the cursor to hand in next time so each turn is given once. It keeps nothing and waits for nothing: the heard rows, the captions state and the cursor come in with the request and the new cursor goes out in the answer, for the person's AI to keep where it chooses.

values.title: Cut my recordings into a video from a plan (runs on your computer)
values.job: Cut my recordings into a video following my plan: which stretch of which recording goes where, lines a voice reads over a held frame, my look on every shot, my graphics laid over it, and only show me the cut once every check I name passes
values.description: Reads a plan (segments in order, each a stretch of a recording from-to, a voiced line or a slide) and a piece table that says, per format, what each segment kind becomes. Cuts each recording frame-exact at the plan's own aspect, with edges that never catch the word before or after and a crossfade where two recordings meet; holds an open-eyed frame under each voiced line; plays a sound-only recording over a borrowed still with its words as captions; colours every shot with the person's look and shot-matches them to one another; places every sound at the exact start of its picture, with one loudness pass. The whole cut is one edit of the Workshop tool media-composition, rendered by its render-an-edit. Graphics are the person's own device templates, laid out clear of the face and drawn once over the whole cut by the overlay renderer the person names. The cut is made in a work folder and moved to the folder the person sees only when it is whole and every check row in the request passes; otherwise it stays in the work folder and the answer names what failed. A plan of slides becomes one picture per slide and a PDF. Steps: timeline (lengths only, nothing made), lay-out (the timeline, the overlay spec and the edit, nothing rendered for the person), build (one plan), run (every plan of a folder, each first through the person's plan checks). It runs on the person's own computer.

values.title: Assess Commons file reuse and prepare credit
values.job: Check one Commons file's exact original license fields, exclude unsupported rights and prepare required source attribution for any objective
values.description: Offline, file-specific check over the page object returned by Commons metadata lookup. Only an explicit Public Domain declaration with Copyrighted=false, Public Domain Mark 1.0, CC0 1.0, or matching canonical CC BY 1.0/2.0/2.5/3.0/4.0 metadata with title, author and source page can pass as eligible_for_selection. BY-SA, NC, ND, missing, conflicting or ambiguous metadata is refused. Output preserves original license/author/title/source and rights-warning values, identifies license class and version, and prepares a text credit with declared changes. It does not render metadata HTML. eligible_for_selection means the explicit license policy is met from source metadata; it is not exhaustive legal-rights verification or automatic permission. Inspect source warnings and intended-use rights independently.

values.title: Assign helpers to the people who need them, within each helper's capacity
values.job: Assign mentors, volunteers or helpers to the people who asked for help when each helper can only take so many, best pairs first, and say who was left without one and why
values.description: operation solve_capacity_constraints takes help_seekers [{ id, match_case_id?, demand? }], helper_candidates [{ id, capacity_ref?, session_ref?, mode? }], capacities (by helper id, or a list in helper id order), and your answers about pairs: eligibility [{ help_seeker_ref, helper_candidate_ref, eligible, reason? }] and ranking [{ help_seeker_ref, helper_candidate_ref, score, explanation? }]. The best-ranked eligible pairs are taken first; a helper is never booked past capacity and nobody is assigned to themself. operation solve_expected_value_capacity_constraints takes scored candidates (as for tool:form-matches) with expected_value, group_size, capacities and exclusive_participation, and needs a clear cut after each seeker's demand. propose_assignment turns a solved answer into proposals; record_outcome records outcome_fact_refs for one assignment_proposal. Returns assignments (state proposed), unmatched (with reason: capacity_exhausted, no_eligible_helper, indistinguishable_expected_value, ...), capacity_usage and how much work was done. Rounds that swap who helps and who is helped are two requests.

values.title: Put my own domain on a site
values.job: Put a domain name I own in front of my published website
values.description: Makes your own domain (domain, like shop.example.com) show the site (installation). Give your account's address (account, the 64 characters after /a/ in your Trillion address): the TXT record names it, so only you can attach your domain. Give the host your computer answers on (points_at): the address record points at it, and the suffix, proof_label and proof_value_prefix the forwarder's settings name. Returns the two DNS records to add at your domain's DNS host; the address answers once the TXT record is visible.

values.title: Find where test passages also appear in a classifier's training rows
values.job: Find whether the passages a classifier is tested on also appear in the rows it was trained on: the same text, the same family or the same whole request
values.description: Give training_rows and target_rows (each a row, or a row with state, whose state holds target_text and may hold reader_context and reference_text), and optionally training_source and target_source ({ source_id, blake3, path, schema }). The answer lists every target whose text appears in a training row's target, reader context or reference (exact, or after NFKC, case and whitespace folding, on word boundaries, for targets of at least 16 characters; shorter ones are named unassessed), every same-family pair and every identical whole state. Source identities come back as safe tokens only, never paths. No match is only absence of these overlaps, never proof of independence.

values.title: Blur and silence everyone who has not agreed to be filmed
values.job: Make a copy of a video with every face blurred and every word silenced except those of the people who agreed to be filmed, before it is posted or shared
values.description: Give video, a video in the person's files, and agreed, pictures of each person who agreed to be filmed (a clear picture of their face; the person themself included). Every face in every frame is found; a face that matches someone who agreed stays as it is, and every other face, including one it cannot be sure of, is blurred past recognition. Give agreed_voices too, a recording of each of them speaking, and every word said by anyone else is silenced, judged half a second at a time; without it the sound is copied unchanged. The original video is never changed. The copy is kept in the person's files under Made by tools, named by name when given. Returns how many faces were seen, blurred and kept, how much speech was silenced, and any agreed picture in which no face was found. Faces are found with YuNet and recognized with SFace (OpenCV Zoo) and voices told apart with CAM++, on the tool's own computer; nothing leaves it.

values.title: Break down visits and sales by source
values.job: Break down visitors, leads and sales by where they came from (source, campaign or any tracked field), with conversion rates and revenue
values.description: Counts each visitor once by their first visit, then gives one row per source (or campaign, or any field the visits carry): visitors, each outcome you track (leads, purchases, sign-ups) with its rate, and revenue and revenue per visitor when conversions carry a value. can_break_down_by lists every field the visits allow; a conversion with no outcome counts toward the project's first one.

values.title: Brief a profile of how someone does their thing
values.job: Work out how a person or creator does their thing, such as their style or voice, from what they have made or said
values.description: Give the profile's name, the subject's name and the subject's own records (what they made or said). Returns what you need to derive the profile: the records, the rules for the answer and the shape of the answer. It asks no model; you derive the items, then give them to tool:keep-a-profile. An empty list of records is refused.

values.title: Prepare the research request for a prospect
values.job: Get the instruction my AI writes a research profile of a company or a prospect from: fit against my criteria, the biggest problems the material shows, why now, a case study to cite, ways to reach them
values.description: Give key (one short name for the prospect, such as its website address, the same in every later action), criteria (what makes a good prospect for you), and the gathered material: material (one text) or evidence ([{ id, text }], such as a job post, a page of the company's site or its reviews, gathered with the other tools of this folder or tools/browse-public-page). Optional name, url and profile_ref (prospect:<key> when left out). Returns requests (as tool:write-a-profile-request does, with the prospect instruction before the material), row_id (where the profile is kept) and profile_shape (each field the profile must hold). The profile rules are DATA in do-work/prospect-list.json. It asks no model and keeps nothing: your AI writes the profile as one JSON object from instruction_text and hands it to tool:keep-a-prospect. Refuses a request with no criteria or no material.

values.title: Brief a triage of one incoming item
values.job: Decide what to do with one incoming item, such as a message, note or finding, by weighing it against what the person cares most about
values.description: Give the item (a ref, an optional version, and what it says), the person's priorities, the dispositions an item can be settled as (each a ref and a label; exactly one is the fallback; blocked_default and needs_objective are optional), the least confidence an answer may have (0 to 1) and, if the person wants limits, the most words the rationale and the objective may have (max_words). Returns what you need to judge it: the item, the priorities, the dispositions, the rules for the answer (including fail closed to the fallback; where a disposition needs an objective, that it is the smallest safe, reversible assignment that produces evidence and may not authorize messages, spending, publishing, promises, credential changes, live changes, anything illegal, deceiving or harassing anyone, or taking what belongs to another party) and the shape of the answer. It asks no model; you judge, then give your answer to tool:settle-a-triage.

values.title: Give a variant sound palette one gain so its effects track is as loud as the reference (runs on your computer)
values.job: Scale my variant sound palette by one common gain so its effects track has the reference track's loudness
values.description: The variant palette's layer over the cue plan is measured, and every sound in it scaled by the one gain that brings it to the reference layer's integrated loudness, so per-sound balance and cue gains stay and a listener compares the sounds, not the level.

values.title: Bring back my similar decisions
values.job: When I am about to decide something, show what I decided in similar decisions before, what came next and how each turned out
values.description: Reads the person's own decision records. The newest ones are weighed by the words their goals share with the named decision's goal, plus a point for the same method (read-data/decide-with-a-method.json `similar`). The closest are kept, closest first, limit of them (10 when not given, never more than 50). Each comes back with its goal, its method, the option it chose, its next action, its status (from its own current evidence) and its observed and reported results. Only those few are read whole, and nothing leaves the person's account.

values.title: Build an option on its own copy of my FilmCraft project and export its preview (runs on your computer)
values.job: Build one picked option on its own copy of my FilmCraft project with filmcraft-cli and export its preview
values.description: Copies the chapter's base FilmCraft project to projects-round-<n>/<id>.fcproj and makes every edit of the option's spec with FilmCraft's own headless commands (filmcraft-cli --save run; never the live app): a stitched opening (prepend), cuts, earlier heads (head_extend), frame holds with the grade kept over them, a still on its own track for a hold, muted and raised or lowered stretches of the cut's sound, scale keyframes and the overlay with its sound. Then exports the preview range at the settings' format and scale under one render lock for the computer, masters its sound to the settings' loudness in two EBU R128 passes and takes its still, into work-round-<n>/pending/ (never a folder the person watches). With plan true it runs nothing that writes and answers the exact command list. With how "composite" an overlay-only option is composited onto the chapter's FilmCraft export of the cut instead of a new export. With overlay it first renders the overlay with tool:render-a-motion-graphics-overlay. Every folder, name, level and the lock come from the film's list:settings row.

values.title: Build a markdown section from entries, word for word
values.job: Write one markdown section out of a list of entries (what people said or wrote), keeping every entry's words exactly as they came in
values.description: Give a heading and one or more sources, each a JSON document holding a list of entries. Every line of an entry's text is written behind a quote marker and nothing else about it is changed (blank lines, trailing spaces, headings and code fences inside an entry stay as they were), so the section is a record and not a paraphrase. Entries keep their order and are grouped by source. The names of the fields to read (the list, the text, a label, a time stamp, a group name) are inputs. A source with no list, an entry without its text field, and sources holding nothing are refused, because an empty section looks the same as one that found nothing. The result is ready for tool:place-a-section-in-a-markdown-document.

values.title: Build a screen from lines of changes
values.job: Build a screen made of shared parts from the lines of JSON changes an AI wrote for it, and say which lines or parts did not fit
values.description: Give text: lines, each one RFC 6902 change (add, replace or remove), a list of changes, or a whole spec, to { root, elements, state, reads }; optionally requests, the screen's declared requests by name. Every complete line is applied in order; a line that is not JSON, uses another op, changes another path or is too long is left out and said without stopping the rest. Returns spec (each element checked against its part's declared props and fixed where it can be), said (the lines left out), fixes and problems (an unknown part, a missing required prop, no root or a root never sent).

values.title: Build the request that starts a seller's payment setup
values.job: Build, without sending it, the payment provider (Stripe) request that starts a seller's payment setup and gets their hosted onboarding link, or any other request the folder's operation map names
values.description: Calls buildStripeHttpRequest (tools/shared-code/src/build-provider-request.mjs) with the input: operation_id names one row of tools/shared-code/src/provider-operation-map.json (operation:create-connected-account and operation:create-account-link start a seller's setup and its hosted onboarding link; the map has every other operation too), input_facts holds what the request says (operation_subject becomes the form-encoded body of a write or the query of a search, provider_object_ref fills the address, acting_account the Stripe-Account header where the row declares it; a subject id becomes client_reference_id), idempotency_key becomes the Idempotency-Key header of a write, api_version_policy the Stripe-Version (the map's current version when left out) and required_credential_ref the name of the key a sender would use (credential-class:stripe-restricted-key when left out). Answers the finished request: method, url, headers, body, auth { scheme, credential_ref } and api_version. It holds and reads no key, puts no Authorization header on the request, sends nothing and moves no money: the request is for a sender (or a person) to look at first. Refuses an operation the map does not name and a missing provider_object_ref where the address needs one. The old screen also sent the request with the seller's own key and took the seller to the onboarding page the answer names; this run does neither.

values.title: Prepare records for my lists with their sources and basis (runs on your computer)
values.job: Take records I keep in files and prepare everything to put them into my lists as records, each value with where it came from and how sure we are, in batches I can send
values.description: Reads the mapping and source files from the one folder the person granted this tool. The records a mapping reads (a lists_read or a `kind: records` source, by type and id prefix) are not read here: the caller's AI reads them from a store and hands them in as `records`. Maps each source by the person's rules, then returns counts, pending or diverted items and the write commands as result data. It writes no local file and sends no records. A row with no address, two rows with one id, a link to a row that does not exist, a value over the limit or a basis naming too many sources is refused by name. It knows no record kinds or lists: all of it comes from the mapping.

values.title: Build the train rows and held-out test lines for teaching a small model my rules (runs on your computer)
values.job: Make the training set to teach a small model my writing rules, with the test lines held out before any training
values.description: Reads the person's laws, their writing rules (one yes-or-no question per law, which answer fails, and which ruled-bad sets count as bad for it), the lines they ruled on, an optional transcript of them speaking, an optional folder of other people's caption files, made-up training lines and their held-out lines. Splits real lines by source before any training (ruled lines by the heading they sit under in a folder of guides, the transcript by halves, captions by video), keeps never-train and held-out lines out of training, and writes items.json (every real line with its side, sets and the laws it breaks) and train.jsonl (one row per law and line: question, options, gold answer). The same request always makes the same rows.

values.title: Calibrate a camera frame
values.job: Calibrate a camera's view of a court, table or screen once from four corners, so every later point is measured in that frame
values.description: Give min_confidence (the floor an automatic result must reach) and detected ({ corners: four [x, y] in the order top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left, confidence }) as a corner detector gave it, or null; manual_corners (four [x, y] from a guided manual adjustment) are used when the automatic result is missing, too unsure or unusable. points ([[x, y]]) are mapped into the frame. Answers state (calibrated or needs_manual), source (auto or manual), the confidence seen, h (the projective map to the unit square) and failures: each failed automatic attempt with its reason, for the caller to keep as training data. Corners that are repeated or in a line are refused in words. It runs no detector and keeps nothing.

values.title: Measure whether a small model can answer my check's question, on lines I already ruled on (runs on your computer)
values.job: Ask a small model my check rows' questions about every line I already ruled good or bad, and fit where each row should pass and fail a line, and whether it is usable at all
values.description: Give settings_record (the person's setting row for this tool as the person's store gives it: its fit bars, good_sets, frame and models), rules (the person's check rows with an ask, { id: record:check:<id>, value }), lines (the name of the set of labelled lines) and line_rows (the labelled-line check rows of that set and of the sets the asks' examples name, read by the caller's AI from list:checks). Ruled lines (each with good) count by their own ruling, optionally only one split and only those with context (context_only); lines kept by set count as good when a set the setting's good_sets names holds them. Each line is asked one question a sentence and scored by its worst sentence, then tool:fit-pass-and-fail-lines fits t_fail, t_pass, AUC, recall and the held-out shares with the setting's bars (fpr overrides fail_good_share_at_most). Answers { <rule id>: finding } and keeps nothing; the person's AI writes a finding into that row's ask.calibration. Lines a model was trained on must never calibrate it.

values.title: Call a treg endpoint
values.job: Call any endpoint in treg's catalog by its id, with its inputs, paid from the person's treg balance, never above a cost ceiling the caller names
values.description: Sends one call to treg for the endpoint id given, with the person's treg token from their saved treg key (the token is placed as the request leaves and never shown), and answers the provider's reply as treg relays it (a routed treg.* endpoint answers {output, raw, _treg}). Send the method the catalog names (endpoint.method), its query fields in query and its body fields in body, exactly as tool:read-a-treg-endpoint-and-its-price lists them; a path field goes in query. max_cost_usd is sent as treg's X-Treg-Route-Max-Cost: treg documents that a call it would bill above it is refused with HTTP 402 route_max_cost before anything is charged. This SPENDS the person's treg balance: read the endpoint's price first, say it to the person, and keep max_cost_usd at what they agreed to. A reply outside 2xx is an error that quotes treg: 402 is an empty balance or the ceiling, 503 provider_capacity_unavailable names other providers of the job; failed calls are not billed. The answer's headers (beside the reply, lower case) say what the call cost and how to follow it: x-treg-cost-micro is the charge in millionths of a US dollar (on an asynchronous submission, the amount held until the task finishes, not a charge; on a replay 0, with x-treg-original-cost-micro), x-treg-call-id is the call's id (keep it), x-treg-served-by the provider a routed call used, x-treg-cache a cached answer, and x-treg-async the descriptor of an asynchronous task. Tell the person the cost with each answer. An answer of 202 with _treg.outcome pending is a task still running: follow it with tool:read-a-treg-call and its call id, never by calling again. A team's own registered tool is called the same way, as <tool-name>/<path>.

values.title: Cancel a booking on my calendar
values.job: Remove a booking's event from my own calendar
values.description: Deletes one event from the person's own Google calendar, with the person's own calendar account (the held value calendar-account); Google tells the attendees. An event already gone counts as cancelled. Answers changed, or error and why.

values.title: Cancel a Codex run on this computer
values.job: End a running Codex run's process group and read back that it is cancelled (harness/codex-runs.mjs cancelCodexRun)
values.description: Ends the run only while it is still the same running process (its start time is checked). Answers the state and cancelled true when it was running; a run that is not running answers cancelled false.

values.title: Cancel a Stripe subscription
values.job: Cancel a buyer Stripe subscription now, or at the end of what they have paid for
values.description: Give subscription_id, and at_period_end: true to keep the paid period running and stop the next renewal. Uses the Stripe key of the seller connection that seller_connection names (service_connection:stripe is your own).

values.title: Cancel prepared resource usage report
values.job: Release only an unsent usage report; retain possible provider charges for reconciliation
values.description: Release only an unsent usage report; retain possible provider charges for reconciliation. Takes the report row and the cash row its cash_id names, as the caller read them, and answers the rows to keep (the cancelled report and the released cash) for the caller to write while both are still at the versions it read.

values.title: Captions of what is being heard
values.job: Show the captions of a listening and fix a word, a speaker or a line in them
values.description: Answers the last captions of a listening from its heard rows (`heard`), with the person's corrections applied, after applying the caption ops given: on, off, edit { id, text }, speaker { id, name }, hide { id }, show { id }, undo { id }. The corrections are in `captions`, the state the last answer gave, handed back with the next request; a heard row is never rewritten. It keeps nothing: the new `captions` state is in the answer, for the person's AI to keep where it chooses.

values.title: Is this capture a repeat?
values.job: Say whether a captured text (screen words, a transcript) is the same as, or nearly the same as, one already seen, before it is kept or uploaded, and forget what was seen in a span when that span is erased
values.description: Give action seen with text (and at, an ISO time; now when left out), or action erase with from and to (ISO times). Give entries, the memory the last run answered (none on a first run). Answers duplicate (false, exact or near) and of (the exact hash of the earlier text), or forgotten (how many were erased), and always entries, the memory to give back next time. Exact means the same text after normalising; near means a 64-bit SimHash within near_bits; texts under least_words_for_near words are never near. Settings: read-data/capture-dedupe.json.

values.title: Places capture must not read
values.job: Say which categories of places (banking, health, social, shopping, adult content, entertainment) a screen or browser capture must not read, whether one address is in them, turn a category on or off for the person, and take in more domains as a cursor diff
values.description: action list (the default) answers each category, whether it is on and how many domains it holds, and the cursor. check with address answers its category among the ones on, or null; a subdomain counts, a look-alike does not. set with category and on answers the categories on and prefs, the person's choices to keep. diff with diff ({ from, to, add: [{ domain, category }], remove: [domain] }) is applied only when from is the state's cursor, and answers the cursor and state to keep; a removed domain stays removed over the seed. Give prefs and state from the last answers (defaults when left out). Settings and the seed: read-data/capture-exclusion.json.

values.title: Carry a computer to a meeting point
values.job: Say what a public host must run so my computers behind a router can be reached through it, and which port each one gets there
values.description: Takes the id of a way row (frp, rathole and ssh-reverse-forward are shipped; pass `ways` to use rows of your own), the meeting point's relay host (its hostname and the values the way's text names, such as control_port) and the computers carried to it, each with its id and the value the host needs to admit it (`server_value`: a token, or a public key). Answers the ordered steps the host runs (a file to write with its mode, or a command to run), the arguments of the program that serves the meeting point, and the program's pinned download. Each computer's port at the host is a stable hash of its id into a range held as data; two computers that hash to one port are refused, and one of them is given a `salt`. The computer's own half is kept running by `serve` under the init row for its kind of computer; run the file's `install` on that computer. The tool holds no vendor, operating system or host: each is a row.

values.title: Carry connections from a computer
values.job: Carry iMessage and the other connections only this computer reaches (WhatsApp and similar) to the person's account, sending what arrives and what the person's AIs ask to send, while the computer is on
values.description: Says how carrying this computer's connections is going: program connections, whether it is running on this computer, and whether the person's installed set wants it. Installing this tool turns carrying on for this computer; removing it stops it. Takes no input.

values.title: Catalog a channel's videos by format, with views against the channel's rolling baseline (runs on your computer)
values.job: List every video of a YouTube channel with its format (episode, side piece, compilation, members-only, short, or a series of its own) and how its views compare with the nearby videos of the same format
values.description: Reads <youtube_folder>/flat/<channel>-videos.json and -shorts.json (yt-dlp flat playlist dumps) and, when present, <id>.info.json in captions/, videos/ or comments/ for the exact upload date, likes and comments. A video's format: short for the shorts list; the format of the first of the person's series_prefixes its lower-case title starts with; compilation when the title holds one of compilation_words; members-only with no views; side when side_pattern matches the title or it is under 3 minutes; else episode. Its baseline is the median views of the 10 same-format videos on each side in list order. Writes <data_folder>/catalog.tsv.

values.title: Change a booking's status
values.job: Work out a booking's new record for confirming, cancelling, completing or marking a no-show, only in the ways a booking may move
values.description: Answers the booking record moved to a new status: waiting bookings can be confirmed or cancelled, a confirmed one can be completed, marked no-show or cancelled, and a finished one never moves. A cancel carries its time and reason. Asking for the status it already has changes nothing. A move that is not allowed is refused with the moves that are. It keeps nothing: the AI keeps the answered record. A waiting booking whose time has passed can be cancelled but not confirmed, and one that did not hold its time is confirmed only if the time is still open among the other `bookings` given.

values.title: Change fields of documents in my folder list
values.job: Change document frontmatter, write whole text or remove a document in a granted folder, using its read identity and publication requirements
values.description: For each row { id, values: { note.<key>: value or null }, if_identity } rewrites only the named frontmatter keys; other keys, comments and body remain. Values must fit the folder's declared property kinds; file facts cannot be written. Whole text and removals require the read identity (null for creating an absent document). Exact paths with declared text_extensions may select other UTF-8 text files, which accept whole text only, without note properties. Ordinary folders compare identity before rename or unlink and require externally serialized cooperating writers: they do not provide arbitrary-writer filesystem CAS or an OS-confined path handle. require_atomic demands a genuine atomic confined publication owner and refuses before filesystem effects when the adapter cannot supply one; it is never downgraded. List-original sources pass this requirement to their change owner. The answer names kept identities and removed documents.

values.title: Finish, fail, give back, hand on, withdraw, flag or remove a task
values.job: Record what happened to a task: finish it with its result, say it failed, give it back, hand it on to someone else, say what blocks it, take back one I gave, or remove it
values.description: Reads the task id and makes the move action names, by the rules in task-moves.json: finish (the taker; needs result, may add summary and check) and fail (the taker; needs result: why) end it as Done or Broken; release gives it back to To do (the taker, or anyone once it is held longer than the stale-take time; because says why); hand-on replaces the assignees (required) and gives the task back to To do with no taker (the taker, or the giver while it waits); stuck says what blocks it (anyone, so a watcher can flag it; needs words) and unstuck clears that; withdraw takes back a task still waiting (its giver; because); wait keeps recoverable work blocked on this same task with continuation {owner, action, after, reason}; resume returns it to waiting when due (its taker, giver or continuation owner); plan saves the acceptance a finish checks (the taker); edit changes a waiting task's words, assignees or acceptance (its giver); remove deletes the record (its giver, or anyone once it is finished). The move is one write of the whole task conditioned on the value just read: when the task changed meanwhile nothing is written and the answer is moved false with reason changed and the task as it now is. A move the rules do not allow is refused, saying why. A finish also needs check: the exact saved outcome, checked_at during this take, consumer evidence ({ref, observation}), and one matching check per saved obligation. This records accountable observation and does not itself prove its truth. The caller hands in every record it reads as input.records; this tool reads no store and names no store method. Each write it makes comes back as keep, for the caller to keep in the person's own store.

values.title: Change cells or words in a spreadsheet or document, keeping everything else (runs on your computer)
values.job: Change the cells of a spreadsheet or the words of a Word document by rules, and write a new file that keeps every other part, style and chart as it was
values.description: Takes the file and a rules file (a JSON list). A rule is one of: kind cell (match by formula_contains, value_equals or text_contains, optionally on one sheet; set a formula, a formula_replace, a value or a text_replace), kind shared-string (match equals or contains; set text or replace), or kind document-text (match equals or contains; set text or replace). Cached values are written beside formulas so the next reader sees the intended value without a recalculation. Every part it does not change is copied byte for byte. The report gives how many places each rule changed; a rule that matched nothing is reported with a warning, never silently accepted. The input file is never changed; the new file is written to the output path.

values.title: Change my groups: add, move, order, nest and remove
values.job: Add things to my groups, lists or collections, move and reorder them, put some into a new group inside, take a group apart, or bring a whole folder tree in as groups
values.description: A group is any list of addresses (records, pages, people, other groups) in an order; a member whose address is a group nests that group. changes is a list applied in order as one change: ensure-group, add-member (nodeRef, memberId, role?, presentation?, placement?), remove-member (memberId), reorder-member (memberId, placement), move-member (memberId, toGroupRef, placement?), set-member-fields (memberId, role and presentation, null clears), patch-member-presentation (memberId, presentation merged into what is there), group-members (memberIds, toGroupRef: the new group, wrapperMemberId), ungroup-members (wrapperMemberId), delete-group. Every change names groupRef { family, parts }; a placement is { index }, { before: memberId }, { after: memberId } or { at: start | end }. Member ids are yours: nothing is invented. tree (optional) is { family, records: [{ node_id, parent_id, ordinal, role, title, external_identity, attributes }] }: nodes with role group become groups and every node is placed in its parent by ordinal, its title and attributes kept as presentation. The groups touched are found among the records handed in; a group can never end up inside itself, and a repeated member id is refused, so the whole change is refused and nothing is written. Only groups that changed are kept: keep holds each changed group record { id, type, value, expected } (value null removes a group that is gone, expected is the record as it was handed in, null for a new one). The run writes no store. Returns groups (every group the change read or made, as it is now), written (how many records changed), removed (record ids), unplaced (tree nodes not placed, with why) and keep.

values.title: Change speed over part of a video
values.job: Play part of a video in slow motion or sped up, such as the moment of contact at half speed, and optionally keep only a window around it
values.description: Plays the stretch from `from` to `to` (seconds) at `speed` (0.5 is half speed) with the sound, the rest at normal speed, keeping only `keep_from` to `keep_to` when given. Saves the new video in your files.

values.title: Change what holds me
values.job: Set the one thing I must do aside with a reason, hand it back to my AIs, choose what turning the hold off costs me, ask to turn it off, or turn it back on
values.description: Reads and keeps nothing.
