Answers your hold setting after a change, by your hold rules: set-aside needs a reason of the rules' length and lasts the rules' minutes, a few times a day; hand-back gives the rest of the thing to your AIs by one of the rules' ways and leaves the hold; choose-stake picks what turning off costs, in force once the stake before it has run its delay; turn-off takes effect only after the stake's delay and comes back by itself; turn-on is at once. state is your hold setting as you last kept it; the answer holds the whole next setting (state) and the tasks the change makes (jobs, calendar-task records under stable ids with real producer provenance), for you to keep together.

values.title: Check my app's bundle only uses what each package made public
values.job: Stop a build that takes a file from a package that did not declare it public: read the bundler's own list of what went into the finished bundle and report every import that reaches into a package's private files
values.description: Give metafile_file (the bundler's metafile, esbuild's shape, a path inside the folder the person granted for reading), packages_root (the folder whose sub-folders are packages), declaration (how a package declares its public files: file, the name of the declaration file in each package folder; entries_at, the dotted path to the list in it, or empty for a root array; optional kind_at and kind together filter entries by their kind; path_at names the file or folder inside an entry, or is empty when each entry is itself a path string) and optionally bundle_root (what the metafile's relative paths are relative to; the granted folder when absent). The tool has no default declaration. Each import from outside a package to a file the package did not declare, and each use of a package whose declaration file cannot be read, is a finding in words. Imports inside one package, to files no package owns, to external modules and to virtual modules are not judged. Returns ok, edges_checked, packages_reached and findings.

values.title: Check a buyer may open something
values.job: Decide whether a buyer may open one gated thing (a page, a lesson, a publication) from the access it requires
values.description: Takes the scope the thing is gated by ({ schema: "addressed-expiring-value-scope/v1", value_ref, instance_ref, required_access_refs }) and the buyer. A thing that requires no access is open to any named buyer; otherwise the buyer must hold any one of the required access refs now (tool:see-who-holds-paid-access works that out from the access rows the request carries: payment_events, offers, grants, rules, lifecycle). Answers authorized true or false: a scope that is not exactly that schema, no buyer, or access that cannot be worked out is false with no revision. Otherwise the answer carries membership_revision, which changes when the buyer's access changes, so an action admitted on it can fail closed when membership moves.

values.title: Check that a check row proves what it says
values.job: Check that each check row a person is about to write judges what it says: every text it should pass passes it, and every text it should refuse is refused
values.description: Give rows: the check rows of a person's Checks list ({ id, kind: check, says, kinds, a test such as words, pattern, exact or path with where_pattern and allow_exact, and fixtures: { pass: [...], refuse: [...] } }). Each row is judged alone by the one judge (tools/check-against-a-persons-rules-and-verdicts, rules mode) on each of its fixtures: a fixture is a text, { text } or { view }; a text given to a row that reads a value is placed at the row's path. Returns holds (true only when every row with a test holds), rows ([{ id, holds, checked, wrong: [{ expected, fixture, got, findings }], no_fixtures?, broken?, read_by_a_model? }]) and lines saying what is wrong. A row with a test needs at least one pass and one refuse fixture; a row with no test is read by a model and holds null. Nothing is read from or written to anyone's records.

values.title: Check that a template built from my packaging ledger still matches the ledger and lost nothing (runs on your computer)
values.job: Check that the template made from my packaging ledger joins back to the right videos, files and caption events, and that nothing from the earlier version was lost
values.description: Reads the ledger and a compiled template (the TEMPLATE.json that tool:make-a-word-template made from the projected source) for one source key and checks, record by record, that every video's title, description, thumbnail words, thumbnail analysis, caption references and hook evidence join back to its ledger row and to the BLAKE3 identities of the metadata, image and caption files, with no caption text copied. With --before-compiled and --before-ledger it also checks that every record of the earlier compiled template is still there with the same fields (older inline caption excerpts may only become event locators) and that the ledger kept its earlier bytes as an exact prefix, adding only the --expected-new-video-id rows under the source key.

values.title: Check a computer from outside
values.job: see what anyone on the internet can see of one computer (open ports, certificates, its SSH version, its domains' registration, how long a connection takes) and say where it differs from what the computer's row declares
values.description: Give the computer's public address, the ports its row declares and the names it serves. It tries every port in settings.json ports_to_try and every declared one, reads each name's certificate and its domain's registration expiry (RDAP), reads the SSH version line, and times the connection. It answers what it saw and the findings: an open port the row does not declare, a declared port that does not answer, a certificate or domain within its warning days or unreadable. It logs in to nothing and writes nothing; every connection goes through the run's own proxy.

values.title: Check a connection
values.job: Check that the person's connection to a place still reaches its account, before a post is set to go there or a read is made
values.description: Asks the place which account the person's connection signs in as: give place (the slug of a place in read-data/post-places.json that declares a check) and account_id (one of the person's accounts of that place's kind, from tool:list-post-destinations). It asks with the value the person's vault holds for it, placed only as the request leaves, never shown. Returns what the place answers (the account's id and name or username; for YouTube also the channel's uploads playlist id). A refusal (an expired, revoked or under-scoped sign-in) means the person connects that place again. It posts nothing and changes nothing.

values.title: Hear a made cut against its plan: loudness, long silences and every spoken line (runs on your computer)
values.job: Listen to the cut you made from my plan: how loud it is, where it goes silent too long, whether every line I planned is heard and starts and ends where it should, and show me a few frames
values.description: Reads a made cut and its timeline (the one tool:assemble-a-plan-into-a-cut writes: each segment's kind, text, start and length). Measures its integrated loudness and every silence longer than the person's limit, reads each spoken segment with a speech reader (mlx-whisper, or any command the person gives) and compares it with the plan's line: the share of the words heard, the words missing, and whether it starts and ends on the plan's words. Takes the frames the person names (the first, middle or last segment of a kind) and lays them side by side. The report keeps listened_by, who listened to the cut end to end, which only a person sets. Exit 2 when a segment is to check, so it can stand as a check row of the cutter.

values.title: Check a destination is honest before it is published
values.job: Check a progress or results screen description before publishing it: it must not ship made-up numbers, ranks, bars or percents before the owner has worked them out
values.description: Give a destination descriptor and, if you want, refuse_keys: keys that may not appear anywhere in it. Returns honest (true when nothing is wrong) and every problem in words: a missing ref, subject_ref or statement, bars, stats, percents, ring labels, ranks, actors or fractions that are filled in instead of starting empty, and any refused key found.

values.title: Check a draft carries its profile
values.job: Check that a draft made for a person carries the references to the profile that shaped it and the profile it is checked by
values.description: Give the draft (a list of blocks, each an object), the names of the fields that must carry a profile reference, and optionally the profile's name. A field passes when some block of the draft holds a non-empty value in it, and, when you gave the profile's name, when one of those values is that name. Returns whether the draft fits and, for each field, whether it passed and why not. It judges references only, not the words.

values.title: Check a film's copy against a person's rules and verdicts
values.job: Check every line of a film's copy files (a script table, titles, cards, a post, a description, prose or narration) against the person's own branch of their checks, with their film readers and settings
values.description: Takes the person's settings row for this tool (list:settings, the record itself as settings_record) and reads the rules of one branch of their one Checks list (its own rows and every row of the branches above it; the nearest branch with judge_settings makes their verdict rows) from the records handed in (`records`; the run reads no store). Reads the lines of each file handed in by the layouts their settings name (Markdown table columns by file name, fenced post text, blockquotes, paragraph files, plain lines, JSON lines), or by a declared reader (sectioned prose, cue narration, a JSON owner's paths). Marks a line the person's own recorded words when every word is in a recording span the piece's plan cites, so a row written for added words only holds there; attaches each line's context and the reader-knowledge findings it is handed. Answers per line pass, fail or uncertain with every finding, the questions a model should answer by id (send them back as answers), the report with the BLAKE3 identity of each file, the reader settings, the rules and the checker, and exit_code (0 passed, 1 failed, 2 unqualified, 3 uncertain). Nothing is written.

values.title: Check a folder's files against rules I wrote
values.job: Check the source files of a project folder against rules the person wrote down, and say which files break which rule, where, and why the rule exists
values.description: Give rules: one row each, { kind: "source-file-rule", id, why, scope: { path_matches, path_excludes }, applies_when: { all | any | content_matches | content_absent }, subject: { named: "path" | "text" | "every_path" }, violation: { unit: { split }, forbidden, required, exempt }, message }. A pattern is a regular expression, or { pattern, flags }, or { collected: { pattern, capture } } to match any value found in the text being judged. forbidden and required mean AND across a list; exempt means OR. The rule is data: the checker knows no rule. Optional under (a sub-folder to judge) and recorded ({ known_findings: { <rule id>: ["path" or "path:line"] } }) to compare against a written baseline in both directions. Runs over the folder the person granted for reading, using git's listing when the folder is a repository and every file otherwise; it reads the files as they are on disk and refuses links and special files instead of following them. Returns passed, said, violations ({ rule_id, path, line, evidence }), report (findings grouped under each rule's why), rule_coverage, refused_paths, dangling_paths, files, ratchet. A run where no file met a rule is not a pass.

values.title: Check a model loop's calls for spinning
values.job: Say, from the tool calls a model loop made in order, when it should be nudged for repeating itself and when the job should be given back because it keeps repeating or its tools keep failing
values.description: Give calls (each { name, args, failed, malformed }) in the order they were made and, if wanted, rules ({ repeat_nudge_after, repeat_give_back_after, error_budget, words }; the shipped ones in read-data/loop-guards.json otherwise). A call is the same call when its name and its arguments match, whatever their key order. A malformed call (arguments that were not JSON, a tool the loop may not call) never counts. Failures count only in a row; one success clears them. Answers steps (each { at, nudge } or { at, give_back }) and, when the job should go back, give_back and the call index at.

values.title: Check a package's declared permissions
values.job: Say whether a package's manifest names only permissions the host has a row for, and what each permission it names lets it do
values.description: Give manifest ({ permissions: [ids] }) and, if wanted, permissions (the host's own rows, each { id, says, calls }; the shipped rows otherwise: network_egress, read_files, write_files, run_programs, use_microphone, read_screen). A permission with no row is refused, never ignored. Answers ok, unknown (the ids with no row), needs (the rows of the ids it named) and why when one is unknown.

values.title: Check that an intake batch landed in my packaging ledger exactly, changing nothing (runs on your computer)
values.job: Check that the videos I admitted are in my packaging ledger with the right titles, thumbnails and caption evidence, and that nothing else changed
values.description: Reads an intake manifest, channel catalog and review record and the ledger before and after, and checks without writing anything but its report: every reviewed video has a row under the source key and channel; its title matches the catalog and intake; its metadata file, thumbnail image and every caption evidence file match the BLAKE3 identities in the row; each hook locator points at a real caption event with the same times and carries no caption text; every provenance file exists; and every other row of the before ledger is unchanged (and, without --update-existing, the ledger grew by exactly the batch).

values.title: Check a page for search and answer engines
values.job: Read one public page the way a search or answer engine does, from the HTML it is served with and no script run, and say which checks it passes, which it misses and how to fix each
values.description: Fetches one public HTTP or HTTPS page, its host's robots.txt and, up to a set number, the pages it links to, and checks the served HTML against check rows: readable text without a script, one clear definition in the first words, a question as the first subheading, headings in order, named controls and labelled fields, structured data, a canonical address, published and updated dates, robots rules that let the answer-engine crawlers in, working links and more. A page that asks not to be indexed (a noindex robots tag) is not scored. It answers score (the share of scored checks that pass, among those that could be run), passed, failed, missing (each failed scored check with what it says, how to fix it and up to three examples), suggestions (failed checks that never change the score), and not_checked (checks that needed something that could not be read). The check rows ship with the tool and a caller may pass its own rows as checks, or name check ids to skip. It follows a small number of redirects, keeps at most 2 MB of a page and does not sign in.

values.title: Check a pipeline's stages for mistakes
values.job: Check a sales pipeline or any set of stages for mistakes: stages nothing can reach, a way out of a finished stage, or a move to a stage that does not exist
values.description: Give the stages, the moves allowed between them and the start stage. Returns sound (true when there is nothing wrong), each problem in words, and which stages are and are not reachable from the start.

values.title: Check a post
values.job: Say whether a post is ready for each place it is going, and what each place will refuse, before it is approved or set to go
values.description: Give post_id and records (the post and the person's connection records). Returns, for each destination, ready, problems (what that place will refuse, in plain words: words too long, a video or picture it needs, a kind or size of file it does not take, a setting it needs such as a video title) and not_checked (what could not be compared here, such as a video's length nobody gave, or whether the file is still in the person's files); and for the post, ready and said. Fix a problem with tool:draft-a-post. It changes nothing.

values.title: Check a presentation plan is ready
values.job: Check a compiled presentation plan against available capabilities and fresh observations before authorization
values.description: Give plan, capabilities (an array of available capability names), observations (keyed by requirement key, each with value, method and observed_at_ms), and optionally now_ms. Returns setup problems or ready_to_authorize. Requirements must declare accepted methods and a finite nonnegative max_age_seconds. Operator evidence cannot stand in for a sensor-only requirement. Input observations are caller-supplied; the tool does not authenticate sensors, grant permission or start recording.

values.title: Check that a library of records is valid (runs on your computer)
values.job: Check that my library of record files is consistent: every id a record names exists, ids are unique, counts match, tables use only their allowed values, and files derived from a source are not stale
values.description: Reads a library of JSON record files on the person's own computer through a schema file the person gives (it names the files, the relations that must hold between them, the tab-separated tables and their allowed values, the builders of files derived from other files, and the commands that say a derived file is stale). Runs every check the schema declares and prints one report: how many passed, which ones broke and exactly which ids or values break them, the table cells outside their allowed values and which derived files are stale. It changes nothing. It knows no record kinds: every file, id field and check comes from the schema.

values.title: Check my port or replica keeps its promises to its reference
values.job: Check a contract for work taken from a reference (a source ported, a behaviour ported, a visual replica, an inspiration, an anti-reference): the source and its identity, what must be preserved, and the proof (retained source lines, required mechanisms, measured pictures and pixel difference)
values.description: Give contract (the contract itself) or contract_file (a path inside the folder the person granted for reading), stage (pre-edit before the work starts, completion, the default, when it is done) and optionally target (a path the contract must own). A contract names schema (reference-adaptation-contract/reference-grounded-adaptation), id (REF-...), status, mode (SOURCE_FIRST_PORT, BEHAVIORAL_PORT, VISUAL_REPLICA, INSPIRATION_ONLY, ANTI_REFERENCE or NO_PRIOR_OWNER, a claim that nothing older does the job, carrying the search that found nothing), directive, sources, targets, preserve, allowed_deltas, banned_substitutions, baseline and proof; every identity is the BLAKE3 identity 1f:<64 hex> of the exact bytes. Paths are read relative to the granted folder. Source drift, a copy directive relabelled inspiration, a missing target, retained-line and mechanism proof, and for a visual replica the measured geometry, the picture identities and an independently measured pixel difference at or under three percent are all checked. Returns valid, errors (each in words), id, mode, status and measurements.

values.title: Check a rendered video's frames, joins and audio (runs on your computer)
values.job: Check my finished video for mistakes a viewer would notice: a stray frame at a cut, a cut inside a word, graphics off the frame or over a face, text too small, sound effects too quiet or harsh
values.description: Reads a rendered video (and, for the checks that need it, a JSON spec of its cuts, held frames and the graphics laid over it, plus the overlay render with alpha) and runs checks on its frames, joins and audio: in-frame, joins, word-clip, jitter, text, face, exits, dwell, type-sync, backing, movement, sound-balance, sound-harsh, sound-loops, sound-sync, settle, tempo, zoom, camera, motion-blur, internal-text, text-size, info-added, math-shown, cue, broll, placement, filler-words-cut, cutout-bottom, bridge (a local ollama model), held-face (Apple Vision), and, for a film made as several options per moment with a technique ledger, variety, devices, reused-footage and label-time. Its other commands make a fresh-viewer review pack (contact sheets, transcript, rules) and keep the technique ledger (variety, declare, map-add). Which checks run and every number and word list they use are the person's own limits, a JSON file the person gives (their AI reads the rows from the person's own records); the tool has no defaults, and a check with no limits row says so instead of passing. Each check prints PASS, WARN or FAIL with the seconds it happens at; a check that cannot run says why. It runs on the person's own computer, never on a server, and changes nothing it reads.

values.title: Check a sign-up
values.job: Prove a public address takes a new account end to end: sign up, sign in and read a signed-in page
values.description: Signs up one synthetic account at the origin with a software passkey made for this run only, signs in with it under the new account's address, and reads a page only a signed-in person sees, then the same page without the session. Answers each step's HTTP status, the new address and whether the signed-in read answered 200. The passkey leaves with the process, so the synthetic account can never be signed in to again.

values.title: Check a sound-effect palette against its spec and licences (runs on your computer)
values.job: Check that every sound in my palette has the right format, length, quiet edges and an allowed licence
values.description: Every rendered palette file against PALETTE.json: rate, channels, sample peak, fade edges, length equal to the trim, and a licence entry in the manifest that is not blocked; music files given have the palette's rate and channels and last long enough. Exit 1 on any failure.

values.title: Check a move to another stage
values.job: See which stage a deal, order or applicant is in, which stages it can move to next, and whether it may move to the stage you want
values.description: Give the stages (a pipeline, deal stages, order states), the moves allowed between them, the start stage and the record's moves so far. Returns where the record is now, every next stage with why it is or is not open, and, when you name a stage in to, whether it may move there and the move to keep with the record. A finished stage never has a way out, and a move naming a stage that is not declared is refused.

values.title: Check a Stripe event
values.job: Check a Stripe webhook before believing it (its age and its signature), and read it as a payment event to keep
values.description: Give the raw payload exactly as received and the Stripe-Signature header as signature_header. The signature is checked with the webhook signing secret of the seller connection that seller_connection names. Returns the payment event, or why it was not believed. Nothing unchecked is kept.

values.title: Check that my video moves as much as the one I copied (runs on your computer)
values.job: Tell me whether the video I made is as lively as the video I am copying, or holds still too long
values.description: Measures how much a reference video moves (the share of frames where the picture changes, and its longest still hold), sets the person's bar from the whole reference, then measures the piece from its start to the second its end card begins, at the same still threshold, and says whether it passed each row of the bar. The bar is not built in: the person passes a record of kind motion-bar, whose rows each name a measure, a relation (at_least or at_most) and either a multiple of the reference's own value or a fixed value. The bar always comes from the whole reference, so trimming a piece never moves it. Moving-pixel share is a measure of conformance to the reference, not of readability or quality. The measuring is done by this tool with ffmpeg and ffprobe, which it calls as declared programs; it reaches into no other app.

values.title: Check words or anything made against a person's own rules and verdicts
values.job: Check words, a title, a script line or a plan against a person's own rules and the verdicts they already gave, and say pass, fail or uncertain for each, with why
values.description: Give the units to check (each { text, kind } or { view, kind } for JSON such as a plan, with optional facts, field, context and findings you already have), rules (rule rows judge-words runs, and ask rows a model answers), and the person's own rule document (verdict_rules) and stands (stances, as tool:read-where-you-stand gives them), read from the records handed in (`records`) or the files given. Or give a branch in place of rules and verdict_rules: one of the person's branch rows (a node of kind branch in their one Checks list, list:checks, such as the kind of thing being made: a book, a script, an article, a post), and the rules are read from the records handed in: one tree in one list, every node naming the node it is part_of; the rows part_of that branch or a branch it is part_of, each branch read on its own (a branch below is never judged), plus the rows of every list a branch names in check_lists; step rows (questions of a decision step) and rows set Off are left out, a row that states no test (no words, pattern, exact, check, groups, path, evidence, ask or part) but says something is a reading row: a question a model answers once for each whole unit, made from the tool's own DATA over the row's words, carrying the calibration and model of the nearest branch's reading_settings, and listed in read_by_a_model; a piece of a source file, or a row that says nothing, is never judged: it is counted in rows_used.skipped.no_test, and a branch with only such rows answers no-applicable-rule; and the rows of the nearest branch carrying judge_settings (and of the branches extending it) are their verdict rows under those settings, the inherited rows generic rules. The answer then adds branch, lineage (nearest first) and rows_used. Their exact stand on a thing decides first: disagree fails, partly holds at review and fails at final, agree passes and clears the generic rules they named. Then their stated rows fail and their inferred rows (at_most uncertain) only hold. Nothing passes on silence: a thing nothing of theirs judges is novel, and an ask row never passes without a calibrated answer. The answer lists the questions a model may answer, by id; send the answers back in answers to use them. With branch the questions of a branch of hundreds of reading rows come in pages that each fit one answer: one entry for each rule (its ask said once, what every rule shares once in ask_all, a unit's own words never copied), and questions_page.next is the questions_after of the next call. Nothing about any person is built in.

values.title: Check my AI action policy
values.job: Check my AI action policy before I rely on it: rules it cannot evaluate, unknown behaviours, repeated ids and rules that can never decide because an earlier rule always does
values.description: Takes the fields the policy rules may read from an action and the policy (rules in order, each with an id, an optional `when` rule tree and a `then`). Answers ok and a list of problems, each with the rule id, a problem name (unknown-behaviour, incomplete-when, repeated-id or never-decides) and a sentence saying what is wrong. A rule never decides when another rule with the same `when` always holds first: any rule with the same `when` as a refusing rule, or an earlier rule with the same `when` as it. Nothing is changed; a request that cannot be run is refused with a sentence that says what to send.

values.title: Check how an installed app is hardened
values.job: Read how an installed macOS app is hardened, from its files and the system's codesign without launching it, and say in words what falls short: Electron fuses left weak, a missing hardened runtime, forbidden entitlements, an integrity hash nothing enforces
values.description: Give app: the full path of an installed app bundle (such as /Applications/Sample.app) inside the folder the person granted for reading. The app is never launched; only its Electron framework binary, its Info.plist and the system's codesign output are read. Returns app, findings (each { kind, name?, state?, said }) and ok (true when there are none). What cannot be read (no app bundle, unsigned, no fuse block, an unknown fuse version) is a finding, never assumed fine.

values.title: Check a commit's files against rules I wrote
values.job: Check the files of a repository's commit, as its host serves it, against rules the person wrote down, and say which files break which rule, where, and why the rule exists
values.description: Give archive (the https address of a .tar.gz, such as a host's archive of one commit) and rules, as tool:check-a-folder-against-my-rules takes them, with optional under, recorded, subjects_from and credential_name (the held name of a token a private repository's archive needs, sent only to the archive's own host). subjects_from computes, every run, a set a rule collects from (collected.from_subject) that the archive cannot hold: each value a pattern captures in the files of archive was, less those it captures in archive now (such as the tool ids another repository stopped declaring), with moved naming a value's new home. The archive's regular files are written into a private folder of this run (one top folder every path shares is dropped), judged by the same engine, and removed before the answer; a file larger than the DATA bound is not read: skipped_paths names each with its size and why, and a run where a rule covers one (unjudged_paths) is not a pass. Nothing on the person's computer is read, so a change is judged as it was pushed. Returns passed, said, archive, written, skipped, violations ({ rule_id, path, line, evidence, moved_to when its value's new home is recorded }), subjects (how many values each computed subject holds), report, rule_coverage, files, ratchet. A run where no file met a rule is not a pass.

values.title: Check an email sending domain
values.job: Ask my email-sending account to check a domain's DNS records again so it can be verified
values.description: Asks the person's email-sending account (Resend), with the key they connected, to check one domain's DNS records again, by the domain's id. The check runs on the account's side; tool:read-an-email-sending-domain shows the result.

values.title: Check my challenge definitions
values.job: Check my time-boxed challenge definitions are complete before I enroll anyone in them
values.description: Takes a list of challenge definitions and checks each one: its kind, id and label, the window it runs (a unit and a positive length, any unit), the reference to the rule that scores who fits, the reference to the content it walks through, the lowest score that joins, and an optional objective reference. Answers one result per definition: its id, whether it is valid and every problem found. It does not follow the references; the records they name are checked by their own owners. A window is an overlay on engagement, never a reason to take content away.

values.title: Check claims cite sources that were read
values.job: Check that each claim in an answer cites a source that was really read, and none cites one that was not
values.description: Takes the claims of an answer (each with citations naming a source id) and the ids of the sources that were really retrieved. A claim is grounded when at least one of its citations names a retrieved source. A claim with no citation is not grounded, and a citation to a source that was not retrieved is a fabricated reference that fails the whole answer. The answer is grounded when the share of grounded claims reaches min_grounded_ratio (1 when left out) and nothing was fabricated. An empty answer is never grounded.

values.title: Check a community's matchmaker settings before keeping them
values.job: Check that a community's matching settings can run: cadence, sizes, the evidence contract and the questions that cover every factor's citations, consent, follow-up hours, words for every job, refusal and state, contact pattern, limits and experiments
values.description: community is the value of a match-community record: { title, owner, created_at, matching }. Returns usable and problems, each a plain sentence naming the field to fix. matching holds every_days, round_hours, shortlist_size, posting_cap, group_size, cadence_label, default_on, contract (the match-evidence contract: factors, primitives, scope_fields, questions, citation_requirements, authority, forbidden_interventions), questions (the contract questions this community asks, which must cover every claim kind a factor cites), expected_value? (minimum_expected_value, minimum_distinguishable_delta), initiative { required_level, pre_authorized_levels }, grouping?, consent { answer_hours, selection { approved_values, veto_values }, yes_needs { field, equals }, screen }, follow_up_hours, jobs (profile, score, consent, topics, follow_up: { said, job } with {name} fields), words, state_words, contact_pattern, limits, discover { offers, seeks } and experiments? ([{ id, arms: [{ id, weight, jobs }] }]). Nothing is written.

values.title: Check copy before a person reads it
values.job: Check text, Markdown, pages, JSON, decks and picture readings against the rules you send, and the whole set against your required lines, audience, offers and counts, and say pass, fail, held or uncertain for each unit
values.description: Give words as text, texts, Markdown, value (any JSON; fields names which keys hold words, or "strings" for every string), units, sources (JSON with its place), html (pages), decks (a rendered deck's HTML) or pictures with their readings. Markdown reads headings, paragraphs, list items, table cells and fenced display text; unresolved quotes, preamble before a declared document title and unsupported blocks stay coverage problems. It retains each block's role and field; for findings whose context is not established, name the matching rule ids or grammar check names for review, which keeps those findings uncertain and leaves other findings in force. Give rules (one row each: words, pattern, exact or a named grammar check) or leave them out to use mechanical grammar rows. Optionally give required (locked lines, features, baseline ids, approvals with the person's own words and the text they sit in), audience, offers and counts, and the person's verdict_rules and stands. Nothing about any person is kept here; their rules are input. A source with no words, a required line gone, a row for the wrong audience, a count that is not a published list view, an offer listing fewer lines than the others and a picture with no reading are problems, never passes. Model questions come back as questions; send answers on a second run.

values.title: Check a value has enough support
values.job: Check that a value has enough independent support before my AI acts on it
values.description: Takes named checks (each passed or not, some required) and how many of the optional ones must agree. Permitted only when every required check passed and enough optional checks passed. No checks at all is not permitted. Answers permitted, which required checks failed, which optional checks agreed and the reason in words.

values.title: Check the places I let my AI write in keep a history
values.job: Check that every place declared writable (on the promise that something keeps what is written there, such as a version history) really keeps it, and say which keep nothing
values.description: Give the declaration (the JSON that lists the places, or declaration_file, a path inside the folder the person granted for reading), places_key (the key that holds the list, found at any depth), id_key (the key naming each place), bases (folders inside the granted folder a place may live under; "" is the folder itself) and retention_kinds ([{ kind, marker }]: a kind keeps what is written when its marker, a file or folder name such as a history folder, is present at the place or any ancestor up to the granted folder). exemptions ([{ place, why }]) names places that keep nothing on purpose; they are still examined and shown with their reason. A declared place with no folder here is unresolved, never a finding. Reading zero places is refused, never a pass. Returns passed, places_declared, examined_count, keeps_nothing_count and each place with what keeps it.

values.title: Check that the code my commits delete names where it went
values.job: Check a span of commits in a checkout: every source or test file they delete names its new home (a moved-from receipt) or the decision that retired it
values.description: Grant the checkout to read (one of the repositories read-data/rules.json names) and give range, two of its commits as <from>..<to>, and optionally repository, its name when its folder is named otherwise. Receipts in the other repositories are read from their checkouts beside it; one with no checkout there is listed in unread and its receipts are not counted. The same judge the check row record:check:deleted-code-names-its-home runs before each commit and push. Returns valid, judged (each deleted or renamed file with its home and how it was found), errors (each in words) and unread.

values.title: Check my documents have not fallen behind their source
values.job: Check that documents which each claim to reflect one source (summaries, translations, copies for other readers) still carry the source's newest numbered item, and the markers each must hold, and say which have fallen behind
values.description: Give sets: one record per source, { set_id, source, unit_pattern, required_markers?, mirrors: [{ document, required_markers? }] }, every document a path inside the folder the person granted for reading. unit_pattern is a regular expression for the identifier the source and its mirrors share (its first capture, when it has one, is read as a number, so item 99 sorts below item 218). A mirror is behind when it lacks the source's newest unit; being shorter than its source is not a finding. required_markers are literal strings a document must carry (a set's apply to every mirror, a mirror's own replace them). A document that does not exist is reported as missing, not as stale. Returns agrees and, for each set, newest_unit, the mirrors behind with what each lacks, the markers missing and the documents missing. A run over no set is refused.

values.title: Hear every recorded stretch my video plans cut, before anything is rendered (runs on your computer)
values.job: Before I render, listen to every stretch of recording my video plans cut and tell me which ones start or end in the wrong place, and what in the plans themselves is wrong
values.description: Reads a folder of cut plans (tool:assemble-a-plan-into-a-cut's plans) and, for each segment that cuts a recording, cuts that stretch from its source through the cutter's own lookup (so it hears what the render will cut), reads it with a speech reader (mlx-whisper, or any command the person gives) and compares the first and last words heard with the plan's text: a stretch that catches a neighbouring word or loses one is listed to check. Before that it checks each plan against the person's settings: a line drawn from the person's question library must name a question that is there and whose evidence the person allows, and a card that points at another plan must point at one that exists (or at a plan title). It changes nothing it reads. Exit 1 on a plan failure, 2 when only stretches are to check, so it can stand as a plan check of the cutter.

values.title: Check every claim my narrator makes, spoken or on screen, against my facts and sources before it is voiced (runs on your computer)
values.job: Check every sentence my narrator says and every text on screen against the facts I keep and the sources I cite, and tell me which claims fail and why
values.description: Reads a run's shots (shots/<id>.json: the voice script and the on-screen events), their claims files (claims/<id>.json: one entry per spoken sentence and per on-screen text, each citing world facts, source wordings, transcript quotes or saved frames), the person's world rows (lists.json, rows/<list>.json, relations.json: entities, facts and relations) and their sources file with its plain-text extracts. The world's own check runs first (row shapes, links, roles, every fact's words at its transcript second or file line); then each shot fails a claim that: is not covered (script or screen text without an entry, or an entry for nothing); is about the subject but has no support said by someone other than the narrator; ignores a world fact on one of its topics; quotes a source or transcript that does not hold the words; is stronger than its source on a strength scale; says a number not derived from its cited numbers or outside its qualifier; breaks a bound a world fact sets; makes a comparison the numbers do not hold; counts a number in another container than its source; says something is visible without a saved frame; uses a private, believed, past or planned fact without saying so, a claim not recorded as its speaker's statement, or a conflicting fact it has not weighed; or carries a hedge or attribution phrase. Every rule word (strength scales, qualifiers, subject words, labels, tense markers, quantity units) is the person's settings, and the hedge phrases are their no-hedge check row's words. Prints each shot's report lines to standard error and one JSON answer.

values.title: Check every piece of a person's files has a check or a reason
values.job: Say, for each of a person's source files, how many of its pieces have a check, how many a recorded reason, and which are uncovered
values.description: Reads the Checks rows handed in as records (the person's AI reads them from its own store: the ids of their Checks list and its rows whose kind is piece, as tool:split-a-document-into-pieces kept them, without their text), folding each piece into a running tally, so the run holds counts and a bounded number of named pieces. The run reads and writes no store. A piece is covered when checked_by names check rows that all exist, or when no_check has a reason (and every row its covered_by names exists). The answer: totals over every file, and per source file its pieces, those with a check, those with a reason and how many are uncovered, naming the first uncovered pieces by id, section and lead; status failed when any piece is uncovered. Checks and covered_by naming rows that do not exist are counted and the first named. The answer fits at most most_bytes of JSON: when more files remain, next is the after of the next page; with file, the page names that file's uncovered pieces by id, after after. Nothing is written.

values.title: Check answers to a form
values.job: Check a person's answers to a form's questions and say which are missing or not valid, and why
values.description: Checks each answer against its question: a required question left empty, a number outside its range, text too short, too long or not in the right format (an email, a phone number), or a rating off its scale. Question types (text, long text, number, rating, choice, a reference to a file) are rows with their own rules, and each question can lay its own rules over them. Returns every question's verdict and message, whether all answers are valid, and the first one to fix.

values.title: Check pages at every width and device setting
values.job: Open each page I give at every width and device setting and read every piece of text a person can see, refusing text that cannot be read, is drawn in a font the page did not ask for, is cut off or makes a phone scroll sideways
values.description: Opens each of screens (each { id, html, route?, fonts?, ready?, steps?, widths?, modes? }) in a headless Chromium through Playwright (headless-browser/launch.mjs, with its quiet switches and one-browser-at-a-time admission), at every width of views.json (phone 390x844 with no sideways scroll, tablet, desktop) and in every mode (light, dark, forced colours, Dark Reader), or the widths and modes asked for, through runMatrix (check-screens.mjs). The page's HTML is answered by the browser itself at its route on a made-up origin; any other request the page makes is aborted, never sent. Each view is scrolled window by window and every visible text node is judged: contrast under WCAG AA against the colour really behind it, a glyph drawn by a platform font the screen does not declare in fonts (system names such as system-ui never count), text cut off or outside the window, a phone page wider than its window, and a control with no accessible name; a screen that does not open is a failure. allowlist (allowlist.json's shape, none when left out) drops a proven false positive or keeps a decided look as reported. Answers passed, failures ({ screen, width, mode, probe, selector, text, detail }), reported, counts (failures per probe) and report (views read, texts read, seconds per phase). Writes no file and keeps nothing; needs a Chromium Playwright can find. Refuses a screen without an id or html, two screens at one route, and a width or mode views.json does not name. The deploy check also opens a live origin or a Worker, takes pictures of failures, runs the real Dark Reader extension and refuses a deploy; this run checks only the pages given.

values.title: Check whether a tour step may move on by itself
values.job: Decide whether a guided-tour step has met its advance condition: tapped next, touched the highlighted thing, answered, watched enough of a video, waited long enough, finished an embedded form, or a fact someone looked up has the right value
values.description: Give the step's advance condition ({ op, args }) and what is known now (signals: next_tapped, target_interacted, answer, media_ratio from 0 to 1, elapsed_ms, surface_completion_refs, owner_readbacks keyed by the fact's ref). Ops: tap-next, target-interacted, answer-given, media-watched (args.min_ratio, default 1), timeout (args.ms), surface-completed (args.completion_ref), owner-readback (args.readback_ref, answer_fact_ref or objective_answer_ref, with required_values_present, required_nonempty, required_answer_values, accepted_states or required_states), and all-of / any-of over a list in args.of, nested as deep as written (an empty all-of is false). Every threshold is in the condition. An op that is not defined answers false, so a typo never pushes a person on; they can still move on by hand.

values.title: Check an imported history receipt
values.job: Create an imported account history receipt or verify its immutable archive references by reading the files through this run’s records door.
values.description: Create an imported account history receipt or verify its immutable archive references by reading the files through this run’s records door. All opinion settings are caller rows or explicitly selected content-setting records. No old Worker store is imported.

values.title: check incoming attachments
values.job: Check that every file attached to a batch of incoming messages or arrivals belongs to my Files and fill its actual name and media type. Refuse the batch before acceptance when an identity is missing, malformed or unavailable.
values.description: Check that every file attached to a batch of incoming messages or arrivals belongs to my Files and fill its actual name and media type. Refuse the batch before acceptance when an identity is missing, malformed or unavailable.

values.title: Check live orders with the broker
values.job: Check my live orders with my broker: which are filled, at what price, and which never got there
values.description: Give routes (the same routes the orders were placed with, each with status_request and open_statuses). Give records too (the live trade-order records to check, and the trade-day-spend records, read from the store that holds them). Every live order still open (sending, unknown, or a status in the route's open_statuses) is asked about at the broker, and its record takes the broker's real status and fill; order_ids checks those orders whatever their status. An order the broker never named and does not know is marked not-placed and its day's spend is given back. Nothing is kept here: the answer's records are the changed trade-order and trade-day-spend records and a trade-order-event for each answer, for you to keep. The held live-broker-credentials reach only the request.

values.title: Check that a match rests on what people actually said
values.job: Turn people's intake answers into scoped profiles and check that a proposed match's scores cite what both people actually said before anyone is matched
values.description: Everything about the intake is the contract you give: factors, primitives, scope_fields, questions [{ question_id, claim_kinds, primitive_ids, scope_field? }], citation_requirements per factor [{ side: subject | candidate, any_of: [claim kinds] }], authority [{ name, claim_kind, list? }] and forbidden_interventions (the authority entry whose values block a proposal). operation build-profile takes participant_ref, answer_facts [{ question_id, answer_fact_ref, value, evidence_refs? }] and connected_source_facts (each must carry its consent, access lease, field scope, observation and expiry times and whether it can be revoked, or it is not evidence) and returns the profile: claims, the scope, coverage per primitive, authority, status grounded or partial, and problems. operation check-assessment takes subject_profile, candidate_profile, assessments (per factor: score in (0, 1], rationale, inference_ref, the claim refs it cites on each side and evidence_refs) and proposed_interventions, and returns per-factor evidence with status grounded or no_justified_match and the reasons; a proposal either person forbids blocks every factor. Nothing here scores: scores come from whoever assessed, and only cited ones pass.

values.title: Check nested input within limits
values.job: Check an untrusted nested value (an imported document, pasted rich text, list row values from an AI) before it is rendered or stored: refuse it in plain words when it is nested deeper than 100 levels, holds more than 100,000 values, or refers back to itself
values.description: Give value (any JSON) and, optionally, limits ({ max_depth, max_nodes }) tighter than the defaults. Returns ok and nodes when the value is fine, or ok false with reason (too_deep, too_many_nodes, cycle), the limit crossed and said, the words the person reads. The walk keeps its own stack, so a very deep value never overflows the call stack.

values.title: Check the names a change brings in
values.job: Check the folder and file names a change brings into a repository against the person's naming rules, and say which name holds a codename, a status, a time or a technical metaphor, with the word and why
values.description: Give rules: { words: [{ why, words }], patterns: [{ why, pattern }], passes: [outside names such as a product or a file format], repositories?: [owner/name] }, and optionally range: from..to (two commits of the granted repository; without it, its staged index). Only names the change brings in are judged: each added or renamed file, and each folder of its path the base tree did not hold. A name is read as words (split at - _ . and spaces and where lower case meets upper case, its extension left out); a word in passes is never refused, otherwise the first word listed in words or matching a pattern fails the name with that row's why. Returns valid, judged (how many names) and refused [{ path, name, word, why }].

values.title: Check paper orders with the broker
values.job: Check my paper orders with my broker: which are filled, at what price, and which never got there
values.description: Give routes (the same routes the orders were placed with, each with status_request and open_statuses). Give records too (the paper trade-order records to check, and the trade-day-spend records, read from the store that holds them). Every paper order still open (sending, unknown, or a status in the route's open_statuses) is asked about at the broker, and its record takes the broker's real status and fill; order_ids checks those orders whatever their status. An order the broker never named and does not know is marked not-placed and its day's spend is given back. Nothing is kept here: the answer's records are the changed trade-order and trade-day-spend records and a trade-order-event for each answer, for you to keep. The held paper-broker-credentials reach only the request.

values.title: Check words for personal data
values.job: Before words go to a model that is not on the person's computer, check on the computer whether they hold personal data (email addresses, phone numbers, card numbers that pass the checksum, IBANs, national ids, and by a model on the computer a name with an address or health details), and offer the person the choice: send as it is, do it on this computer only, or keep it back
values.description: Give text, and model ({ endpoint, model, timeout_seconds } of a model served on this computer) to also ask the model questions. Answers contains, kinds ([{ kind, how: rule | model, count or share }]), model_checked, choices (when something was found) and said. Only counts and kinds come back, never the matched text. With no model named, or one that does not answer, said says only the rules were checked. Shapes, questions, threshold and choices: read-data/personal-data.json.

values.title: Check a pick prompt or result for wording the person does not want
values.job: Check the words of a free pick prompt, its choices or a result summary against the wording the person does not want used (for example talk of money) before they are written
values.description: Give the texts to check, each as { field, text }, and banned_terms: the person's own list of words and phrases. Nothing is shipped as a default list. A term is found anywhere in a text in any letter case (so a short term also matches inside a longer word); a phrase written with spaces matches any run of white space. Returns passed and, for each hit, the field, the term and a message. An empty list passes everything. Refuses texts or terms written wrongly.

values.title: Check the proof behind finished work
values.job: Check whether the proof given for a finished task is something someone else could go and check, or just a claim
values.description: Reads the proof recorded for one finished item and answers CHECKABLE when it names something a second person could look at (a command and its result, a count, a file, a measurement, a screen to open, a wall that was hit) or VAGUE when it asserts, restates the task, or describes a feeling or an intention, followed by one sentence saying why. It judges only whether the record can be trusted, not whether the work is good.

values.title: Check prose against its writing rules and its review evidence
values.job: Check a piece of prose against the wording I rejected, the text that must stay as it is, the sections it must have in order, and the reviews and source evidence it needs, before I call it current
values.description: Reads a prose document, a writing profile (schema writing-profile-v1: rejected wordings and superseded terms with their authority, protected literals, required sections in order, required source components, allowed original sources by BLAKE3) and, optionally, a review manifest (schema writing-review-v1) bound to the document's BLAKE3 and each paragraph's BLAKE3. Finds rejected wording through case, width, punctuation, soft-hyphen and inline-emphasis variants, in the document or (when a rule says heading) only in headings; a protected literal changed or missing from the visible text; a required section missing, repeated or out of order; a paragraph no current review covers; a required source component without literal source and destination evidence (checked with the span verifier in this folder). Answers checks_satisfied, review_required or known_failure, or invalid with the kind of input fault. The report omits bodies and caller names and is created new. Zero findings is not proof of meaning, voice or approval.

values.title: Check that quoted words are the exact bytes of their source files
values.job: Check that every quote I took from a source file is still the exact text at the byte range I recorded, in a file whose BLAKE3 is the one I pinned, and find which words of a text are the source's own literal words
values.description: Reads a bindings manifest (schema synthetic-d245bc86d584) naming each source file by absolute path and BLAKE3 and each quote by its source, text and UTF-8 byte range. Hashes the bytes read, refuses a source whose hash changed or that is not valid UTF-8, and compares each quote with the literal slice, with no normalisation and no automatic offset repair; a mismatch says whether the text occurs elsewhere in the source. The readback names sources and quotes by their zero-based positions only, never their paths, ids or bodies, binds itself to the manifest's BLAKE3, and is created new (an existing report is never replaced). The module also exports literalPieces, which finds the longest runs of a text's words that occur in a source in order and lists the words that do not. Literal evidence only: it does not authenticate a speaker or judge meaning.

values.title: Check someone is in a space
values.job: Say whether a person is a member of a shared space right now, and why not when they are not
values.description: The one answer to whether a person is a member now. It reads, from `records`, the space's join rows, the person's member row and what they hold now (paid-access), and answers member true or false with a state: member, lapsed (their access ended; they are members again the moment it holds), left, removed or none, plus the reason in words and their type and how they came in. A person who holds the access again after a refund is a member again with nothing written in between.

values.title: Check whether my spoken takes are complete with a small model (runs on your computer)
values.job: Test whether a small decider model on my computer can tell a complete, usable take from one cut short, restarted or self-corrected, on takes made from my own transcripts
values.description: Give transcripts (a folder of word-timed transcript JSON) and model (a decider snapshot). Takes are built from real sentences: as said (usable) or with one controlled fault (not usable), so the labels are true by construction. Returns accuracy, accuracy per fault, and how many it answers and gets right at confidence 0.7, 0.8 and 0.9.

values.title: Check the X connection
values.job: Check that the person's X connection still reaches its account, and say which account it is
values.description: Asks X which account the connection signs in as (GET /2/users/me, the x descriptor's verifyRequest), with the access token the person's vault holds for it, placed only as the request leaves and never shown. Returns X's answer: data.id and data.username. A refusal (an expired or revoked sign-in) means the person connects X again. It changes nothing.

values.title: Check what a buyer paid
values.job: Check that the money a buyer actually paid is a price my offer declares, before giving them what they bought
values.description: Give offers (your offer rows), offer_id and paid ({ amountCents, currency }), and optionally quoted (the amount, currency, cadence and priceOptionId that were quoted). A per-unit price is accepted only for an amount some whole unit count produces.

values.title: Check when I am busy
values.job: Read when my own calendar shows me busy between two times
values.description: Asks the person's own Google calendar when it is busy between two instants, with the person's own calendar account (the held value calendar-account). Answers the busy intervals, or unknown with the reason when the calendar cannot be read: unknown is never an empty free answer, so offer no times it guessed. Changes nothing.

values.title: Check that an AI keeps its work in Trillion, not on disk
values.job: Check whether a file an AI is about to write belongs on disk or in the person's Trillion lists, and say which list and which row keeps it instead
values.description: Give rules ({ source_repositories: [owner/name], scratch?: '.git/scratch', new_files_refused?: [{ why, pattern, except?, list? }], list_copies?: [{ folder, list }], list_copy_sync?: regular expression, refused_places: [{ place, why, list? }] (place: a path, ~ the home folder, * one folder, ** any), lists: { <list id>: { type, id_prefix?, value } }, default_list, classifier?: { rubric, providers, timeout_seconds, pass_answers, lists_by_answer? }, says? }) and call: the tool call ({ tool_name, tool_input }: a Write or Edit's file_path, or a Bash command). Every path the call writes is found (redirects, tee, cp, mv, install, ln, mkdir, touch, dd, curl -o/-O, wget, mktemp, tar -x, unzip, git archive -o; a cd earlier in the command moves relative paths) and placed: in a checkout whose origin is a declared source repository it passes when tracked, when it is the scratch, or when new, not ignored and matching no new_files_refused row; a list_copies folder or a refused place (the longest match wins) refuses it naming its list. A path no rule places is asked of the classifier (tools/ask-a-small-model-for-a-verdict ask) with a timeout; a model that fails passes it with a warning. Returns valid, judged, passed [{ path, how, why }], refused [{ path, how, why, list, keep: the row { id, type, value } that keeps it instead }] and warnings.

values.title: Check that a rewrite kept the template's words (runs on your computer)
values.job: Tell me which words of the original a rewrite deleted, replaced or added, and whether the slots were filled from real sources
values.description: Judges any script (markdown with fenced dim blocks, a table column, or plain text) or any piece JSON (a fill, a measured render, another template) against a template, dimension by dimension: words by difflib on normalised words, categories by sequence alignment, numbers within a limit, timed events within a tolerance, boxes, colours and vectors by distance. Reports every fixed word deleted, replaced or inserted, every slot run as sourced, empty, unsourced, removed or still holding the original's value, the share of fixed words preserved, the worst lines and an annotated line view. A change listed with a reason in an exceptions file counts as preserved and stays visible. With --check it exits 1 unless every judged dimension meets its threshold, nothing unexcused was inserted and every slot fill has a source.

values.title: Check writing against its recipe
values.job: Check something written from a recipe before it goes anywhere: it cites only the sources given, it keeps the recipe's rules and reviews, and it is shaped for the next tool
values.description: Give recipe_id or recipe (as tool:compose-a-writing-instruction took), writing (the JSON object you wrote in the recipe output shape), grounding, work_item, context and review. For ordinary recipes, review is { accepted, verdicts: [{ id, accepted }] }. For an opt-in gate_policy.evidence_contract of source-backed-claims/v1, also give evidence_packet with exact source editions, claims, scopes and UTF-8 quote spans; writing must include exact draft_text and matching claim refs/version/text/scope/source_refs. Semantic review then binds each required verdict to the exact draft, claim version and scope, and source edition set. Reviewer attribution is caller-supplied and is reported unverified; it is not authenticated. Rights metadata is preserved but does not authorize publication. Checks stop at first refusal, then build one delivery request for the named owner tool. A refusal has no delivery.

values.title: Check writing from a file
values.job: Check a source backed writing request from a file the person granted to be read, without sending the source bytes in the tool call
values.description: Give file (a relative path in the folder you granted the tool to read), and optionally recipe_id or recipe to override the request's recipe. The file is bounded to 8 MiB and must be a regular JSON file inside the granted folder. It uses the same writing gate as tool:check-writing-against-its-recipe and returns only that gate result; the file contents are not returned.

values.title: Choose a content style
values.job: Choose a content style manually or from ordered rules for the supplied media shape
values.description: Give shape (the available input properties), rules (the rules document), optionally mode (manual or rule), and definition for manual selection. Returns the first matching definition, mode and unchanged shape. The container row runs no local AI or caller-supplied program. An unmatched rule reports local_ai_required; authorized local CLI callers retain the original AI mode with their rules file.

values.title: Choose which options go ahead together
values.job: Choose which of several options (a person, a workflow, a tool, a place) go ahead now: every worthwhile one that does not compete for the same thing, the best where they do
values.description: configurations [{ id, configuration_kind (any word), expected_value, scope: { <field>: text }, required_resource_refs?, collision_refs? }] and scope_fields (the scope every configuration must name). Every configuration with a positive value and a complete scope goes ahead at the same time; two compete only when they share a collision ref, and then the higher value wins. Two that share a collision ref and are within minimum_distinguishable_delta of each other are both held back rather than picked between. Returns selected, rejected (with reason: non_positive_expected_value, scope_missing, resource_collision, indistinguishable_expected_value, ...), configuration_requests (state proposed) and counts.

values.title: Choose how each file is shown
values.job: Classify each file by its name and media type to choose how it is shown: as code, markdown, a diff, a picture, JSON or plain text, with the language, icon and label it is shown under
values.description: Give files ([{ path, mime_type? }]): each file's name or path and, when known, its media type, which wins over the extension. Answers classified, one per file in the order given: renderer (code, markdown, diff, image, json or raw), language, icon, label and the mime_type it was taken as. It reads only the names and types it is given: no file is opened, nothing is drawn, nothing is sent, and the signed-in classification owner the screen asks first is not called, so the answer is the file-content renderer's deterministic fallback. Refuses an empty list or a file without a path. The screen (show/FileContentRenderer.tsx and the media player) also draws the file, plays sound and video, pages PDFs and edits the facts kept about a file; this run does none of that.

values.title: Choose how I am notified
values.job: Keep one of a notification setting's options as this person's choice
values.description: setting is the setting's name and choice one option id from tool:my-notification-choice. A choice that is not one of the options is refused with the options named. A setting that is not described, or describes no options, has nothing to choose from: it returns changed false and says so in said, and keeps nothing. Returns { setting, choice, previous, changed, said }; choosing what is already chosen changes nothing.

values.title: Choose the programs left running
values.job: Choose which running programs were left behind by a session that ended, judged only by the person's own left-behind and never-stop rule rows
values.description: Reads nothing and changes nothing. Give programs and complete as tool:list-running-programs answered them with commands, left_behind (the person's rows saying how a program is left behind: parent_pid and/or session_owner_gone, older_than_minutes, and optionally cpu_share_at_least, command_pattern and name_pattern, every condition holding at once) and never_stop (the person's rows naming a command_pattern and/or name_pattern that is never stopped). A list not given is refused, never read as empty. A program whose session still has an owner, or that the rows cannot be judged on, is always kept. Returns read (how many rows of each list it read), picked (each program to stop with the row that says so and why), kept (the programs a never-stop row kept) and said.

values.title: Choose the feed each widget shows
values.job: Say which feed each widget on my phone or Mac shows: the one I picked for it, or else the feed its size takes from the surface's feeds in order
values.description: Give the surface (widgets, watch) and the widgets on it, each with its size (small, medium, large or extra_large) and the feed the person picked for it if any, and optionally how many rows each feed has kept (a feed with rows is taken first; with no counts every feed counts). Returns the surface's feeds in the order they are taken, and for each widget its feed and whether that feed was picked or taken from the order. A picked feed may be any feed the glance DATA names. Nothing is read, kept or drawn.

values.title: Choose the name I show in a space
values.job: Check a member's chosen name for one shared space and answer their member row with it, for other members to read
values.description: Answers the person's own member row with the name set, at most 80 characters, under `keep` for the caller to store. Only a current member may. Members read this name and nothing else about them; their contact is never shown.

values.title: Choose which of my workflows fire for these parts of a seed
values.job: Say which of all my workflows, and the Workshop's I have installed, fire for each part of something that arrived, from the conditions each workflow carries on its own row
values.description: Every workflow is a candidate branch of the one tree. Takes parts: the parts of one seed, each an object of its typed fields (for example kinds, subjects, people, niches, own_words; the fields are whatever the conditions read). Is given the person's own workflow rows as values (own), read by the caller from wherever the person keeps them, beside every recipe this Workshop installs; it reaches no database; when both hold an id the person's row wins, and when it holds no conditions the installed recipe's are used. Each workflow's conditions are its fires_when (branches/fires-when.json): a list of { label, condition: { fields, tree }, made_by, state }, the same fields and tree tool:filter-rows-by-rules takes, evaluated by the same formulas engine over the parts. Answers chosen (one row per workflow, part and condition that kept it, ranked within each part by specificity: score is the sum over the tags or rules the part met of log(workflows with a condition / workflows holding that tag), times the condition's measured weight, rank 1 best), broad (conditions that kept more than half of the parts, to be rewritten), unfinished (conditions with a rule the engine cannot evaluate or no rule at all, which choose nothing), unconditioned (workflows with no condition On, by id and label, to be judged by their words), unmatched_parts and the counts. Nothing is written; no workflow, branch or tag is named in the tool.

values.title: Choose what one visitor sees
values.job: Pick which version of a page, offer, headline or feature one visitor gets, from rules you write as data, keeping the same visitor on the same version
values.description: Scores every candidate version with a decider (a rule written as structured data: a split by visitor, a switch on what is known about the visitor, a preference for the version with the best recorded result) and returns the winner, the full ranking and any findings. The same visitor key always lands on the same version. One candidate is a feature flag, two or more is an A/B test, a decider that reads recorded results is a bandit. A candidate set or decider that does not validate is refused with every problem listed.

values.title: Keep principles from captioned videos, each backed by a quote checked word for word (runs on your computer)
values.job: Collect the principles that creators and teachers state or show in their videos, with the exact words and the second they say them, prove every quote is really in the captions, and rank each principle by how many independent channels back it and how well their videos did
values.description: Works on a folder of YouTube caption files (<id>.en.json3) with their <id>.info.json. corpus: one line per captioned video with its channel, title, views, kind (short or video), the captions as timed lines, and how many times its channel's usual views the video got (the usual is the median from a views table the person gives, or from the folder itself). candidates: the best 40-second windows of each video for what the person wants principles about, scored by their topic words, advice-giving phrases, a matching title and how well the video did, per channel, plus the first 45 seconds of each channel's best videos. find and verify: the second a quote is said at, and a check that every quote in the person's rows is an exact substring of its video's captions (ignoring case, white space and curly apostrophes), telling a wrong quote from a missing caption file and a quote at the wrong second. registry: merges the person's working rows (their own groups, lane names and stage names, passed in as files) into one registry of principles ranked by evidence strength (for each independent channel the best of log2(1 + the video's times-the-usual, capped at 64), halved when the quote only demonstrates the principle), with sources linked to the second, demonstrations, and contradictions linked both ways. extract: reads every part of every video with a chat model the person names (Ollama, MLX, llama.cpp or any OpenAI-compatible server, given as {url, model}), asking for the rows their own asks file describes, from any domain; each row's quote is put back onto the exact caption words and the seconds they start and end, rows whose quote is not in the captions are set aside with the reason, and a stopped run continues from the next unfinished video. coverage: videos, shorts and words per platform and channel, and how many videos the person's rows already cite. index: a Markdown page of the registry with its counts, strongest principles and their sources, demonstration-only principles, contradiction pairs, and principles per stage, channel and lane, written into the person's own Markdown template: their words stay as written, marked sections are filled from the registry, and principle ids, counts and evidence named in their words are filled in. Word-timed transcripts from other sites are read too. What the principles are about, how advice sounds, what rows a model is asked for, and how rows group and are named for stages come only from the person's files; the tool holds none. Only extract sends words anywhere, to the model the person names; with a local model nothing leaves the computer and no key is needed.

values.title: Give a record the label of the first rule it meets
values.job: Give a record the label of the first of my rules that holds: each rule has clauses over facts read from the record (is present, is absent, at least, at most, equals), and I get the rule's key, label, tone and severity, or none
values.description: Takes a record, the facts to read from it (a key, a path, and how to read it: present, as a number, as an age in seconds up to now_ms, or as it is) and rules in order (a key, a label, an optional tone and severity, and clauses over facts). Answers the first rule whose clauses all hold, with its key, label, tone and severity exactly as given (null where none was given), or no result when none holds. A request that is unfinished (a rule with no key, label or clause, a clause naming a fact that was not declared, an operator that is not listed, an age fact with no now_ms) is refused with a sentence. The tool names no label, tone or threshold; the clock is now_ms, never read.

values.title: Re-voice the spans that are still bad, in the speaker's own voice (runs on your computer)
values.job: Where the speech in a recording is still unusable after cleaning, say the same words again in the speaker's own voice, with the same timing
values.description: Takes the output folder of tool:grade-and-repair-speech-audio and the same spans file, and for each span still graded clone: checks that the span's speaker is the voice of the reference recording (wespeaker embeddings; similarity at or above the threshold in the person's settings) and refuses it otherwise, so nobody else's voice is cloned. A span that passes is split into phrases at the pauses of the original; each phrase is spoken by the settings' clone model in the reference voice, read back by whisper (zero word errors against its words), stretched to the time the original phrase took (never more than the settings allow) and laid at its original offset, so the span keeps its length and every phrase starts where it started. The span is kept only when the whole read has zero word errors against its text, and is then marked cloned in grades.json. The reference must be a clean recording of the person who agreed to be cloned. It runs on the person's own computer, never on Trillion.

values.title: Code the comments that name a character with the person's codebook (runs on your computer)
values.job: Sort the viewer comments about a character into the person's codes (what they enjoy, miss, dislike, and so on) and count comments and likes per code
values.description: Reads <data_folder>/comments-character.tsv (collect-the-comments-that-name-a-character); each comment gets every code of the person's codebook ({code: regular expression}, any case) it matches, judged by the one word judge, tools/judge-words, or mention-only. Writes <data_folder>/comments-character-coded.tsv and prints comments and likes per code.

values.title: Find the questions my viewers really ask and the moments where I already answer them (runs on your computer)
values.job: Find the real questions people ask in the forums and video comments my audience reads, sort them into my topics, tell me how often each comes up, and find the moments in my own recordings where I answer each one
