values.description: Works on files the person already has: forum posts (tool:keep-forum-posts-from-a-public-archive keeps them) and video comments (tool:keep-channels-latest-videos-and-captions keeps them with also: ["comments"], or a yt-dlp info.json). `candidates` keeps every sentence that ends in a question mark, is 6 to 40 words long and is the writer's own question (first person, or a direct how, why or what), with its own link, word for word; nothing is rewritten. `keep_comments` keeps the whole top-level video comments that ask a question or state the writer's own situation, tags each with the person's tag columns (their keep rules and tags are settings), and writes them most-liked first with a page of the most-liked per tag. `rank` gives a first reading order: each candidate in the person's bucket whose patterns hit it most. The person (or their AI, with them) picks the questions worth keeping; `build_library` then measures how often each picked question recurs (how many other sentences of the whole sample mean nearly the same thing, plus its score or likes) and finds the moments of the person's own recordings that answer it (nearest by meaning, then re-ranked by a cross-encoder, a strong match or a possible one). `rematch` matches again against an archive's tagged moments too, each with its reach (whether the recording can be cut now). `embed_moments` makes the moments from word-timed transcripts. `add_package_questions` adds the questions of a research package, keeping a researcher's hypothesis apart from a viewer's own words. `apply_gate` checks every asker line with tool:check-copy and the person's rules. `remap_picks` keeps the picks on their questions after the candidates are found again. `reports` gives the shortlist, answers by reach, a review page, the chosen questions and their brief, comment counts and a vector check. The person's buckets, codes, overrides, inferred questions, package readings, reach rules and words are their list:settings row record:setting:collect-and-rank-viewer-questions~<scope_kind>~<scope_id>, read through tools/settings from a file holding it. The models (sentence-transformers bge-small-en-v1.5 and bge-reranker-v2-m3) run on the person's computer; nothing is sent anywhere and nothing is paid for.

values.title: Collect the comments that name a character, per video, with their likes (runs on your computer)
values.job: Find the viewer comments that talk about a character, per video: how many, their share of the likes, and how many of the most liked ones
values.description: Reads <youtube_folder>/comments/<id>.info.json (yt-dlp --write-comments); a top-level comment names the character when the person's mention_pattern matches it (any case), judged by the one word judge, tools/judge-words. Writes <data_folder>/comments-character.tsv (every such comment, most liked first) and comments-summary.tsv (per video: comments read, mentions, their share, their share of the likes, mentions among the 20 most liked).

values.title: Commit the chosen changes
values.job: Commit what is chosen for the next commit in a project on the person's computer, with a message
values.description: Give folder (the full path of the project folder the person has let this tool use) and message (what this commit says). Commits what is staged, as the person's own git settings say who made it, and returns the project's changes after it. It does not stage anything itself and does not send the commit anywhere. With nothing staged, git's own words say so.

values.title: Compare two AI builds on trap tasks
values.job: Score two builds of an AI's behaviour on the same trap tasks from the calls each run recorded, and say on which tasks they differ
values.description: Give left and right: each arm's trace { arm, runs: [{ task_id, state, calls: [{ tool }] }] }, written from the calls its runs recorded (never from what a run said about itself). Both are scored over the whole trap battery this tool carries (src/behavior-evals.json; each task drawn from a waste or failure class, scored by max_calls, forbids_tool, requires_tool, calls_before and ends_in), or over battery when given. A task an arm has no run for scores 0 and stays in the denominator. Returns arms (score, of, ran, classes, tasks), same_denominator and differ.

values.title: Compare two versions of a diagram
values.job: Tell me what changed between two versions of a diagram: boxes and arrows added, removed or changed, and what changed on each
values.description: Takes a before and an after, each with boxes (an id, and optionally a label, a size, a lane and a style) and arrows (from, to, an optional id and label). Boxes match by id. Arrows match by id when they have one, else by from, to and label. Answers the boxes added, removed and changed (the label, lane, style, width or height that differs, each with its before and after) and the arrows added, removed and changed (an arrow with an id whose label, from or to differs), all ordered by id; an arrow without an id is named "from -> to" or "from -> to : label". Two diagrams that differ only in the order of their lists have no difference. Positions are not compared: lay both out and compare their positions where that matters.

values.title: Compile a presentation plan
values.job: Compile source material and a selected format into a presentation plan with its claims and setup requirements
values.description: Give material (id, title, claims and fields), format_id and formats (a document with a formats array). Returns rendered beats, the unchanged claim snapshot, source references, capabilities and setup requirements. Missing fields and claims are refused together. It neither saves the plan nor grants recording or publication authority.

values.title: Build the instruction to write from
values.job: Build the exact instruction to write something from a writing recipe and the person's material, before writing it
values.description: Give recipe_id (from tool:list-writing-recipes) or your own recipe (instruction_plan.prompt_template: literal text, { block_ref }, { slot: work_item, path }, { slot: schema }, { slot: grounding, label } and conditional segments; optional output_contract, gate_policy, delivery_target, context_retrieval, work_item fields), work_item (the person's text and the answers the recipe asks for; missing answers take the recipe's defaults), grounding (source excerpts, each with its id) and blocks (your own instruction blocks, replacing kept ones of the same id). Returns instruction_text to write from, input_refs, output_kind, output_schema, and the recipe's gate_policy and delivery_target. Write from instruction_text yourself, then hand what you wrote to tool:check-writing-against-its-recipe. Nothing here writes or sends anything.

values.title: Build thumbnail candidates from my frames with layout templates (runs on your computer)
values.job: Make thumbnail candidates for my video from real frames of my footage, laid out like proven thumbnails: my face, the thing, big words, arrows and tags
values.description: Six layout templates read off strong reference thumbnails (a claim box across a split, a big face beside stacked words, a magnifier on a flaw, price tags on a flat backdrop, a held object with quoted words, a corner face with stroked words) compose 1280x720 candidates from the person's full-size frames and cut-outs: crops, punch-up, white sticker outlines with shadow, boxed or stroked words, curved arrows, price tags, a magnifier. Each candidate is one row of values in the person's settings row (which frame, face box, words, sizes, arrow ends); the font is the person's.

values.title: Connect an account by signing in to the service
values.job: Connect an account (Gmail, YouTube, Instagram, any service whose sign-in is switched on) by signing in on the service's own page, starting it with the values the new connection should have
values.description: The page routes GET /work/api/connect/start and GET /work/api/connect/callback, run for the page's account (or by an AI with { path, method, query }). Start: query service (a descriptor vendor of this folder's records.json whose sign-in is switched on), each starting value of the new row of list:service-connections (its choice and boolean fields: status, read_only, can_send_as, can_be_primary), and optionally account (the account meant: the service is asked to pre-choose it and the callback refuses any other), wait_seconds (how long the link waits to be opened) and return_to (a path on this site). It keeps nothing: the state it hands the service holds the pending sign-in (the service, the new connection's id, the starting values, the scopes, the account meant and when it expires), signed with the vault's own sign-in key (sign-in-state-key, Ed25519 through secrets:sign), and the PKCE verifier is that key's signature over the state, made again at the callback. It answers { authorize_url, service, connection_id, expires_at }: the service's own sign-in address for the person to open (the engine lets no route tool answer a redirect). The list and its sign-in app rows (which hold the app's id in the open) are given as `stored`. Callback: the service sends the person back with code and state; a state whose time has passed, or whose facts the vault does not sign the same, a service error, a missing code or a descriptor that no longer matches answers why and saves nothing. A state is used once because the service takes its code once and the verifier binds the code to that state. Otherwise the code is traded for the tokens by this folder's http rows (kept sealed in the vault as the new connection's fields: the connection is held there), the connection is checked with the service, and the service-connection row with its starting values is answered under `keep`, for a caller that keeps rows. With no sign-in key in the vault, nothing is sent and the answer says how to make one. The answer is a plain page that says connected, or why not. No token, verifier or secret is in any answer.

values.title: Connect an AI app on this computer to Trillion
values.job: Read, preview, add or take out the Trillion MCP entry in AI apps on this computer (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor)
values.description: Runs harness/setup.mjs with --action mcp-inspect, mcp-preview, mcp-register or mcp-unregister for the AI apps named in client (a comma-separated list of claude-code, codex, gemini-cli, cursor). mcp-inspect and mcp-preview write nothing: they answer each app's config file path, whether a Trillion entry is there now, and a review_hash for the exact change. mcp-register writes the entry only when given that review_hash as reviewed, so the person sees the change before it is made; mcp-unregister takes it out. Claude Code and Codex use the bridge the Trillion Mac app installs, which keeps the account key in Keychain; an entry here does not by itself sign the app in (each result's sign_in says how). Exit 0 means every app was handled, 2 means one was blocked or has a custom entry, 1 means the request was wrong (standard error says what to change).

values.title: Copy a file into a storage place
values.job: Copy one of the person's files, any size, into a folder of a storage place they were given, or say plainly that they may not add files there
values.description: Asks the storage place whether the person's account may add a file to the folder; when it may not, answers that in words with the folder's name and copies nothing. Otherwise opens one resumable upload with the account's connection and sends the file to it one piece at a time, each piece read by byte range from the file's address (a share link of the person's files), so memory holds one piece whatever the file's size. The places are DATA (read-data/storage-places.json: Google Drive and OneDrive today; a new kind is an entry). The account's key arrives on descriptor 4 and goes only to the place's own host, or to Composio when the account was connected there; the upload's own address is never answered.

values.title: Copy a website
values.job: Copy an existing live website, its pages as visitors see them plus its pictures, styles and fonts, into the files a public app is published from
values.description: Opens each page of the site in a headless browser, waits for it to finish drawing, and keeps it as a visitor sees it with its scripts taken out; follows the site's own links up to the page limit and fetches same-site pictures, styles and fonts. Copied addresses point at the copy; omitted pages and files keep their original addresses. Returns site.json in your files: { files: { path: contents } }, which publish_public_app_definition takes as its files, and a list of what could not be copied and why. Works on public web sites: the engine lets it reach nothing else.

values.title: Correct a message recorded as the person
values.job: Correct a message kept as the person's own words when it was really said by a diagnostic, a peer or generated context: the corrected message keeps its text and time, and the false row, its arrivals and its thread row retire
values.description: Give the kept message's id, the speaker it really came from (sdk diagnostic, peer or generated context), the evidence, and the rows read from the store ([{ id, type, value }]: the message, its arrival rows and its thread index row when there is one). Answers the correction under `correction` and the rows that change under `keep` ([{ id, type, value, expected }]) for the caller to store. Only a kept person message can be corrected, and the same correction again answers the first one.

values.title: Correct a resource usage settlement
values.job: Answer the next, corrected version of a supplier-cost settlement under the original purchased terms, with the exact customer refund, credit or additional-authority obligation each payer now owes
values.description: Answer the next, corrected version of a supplier-cost settlement under the original purchased terms, with the exact customer refund, credit or additional-authority obligation each payer now owes. Give previous, the settlement and allocations this settlement_id last answered, with the corrected invoice and payers and the reason. This run reads no rows and keeps nothing; the caller keeps the old version beside the new one.

values.title: Correct a message decision that names another app's chat
values.job: Point a saved message decision back at its original chat, and keep what it replaced
values.description: Rewrites a message decision's reason, next action, success measure and move to continue its handoff in the original chat it came from. The caller reads the kept person message, its source chat and the handoff by SQL and hands them in as facts, with the agent name the handoff must carry: the message must be the person's and in that chat, the handoff must have arrived from that message, and the decision must be an act that names another app. The replaced decision moves to decision_history and the generation rises by one; an exact repeat answers already_corrected and writes nothing. Any mismatch is refused and nothing is written. Its records are handed in as records and what changed comes back as keep.

values.title: Correct when a message was written
values.job: Show when the person actually wrote a message they kept without its original time: the message keeps its id, text and links, with the exact time and the evidence
values.description: Give the kept message's id, the time it was really written (any past time; never one ahead of the clock), the evidence, and the rows read from the store ([{ id, type, value }]: the message and any earlier time correction). Answers the correction under `correction` and the rows that change under `keep` ([{ id, type, value, expected }]). Only a kept person message can be dated, never after its capture time, and the same correction again answers the first one.

values.title: Check and total cost measurements
values.job: Check cost observations, forecasts and billing evidence and return their rows, and aggregate only comparable measured units from observations in the request
values.description: Takes the observations, forecast, billing evidence or forecast rows in the request, which the caller read from its store, and returns the checked rows (their ids and values), grouped totals with scenario, currency, source revision and time windows kept distinct, or the latest refresh state. Corrections and unknown coverage are preserved. Reads and keeps nothing; the caller writes returned rows through its store.

values.title: Count a character's turns from the speaker marks in captions and the pitch of each turn (runs on your computer)
values.job: Count a character's turns in each episode a second, independent way: the captions' speaker-change marks, and whether each marked turn is spoken high
values.description: For each episode in <data_folder>/catalog.tsv with <youtube_folder>/captions/<id>.en.json3 holding at least five '>>' marks and an <id>.emb.npz (do-work/find_voice.py embed) in <data_folder>/voice or extra_voice_folders: a marked turn (to the next mark, at most 30 s) whose median window pitch is at least ratio (else the settings' caption_turn_pitch_ratio) times the episode's median pitch is the character's. Writes <data_folder>/character-caption-turns.tsv with the turns, seconds and seconds in the first 5 minutes.

values.title: Count a paid installment in Stripe
values.job: When a pay-in-N plan invoice is paid, count it, and stop the plan after the last one so no extra invoice is ever made
values.description: Give subscription_id and the paid invoice_id. A replayed invoice is counted once; the last installment keeps the buyer access and cancels the subscription. Plans that are not pay-in-N are left alone. Uses the Stripe key of the seller connection that seller_connection names (service_connection:stripe is your own).

values.title: Count a show's running jokes, lore names and rituals across its captions (runs on your computer)
values.job: Count how often a show's running jokes, lore names and rituals come up across all its captions, when each first and last appeared, with one example
values.description: Each caption line of each catalog video (<youtube_folder>/captions/<id>.en.json3, else .en*.json3) is judged against the person's terms ({term: regular expression}, any case) by the one word judge, tools/judge-words. Writes <data_folder>/lore-terms.tsv: per term, the mentions, the videos, the first and last upload date and the middle mention by date as an example (id, second, the line with its neighbours).

values.title: Count my AI conversations per app
values.job: Count the AI conversations in my records per app, and how many messages each app's conversations hold
values.description: Reads the rows of the person's AI conversations list (record:ai-conversation) from the rows handed in, only their app and messages fields, and answers the number of conversations and messages per app, most first. Reads nothing else.

values.title: Count the real bad rulings on lines
values.job: Count how many lines a person ruled bad, whether that is enough to let a model row fail lines, and how many of them each model row catches
values.description: Give rulings (the person's ruling rows of list:checks, type record:check with id prefix record:check:ruling-, as records or values) and settings_record (the person's setting for this tool: real, who counts; needs, fields a ruling must carry to count; needed, how many real bad rulings a model row needs before it may fail lines; and optionally verdict, the bad word, and default_kind), or those fields themselves. Returns real_bad_film (the real bad rulings), needed, promotion_allowed, counts (every "<by> <verdict>" of the log) and bad_lines (one per text: text, kind, where), the lines to check. Send again with rules (the model rows, [{ id, ask: { calibration: { t_fail } } }]) and results (the check's results on the bad lines: [{ text, uncertain: [{ rule, p_fail }] }]) to add escalated_by_any, per_rule (lines each row catches at its own t_fail) and unanswered. It runs no check and writes nothing.

values.title: Count where a person stands
values.job: Count the stands a person has taken, by kind of thing and by stand, with how many changed their mind and how many took a stand back
values.description: Give stands: the stands read back (each the answer of tool:read-where-you-stand, or a stance record's value: kind, stance, and earlier when its history was read). Returns read (how many), by_kind ({ kind: { stance: count } }), with_history (stands with earlier stands) and taken_back (read with no stand now). It reads and writes nothing.

values.title: Start a space
values.job: Start a shared space with this person as its owner and first member, as its space row and the owner's member row, for the caller to store
values.description: Answers the new record:space row and the owner's record:space-member row under `keep` for the caller to store. This person is the owner and first member. A space id already in the records is refused. A community is joined by its own rules and is not made here. It replaces the old create_membership.

values.title: Credit the kept lines to who wrote them
values.job: Credit each line of a text's newest version to whoever first wrote it, an AI or a person, from its versions, and count how many kept lines are each writer's
values.description: Give versions, oldest first, each { by, text } (by is the writer: ai, person, or any name). Answers by ({ writer: lines }), kept (lines in the newest version) and versions. It counts kept work, not generated work: a line edited away is not counted, a line a person rewrote is the person's, and spacing alone is not a rewrite (lines compare by the BLAKE3 identity of their normalized text, src/kept-work.json). It keeps nothing.

values.title: Credit what visitors did to the version they saw
values.job: Join who saw which version with who bought, signed up or clicked, so each version's results can be read
values.description: Takes two lists of records (which visitor was assigned which candidate, and which outcomes each visitor produced) and a join that names the fields of each, and returns one observation per visitor, outcome and candidate with how many times it happened and the value it carried. The same records always give the same observations. A join that does not validate is refused with every problem listed.

values.title: Critique a public page
values.job: Judge public web pages (one page, or every page a sitemap lists) against the saved craft rules at phone and desktop width, with a marked picture of each
values.description: Opens the page (url), or every page a sitemap lists (pages_from, less the paths skip names), at 390 and 1280 pixels (the widths are DATA in tools/page-critic/read-data/page-craft-rules.json) and checks it against the craft rules: headings wider than their measure, body text wider than about half the page, small label lines above headings, text too close to the browser's edge, links to anchors that are not on the page, links that do not open, cards that look openable but are not, a page whose newest date is older than fresh_within_days (one number, or { "/path": days } for some pages), a page many screens long, and controls that look the same with a pointer on them. Each finding says what to change, in plain words, and where; each width is kept as a whole-page picture in your files with every finding boxed and numbered. The page is only read.

values.title: Find the techniques from anywhere that would work for what you are making (runs on your computer)
values.job: Take what I am making (a sales page, a lesson, an app's first screens, a pitch) and find every technique I have kept, from any medium, whose reason for working serves it, which ones work better together, and exactly how to use each one here
values.description: A writer model turns the goal into wants (what must happen in the mind of the person it is for, or in the system it runs on), each naming the properties of the shared vocabulary that must change. Every technique whose operates_on holds one of those properties is joined exactly, its mechanisms ranked by how many media they span, and the writer picks the mechanisms that serve each want. The answer is the techniques holding them, whatever medium each came from, spread over media. Pairs come from the rows' own fields: 'prepares' when one technique changes a property another needs, 'covers' when two serve different wants. The writer adds one concrete line per technique and pair for the goal's own medium, and drops any a constraint rules out (listed in ruled_out with the constraint). Terms the writer names that are not in the vocabulary are listed in unknown. Rows need the crossing fields that tool:say-why-a-technique-works gives them, and the vocabulary their terms come from. Uses a chat model the person names (any OpenAI-compatible server, such as Ollama on their computer).

values.title: Cut a hostname over to a new address
values.job: Point one exact hostname of mine at a new server's address, keeping every other DNS record and route, and roll it back if I ask
values.description: Through the DNS provider description handed in as `dns` (the file the person keeps for it): `prepare` reads the zone and answers a `receipt` holding the one address record or managed binding that `hostname` holds now; `activate` points it at `address` and reads it back; `rollback` puts back what prepare read; `status` answers where the cutover stands without asking the provider; `keep-healthy` keeps `hostname` answering with exactly those of `candidates` (front-door computers, each `{ address, health_path? }`) that answer HTTP 200 on their health path, adding the healthy ones before it removes the others and refusing when none is healthy. `activate`, `rollback` and `status` take the `receipt` an earlier answer gave, and answer the changed receipt; the tool keeps nothing, so the person's AI stores it. Before every change it checks that no other record, guarded list or binding changed since prepare, and refuses when one did. A change whose answer was lost is reconciled from what the provider shows, never sent twice. The DNS key comes from the vault by the description's vault name and is never shown.

values.title: Cut a clip and caption it
values.job: Cut one stretch out of a video and burn in its spoken words as captions
values.description: Keeps `from` to `to` (seconds) of the video and burns the words spoken in it as captions in the style you name (see style), for example words that light up as they are said. Without a transcript it only cuts. Saves the clip in your files.

values.title: Decide whether to nudge a person
values.job: Decide whether a person should get a nudge now, honouring their opt-out and a rate limit
values.description: Takes a person's context (a risk number, whether the rate limit still allows a nudge, whether they opted out) and the person's threshold, tone and framing. Checks in this order: opted out, rate limit, then risk. Nudges only when the risk is a number at or over the threshold. A missing context, an unknown risk or a threshold that is not a number means no nudge. The tone and framing come back exactly as the caller gave them. When allowed_tones is given, the nudge is only sent in a listed tone; any other tone means no nudge.

values.title: Decide what happens to a video at ingest
values.job: Decide whether an uploaded video is kept as it came, converted to the one playable format (MP4), or kept with the reason it could not be converted, and give the conversion's arguments
values.description: Give name (the file's name), media_type and byte_length. Answers action (keep or convert), said (the plain sentence for the person or the AI, null for a file that is not a video) and, for a conversion, plan: from, to, output_name and the ffmpeg args (with {input} and {output} for the runner to fill). converts lists the types it converts. An upload is never refused: a type with no conversion row, or a file over the size one conversion takes, is kept and said says why. It runs nothing: a computer's ffmpeg or a container does the work.

values.title: Decide whether my AI may take this action
values.job: Decide whether an action my AI is about to take may run, must ask me first, or is refused, from my action policy, the grants I gave and what I declined
values.description: Takes the action (for example a tool, a target and arguments), the fields the policy rules may read from it, the person's policy (rules in order, each with an id, its words, an optional `when` rule tree and a `then`, plus an optional `otherwise` and `paused`), the grants given, the actions declined with when, the time of the person's last message, the actions the person asked for, the thread, whether anyone can be asked now, and the time now. Answers allow, ask or refuse, the rule, grant or earlier decline that decided, its words, what to do about retrying, the action's identity, the grant to mark used (for a once grant) and the rules it could not evaluate. Order: a paused policy refuses; refusing rules come next, and a refusing rule it cannot evaluate refuses too; an action declined earlier stays refused until the person has spoken since; then a matching grant allows; then the other rules in order (a rule it cannot evaluate is skipped, never allows); then the policy's `otherwise`, else ask. An ask no one can be asked becomes a refusal that says to continue without it. With dry_run the same decision is answered with enforced false, so the caller lets the action run and keeps the record of what would have been decided. A request that cannot be run is refused with a sentence that says what to send.

values.title: Decide a whole decision in one call
values.job: Open a decision, answer every row of its method and make it, in one call
values.description: Opens a decision, records its answers to every row of its method and makes the decision, as tool:start-a-decision, tool:record-method-answers and tool:make-the-decision do when sent one at a time, each step checking what it checks. Answers and the decision come from the input; nothing is invented. Nothing is kept if any step refuses. The caller hands in the records it read as records, and what changed comes back as keep, each record with the value it was handed in with.

values.title: Decide the replies
values.job: Say which automatic reply to send now to each message or comment a person received on one of their connected places, by their keyword rules, and which to leave and why
values.description: Says for each item of one place whether a rule's reply is to be sent now, from what the request holds: the person's reply rules (their reply-rule rows, in order), the place's row (read-data/reply-places.json: where its items come from, whose words are the person's own, how long a reply is allowed, who it goes to), the items of that place handed in as pulled.<channel id> (a channel with nothing handed in is named under not_pulled), the person's own id at the place (self_id) and the replies already kept (their reply-kept rows). The rule must match, the item must be someone else's, and the place's window, if it sets one, must still be open. A reply already kept is never chosen again. The person's AI reads those rows from their store and gives them; the tool reads nothing, sends nothing and keeps nothing: the place's send row (its send_tool) sends one chosen reply.

values.title: Decide what a paste becomes
values.job: Decide what a paste into a message or note becomes: a normal insert for short text, a named text file for a long paste, or attached images when the clipboard's markup has no words of its own, with the words the person reads beside the attachment
values.description: Give clipboard ({ text, html, files: [{ type, name }] }) and, optionally, now (an ISO time for the attachment's name). Returns action insert, attach_text (name, text, media_type, said) or attach_images (files, said). Text over 5,000 characters becomes a file; an image attaches only when the markup carries no text of its own (style and script bodies are not words).

values.title: Decide what a said-done answer means
values.job: Given one ask and the classifier's answer, say whether the row is settled, left alone, or handed to the AIs
values.description: Pure. probability at or above 0.7 gives verdict done with the settle values; below 0.35 gives not_said and nothing else; between them, or with no answer (null), gives unsure or no_classifier with the hand-off job, once per message and row. The thresholds are DATA in src/said-done.json. It settles and hands off nothing.

values.title: Delete a draft
values.job: Delete one draft permanently.
values.description: Delete one draft permanently. Takes provider (an id of read-data/mail-providers.json) and connection (the person's account of that provider, by its handle only: {connection_id}). Runs as that account with the key the person's vault holds for it; the engine hands the key to this run alone and it is placed only in the request to the provider's own host, never shown. Answers the provider-neutral rows of read-data/neutral.mjs, never the provider's own payload. A provider that does not offer it says so in words.

values.title: Delete, archive and put back my files
values.job: Delete or archive a person's files and folders into Recently Deleted and Archived, put them back exactly as they were, change how long each keeps things, and say what is due when, with the time left on each
values.description: Give files ([{ name, identity?, byte_length?, modified_at_ms? }], names starting with /), now (the ISO time the run starts at) and steps, run in order: { op: delete | archive, items: [{ name } | { identity }] } takes a file or a whole folder out of the person's Files into Recently Deleted or Archived; { op: put_back, items: [label or id] } gives every name back exactly as it was (never over a name another file took since); { op: keep_for, after_days: { deleted?, archived? } } sets how many days each keeps things (null: until put back); { op: sweep, at } moves on what is due by then: an archived thing moves to Recently Deleted, a deleted one's names are gone for good. Answers steps (what each answered, refusals included), set_aside (each item as the screen lists it: label, state, names, bytes, where, due_at, days_left, due_words), names (what Files still shows), gone (the identities whose names went for good) and keep_for. Every step is namespace-set-aside.mjs's own setAsideStore over namespace-store.mjs's tables, in an in-memory SQLite database: no byte is deleted, nothing is kept after the run, no file is written and nothing is sent. Refuses no files, an unknown step and what the store refuses (a name not starting with /, the whole Files, a day count out of range). The screen also releases storage by the person's rules; this run does not.

values.title: Derive current API description tools
values.job: Derive the current tools of one native-selected source without opening account records
values.description: An installed inner source resolver. Native source admission supplies current configuration, original definitions, exact cache snapshots as task DATA and retains their real root/currentness witness through effects and output. Only need and wait are input. Native-only planning derives exact current cache ids through this same owner. The derivation opens no records descriptor, enlarges no caller record rights and writes no durable cache. Credentials remain with the native connection owner.

values.title: List what a presentation runtime exposes on a slide, a shape and the notes (runs on your computer)
values.job: Print the property names a presentation runtime exposes on one slide, one shape's text and the speaker notes, so an edit request is written against the real names
values.description: Opens a presentation with the runtime module, takes its first slide and the first shape that has text, and prints the property names found on the slide, the shape's text object, the notes object and its text frame, plus the first shape's text and the notes text. Read-only.

values.title: Describe a tool
values.job: Show me one tool's whole row, so I can see how it is written and how to call it
values.description: Give the tool's id and the rows the Workshop answered (tools:list) as shared. Takes your own saved row of that tool (record type tool, id tool:<tool id>) as saved, read by your AI from your store; it reads no store itself and keeps nothing. Your saved row, unless deleted, replaces the shared row of the same id. Answers the tool's descriptor, who made it (this account or shared), the sample rule of the place it runs (read-only or dry-run samples on a person's own computer, owed until a computer connects), the sample-run checks of your own runnable tool, and the next call to make: save_tool for your own, run_tool for a shared tool that runs, nothing for a screen. A tool there is nothing of to describe answers an error naming find_tool_for_job. It reads one row and changes nothing.

values.title: Describe my connected accounts
values.job: Say in plain words, for each of my connected accounts, which one is primary, what its sign-in allowed, what Trillion copies from it, what stays live and what Trillion may do with it
values.description: Give connections ([{ connection_id, vendor, service, account_label, status, connected_at, grant_scopes_known, grant_scopes, can_send, visibility, carried_by, capabilityChoices }]) and when wanted chosen ({ vendor: connection_id }, the kept primary choice), arriving ({ vendor: [labels of event sources listening] }), local_copies (connection ids a computer may keep the sign-in of) and capabilities ({ vendor: [{ id, label }] }). A service with several accounts and no choice uses its earliest; a choice that no longer holds is ignored. Groups say only what the provider reported. Returns primary and accounts [{ connection_id, primary, allowed_groups, words: { copied, live, allowed }, steps }].

values.title: What holds a device
values.job: See which holds are keeping apps closed on the person's computer and when each ends
values.description: Answers every hold still lasting.

values.title: Dictation text and dictionary
values.job: Turn dictated words into clean text for the app the person is in (spoken commands, the app's style, their dictionary and snippets), give the hearing prompt that biases recognition, learn from the person's edit, and keep their dictionary, snippets and dictation history
values.description: Give action: clean (text, context, entry_id?; polish or command are asked of the model server on this computer (the dictation-polish job of tool:ask-a-model's models) and leave the text as it was when none answers), bias (context), learn (inserted, final, entry_id?), add (from and to, or kind: snippet with says and expands_to), list, edit (id and fields), delete (id), history, or erase (entry_id, or all). The rows and the history are kept in the folder the person granted. Putting text at the cursor is tool:type-dictated-text.

values.title: Dismiss waiting tours
values.job: Dismiss the tours waiting for me without showing them
values.description: Marks waiting tours seen without showing them: every waiting tour, or those named in tour_ids, in one move of your tour progress record (the move closing a tour makes), so none starts by itself again; each can still be shown by name. Give own_tours, progress and show_rules as for list-waiting-tours. Nothing is written here: it answers keep, the progress record it would write with the progress you gave as expected, for you to keep in the store that holds it; a record changed meanwhile is not written over.

values.title: Draft a funnel
values.job: Start a new funnel with a title and its steps, or add steps to a funnel I already have
values.description: Gives back a funnel-definition record for the person to save in their own records: a new one from a title (with an id that cannot clash with another funnel of the same title) and the step titles, or the person's existing one with steps appended after its last, every other field of it kept as it is. Steps start as titles only; pointing a step at a workflow step, an offer or a measure is adding a ref to its row. A new funnel has only the steps asked for: nothing is made up.

values.title: Draft a post
values.job: Work out a post as a draft for the person to look at (its words, its video or picture, where it goes and when) and answer the post row to keep
values.description: Give caption (the words), media (the file as the person's files list it: { identity, name?, media_type?, byte_length? }) with media_facts ({ duration_seconds, width, height } the file does not say), destinations (account_id values from tool:list-post-destinations), caption_by_platform ({ platform: words }), settings_by_platform ({ platform: { ... } }, like a video title), link (an https page; it is added after the words, tagged with the post and the place), scheduled_for (a date and time with its zone), time_zone, source ({ kind, id } of the record it came from, kept as given), format_id, reaches (the people it contacts first, each with where they were found) and drafted_by (the AI writing it). Give post_id to change a draft; changing an approved post, or a scheduled one nothing was sent for, makes it a draft again. Returns post, ready (as tool:check-a-post gives it), said, and the post row to store under `keep`. Give records: the person's connection records, and the post when post_id changes one. Nothing is posted or stored here.

values.title: Drive my browser
values.job: Drive a web page across several calls through the person's own signed-in browser, in a window of its own, until they take it back
values.description: One call of a browser session (browser-session.json): do is tabs, open, close, navigate, back, forward, act, read, lock, release or end, with the session, tab, url and steps that verb needs. The session owns an unfocused window and only the tabs it opened; the person's own tabs are never touched; the person's lock takes the browser back at once. Refused in words when no browser is connected to this computer.

values.title: Operate the person's computer screen
values.job: Click, press, type, scroll, drag or use keys on the person's computer, finding the target by what it is called and checking afterwards what really changed
values.description: One call looks at the screen, finds the target, does the action, looks again and says what changed. action is one the computer keeps (tool:screen-actions lists them; new ones are added as data on the computer). Give expect, a list of { target, min?, max? } or { changed }, and verified says whether the screen shows it; without expect, verified is null and the change seen is reported. dry_run shows the steps without doing them. Press and set_value act through the accessibility tree and do not move the person's pointer; click, type and key do. A target that moved or vanished is refused, never guessed. Uses this Mac's existing Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions. The person can turn on an optional grant policy in their screen-driving settings folder; calls cannot change that policy.

values.title: Edit a copy of my Premiere project from a plan: insert, cut, move, reorder (runs on your computer)
values.job: Make a new copy of my Premiere Pro project with these edits done on the timeline: put these files or placeholders in at these points, cut these stretches, move this part, or rebuild the sequence in a new order
values.description: Reads a Premiere Pro project (.prproj, gzipped XML) and a JSON plan of ops, and writes a NEW project with the edits made in its XML. It never opens, launches or scripts Premiere, and never writes the input project. insert: at a timecode every track opens a gap of the insert length, then each piece (a file, probed with ffprobe, or a labelled black placeholder) goes on its track; the next video track can be created. cut: a range is deleted and the rest closes up. move: a range is taken out and put back elsewhere. assemble: the sequence is rebuilt from listed ranges in order. A range is sequence timecodes, a source range of a clip in seconds, or an insert made earlier in the plan. One remap engine razors every video and audio item at every boundary and carries picture, sound, links, captions and a full-length adjustment layer along. Before writing, the result must pass structural checks (unique ids, every reference resolves, nothing left unreferenced, tracks in order, no overlaps) and a gzip round trip. An existing output is replaced only when the person's written record (--written, kept with their film) shows this tool wrote exactly that file; anything else is refused. Refuses rather than guesses: another frame rate, mono audio, a video file carrying sound, a missing track, drop-frame timecode, a partial adjustment layer, a colour interpretation override. Companion commands in the folder: compile_edit_plan.py (an EDIT-PLAN new order plus word timings into a plan, with pause trims), validate.py, prdump.py (a timeline listing), proxy_render.py (an ungraded ffmpeg check render) and grade_check.py (pre-graded plates against a graded export).

values.title: Edit a presentation's text and slide order from a request, then read it back (runs on your computer)
values.job: Change the words on slides, rebuild a slide, change speaker notes, delete slides and reorder them in a presentation file, and read the new file back as proof
values.description: Takes a request file naming a presentation runtime module (any module exporting FileBlob and PresentationFile with importPptx and exportPptx), the source and output paths, and per-slide edits by ORIGINAL slide number: replace_text (keeps every other shape), notes, or a whole rebuild (bg, text items, rectangles), plus delete and slide_order. slide_order is applied last and must list every surviving slide exactly once, or the whole request is refused. The report gives each slide's actions and how many shapes each replace_text rule matched (0 when none), then the new file's slide titles in final order and its notes: the readback, not the request, is the proof. The source is never changed. Fonts come from the request (fonts.regular, fonts.bold, or typeface on a text item); none are assumed.

values.title: Edit a transcript
values.job: Edit a recording's transcript the way the transcript reader does: name a speaker or take the name back, split a passage before a chosen word, and write the passages as plain words to copy or export
values.description: Give passages ([{ start, end, text, speaker?, speaker_was?, words? }], times in seconds, each word { word, start, end }) and, in order, edits: { op: name_speaker, from, name } says every passage of one label under a name and keeps the label it had in speaker_was; { op: take_name_back, name } restores it exactly; { op: split, passage, word } splits one passage just before a word, the first half ending where the second begins. Answers passages (the edited list; words, times and order never change), speakers (in the order they first speak), named_speakers (the ones named by the person) and text (each passage as 'Speaker  0:05' over its words, the Copy transcript and Export PDF text). Each edit is read-data/edit-transcript.ts's own. Refuses no passages, a passage without start, end and text, an unknown op, an empty name, and a split at the first word or past the last. It reads, saves, plays and sends nothing; the reader screen also follows playback, searches the words and reprocesses in another language, which this run does not.

values.title: Edit an image locally
values.job: Edit an image from your files using an image editing brief and your chosen local model
values.description: Runs MFLUX on your Apple Silicon Mac through its public, MIT-licensed MCP server. Uses your computer for inference. The selected model is explicit; no paid provider or hosted inference fallback. First use downloads that model. Returns the completed PNG in your files.

values.title: End decisions no one will carry on
values.job: Close decisions that will never be carried on, and keep why
values.description: Sets each named decision's status to ended and keeps the status it had (previous_status), ended_at, ended_by and ended_because, with every other field unchanged and nothing deleted. Each write is conditioned on the value just read: a decision that changed meanwhile answers conflict. A decision whose root is too large to send with its condition in one 64 KiB message is ended through its record layout instead, checked by a second read just before the write, and answers laid_apart. One the door still refuses as too large is left as it was and answers too_large. A decision in outcome_verified, correction_needed or verification is not ended. 1 to 256 decisions per call.

values.title: End shares whose condition failed
values.job: End the shares I let people run my tools by, once the end I gave each has passed, so none stays open past its time
values.description: Judges every share that lets people run your tools, from the run shares the caller lists from your store (each with the end rule you gave it, if any, and when it was last used), and returns the withdrawal of each whose rule says it has ended: until, a time that has passed, or unused_days, that many days with no use counted from the later of when you set the rule and its last use (each use starts the days again). A share with no rule never ends here; it stands until you stop it. The engine keeps your rule beside the share and reads none of it: it admits a person while their share is kept, so a share ends when this withdraws it. A rule it cannot read is left alone and counted as waiting; a share the engine lists with no last use is judged by its until alone and counted as unjudged. Change a rule with tool:share-anything op end and the next run acts on it. It takes the listed runs as input (runs) and reads no store itself; a caller that runs it every hour, the grain the engine writes a last use at, gives it the runs and writes what it returns.

values.title: Clean a recording's noise and find where the speech is
values.job: Clean the noise out of a recording on my own computer with what it can afford, and tell me where the speech is
values.description: Cleans a recording on this computer (`file`, a path; it is never changed): picks the most expensive noise-removal tier within the CPU budget whose ffmpeg filters (and model file, in the models folder the person granted) exist here (light, near-voice, neural), makes the cleaned sound as the run's declared output (named in `files`), and answers the speech places found by a silence-detect pass, in seconds of the original. When no tier fits, `files` is empty, nothing is cleaned, and `why` says what is missing. Nothing is read from or kept in the person's records or files.

values.title: Enrol someone's voice or face so they can be named
values.job: Let the person's AI name this person later by their voice or face, after they agreed to be known that way
values.description: Measures a recording of one person speaking, or a picture or video of one person's face, or takes a voice heard in a listening, and keeps it as that person's print so later recordings and pictures can name them. It refuses before it measures anything unless `consent` says who agreed to be known by their voice or face and how. Enrolling the same name again adds samples and the new consent words to the same print and keeps the earlier ones. The voice-print, face-print and listening-voices record kinds are stays_on_this_device: true: the numbers of a print are kept only on the device they were made on and are never shared, exported, synced or sent to a model off it. The answer says how many samples the person has, never the numbers.

values.title: Enroll someone in the challenges that fit them
values.job: Decide which time-boxed challenges one person joins from their scores, and build their enrollment records
values.description: Takes the challenge definitions, the observer's score for each challenge (scored beforehand, for example with the tool that scores candidates for an observer), who the observer is, when they start and the status word a new member starts in. A challenge joins the observer when its definition is valid and the score reaches that challenge's own min_score; a person may join many. Answers `enrollments`, each with its record address and the record to store (the window is copied from the definition now), and `skipped`, each with the reason: an invalid definition, no score given, or a score below min_score. Re-running for the same pair gives the same address, so storing it twice keeps one record. The tool holds no clock and no status words: started_at and status_key are required.

values.title: Teach listening someone's voice or face
values.job: Teach this person's computer to recognise someone, by a recording of their voice, a picture of their face, or a voice it already heard while listening, so what they say is named as theirs
values.description: Runs on the person's computer. Give name, kind (voice or face) and consent (who agreed to be known here, and how: nobody is enrolled without it), and one of: path (a file on the computer), file (a recording or picture in their files), or heard_voice (a voice the computer heard while listening, like voice-2, from the listening that was running at heard_at, the time a turn of that voice was said, else the latest unless session names one); everything that voice already said in that listening is then named as theirs too. me true marks the person themselves, so their words arrive as theirs. A face enrollment keeps their picture. Several samples make it surer: enroll again to add one.

values.title: Evaluate a formula over rows
values.job: Evaluate a formula over each row of a list: read a value from the row, then run a pipeline of steps (and, or, not, equals, more than, less than, is in a list, position in a list, lower-case, contains, starts with, join, is empty, is unknown) over it
values.description: Takes a binding (select from the row at a path, or a stated literal, then a transform list of { op, args }; an argument may itself be a binding evaluated over the value the step receives) and rows, or the formula written as text instead of the binding (=price * quantity, IF(@.done, "yes", "no"), FILTER(items, |x| => x.age > 3); the functions are the rows of rules/text-formulas.json), which the engine compiles into the binding it means. Answers one value per row, in order, and the rows that could not be evaluated with the reason (a step given a value of the wrong kind, or a step that is not supported). Three-state logic: and, or and not answer true, false or unknown, and a comparison with an unknown side is unknown. Nothing outside the row is read.

values.title: Evaluate a writing-voice classifier on labelled passages
values.job: Check how well a small classifier judges a writer's voice: validate the labelled challenge passages, plan the questions, ask the classifier each one, and report its choices, probabilities, abstentions and accuracy by criterion, family and source
values.description: Give data, a challenge of labelled passages (schema book-voice-decider-challenge-v1, v2 or v3), and an action. validate checks the challenge (unique ids, one split per family, typed blocks, criteria, labels) and counts the model questions; plan returns the exact request each passage would send (the passage and only its criterion-scoped or pinned reference context, never the general context, which can hold labels); evaluate asks the classifier (the endpoint and model in the person's list:settings row for this tool, settings_record, as the person's store gives it and tools/settings reads it) and answers the report: every choice with its full probabilities, a decision that is the choice only when its probability is over the criterion's diagnostic minimum (else uncertain), confusion matrices and abstentions by criterion, family and source kind, and errors kept as errors, never passes; a section heading is judged over every source-bound chunk of its section (one fail fails it, all pass passes it). A reply whose model or serving identity differs from the classifier's health is an error. replies plays recorded exchanges in place of the classifier (a stand-in: a request with no recording is refused). check-report checks a stored report against its challenge (identity, request policy, every captured request and raw response). Nothing is trained and nothing is written; the person's passages and labels are input only.

values.title: Expand a canned reply template
values.job: Fill a canned reply template with the details of a request, such as a name or a button label, and give back the finished reply
values.description: Give a template (any JSON in which a value to fill is written as {"$kind":"binding","select":{"from":"dataSource","key":"caller_request","path":"label"},"default":...}) and the details to fill it from: caller_request, provider_record and data (each top-level entry of data can also be named as a key). If you give no template, the provider_record's template is used. Returns the template with every binding replaced; everything else is kept as it was, whatever its shape. A binding that finds nothing gives its default, else null (select.required changes nothing). An object key named itemTemplate is kept as written. A template that is present and null gives null. A binding that reads from another source or has a transform is refused by name. It sends nothing and keeps nothing; the caller delivers the reply.

values.title: Save anything as a file: a list, a table, a document, a board, words or a picture, as PDF, Word, Excel, CSV, Markdown, text, web page, SVG and more
values.job: Turn one document made of headings, words, lists, tables, graphs, calendar events and pictures into a file in the format asked for, and give the file back
values.description: Give the document and the id of a format. The document is { title?, blocks }. A block is one of: { kind: heading, level 1 to 6, text }; { kind: paragraph, text }; { kind: list, ordered?, items: words or { text, children } }; { kind: table, title?, columns: [names], rows: [[cells]], currencies?: [code or null per column] } (a cell is words, a number, true or false, or null; a column with a currency code such as USD is written as money, $1,234.56, in PDF, Word, Markdown, text and web page, and kept as a number in CSV and Excel, with a money format in Excel); { kind: graph, title?, nodes: [{ id, label? }], edges: [{ from, to, label? }] }; { kind: events, title?, events: [{ title, start, end?, description? }] } (start and end are ISO dates or times); { kind: picture, title?, svg } (one complete svg element); { kind: ink, operations, styles?, target?, default_stroke? } (the ink marks of a space, drawn as a picture). The format is one row of the formats list (tool:list-the-file-formats-an-export-can-make): pdf, docx (Word), xlsx (Excel), csv, tsv, markdown, txt, html, slides (a web page with one printed page per top heading), svg, png, json, ics (calendar), mermaid, dot, graphml, opml and freemind. A format that does not draw a kind of block writes it another way: a graph or events as tables. A kind it cannot write at all is refused by name, never dropped. A person's own format can be given whole as format_row (the same shape as a row of the list) instead of an id. file_stem names the file (a plain name with no folder; the document's title when left out). The answer has filename, mime, byte_length and base64 (the whole file), and text as well when the file is text. The page of PDF and SVG is the paper the request names, else the region of its locale, else US Letter, in portrait or landscape. A PDF is written in Helvetica; a character that font cannot draw stops the export with the character named, and nothing is replaced. png comes back as the svg, with finish set to raster-png: a page draws it to a canvas.

values.title: Export a Markdown book to Word through its writing checks, and verify the Word file and its PDF against the source (runs on your computer)
values.job: export a markdown manuscript to word and verify it against its source
values.description: Takes the book's settings row (record:setting:export-documents-to-files~piece~<book_id>, list:settings, the record itself as settings_record): its manuscript, role (current_prose, comparison or historical_reference), the BLAKE3 its bytes must have, a retained Word template and output folder, and for current prose the checks branch, writing profile, reviews and captured book-voice runs in its evidence folder. For current prose it first runs the book's checks branch of list:checks (tools/check-against-a-persons-rules-and-verdicts, branch mode) on the exact bytes and stops when they do not pass; then the writing gate checks the writing profile and review evidence (tools/pin-files-by-content), and the captured voice-classifier run and its qualification benchmark (tools/train-and-evaluate-a-writing-voice-classifier). Only then is the Word file built from the template (title, a clickable contents list with page fields, heading bookmarks, native tables, lists, quotes, footer page numbers), read back and compared to the source. verify_book_against_its_source.py checks the Word file and a rendered PDF against the source (outline, contents links, page map, body text with two PDF readers) and can repair confirmed ligature mappings. Passing proves coverage and regression checks only, never author approval.

values.title: Give yt-dlp my browser's YouTube login (runs on your Mac)
values.job: Let yt-dlp download as me: export my browser's YouTube login to a cookies file
values.description: Reads one profile of a Chromium-family browser on macOS (Arc by default; also Chrome, Chromium, Brave, Edge and Vivaldi), decrypts its cookies with the key the browser keeps in the macOS keychain under its own name (for Arc, "Arc Safe Storage", which yt-dlp's own Chrome reader does not ask for), and writes the cookies of youtube.com and google.com (other domains if asked) to a Netscape cookies.txt that yt-dlp reads with --cookies. The file is written readable by its owner only. It holds the person's login: it must stay on their computer and never be shared or committed. macOS asks the person once to allow the key; a wrong key is refused rather than written garbled.

values.title: Export an editor timeline
values.job: Export an edit as a timeline file (Final Cut Pro XML) that Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve or Final Cut can open
values.description: Writes the edit (the same format render-an-edit takes, with encode width, height and fps) as an xmeml timeline naming each source by the path it has on the editor's computer, saves it in your files, and says what the file could not carry.

values.title: Turn my records into rows for my Trillion lists (runs on your computer)
values.job: Take records I keep in files (JSON, spreadsheets saved as tab-separated text, markdown tables) and prepare them as rows for my lists, using a mapping I write once
values.description: Reads a mapping file the person gives: the lists to make and, for each source of records, where the records are, which to drop, what to work out from each and how a row is made from it (fields copied, filled into templates, read as numbers or dates, mapped to a list's choices, joined, counted in a file). Writes make_lists.json, the rows in batches and a manifest into a folder the person names. It sends nothing: the batches are put into the lists afterwards. Row ids are stable, so loading the same rows twice updates them. Rows whose ids are in a skip file are left out, so existing rows are never overwritten. When two records make the same row id the mapping must say which one to keep, because choosing silently would drop a record. A re-run replaces only the files an earlier run wrote. It knows no record kinds: every file, column and list comes from the mapping.

values.title: Extract the sound from a video
values.job: Take the sound out of a video as a small audio file, for example to transcribe it
values.description: Saves the video's sound as a mono 16 kHz MP3 in your files (about 0.5 MB a minute), small enough for the speech-to-text tool.

values.title: Fade live ink marks
values.job: Work out how visible each ink mark drawn live on a canvas or screen is at a given instant, so live marks fade instead of piling up, and when each is gone
values.description: Give now (the instant to look at, an ISO time or milliseconds since the epoch), fade ({ hold_ms, fade_ms }: how long a mark is fully seen, then how long it takes to go) and marks ([{ ref, created_at? }]). Answers marks, one per mark in the order given, each with opacity (1 until hold_ms has passed since created_at, falling in a straight line to 0 over fade_ms, 0 after), shown and gone_at (the ISO instant it goes, or null for a mark with no usable time, which never fades), and the counts shown and gone. It reads only what it is given: no clock is read, nothing is drawn, no mark is changed or deleted. Refuses an empty list, a mark without a ref, a now that is not a time and a hold_ms or fade_ms that is not a number of zero or more. The screen (show/GraphCanvas.tsx, show/AddressedMarkLayer.tsx and the mark toolbar) also lays a list out as linked cards, takes the pen and keeps each stroke; this run does none of that. Folding, shaping and erasing marks are the tool:see-the-ink-marks-on-a-space, tool:turn-a-drawn-stroke-into-a-mark-shape and tool:find-the-ink-mark-to-erase rows in tools/draw-ink-marks; exporting marks as a picture file is the ink block of tool:export-a-document-to-a-file.

values.title: Download chosen free sound effects with their licences (runs on your computer)
values.job: Download the sound effects I chose, reading each one's licence first and keeping a manifest
values.description: Each selected Freesound item's licence is read on its own page first: only CC0, CC BY 3.0 and CC BY 4.0 are downloaded, the rest recorded as blocked; Mixkit items under its free licence. Every entry (page, author, title, licence as read, description excerpt, date, address, local file) goes to the manifest.

values.title: Sort what I said in my recordings into topics and rate how usable each moment is (runs on your computer)
values.job: Go through my transcribed recordings, cut them into moments, file each moment under topics, and tell me which moments stand alone as a usable idea, story or lesson
values.description: Cuts each transcript (a <name>.words.json with segments) into moments (a new one starts after a silence of 4 seconds or past 120 words), then asks a model that runs on the person's own computer (Ollama) which topic buckets each moment belongs to (0 to 3) and how much it stands alone as a usable spoken idea, claim, story or lesson (0 to 1: camera setup, filler and half sentences score near 0, a complete quotable idea 0.6 to 1). The model judges each moment only from its own words. The buckets come from a vocabulary file that starts from a short seed and grows as the model proposes new buckets, so the person can edit it. A moment the model leaves out of its answer is asked about again alone. The tool writes the moments, their buckets and relevance back into each transcript (or to a separate file with --dry-out), can tag a long file of moments one batch at a time and continue after a stop, and reports how many moments each bucket holds and how many are usable. Transcripts with no times at all (a cloud-results copy's text) are cut by do-work/cut_text_into_moments.py into moments of whole sentences up to 120 words, each placed by its share of the text (and by seconds when the recording's length is known), with each transcript's source in the person's file store and identical copies kept once and named; it answers how many moments and transcripts each source holds and how many hours of media they cover. tag-moments then files those moments. Nothing leaves the computer, nothing is paid for and no key is needed.

values.title: fill a list from a feed
values.job: Keep one of my lists filled from a JSON, RSS or Atom feed, leaving edits intact unless update_existing is requested. Reads candidate row ids, keeps media in Files, and can stamp a successful run. Shared-library input is available only to hosts supplying its admitted library owner.
values.description: Keep one of my lists filled from a JSON, RSS or Atom feed, leaving edits intact unless update_existing is requested. Reads candidate row ids, keeps media in Files, and can stamp a successful run. Shared-library input is available only to hosts supplying its admitted library owner.

values.title: Fill a script template's blanks from sourced phrases with small models on my computer (runs on your computer)
values.job: Fill the blanks of my script template with true, sourced phrases chosen by small models on my computer: gather the phrases, rank them per blank, add the typed candidates, let a model choose, and render the fills with their drift
values.description: make_candidate_pool gathers short phrases with a checkable source (a listing, a site's JSON, git histories, a product name, ages); template_blanks (read-data) reads the template's lines and blanks; rank_pool_for_blanks keeps a cross-encoder's 12 best per blank; make_typed_options adds every candidate of the blank's type; choose_fills_with_decider, judge_filled_lines_with_decider and choose_fills_with_language_model choose; render_choices_as_fills writes the fills (abstaining below a line) through tool:fill-a-word-template and measures the drift. A blank of type PERSON-LINE is never filled from a pool. Steps: make_candidate_pool, rank_pool_for_blanks, make_typed_options, choose_fills_with_decider, judge_filled_lines_with_decider, choose_fills_with_language_model, render_choices_as_fills.

values.title: Fill a template's slots with sourced values and nothing else (runs on your computer)
values.job: Put my own numbers, names and product into a template without changing any of its other words, and show where each value came from
values.description: Takes a template and a fills file giving each slot a value and its sources (a URL, git:<repo>@<commit>, a file line, a timestamp or a time range). A value counts only when every source is checkable and the value's words and numbers appear in a cited source; otherwise the slot stays visibly empty as [TYPE: no source yet] and is listed with the reason and what would fill it. A source can be one of the person's recorded moments (a time range of a word-timed transcript), and the fill then keeps where the value plays. It refuses any id that is not a slot, so the fixed words cannot be changed. Writes the filled script as markdown with the sources table, and with --piece the filled piece for checking and re-timing.

values.title: Fill a screen's inputs from my words
values.job: Fill a screen's inputs from the words a person typed, such as timer 25 min or lunch with Ruth tomorrow at 1, by each input's format, choices or type, with no model
values.description: Give schema (the screen's input schema, { properties }), words, and now (the device's time, ISO) for words like tomorrow or in 20 minutes; used ([[start, end]]) are the spans of the words that picked the screen, which are not values; choices names labels for enum values. Answers values (only what the words give and the schema accepts; anything uncertain is left for the person) with how each was read. Parsers and their words are src/input-parsers.json.

values.title: Keep the rows that match my rules
values.job: Keep the rows of a list that match my rules: a tree of comparisons (is any of, has all of, contains, is more than, is between, is empty, is known and more) joined by all-of and any-of groups, each group optionally negated
values.description: Takes records, the fields the rules may read (an id, a kind and a path into each record) and a rule tree. Answers the positions and the records that match, the field ids the rules read and the rules left out because they are not finished (an unknown field or comparison, a comparison the field's kind does not offer, missing values), never guessing at them. A tree with no finished rule keeps every row. A value that is unknown never matches a comparison that cannot tell (contains, starts with, more than, less than, between and the like) nor its negation (does not contain, has none of), but an unknown value is simply not in a list and not equal to a word, so is none of and is not keep it. A group whose combinator is not one of the listed ones is refused with a sentence. A row whose value is of the wrong kind for a comparison is counted in error_rows and left out. The comparisons are rows of data: send operators to add or change them, or leave it out to use the ones list-comparisons shows.

values.title: Find a completed Stripe checkout
values.job: Find the completed Stripe checkout for one buyer and offer when the buyer browser never came back
values.description: Give offer_id and the buyer customer_email, or a created_after_unix time to look from (then exactly one match is needed). Returns the session id if found, or why not. Uses the Stripe key of the seller connection that seller_connection names (service_connection:stripe is your own).

values.title: Find a published destination
values.job: Find the destination screen an owner has published (a progress page, a results page) among saved records, for one person or subject, and read it safely
values.description: Give rows (records shaped {record, payload}, the payload being the decoded destination-descriptor), the destination's ref and, when the descriptor is for one subject, that subject_ref. Returns found, the descriptor read within safe bounds (at most 64 sections, 200 items each; malformed parts dropped) and finished_refs, the items the owner marked to celebrate whose own percent is 100 or more. A descriptor for one subject is never returned when no subject, or another subject, is given. Nothing is added up or ranked here.

values.title: Find where a spoken passage starts and ends in a recording's word times
values.job: Tell me the exact seconds a passage I quote starts and ends in a recording, read a recording's words back as timed sentences, or keep its word times in the one file shape my plans cut from
values.description: Works on a recording's word-time file (a words list of {text, start, end}, the {t, start, end} words the transcription tool writes, or Whisper's segments with words), in the folder the person let this tool change. step span: given the passage's first words and last words (and after, a second to search from), answers the start of the first word, the end of the last word and the words between, so a cut lands on word edges; words match ignoring case and punctuation. step sentences: every sentence (ended by . ? or !) whose words start inside from and to, with its start and end. step words-file: writes {source, timing, words} to out, adding offset seconds to every time (a window heard alone). Instead of words, clip names <words_folder>/<clip>.words.json, where words_folder is the person's setting (their list:settings row, named by settings_record); timing and round_to are settings too. It reads only the word-time file and writes only out.

values.title: Find action moments in a video
values.job: Find where the action happens in a video, such as the moment a ball is hit, and give each moment's time in seconds
values.description: Ranks the moments where a sharp sound meets movement in the picture (a racket meeting a ball, a clap, a landing) and returns their times in the video's own seconds, strongest first. Search the whole video or only a stretch of it.

values.title: Find the beats in music
values.job: Find the beat times in a song or in a video's soundtrack, to cut on the beat
values.description: Returns the time of each beat (seconds) and the tempo in beats per minute.

values.title: Find the rows nobody uses
values.job: List the rows of a list that nobody uses any more, so they can be cleaned up, leaving out rows a person verified and whose review is still current
values.description: Give list ({ id, title_field, fields }), rows ([{ id, title, values }]) and heats ({ <row id>: { heat, at } }, the use-heat records kept for the rows). Heat halves every 30 days; a row is cold below 0.5. Rows whose review_state is Verified and whose review_due is still ahead are left out. owner narrows to one owner. Answers rows [{ id, title, heat, last_used }] and complete, with next_cursor when it stopped early.

values.title: Find events in a video against what it has been like so far
values.job: Find the moments in a video that stand out from what the video has been like up to then, such as each stroke in a rally, and give each one's time and how certain it is
values.description: Walks the video as frames of loudness rise and picture change and keeps a running baseline of each. A frame well above the baseline from before it is an event, so a loud or busy video is judged against itself. Each kind of event is a head row with its own weights, thresholds and quiet time after a hit, so a head can be retuned without touching the rest. The detector is a row too: `adaptive` walks the running baseline, `sound-and-motion` ranks the sharpest sound with movement. Search the whole video or only a stretch of it.

values.title: Find the faces in a picture or video and say who they are
values.job: Find every face in a picture or video and name the ones that belong to people who agreed to be known
values.description: Finds the faces in a picture, or in a picture taken from a video every few seconds, and answers each face's place (the second, the box in pixels) and who it is: the person's name when one enrolled face is clearly the closest, every person it could be when two are too close to tell, nobody otherwise. Changes no file. Thresholds are inputs; the starting values are not yet calibrated on the person's own consented pictures. The face-print record kind is stays_on_this_device: true: prints are read here and never leave the device they were made on.

values.title: Find my files in my index
values.job: Find a person's files by words, name, place, kind or spoken words, in a file index that already exists on their computer
values.description: Give index_dir (the full path of the folder that holds the index, one the person has let this tool read) and query (the words to look for). The index is a JSON-lines file with one row per file (index_file, default assets.jsonl) and an optional types file (types_file, default content-types.json) whose type_keywords turn a word such as a kind of file into a type and whose stop_words are ignored. A search matches file names, folder paths, tags and the words spoken in or written in the file, ranks name above tag above folder above text, boosts adjacent words and files that hold every word, and never returns another type than the one asked for (type, or a type word in the query).
