Returns each hit's path, display_path, root, type, identity and size with its score, and how many candidates each root held, so an absence can be told from a thin index. fields names the row field for each of path, display_path, name, root, type, tags, text, identity and size when the index uses other names; weights changes the ranking weights; other_lanes holds hits a caller already has from a meaning or picture search (rows with scores) to be merged with the word hits. names (instead of or beside query) looks up where named files are kept: a name matches a file whose name without its extension equals it, or starts with it, ignoring case, when the name ends in *; type and root narrow the rows; the answer's by_name gives each name's display paths and not_in_index lists the names no file matched. index_dir is required unless the person's settings (settings_record, a row of their list:settings, or settings) hold it; their settings fill every key the request leaves out (index_dir, index_file, types_file, type, root, limit, fields, weights, lane_weights). It never builds or changes an index, and it reads nothing outside index_dir.

values.title: Find the glitches in a generated voice take, word by word (runs on your computer)
values.job: Check a voice take made by text to speech for breathy words, pitch breaks, clicks and stretched words before I use it
values.description: Measures every word of a generated voice take: how periodic its voicing is (low is breathy, noise-like), pitch jumps (more than 3 semitones in 5 ms is not a human voice), clicks (sample-level jumps against the local level) and stretched words (time per letter far above the take's own median). Writes <take>.qc.json, one row per word with its measures and flags, and prints the flagged words and the worst five of each measure. The take is only read. It runs on the person's own computer, never on Trillion.

values.title: Find the stretches of a recording spoken in a character's high pitch band (runs on your computer)
values.job: Find where a recording has speech in a high pitch band, as a first look for a character voiced well above the rest of the cast
values.description: librosa yin pitch every 25 ms with a periodicity voicing test; runs of voiced frames in the person's band (pitch_run_band_low_hz to pitch_run_band_high_hz) of at least 0.5 s, joined across 1.2 s gaps, kept when half their voiced frames are in the band. Writes <out_dir>/<id>.json (the runs with their median pitch) and <id>.f0.npy. Pitch alone also catches every other high voice; find-when-a-character-speaks tells them apart.

values.title: Find how records connect
values.job: Find how two of the person's records connect through relations and things that happened, or what several records all relate to and who else shares it
values.description: With from and to: the paths between them, shortest first, each at most max_length steps (default 4, at most 6), each step one relation or one record to an activity it took part in, with the relation or activity it goes through and the role. With of (or from alone): the hubs every one of them relates to (a group, an organisation, a meeting, a person) with how each holds it, and the members: every other record related to those hubs, most hubs shared first. roles, kinds, activities and ended narrow what is walked. It reads the graph once, bounded (at most 20000 records of each kind, 10 paths); complete false says a bound cut it. It works from the rows given as records and reads and keeps nothing.

values.title: Find mail
values.job: Find messages: the ones in a folder (inbox, starred, sent, drafts, trash or all; the inbox when none is given), or, when text is given, the ones matching it across all mail, written in the provider's own search words (from:, to:, subject:, after: where it takes them). One page at a time: pass next_page_token to go on.
values.description: Find messages: the ones in a folder (inbox, starred, sent, drafts, trash or all; the inbox when none is given), or, when text is given, the ones matching it across all mail, written in the provider's own search words (from:, to:, subject:, after: where it takes them). One page at a time: pass next_page_token to go on. Takes provider (an id of read-data/mail-providers.json) and connection (the person's account of that provider, by its handle only: {connection_id}). Runs as that account with the key the person's vault holds for it; the engine hands the key to this run alone and it is placed only in the request to the provider's own host, never shown. Answers the provider-neutral rows of read-data/neutral.mjs, never the provider's own payload. A provider that does not offer it says so in words.

values.title: Find a picture or clip that fits a description (runs on your computer)
values.job: Get a picture or a video clip that fits a few words, from my own media folder or from free-licence stock libraries, and save it as a file
values.description: Takes a description, whether it is a still or a clip, where to save it, and which provider to ask. The provider `bank` looks in one folder of the person's own media: each file may have a sidecar <file>.tags.json holding {"tags": [...]}, and the best match by words in the tags and the file name is copied to the output path (nothing else in the folder is read or changed). The provider `stock` asks the free-licence libraries listed in read-data/stock-sources.json one after another, with the person's own key for each read from an environment variable on their computer, and downloads the first match; only free-licence (cc0) pictures and clips are served. Providers are rows in read-data/media-providers.json: a program that generates a clip from a description is one more row. A request a provider cannot serve (a kind or a licence it does not offer) is refused with what it does offer, and a provider that finds nothing fails saying so; nothing is made up.

values.title: Find the stretch of each music track that follows my film's loudness arc (runs on your computer)
values.job: Find in each candidate music track the window whose loudness follows my film's arc
values.description: Each track's smoothed loudness curve is compared with the brief's arc (Pearson correlation of dB curves) plus measured constraints (the open below the lift, the swell near the top); the best window of each track is cut as an excerpt.

values.title: Find a mailbox's address
values.job: Find which address a connected mail account belongs to, and where its mail stands now (cursor: the point list-new-mail goes on from).
values.description: Find which address a connected mail account belongs to, and where its mail stands now (cursor: the point list-new-mail goes on from). Takes provider (an id of read-data/mail-providers.json) and connection (the person's account of that provider, by its handle only: {connection_id}). Runs as that account with the key the person's vault holds for it; the engine hands the key to this run alone and it is placed only in the request to the provider's own host, never shown. Answers the provider-neutral rows of read-data/neutral.mjs, never the provider's own payload. A provider that does not offer it says so in words.

values.title: Find which X account the person's connection holds
values.job: Find the X account id the person's connected X account holds, so a listening source knows whose posts it reads
values.description: Asks X who the connected token belongs to (users/me) and answers the account's id, username and name. Reads only. The bookmark and like listeners keep this id as their route key, so they start only when it is known.

values.title: Find the nearest places of a brand or name
values.job: Find the nearest stores or places of a brand or name around a start, each with route buttons
values.description: Give name (a brand or a place name) and near (an address or place name as words, or { lat, lon }), and optionally radius_km, most and mode. Reads the open address and places services the settings name, tries the other copies of the places service when one is busy, and answers the nearest places first with their address, distance, opening hours and route buttons. A service that does not answer is told in words, never guessed around. The settings are in read-data/get-there.json.

values.title: Find people in the Network
values.job: Find people in the Network whose listings are close in meaning to a need, or share its words when there is no meaning vector
values.description: Answers the findable people, by handle and never by contact, whose listing embedding is at least the Network's min_similarity close to the need's embedding (sent as embedding); with no embedding, a listing answers when it shares a word with the need. A person who labelled the searcher unwanted-requests or unsafe is left out. Reads the network_records rows of the database named.

values.title: Find new or changed files
values.job: Find the files under a folder the person chose that are new or have changed since the last look, matched by a pattern, without reading what they mean, so a folder of saved things can be followed
values.description: Runs on the person's computer over the folder they granted it to read, and reads only inside it; a link that leads out of the folder is skipped and named in skipped, never followed. Give source_ref (what to call the source). glob is the pattern relative to the folder (default **/*); under narrows to a path inside it; account_prefix looks in each sub-folder whose name starts with it (under_account names a path inside each); include_kinds is file and/or directory. since is the next_since of the answer before: only entries whose state (modification time and size) changed are returned, so a re-run over an unchanged folder finds nothing. most (default 200, at most 5000) cuts newest first and more says there is more. with_hash true also gives each file its content identity (BLAKE3) up to hash_up_to_bytes. window (a number) instead returns the newest that-many files by name and size alone, opening no file. Returns observations { source_ref, native_ref (the path inside the folder), observed_at, state, content_hash, payload }, next_since, more and skipped. Writes nothing.

values.title: Find a thing on the person's computer screen
values.job: Say where a described thing is on the person's screen right now (a button, a field, a line of text) without touching it
values.description: Describe the target by what it is called or what kind it is, never by coordinates. Returns the ranked matches with where each is now. Read-only. Uses this Mac's existing Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions. The person can turn on an optional grant policy in their screen-driving settings folder; calls cannot change that policy.

values.title: Find open times
values.job: Find the times someone can book with me, from my weekly hours, minus what is already booked and what my calendar shows busy
values.description: Gives the open start times over one or more days, in the person's time zone. A time is open when it fits wholly inside a weekly window on that weekday, is not a start in the taken list, does not overlap a busy interval (widened by the buffers before and after), and starts after the minimum notice. Bookings given in `bookings` count too (booking records as tool:request-a-booking answered them): a booking fills a seat of the time it starts at and blocks every other time it overlaps (a cancelled booking frees its time); a day closes once per_day_max bookings start on it, and nothing past horizon_days is offered. Windows, lengths, buffers, seats and limits are the person's own: nothing is assumed.

values.title: Find the videos that did far better than their own channel usually does (runs on your computer)
values.job: Find the outlier videos: the ones that got many times more views than their channel normally gets
values.description: Reads a tab-separated table of videos (one header line, one row per video, from any number of channels or other sources) and writes the outliers: each titled video whose views are at least 5 times its own source's median views and at least 10,000, both thresholds changeable. A source's median counts every titled row of that source with a whole-number view count; rows with no title or no view count are skipped. Writes a table of ratio, views, kind, channel, source, median, n (videos in the median), url and title, in the input's order. The columns are found by number or header name, so any export works. Judges views against the channel's own usual, not against other channels: a small channel's breakout counts as much as a big one's.

values.title: Find people in a list
values.job: Search a list of people or contacts by name, company or any other field, and show each match with a name and details
values.description: Give the people (any records with an id), in records or as a JSON file from your files, and what to search for. fields optionally says which fields to read and how to show them ({key, label, source_keys, searchable, display_role: title | subtitle | detail}); without it every field is read and searched. Returns the matches with a title, subtitle and detail each, how many there are and how many were searched.

values.title: Find pictures by colour or likeness
values.job: Find my pictures by a colour I type or name, or find pictures like one I pick
values.description: Give rows (the pictures' facts: [{ id, palette: ['#rrggbb', ...], embedding? }]) and one of question (words with typed #rrggbb colours or colour words), colour (one #rrggbb) or like (the id of a picture). Colour is compared in CIE-LAB (delta-E 1976): a typed hex within 22 of any palette colour, a colour word within 16 of the top three. like ranks by embedding cosine (floor 0.30) and falls back to palette distance when embeddings are missing or weak; the picture itself is never its own result. Returns ids, by (colour, embedding or palette) and the colours asked.

values.title: Find recurring voices
values.job: Group recurring voices across audio and video files, keep stable voice clusters, and show which files contain the same speaker
values.description: Uses a public CAM++ speaker model on speech windows from your selected files. Returns candidate voice groups and their time spans, keeps cluster embeddings in your account for later files, and shows a person's name only when a name was explicitly attached.

values.title: Find the edits a person repeats
values.job: Find the word changes a person keeps making to drafts written for them
values.description: Counts, over the person's kept edits handed in as edits (kind narrows them), the words removed, added or replaced, each once per draft, and returns the changes found in at least min_distinct_drafts different drafts (3 when left out, never below 2), each with an example edit_id. They are proposals to show the person before saving any into a profile with tool:save-voice. Reads and keeps nothing: the person's AI reads the voice-edit records from its store and sends them.

values.title: Find the rows of a list that need review, by owner
values.job: List the rows of a list set up for review that need someone to look at them, for each owner, with why: never checked, flagged outdated or asked about, past the date it must be checked again by, or empty
values.description: Give list ({ id, title_field, fields, views }: the list as review set_up left it, with its review views), rows ([{ id, title, values }]) and, if you like, owner (one owner's rows only) and now (an ISO time; the current time by default). Each review view is read over the rows: a view's rules by the rule filter of the formulas tool, the expired view by its check-again date against now. Answers owners [{ owner, rows: [{ id, title, reasons }] }], reasons being not_verified, expired or empty, and complete (false when more rows needed review than one answer lists).

values.title: Find scene changes in a video
values.job: Find the times where a video cuts from one shot to another
values.description: Returns every time (seconds) where the picture changes to a new shot. A higher threshold (0 to 1) finds fewer, harder cuts.

values.title: Find the quiet parts of a video
values.job: Find the silent stretches in a video or recording and the parts worth keeping between them
values.description: Returns the silent stretches and the spoken or sounding stretches to keep between them, in seconds, so pauses can be cut out.

values.title: Find the event that starts or replays one guided tour
values.job: Work out the event a Start or Replay control should send to run one named guided tour on demand
values.description: Give the tour records (oldest first) and the id of the tour. Of that tour's triggers, the most specific repeatable one is chosen: a trigger bound to this tour's id and with no once_key first, then one not bound to a tour, then the ones that can be used up. A trigger bound to a different tour is never chosen. The event is the trigger's event kind and its match fields, copied as written, with walkthrough_id set to the tour. Null when the tour has no usable trigger. A tour that is not among the records is refused.

values.title: Find the ink mark under an eraser
values.job: Find which showing ink mark lies nearest a point, so it can be erased without changing any mark
values.description: Give the mark operations, their styles, the space and the point where the eraser touched, with a radius in the space's own units. The nearest showing mark within the radius is found by distance to each of its segments (a closed shape counts its closing edge), and its ref comes back with the effect to record: { hide_refs: [ref] } on a new operation. Nothing is edited or deleted; the earlier marks stay and the new operation hides the one. When no mark is within the radius the ref and effects are null. Marks already hidden are not found.

values.title: Find which guided tour an event starts
values.job: Decide which guided tour, if any, should start when something happens in an app (it opened, a page was entered, a replay was asked for), without showing a tour that was already seen
values.description: Give the tour records in the order they were written (a later record at the same id replaces an earlier one; one marked status deleted removes it; records that are not tours are skipped), the event ({ event_kind, plus any fields }) and the suppression keys already used up. A trigger fires on one event kind and only when every field in its match equals the event's. The first trigger in the order written, over the tours in id order, whose key is not used up wins. The answer names the tour, the trigger with its reason exactly as written, and the key to record so the tour does not start again (scoped by once_key_fields of the event when the trigger names them, so one person's tour being used up leaves another's); a trigger with no once_key has no key and can fire every time. When nothing fires all three are null.

values.title: Find tool servers in a catalog
values.job: Find tool servers for a job in a published catalog and get the address to call each one at
values.description: Searches a published catalog of tool servers (the MCP registry's own list unless another catalog with the same API is named) for every word given, and answers each server's name, what it does, whether it is still active, the headers it asks for, and its address. Give that address to tools:list or tools:run to see and use its tools; a server with no address runs only as a program on a computer. It keeps nothing and sends no key.

values.title: Find when one character speaks in a show's recordings, by voice and pitch (runs on your computer)
values.job: Find every stretch where one character of a show speaks, in all of its recordings, from a few stretches the person labels, even when the character is a cast member's own voice pitched up
values.description: step embed: windows of 1.5 s every 0.5 s of a recording, each with a speaker embedding (pyannote wespeaker-voxceleb-resnet34-LM, from the local model cache), its median pitch and loudness, embedding only the windows high enough to be the character. step seed: add the windows inside the stretches the person names ("a-b,a-b") to <data_folder>/voice/seeds.npz with a label. step score: a logistic model on the seeds finds this recording's confident windows of the character among those that pass the pitch gate (at least the smaller of gate_max_hz and gate_pitch_ratio x the recording's median pitch); their mean embedding is the character's voice in this recording, and a gated window whose cosine to it is above voice_cosine_min is the character; neighbouring windows become turns, written as <id>.turns.json. step batch: embed and score every catalog video of batch_format_order not yet scored, from <audio_folder>/<audio_file>. step rescore: score every recording again with the current seeds. The label, gates and formats are the person's settings (character_label, embed_min_pitch_hz, embed_pitch_ratio, gate_pitch_ratio, gate_max_hz, voice_cosine_min, batch_format_order, audio_file). do-work/check_seed_model.py and check_voice_finder.py check it on recordings it did not learn from: leave one labelled recording out and count window precision and recall.

values.title: Measure where my confidence line belongs instead of guessing a round number (runs on your computer)
values.job: Work out, from my rubric's known cases, how sure a model has to be before I act, by measuring how sure it is on known-true and known-false cases
values.description: Give rubrics_file, optionally rubric_id (one rubric) and band (the name of the confidence band whose at_least is the line, to show where it is now). A model that passes the rubric is asked every case and its confidence on the cases it got right is kept by label; the line goes where the two groups separate, ties to the higher line. If true and false cases overlap it says so and does not lower the line to make a check talk; if the cases are one-sided it asks for cases that expect the opposite answer. Needs a model that returns a probability (a hosted classifier); a model that only writes text has no confidence to measure.

values.title: Check the saved consumer and finish a task
values.job: Finish a task only after its saved acceptance checks pass on the actual persisted consumer
values.description: Reads the exact record target saved in the task's acceptance and applies the shared judge-words rules to its current value. A missing target, failed or unavailable check, mismatched target, stale claim or changed task refuses completion. Receipt strings do not prove success. Keeps the actual consumer content identity and acceptance identity bound to this take. Rights are intersected by the engine with the caller authority; this tool grants no new account access. It is the finish move of the change row with action finish. The caller hands in every record it reads as input.records; this tool reads no store and names no store method. Each write it makes comes back as keep, for the caller to keep in the person's own store.

values.title: Finish a waiting item
values.job: Complete the declared action on the same persisted waiting record
values.description: Works out the declared same-record completion of waiting records and answers the records that change as keep, each { id, type, value, expected } for the caller to store; it writes nothing. Read the records first from the person's own store (each { id, type, value }) and hand them in as records; hand in the person's record:waiting-sources records as sources when they added any. Refuses items whose source has another owner. The built-in asks action is the original Waiting on you list status Done transition; no other source status is guessed. Answers completed (the ids), changed (how many records change) and keep: each changed record as { id, type, value, expected }, expected being the record as it was read. Store each kept record in the person's own store, refused if the expected record has moved, then run tool:verify-waiting-on-me-completion on the records read back. A record already carrying this request_key's receipt answers completed with no write.

values.title: Fit a tool list in a budget
values.job: Shrink a list of tools for an AI so it fits in a number of characters, keeping as much detail as fits
values.description: Give tools (MCP tool entries: name, description, inputSchema), budget_chars (a positive number of characters of the JSON list) and, optionally, names (tools to keep in full whatever the budget). The list is tried at levels full, brief (first sentence of each description), schema-only (no descriptions) and names (schemas reduced to an open object); the first whose whole list fits is sent, and the last when none fit. No tool is renamed, reordered or dropped. Returns tools and listing { level, chars, budget_chars, fits, tools, said when shortened, unknown and unknown_said for names no tool has }. Without a positive budget_chars the list comes back unchanged with an empty listing.

values.title: Fit a pass line and a fail line for a model's yes or no, from lines I already ruled on (runs on your computer)
values.job: From a model's scores on lines I already ruled good or bad, work out where it should pass a line, where it should fail one, and whether its question can tell my good lines from my bad ones at all
values.description: Give bad and good: for each line the person ruled bad or good, the model's probability of the failing answer (a number, a list with one per sentence whose highest counts, or null for no answer). t_fail is set so at most fail_good_share_at_most of good lines fail; t_pass so at most pass_bad_share_at_most of bad lines pass, never above t_fail; scores between are uncertain. The answer gives AUC, recall at t_fail and the share of good lines failed, or failed or left uncertain, each held out (leave one out), and says usable only when every bar in usable_when holds (auc_at_least, bad_lines_at_least, recall_at_least, good_failed_or_uncertain_at_most); otherwise unseparable with the reasons. It asks no model: the scores come from the caller, on lines the model was never trained on.

values.title: Turn Focus on or off
values.job: Switch Do Not Disturb on the person's computer on or off
values.description: on true turns Focus on, false turns it off.

values.title: Forget a person in a community's matchmaker
values.job: Erase a person from a community's matching: what they told it, every match naming them, their asks, answers and jobs, and their place and scores on other members' shortlists and score jobs
values.description: Removes the member record, every match naming the person with its one-to-one group, answers and jobs, their own asks and jobs, and takes them and the scores of them out of other members' asks and waiting score jobs. Others keep their own asks and jobs. Returns forgotten and written. This tool reads and keeps no records: the caller's AI reads the community's records from a store and hands them in as `records`, and puts the answer's `write` (each changed record with the value it expected, null for a new one) in a store.

values.title: Form matches and small groups by grounded expected value
values.job: Match people in a community, club, cohort or mentoring program into pairs or small groups who can actually help each other, and prepare introductions that wait for everyone's consent
values.description: One matching cycle, all of it data: expected_value { factors, scope_fields, minimum_expected_value?, minimum_distinguishable_delta?, require_scope? } names what a match's value is the product of and what scope it is for. Give retrieval_results (one row per subject: { subject, shortlist: [candidates] }, cut to retrieval.shortlist_size each, so work is subjects x shortlist size) or scored candidates. Every candidate needs factor_evidence: a grounded bundle (tool:check-match-evidence) with a score in (0, 1], evidence and an inference for every factor; a candidate without it, or with a value that is not the exact product, forms no group. Similarity from a search only breaks ties. pairing sets group_size, minimum_group_size, include_subject, bipartite roles, exclusion of pairs already met (already_matched, or prior_items), exclusive_participation and names for group sizes. Each group carries a prepared introduction whose send gate is ready only when initiative.required_level is in initiative.pre_authorized_levels and every party's own consent value is in consent_policy.approved_values with no veto in veto_values; connections are given only for those. Returns connections (with relationship_kind), groups, introductions (ready and blocked), reasoning_requests for the chosen few only, configuration_requests, pair_keys, unmatched with details, and how much work was done. Nothing is sent or written.

values.title: Move eligible files from my list to Trash
values.job: Move files and folders my list says I can get back to recoverable Trash after checking the listed sources and recipes
values.description: Give 1 to 100 rows, each { id, value }, and the folder granted for change. Eligibility requires the saved state, no hold, a regular file or folder inside the grant, no top-level link or git-tracked files, at least one source address or recipe, every source answering, every recipe tracked, unchanged and pushed, and no changes within the quiet hours or during the check. A source answering proves availability only, not identical or complete recovery bytes. dry_run defaults to true and moves nothing. A real run asks the native macOS Trash service; it never permanently deletes or empties Trash, and a denied move returns no next_value. Only a confirmed move returns next_value with the moved-to-Trash state. path_bytes and trashed_path_bytes describe observed path allocation, not reclaimed storage; freed_bytes is null because it is unmeasured. The change-a-folder grant may refuse Trash access; this tool never widens it. Field names and state words are DATA in read-data/kept-file-shape.json, overridden by shape.

values.title: Arrange a person's beta app access
values.job: Arrange the TestFlight access a person's setup requires, through the release owner's Apple account, without sending a second invitation
values.description: Give account_id, source_id and request_id (the person's setup-access request), and the app's bundle_identifier and testflight_groups. The release owner's claim resolves consent, setup, policy and the verified email; the tool never takes a recipient. It answers a public route when one is usable, otherwise enrolls the person in the policy's external group and, only when Apple will not notify on its own, sends one first invitation, each change after a checkpoint, and an uncertain change is read back, never sent again. Answers state (available, invited, accepted, installed, awaiting-invitation, blocked, indeterminate, revoked) and reason, never the email. Refused for now: the claim, checkpoint and finish are not operations a tool run can reach at the records door yet (README Not yet).

values.title: Run a read-only checklist gate on my files (runs on your computer)
values.job: Before I am shown anything I made, list the required checks that apply to it and identify which answers are open, stale or failed, without changing my files
values.description: Reads the person's checklist (stages, checks and routes), schema and piece from one folder they grant. It runs the existing checklist gate read-only: every required check that applies to the piece is listed with its current answer state, file identity and criterion pins. It accepts `gate`, `scope`, `audit` without `--hold`, read-only `checklist`, and `library-pending` for the next bounded source-assessment batch in the schema's current work context. It does not create a lock file, first-gate record or pin cache, and it cannot answer checks, run write-producing sweeps or hold files. The same generic checklist consumer still refuses empty or unknown scopes, reports stale answers and requires exact BLAKE3 file and definition pins. A separate write-grant tool handles commands that change the library. Nothing about a person's checklist or piece is known by this tool; the schema owns those details.

values.title: Hold a piece back until every check of its delivery checklist has a pass with evidence (runs on your computer)
values.job: Before I show or deliver a piece, tell me which checks of my delivery checklist are still open, failed or answered on old bytes, record each answer with its evidence, and hold back anything already linked for me to watch that has not passed
values.description: Reads a person's delivery checklist (stages of checks, each routed by the piece header's tags, some asked once per option) through the schema they give, and holds a piece back until every routed MUST check has a pass row. A person's row carries evidence and a name; a machine's row (the rendered-video check, the sweep, the copy check on the person's own branch of their Checks list read from the records they hand in, their verdict rows, their fact gate, the audio measure of an audition) carries the pin of the code and rules that measured it; every row carries the BLAKE3 of the files it judged, so a row on other bytes is open again. It records render-check reports, runs the sweep and the content gates, audits the files linked into watch folders (moving open ones aside with --hold) and lists the options a whole-lane gate covers. Every file name, folder, pattern, stage and rule id comes from the schema's delivery_gate.

values.title: May telemetry send about this page
values.job: Say whether a telemetry sink may send or keep anything about a page or event, from how private the page that was served is
values.description: Give surface (site, public-page, elsewhere, app or service) and path of the served page, optionally declared (the privacy class its handler declared) and sink (page_script, page_events, client_health or server_events). The class is the longest matching route's; a declared class can only make it more private. A surface and path no route names, or a declared class that is not known, is 'unknown', which feeds no sink. Returns class and sinks (the sinks that class may feed); with sink, also sink and may_send. A sink that is not one of the four is refused.

values.title: Turn my written checklist into the checklist file the gate reads, and check that file (runs on your computer)
values.job: Keep one written checklist of mine as the only source, generate the checklist document from it, tell me when the file on disk no longer matches my text, and find the mistakes a hand edit or a typo would make
values.description: Reads a person's checklist text (one section per stage, one table row per check, notes that annotate a check, an optional file of rules whose wording is read from there and never copied) through the `checklist_source` part of the schema the person gives, which holds the regular expressions and constant fields that say how their text is laid out. `checklist` prints the document the text generates, `--check` says in words which checks differ from the file on disk, `--write` writes the file, and `--problems` checks the file on disk for repeated ids, a required flag that is not true or false, a route no reader can evaluate, a per-item check with no rule, an advisory stage that is not a delivery stage, a phase that names no check and counts that do not add up. It refuses a rule that has no row and a note that names no check. It knows no row kind, id shape or route tag.

values.title: Fill video formats with my product's capabilities
values.job: Write a draft script for each of my product's capabilities in each video format I picked: the format's own lines filled with the capability's words, the word count of every line against the format's measured budget, the shots, the filming notes, and every fact still missing listed with what would fill it
values.description: Takes one request: formats (each with its template: lines with a measured word budget and seconds, slots with their pictures, shoot and reuse notes, an optional note, and which words count: all words, or only quoted on-screen words), capabilities (the person's own words for each, any fields), the saved catalog listing of each capability (title, job, steps), the page layout, and optionally an index page. Every text is a template: {dotted.path} fills a value; if, each, replace, after and concat pick, repeat and join values. A hole <<n|label|what fills it>> is a fact the script cannot know yet: it shows as [label], counts as n words and is listed with what would fill it. Returns one page per format and capability with its words, budget and number of open holes, and the index page with a matrix of every fill and any counted buckets. Instead of a request it can take the person's list rows (kinds fill-batch, fill-format, fill-capability, catalog-listing, each object as JSON text in `detail`) and the batch to fill; the page layout and over-budget rule can come from the person's settings row in list:settings (settings_record). It invents nothing: it only fills and counts the words it is given.

values.title: Make images from a prompt with a provider command (runs on your computer)
values.job: Make a picture from a description in words, with the image model or program I choose, and keep the picture
values.description: Takes a prompt and a provider command, which is any program that makes an image: a hosted model's caller (it keeps its own key in the person's environment) or a local model's program. The command reads the request and writes its answer, and the tool keeps each image it returns: an image returned inline is written to a file in the output folder, an image returned as a web address or a file path is named as it is. The result carries the prompt, the provider the command names, the format and every image's place. The provider and the model are the person's choice and are never in the code. With no provider command, or one that fails, is not found, times out or answers without an image, the result is an error that says which; nothing is ever made up. A small program that needs no account (placeholder_image_provider.py: one solid-colour picture per prompt) checks that the chain works before a real provider is wired in.

values.title: Generate an image locally
values.job: Generate an original image from a visual brief with your chosen local image model, for an article hero, thumbnail or illustration
values.description: Runs MFLUX on your Apple Silicon Mac through its public, MIT-licensed MCP server. Uses your computer for inference. The selected model is explicit; no paid provider or hosted inference fallback. First use downloads that model. Returns the completed PNG in your files.

values.title: Make speech from text with a provider command (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn text into spoken audio, in the voice and with the voice program or service I choose, and keep the audio
values.description: Takes text and a provider command, which is any program that makes speech: a hosted voice service's caller (it keeps its own key in the person's environment) or a voice program on the computer. The command reads the request (the text, the voice and language in options, the person's own name for the voice) and writes its answer, and the tool keeps each audio file it returns: audio returned inline is written to a file in the output folder, audio returned as a web address or a file path is named as it is. The result carries the voice name, language, format, length and every file's place. The voice and the service are the person's choice and are never in the code. With no text, no provider command, or one that fails, is not found, times out or answers without audio, the result is an error that says which; nothing is ever made up. A small provider that needs no account (local_voice_provider.py: the voice program already on the computer, say or espeak-ng, writing a WAV) checks that the chain works and speaks for real where such a program exists.

values.title: Get a questions-first classifier ready on this Mac
values.job: Get my question classifier model ready to run on my Mac
values.description: Takes the model's value in the request ({classifier, weights}: a pinned Hugging Face revision, or a local folder), fetches and checks the weights, and names each checked file plus the whole set by BLAKE3. It copies those verified files into one private output tree; the engine keeps the files in this account’s Files and returns their exact identities under files.snapshot. The answer holds the original model file manifest, so another computer can verify the snapshot before using it. A gated model needs the person’s own `huggingface-cli login`. Run it once per model on a computer that has the model. Nothing is written to the person's records.

values.title: A drive's icon
values.job: Get the icon Finder shows for one drive connected to this person's computer, as a PNG picture
values.description: Runs on the person's computer. size is the square size in pixels, 32 to 512 (256 when left out). Returns mount, media_type image/png and base64.

values.title: Free AI models that fit my device
values.job: See which free AI models fit the person's computer (its chip, memory and free space) and which it already has, and have its model server download them
values.description: Runs on the person's computer. Without input it answers the computer's chip, memory and free space, whether its model server runs, and each model offered for it (read-data/models-on-this-computer.json offer) with whether it fits and whether the computer has it. With get "fitting" it has the running model server download every model that fits and is missing; with get as a list of offer ids, those. A model got here answers tool:ask-a-model at once. When the model server is not running it says so in words; it does not install the server.

values.title: Test my models on my questions ahead of time and keep who passed (runs on your computer)
values.job: Calibrate every question in my rubrics file against the models I can ask, once and away from the moment of asking, and keep which model passed each so a later question is one fast call
values.description: Give rubrics_file and remember_file (where to keep the result), optionally passes (default 1). Calibration is the slow part, a model call per known case, so doing it inside a quick question is cut off and starts again. Returns per rubric the model chosen and the scoreboard, or why none was (nothing passed, or nothing could be reached). A model that could not be reached is tried again next time; one that answered and was wrong, or answered too slowly, stays lost for six hours. Changing a rubric's question, cases or bar, or the set of models, calibrates again.

values.title: Give a buyer a paid file link
values.job: Give a buyer a short-lived link to a file they paid for, and refuse anyone who has not paid
values.description: Takes the file's paid-file row (as tool:seal-a-paid-file answered it) and answers grant with a link that expires (the record's ttl_seconds, else 3600), only when the subject is a verified account and holds any of the file's required access refs now (worked out as tool:see-who-holds-paid-access works it out, from the access rows the request carries). Otherwise answers denied (anonymous, not-entitled) or unavailable (no sealed bytes, no such file, access could not be worked out). The file's gate comes from its paid-file row, never from the buyer. It keeps nothing. subject must be the account the door verified from the buyer's own session. The link carries no bytes and no key; every open is checked again by tool:open-a-paid-file-for-a-buyer.

values.title: Give a task to anyone: a person, an AI, another record, or whoever takes it first
values.job: Make a new task, waiting for the ones named to take it, or for anyone when none is named
values.description: Writes one task, id record:calendar-task:<key>, with status To do, its title (title, else the first line of description), its description, its outcome (what done looks like), its priority (urgent, high, medium or low; medium when left out), sent_by (as: the record id of whoever gives it), sent_at, and assignees: the record ids of anyone who may take it. An empty or missing list means anyone may take it, and every assignee must be among the records handed in. source {kind, ref} keeps where it came from; obligations declare parts each checked on its own; acceptance saves the checks a finish must pass. key (or the run's request key) names the task: the write is conditioned on the task being absent, so the same key gives the task once; sending it again answers written with no write, and a different task under the same key answers already-there. The caller hands in every record it reads as input.records; this tool reads no store and names no store method. Each write it makes comes back as keep, for the caller to keep in the person's own store.

values.title: Give back a computer
values.job: Stop paying for a computer's machine: remove its public name and give the machine back
values.description: Removes the public name the lease made, then deletes the machine and the SSH key the lease made, each only after reading it back and finding this lease's own label. A machine the person already runs is only forgotten, never touched. Move the computer's accounts to another computer first: this deletes the machine's disk.

values.title: Give referral rewards
values.job: Work out the rewards my referral reward rules say a code earns and give back the discount and access rows that give them
values.description: Works out the codes exactly as tool:work-out-referral-codes does, from the person's own referral reward rules (given in `rules`), then gives back, in the answer, what the rules give as the rows the existing tools already read. A discount is a checkout-code-adjustment row, so take-payments takes it off a price like any other checkout code: for the friend it is the referral code itself (typed at checkout, for as long as the rule says), for the referrer it is a checkout code of its own named from the rule and the sale. Access is an access-grant row, shaped the way workflow:keep-paid-access-grants keeps them. Every reward has an id made from the rule and the code or sale, so asking again gives the same rows; a reward given twice in one request with different terms is refused with why. A share is not a row: its whole-cent amount is in the answer for the person to pay however they pay people. The tool keeps nothing, sends nothing and moves no money: the person's AI keeps the rows in the person's store.

values.title: Change a video's colour
values.job: Put a colour look or grade on a video and adjust its brightness, contrast, saturation, exposure, warmth or vibrance
values.description: Applies named looks (film grades, camera log to normal colour, VHS, golden hour, film grain and more) and colour adjustments to the whole video, optionally matching its colour to another video first, and saves the new video in your files at its own size and length.

values.title: Grade the speech in my recordings and clean up what sounds poor (runs on your computer)
values.job: Check whether the speech in each part of my recordings sounds good, keep the good ones as they are and clean up noise, hum, wind, room echo and clipping in the rest
values.description: Takes a list of spans (a stretch of one recording, the words said in it and, ideally, the word times) and measures each: loudness, noise floor read from the pauses between words, signal to noise, clipping, mains hum, wind rumble and room tail, against the person's own settings (a JSON file they give; the tool has no values of its own). A span with no fault is kept as it is. A span with a fault is remastered: high-pass, a notch at the hum and its harmonics, then up to three denoised candidates (DeepFilterNet3 full, DeepFilterNet3 limited to the soft limit in the person's settings, ffmpeg afftdn), each finished the same way (pauses ducked when the room was the fault, de-ess, gentle compression, loudness to the person's target) and read by whisper; the candidate whose read matches the original read or the text, with the best signal to noise, wins, and the remastered cut is graded again. Writes grades.json (per span: grade good, remaster or clone, why, the measures before and after, which candidate won) and one wav per span with the settings' handle either side; the source recordings are only read. A span that is still bad after the remaster is marked clone, for tool:clone-speech-that-repair-could-not-fix. It runs on the person's own computer, never on Trillion.

values.title: Hand a request to its owner
values.job: Ask an owner to run an action with what a form, a check or a person supplied, once
values.description: action names the owner and what is asked: owner, action_ref (or action_refs, one request each), optionally id, a fixed input, and copy rows { key, from } or { key, value } where from reads request.<field>, answers.<field> or fields.<field> of the context. context has operation_id (asking again with it is the same request), and optionally record_ref, shape_ref, field_values, answers, linked_receipt_refs, receipt_ref and requested_at. Returns { handed, already, said }: the owner-action-request ids kept now and those already kept, which stay as the owner left them.

values.title: Hand a space over
values.job: Make a one-time code that hands this space to whoever opens it signed in, good for 14 days
values.description: Only the person who runs the space can make the code. The code is shown once; only its hash is kept, as a record:space-handover row the caller stores. It replaces the old hand_over_community.

values.title: Hear the words of a video or recording at a link
values.job: Get the words said in a video or recording at a link, from its captions or heard on my own computer
values.description: Reads the page at `url` with the link reader the person has (read-data/hear-a-link.json fetchers, such as yt-dlp; `link_reader` names its program). The page's own captions win when it has them; otherwise its sound is fetched and heard with the whisper-cli and ggml model the person granted. A link with no words always fails with why. The words are answered and nothing is kept: not on the computer, not in the person's files.

values.title: Hear a recording into timed words on my computer
values.job: Turn a recording in my files into its words with times, heard free on my own computer
values.description: Reads a recording from the person's files (`file`, its name or identity) through the run's files right into the run's own folder, hears it with the whisper-cli and ggml model the person granted (do-work/audio_transcription.py transcribe), and answers text, timed segments and language. The copy is removed once heard; the person's file is never changed. Nothing is sent to a paid speech service.

values.title: Hear a recording another of my devices made
values.job: Hear a recording one of my other devices made and tell me each person's turn in it as that device heard it
values.description: Reads a recording one of the person's other devices made (`file`, its name or identity in the person's files) from the bytes handed in as stored.files into the run's own folder, hears it on this computer with the Whisper model the person names, names each turn from the voices people enrolled (`voice_prints`; tool:enrol-a-voice-or-face), and answers one heard row per turn as tool:listen-for-a-while does, with `device` as the device and times counted from `at` (when the device began recording; now when left out). It keeps nothing: it writes no row and no file, so the person's AI takes the `heard` rows from the answer and keeps them where it chooses. The same `listening` name continues an earlier listening's unknown voices when the last answer's `voice_session` is handed back as `voice_session`. The person's recording rules and `listening_switch` are asked as for a live listening. The copy read for hearing is deleted once heard; the person's file is left where it is. Every answer lists what leaves this computer and what stays.

values.title: Hear one call's sources
values.job: Hear each source recording of one call on its own with a Whisper model on this computer and get the words back in time order, labelled by source
values.description: The old tool:hear-sources (computer/mac-tools.json:241-244 at b7dc53d08a). Hears each recording handed in (`sources: [{ source, path }]`, where source is a row of the hearing-sources DATA: microphone or system-audio) on its own, with the ggml Whisper model the person names (`model_path`), and answers the words in time order labelled by their source row (`me` marks the person's own voice). The whisper-cli and ffmpeg programs are the ones named (`whisper_cli`, `ffmpeg`), else the ones on PATH. `at` is when the call began (a time; the words count from it). It records the session (the program's id, the flags, the sources, a content id) in the session file of the hearing-sources DATA and answers it. It keeps no recording: each copy it writes beside a source is removed once heard, and the person's files are left where they are.

values.title: Say how warm a row is
values.job: Say how much a row is used as of a moment, its use heat halving with time, and the heat record one more use leaves
values.description: Give kept (the row's heat record { heat, at }, or nothing for a row never used), now (an ISO time; the current time otherwise) and used: true to also get the record a use leaves now (null when the row was used within the last 360 minutes, so nothing is written).

values.title: Keep a device quiet until a time
values.job: Turn Focus on and keep distracting apps closed on the person's computer until a set time, for a work session, a meeting or bedtime
values.description: Give until (a date and time) or minutes. apps names the apps to keep closed (a short default list of messaging and video apps when left out); only instead names the apps that stay open, and every other app is closed whenever it opens, for a session where the one thing is all that is left; Finder, Trillion, terminals and Shortcuts are never closed. focus false leaves Focus as it is. The hold ends by itself at its time (at most 12 hours away), so the person is never kept out of their own computer. The first time, the computer opens a Shortcuts window and the person presses Add Shortcut once.

values.title: Hold an output back when risk is too high
values.job: Hold an output back, and give the person's own support resources instead, when its risk is too high or unknown
values.description: Takes a risk assessment (was it run, the risk from 0 to 1 or null, categories) and the person's threshold. The output is released only when the assessment was run, the risk is a number and it is under the threshold. A missing, unfinished or unreadable assessment, or a threshold that is not a number, holds the output back. Held back, the answer carries the support resources the person gave. With an output sent, answers what goes out: the output, or the held-back notice.

values.title: Hold a group to what it agreed
values.job: Work out an agreement a group made, or a session one person planned (a daily meeting, a habit, a deadline): when to remind and check, who kept it, and the scorecard
values.description: Reads and keeps nothing: everything it works from comes in with the request and everything it makes comes back in the answer. The caller keeps the agreement and the marks. keep { group, what, agreed_by, cadence?, policy, agreement? } answers the agreement to keep and, when it says a time, its next meeting and the reminder and the check as something to arm (a repeat or one time); with no time it answers needs_time and arms nothing; agreement is the already held one, to merge into. retime { group, agreement, at, policy, ... } answers the agreement with its time given or moved. remind { group, agreement, policy } answers the sentence. check { group, agreement, arranged, evidence, policy, marks? } works out who came to the last meeting from the evidence handed in (speakers heard, members who wrote), marks each person from the policy, answers one mark_record per person, day and rule to keep, and who missed and any run of misses (marks are the ones already held). mark { group, agreement, person, rule, policy } answers one mark_record with its evidence (a newer mark for the same day replaces the older). scorecard { group, marks, policy } answers each person's points. Nothing is sent or booked: whoever runs it arms the wake, books the calendar and tells the group. The marks and their points, the meeting length, the time zone and the reminder and check minutes are the policy handed in; there is no default. Reading who was heard in a call needs a listening owner; until one exists the caller hands in the names it has.

values.title: How results like this turned out for everyone
values.job: Say how often things worked for other people in situations like mine, without anyone's own result being readable
values.description: Reads and keeps nothing: the caller hands in the pool's result rows (results, each { id, value: { contributor, worked, embedding } }, read from the store that holds the pool), and this is the only answer from them: the results whose situation is at least rules.min_similarity close in meaning (cosine) to the asked embedding, then one vote per contributor, nothing under rules.min_people distinct people, the median across rules.shards contributor shards, the randomized response undone, Laplace noise fixed by the question and by the rows of the shards that answer it (asking again gives the same answer; any join or withdrawal there draws new noise), and counts rounded to rules.people_bucket and rules.share_step. Returns { enough, people_at_least, worked_share? }, never a row or a contributor. rules are the pool's own settings (pooled_outcomes with search.min_similarity).

values.title: Import conversation exports already in my files
values.job: Keep every message of an exported conversation already stored in my account files, including Markdown individual chats, without needing access to a computer folder
values.description: Reads only named account files through find_file/read_file, pins their immutable content identity, checks the complete BLAKE3 bytes, then reuses the canonical conversation importer and message source keys. JSON, zipped JSON and individual ChatGPT Markdown exports share one message owner. Repeated words in distinct occurrences stay distinct. Completed exports are rechecked without adding messages; interrupted writes safely resume by stable source refs. Local timestamps with no zone stay source text. No host folder grant is requested. Imports are private. Missing JSON attachment references are reported; Markdown file references remain in their source text. Each file is bounded to 32 MiB; use the streaming source importer for larger exports.

values.title: Import Markdown as an editable document
values.job: Turn Markdown into the editable document scene tree, keeping its headings, lists, tables, code and source spans
values.description: Provide Markdown text for a bounded result, or use the file adapter with a folder grant for a large editable tree. The result is a Documents page made from the same Container, Text and Image scene nodes used by the editable document model, plus each visible block's exact source token and UTF-8 byte span. The importer uses its declared editing rules for list shortcuts and inline marks, and verifies that exporting and importing the resulting tree preserves its semantic revision. Markdown source byte spans point into the original UTF-8 input; they are evidence distinct from canonicalized output bytes.

values.title: Import a Markdown file as an editable document
values.job: Turn a Markdown file into the editable document scene tree, keeping its structure and source spans
values.description: Reads one Markdown file inside the folder you grant, imports it through the maintained editable Documents parser, and writes the full editable scene tree plus checked UTF-8 source spans to a new private JSON file inside the same folder. It returns only a small summary. Source and output paths are relative to your granted folder. It never overwrites an existing output. Inputs are limited to 500,000 bytes.

values.title: Import my conversations from one source
values.job: Bring every conversation of one app (an AI chat export, Google Takeout activity, or a local AI app's sessions) from this computer into my records completely, one row per conversation and every message, continuing where an earlier run stopped
values.description: Runs on the person's computer over the folder they granted (their home folder). source is one id tool:list-the-conversation-sources-on-this-computer gives; files, when given, names the files (paths in the folder) instead of looking for them. Each conversation is kept as the person's messages (record message, with its source key, so bringing it in again adds nothing twice) and one row of their AI conversations list (record:ai-conversation: title, app, conversation, started, last, messages, models, original_file; labels, people, pursuits and follow-ups they set are never touched). Writes are handed back as keep, in batches, for the caller to write where the person keeps them. Each file has a cursor row (conversation-import-cursor) that moves only past what was kept, so a run that stops, or reaches time_box_seconds, answers more: true and the next run goes on from there; a file already done and unchanged is skipped. Files the messages carried are handed back as keep (file and base64) for the caller to write into the person's files under /messages: an export's file (ChatGPT's file-XXXX, Grok's asset) found beside the export as /messages/<app>/<name>, an image pasted into a session as /messages/<conversation>/<message>-<n>; a file the caller already holds with the same bytes is not written again, and a file not found beside the export is counted (attachments_not_kept), never an error.

values.title: Insert my rendered corrections into a copy of my FilmCraft project as editable clips (runs on your computer)
values.job: Make a new copy of my FilmCraft project with each rendered correction put in at its freeze frame: a frame hold of the same clip, the overlay on the third video track, the voice and the music and sound effects on the second and third audio tracks
values.description: Reads a FilmCraft project (.fcproj, JSON) and writes a NEW project. For each shot named, from <shots>/<shot id>.json (its plate source file and frame) and the three files in <out>/<shot id>/ (<id>-overlay-prores4444.mov, <id>-narrator.wav, <id>-sfx-music.wav), it ripple-inserts a frame-hold segment of the plate's own clip at that frame (the clip's own effects, so its grade applies), razors every clip that spans the point and moves everything after it, extends the adjustment layer over the inserted span, and places the overlay on video track 3, the voice on audio track 2 and the music and sound effects on audio track 3, with each file's facts read by ffprobe. Refuses, saying what to change: an output that is the input, a missing shot file, a missing rendered file, a plate that is not a media file of the project, a frame no clip on the first video track holds. The input project is never written. It does not open or script FilmCraft. The inserts here are the person's own corrections; a project the person protects takes picked options only through its own apply tool, so run this on a copy.

values.title: Install a tool source my rows name
values.job: Install on this computer the tool source one of my rows names (its label, the https archive of its tool folders and the pin of their files), or take it away when the row was removed, so every computer of mine runs the tools my own rows say and none needs a hand step
values.description: One step of the person's own workflow that keeps each of their computers on what their rows say each tool source is. Given {source, address, files_blake3} it installs that archive as the source of that label through the engine's tools:update at the Workshop's address (a new label becomes a new source; the same label moves to the new pin); given {source, removed: true} it takes the source away. The source may be any https archive of tool folders, a teammate's as well as the Workshop's. The run may install only because its row declares the right {at: "@tools", id: "*", operations: ["tools:update"]}, which the person grants by switching on the wake that runs it. It answers the engine's answer with the label: changed, files_blake3, previous, removed, switch_again.

values.title: Keep a long job resumable
values.job: Keep a long job on the person's computer (a meeting summary, a transcription) under a key, so starting it twice gives the same job, its output so far is kept in numbered pieces, and any client can resume reading from a cursor or cancel it
values.description: Give action: start (key, and seed and version when wanted), append (id, piece), read (id, cursor: the last seq read, 0 for all), finish (id), cancel (id) or list. The jobs are kept in a file in the folder the person granted. Returns the job (id, state, stream_url, expires_at, seed, version, chunks), { seq } for append, { job, pieces, cursor } for read and { jobs } for list.

values.title: Join a space
values.job: Work out whether a person joins a shared space by the way its join rows allow (free, or holding the access a row names) and answer their member row
values.description: Reads the space's record:space row and the person's record:space-member row from `records`. A person already in is answered with their type and how they came in, and nothing is answered to keep. Otherwise the space's config.join rows decide, as data: a row {free:true} lets anyone in, a row {access:"<ref>"} lets in a person who holds that access now (worked out by the paid-access reader over your payment events, offers and grants), and a space with no join rows is joined only by invitation (a person gets in by accepting one). A person who left may join again; a person a host put out stays out. The new member gets the type the space's label starts joiners with (or config.joins_as) and may give the name they will show with name. Answers whether they joined, their type and which row let them in, with the new member row under `keep` for the caller to store; a refusal says how the space is joined, in the space's own words (config.words) or the standard ones.

values.title: Join what is being worked on into one tree
values.job: Join the goals, decisions, AIs, jobs, spaces, people, automations and tool runs my records already answered into one tree of what is being worked on and who is doing it, or one goal's branch of it
values.description: Give answers: what each of the work map's reads answered, by name (goals: /work/api/decisions with pursuits and summaries, work: /work/api/ai-work with agents and work, spaces: /work/api/spaces, automations: /work/api/workflows, workshop: /work/api/workshop); a read left out adds no cards. from (optional) is a card id such as goal:g1 to keep only that card and everything under it. The join is the work map's own: read-data/work-map-sources.json says where each kind's rows are, which fields are its id, title, detail, state and time, who does it and what it hangs under; a row whose parent is not shown falls to whoever does it, then to the root. Answers nodes (each card's id <source>:<row id>, source, kind, icon, title, detail, at, status, who; the rows themselves are not given back), lines (parent to child) and counts by kind. It reads nothing from the person's store, keeps nothing and sends nothing. Refuses answers that are not an object, a read name the work map does not have, or answers holding none of its reads. The screen (show/work-map-screen.tsx) also reads those answers itself, draws the cards on the board, by state, as a table and on a timeline and opens a card's screen, and the message task canvas groups message tasks; this run does none of that.

values.title: Say how strong a new password is
values.job: Say how strong a new password is, in the words the sign-in pages show under the new password box, before I sign up with an email and a password
values.description: Give password (text). It is scored as the sign-in pages score it as it is typed (password-strength.mjs, passwords.json): 0 when shorter than min_length (8), then 1, plus one for 12 characters or more and one for three kinds of character (lower case, upper case, digits, others). Answers score, said (the words for that score), min_length, max_length and too_long (whether the service would refuse it as longer than max_length). The password is judged in memory only: it is never printed back, kept or sent, and nothing is signed in, made or changed. The sign-in pages themselves (passkey.mjs, kept in this folder but not run here) do the rest of the old job: they run the passkey step through the browser's WebAuthn, send and check emailed codes and post the email-and-password form; those need a browser and the sign-in service, which this run does not have.

values.title: Check words or anything made against your rules
values.job: Check words, a plan or anything else someone made against the rules a person set, and say what breaks which rule, why, and what to do instead
values.description: The one judge every check uses, with rules only: the caller hands in the rule rows (tool:check-against-a-persons-rules-and-verdicts is the same judge with the person's verdicts and stands, or reading their check rows by branch). Give rules (one row each) and what to check: text, texts, value (any JSON whose words a person reads), artifact (any JSON a rule reads by path, like a plan or a take's measures) or items, each with an optional kind. A row picks words (words, pattern, exact or a named grammar check), named groups of markers (groups: a framework's parts, the feelings or cues a script should carry), values (path, with where or where_pattern to keep only some) or an evidence check over supplied evidence (evidence: exact source spans, complete review, a captured answer set), may apply only to some kinds, may judge every item together as one piece (across), and may say what must hold: required, count_at_least, count_at_most, value_at_least, value_at_most, equals, includes_all, in_order, repeated_at_least, percent_found_at_least or together_at_least. Its because and at_most travel with every finding. Each row may carry a weight; the answer's score is the weighted score of the rows that apply, and min_score fails a request scored under it. Returns status (passed, failed, held when only capped rows found something, no-applicable-rule, no-input), score, findings (with the offset of each word found) and lines in plain words. Nothing passes on silence: a value test that finds nothing is a finding.

values.title: Judge one-shot sounds as whole sounds (runs on your computer)
values.job: Judge these one-shot sound files whole, from first onset to their tail, against a description
values.description: Trim = first onset (-40 dB of peak) less 5 ms to the last sample above -50 dB of peak, then earshot match (against the alternatives), describe, realness and measure on that trim; merged into OUT.json keyed by file and query.

values.title: Judge sound-effect candidates by ear and pick one per sound (runs on your computer)
values.job: Judge the sound effects I generated or found the way my palette was judged, pick the best one for each sound and level it to my real sound
values.description: Every candidate (forged, generated by a local model, or downloaded) is trimmed (an event found by earshot with clean edges, or the whole sound for swells), put in the palette format (rate, channels, fades, peak), and read by earshot: match z for the sound's query, realness, measure. A lead-in (a riser) is cut so its peak sits where the real one peaks. The pick is the highest match z among candidates that are not distorted; a sound may be barred from another sound's source. The pick is scaled to the real sound's active loudness and compared with it (A/B). The tuned values can come from the person's settings record (settings_record).

values.title: Keep one Facebook Page's own token
values.job: Read the one Page the person chose from the connection's sign-in and keep its own token sealed in the vault
values.description: GET graph.facebook.com/v23.0/{page_id}?fields=access_token with the connection's user token, placed from the vault only as the request leaves. The Page's access_token is kept in the vault as the connection's page_access_token field before the reply is read, so it is never in the answer. Run by tool:connect-an-account-by-signing-in-to-the-service at the sign-in callback, for the Page the person named beforehand or the only one the sign-in reaches.

values.title: Keep a file from my computer in my Files
values.job: Keep files from the person's computer in their Files under names they choose: one file or a list of files, each kept in order; a small file in pieces, a large one over the lease road
values.description: Runs on the person's computer with the drives they granted it to see and the folder changes they granted. Keeps one regular file (not a link, not a folder) or a list of them (at most DATA most_files, keep-a-local-file.json) into the person's Files under the names given. A small file is written in pieces that each fit one request; a file above the whole-file threshold goes over the lease road in chunks. A file that is refused or fails is named in refused with its reason, and the others are still kept. Returns kept (name, bytes, media_type, finished) and refused. Deletes and moves nothing.

values.title: Keep a profile of how someone does their thing
values.job: Keep the profile of how a person does their thing, so drafts made for them are shaped by it and checked against it
values.description: Give the profile's name, the subject's name, the items you derived (a non-empty list of objects) and, as refs, the feature schemas, evaluators, generators and validation policy that go with it. Returns the one profile record to keep under the profile's name (the person's store keeps it: workflow:keep-how-someone-does-their-thing); keeping it again replaces it. Empty items, or a ref that is not a non-empty string, are refused.

values.title: Check a prospect row
values.job: Build one row of my prospect list from what a finder found, the researched profile, a status or my notes, checked, for my AI to keep
values.description: One row per prospect, under the key you give, built over the row you hold (give its fields as held; a field you keep by hand stays). action keep (default): found = the facts a finder gave (name, url, place, source, size, signals, score) and/or profile = the research (profile, problems 1 to 3, triggers, case_study, channels). Every problem, trigger and channel carries basis stated (the material says it; evidence quotes it word for word) or inferred (a reading of it, with what it is read from). Send material with a profile and a stated quotation that is not in it is refused. A new row starts at the first status (found, or researched once a profile is checked). action mark: status (found, researched, drafted, contacted, replied, booked, won, lost, dropped) and/or notes, over the row you hold. The answer holds the row as keep ([{ id, type, value, expected }], expected being the row as you handed it in, null for a new prospect); this keeps nothing, your AI keeps the row in your prospect list. The fields, statuses and rules are DATA in do-work/prospect-list.json. It contacts nobody.

values.title: Keep a secret by name in my vault
values.job: Keep one secret value (a key, a token) under a name in my own Trillion vault, or remove the value held under a name, so my tools and AIs can use it by name without ever seeing it
values.description: Stores the value on stdin under the given name in the person's own vault through the engine's secrets:put operation, with the person's own key as the credential. The name is one the vault accepts, and a service connection's own names are refused by the engine. The value never goes on a command line, into a log or into the answer: the answer is {name, accepted}. Accepted means written at the writer, or queued sealed for the writer when this computer is not the writer. Connections keep their values through service-connections; use this for any other secret. With --remove NAME --issuer-status revoked|unknown it removes the value held under that name through secrets:remove instead, reads no stdin and answers {name, removed, issuer_status} (removed false when none was held) or {name, queued: true, issuer_status} when this computer is not the writer. Removing a secret does not revoke it at its issuer, so the caller says whether it was revoked there or is unknown.

values.title: Keep a show rule
values.job: Keep a rule about when something shows, hides or stays quiet for me, or switch a starting rule off or on
values.description: Keeps one rule in your show-rules record (rule; one with the id of a rule you keep changes it), or switches a starting rule off or on (starting: { id, on }). A rule with a problem is refused in its words. Answers the rules after the change and keep: the record to write, with the record as it was read as expected, so a record changed meanwhile is not written over.

values.title: Keep a show type
values.job: Keep a preset of show rules I can switch on, or change one I keep
values.description: Keeps one type (a preset: { id, label, inherits?, rules }) in your show-rules record; one with the id of a type you keep changes it. A type inheriting one it does not find, or itself, is refused in its words. Answers keep, the record to write.

values.title: Keep the person's edit of an AI's words
values.job: Keep what the person changed in words an AI wrote for them, so their voice is learned from it
values.description: Run when the person themselves changed words an AI wrote (a draft's caption): kind (like post), subject_id (what was edited), before (the AI's words), after (theirs) and before_by (the AI that wrote them). Nothing is kept when the words did not really change. Returns edit (or edit null) and keep: the row the store writes. The store keeps only the newest keep_edits edits (workflow:keep-how-someone-does-their-thing retires the older ones).

values.title: Keep action surfaces complete
values.job: Build the versioned action inventory and proof workflow, decorate a newly selected recipe, or check its inventory and proof without changing frozen runs.
values.description: Build the versioned action inventory and proof workflow, decorate a newly selected recipe, or check its inventory and proof without changing frozen runs. All opinion settings arrive as input rows; the tool reads no records. No old Worker store is imported.

values.title: Keep the newest videos of channels and their captions
values.job: List the newest videos of each channel, tab or playlist I name and get each new video's captions with the times they are said, its description and, if I ask, its top comments, without downloading any video
values.description: For each seed (a channel's @handle, id or link, a link to one of its tabs such as /shorts, or a playlist link) lists the newest `newest` videos with yt-dlp on this computer, then fetches the captions (in the first of caption_languages the video has; json3, else WebVTT), the site's description and, with also ["comments"], the top comments_per_video comments of every listed video not in skip_ids. It never downloads a video.
