It asks politely, one request at a time with a drawn wait between requests, at most a set number of requests and budget_seconds per run (the settings file harvest-settings.json in this folder holds every number), and it stops at the first refusal (a robot check or too many requests). It keeps three files in your files: listing (listing.json: every listed video of each seed, with kept_before), captions (captions.jsonl: one line per video settled now, { video_id, url, seed, status ready|empty|failed, language, format, lines [[second, words]], info }) and comments (comments.jsonl). With rows it also answers, as keep, one row per seed or per settled video for your sources list (record:sources:<id>), each field from a fact ({ fact }), a text with {fact} holes ({ text }) or a value ({ value }); give the rows you already hold as held and a row built over one keeps the fields this does not write; each keep row carries expected, the row as it was handed in (null for a new one). It keeps no row itself: your AI keeps the rows it answers. Facts of a video: video_id, title, url, published, duration, view_count, seed, listing_url, source, caption_status, caption_language. Facts of a seed: seed, listing_url, source, listed, kept, finished. The answer says what was done and, when anything is left, `again`: the input to send next; after a refusal wait `wait_minutes` first. Repeat until again is null.

values.title: List completed Stripe checkouts as payment events
values.job: List every completed Stripe checkout since a time as a payment event, so a buyer whose purchase no webhook reported still holds the access their offer gives once the events are kept
values.description: Give created_after_unix, offer_id to list one offer only, and optionally offers (your offer rows, so each event carries its offer's pursuit_ids). Reads the seller's completed checkouts as list-completed-stripe-checkouts does and answers one payment event for each that names a buyer email and an offer; its id comes from the checkout, so the same checkout is always the same event. Keeps nothing: your AI keeps the events where it keeps your records, and paid-access then holds each buyer's access by that email. Answers events, left_out (counts of checkouts with no buyer email or no offer), complete and next_created_after_unix. Uses the Stripe key of the seller connection that seller_connection names (service_connection:stripe is your own).

values.title: Keep the latest posts of forums I name
values.job: Keep the newest posts of the forums I name (subreddits), with their titles, words, scores and comment counts, from a public archive of the site
values.description: For each forum (a subreddit) asks the Arctic Shift public archive of Reddit (a third-party service, not the site itself) for its newest posts, a page of 100 at a time, each page older than the last, up to `pages` pages a forum (6 when left out), and keeps each post's id, link, title, words, score, comment count and time, with the forum and the group you name for it. This depends on that archive staying up. It waits half a second between pages and tries a page four times before it names the forum in `failed`. It keeps one file in your files (forum-posts.jsonl: one line per post). A run that reaches budget_seconds answers `again`, the input to send next (it holds where each forum stopped); repeat until `again` is null. tool:collect-and-rank-viewer-questions finds the questions people ask in these posts.

values.title: Keep keyed things inside a fixed memory budget
values.job: Keep many keyed things inside a fixed memory budget, each read after the first being one array index, and let the least recently used go first when the budget is full
values.description: Give steps, applied in order to a slot table made from capacity_bytes (the budget, 24 MB when left out) and columns (DATA: [{ kind, field, as: number | text }], the fields kept in typed arrays): set { key, kind, value, bytes? } admits or updates a key (bytes is what it costs the budget, its JSON length when left out), find { key }, read { key }, drop { key }, kind { kind } (every key of that kind still held) and clear. Answers answers (one per step: set gives its slot and version, find its slot or -1, read whether it is held and its kind, value, version and bytes) and held (slots, bytes, capacity_bytes, evictions, kinds, words). Nothing is kept after the run: send the same steps again for the same table.

values.title: Collect current measurement coverage
values.job: Discover operation catalogs, source revisions and execution receipts, then return current neutral measurement observations and forecast coverage
values.description: Takes the source configuration in the request (config, the measurement_source_config value the caller read from its store), resolves bounded source and receipt roots plus the configured meter book, and collects with a freshly returned provider-qualified price book. Reads and keeps nothing in the person's rows. New operations under those roots are discovered automatically. Receipt content and source, meter and price revisions are pinned. Missing values, unknown meters, failed work, missing prices, unconfigured roots and incomplete discovery stay unknown. The scheduled workflow persists returned history through the measurement-ledger owner.

values.title: Keep Trillion's standing instructions in my AI's own instruction file (runs on your computer)
values.job: Put, check or take out Trillion's standing instructions as one marked block in my AI harness's own global instruction file, leaving every other line of it as it was
values.description: Reads, writes or removes one marked block in a harness's own global instruction file (Claude Code's CLAUDE.md, Codex's AGENTS.md, Gemini CLI's GEMINI.md; where each is, and its home variable, is a row of read-data/harness-instruction-files.json). inspect answers absent, present, outdated or blocked (markers that are not one start followed by one end) and writes nothing; apply writes or replaces only the block and twice changes nothing; remove takes out only the block. Every byte outside the block is kept, a symbolic link is written through to its target, and the file keeps its mode. A hosted app with no file is answered with the control it has, never written. `text` is the current words; without it the copy in read-data/standing-instructions.json is used.

values.title: Keep public posts by link
values.job: Keep the text, numbers and media addresses of public posts I name by link, through a public mirror, without opening the posts' site
values.description: For each link to a public post (x.com or twitter.com status links; the link pattern is in harvest-settings.json) asks a third-party public mirror for the post as JSON and keeps its text, counts, author and the addresses of its media, never the media themselves. This depends on that mirror staying up: its address is `posts.mirror_base` in harvest-settings.json and can be changed there. It asks politely with the same limits file as the channel harvest: one request at a time with a drawn wait, a bounded number of requests and budget_seconds per run, a stop at the first refusal. Links already kept (skip_ids) are not asked again. It keeps one file in your files (posts.jsonl: one line per post settled now: user, post_id, link, status ready or failed, the post's kept fields or the reason). A run that stops early answers `again`, the input to send next, and after a refusal `wait_minutes`; repeat until `again` is null. With rows one per post, the answer holds the posts as keep for your sources list, built over the rows you give as held, each with expected (the row as it was handed in, null for a new one); your AI keeps them, this keeps none.

values.title: Check a resource usage observation
values.job: Check an attributed measured source attempt, or its unknown outcome, and answer it exact, with a correcting event that points at the earlier one instead of rewriting history
values.description: Check an attributed measured source attempt, or its unknown outcome, and answer it exact, with a correcting event that points at the earlier one instead of rewriting history. Give observation, and supersedes_observation (the earlier observation, as an earlier answer returned it) when this one corrects it. This run reads no rows and keeps nothing; the caller keeps the answer.

values.title: Keep rulings on lines
values.job: Write down rulings on single lines of copy, such as a line a checker flagged for the person or a reviewer's good or bad, as rows of the person's Checks list
values.description: Give rows (each ruling: text, verdict, by, and optionally rule, kind, at, where and any other field kept), existing (the rulings already in list:checks, read from where the person keeps them, so a ruling is written once) and settings_record (the person's row of list:settings for this tool as the person's store gives it: unruled_part_of, the check branch a ruling with no rule goes under; refuse, [{ field, one_of: [values] } or { field, contains_one_of: [path parts] }] such as a test piece or a temporary folder; place, { field, pattern } that reads a ruling's place from its where; hand_rulings, the words a ruling given by hand may use; escalated_verdicts), or those fields themselves. by_hand true checks hand_rulings. Returns write, { records } to keep where the person keeps its Checks list: one record:check per text, verdict, by and rule (id record:check:ruling-<BLAKE3 hex>, kind labelled-line, or escalated-line for an escalated line, part_of its rule or unruled_part_of, its copy kind as line_kind), and fresh, how many are new. A write holding a refused row is refused whole. It writes nothing.

values.title: Keep the shared Workshop checkout on origin/main
values.job: Every five minutes, bring the shared Workshop checkout on this computer up to origin/main, keeping every file someone is changing, every untracked file, and every commit not on origin, and saving the whole working state on a local rescue ref first.
values.description: One pass over the granted checkout (--root). It refuses, touching nothing, when the checkout is not on branch main, when .git/index.lock exists, when a merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert is in progress, or when git fetch fails. Otherwise it saves the whole working state (tracked changes, untracked files, and commits not on origin/main) as a local refs/rescue/workshop-shared-<time> commit that is never pushed, then keeps every path whose bytes differ from both HEAD and origin, and every path changed in the last 120 seconds, skips the clean ones changed in the last 120 seconds until the next pass, moves HEAD and the index to origin/main with git reset --mixed, writes origin's bytes over the clean paths, and names the files origin deleted (with a removal proof) for disk-guard's removal list. It never deletes a file and never runs git reset --hard, git clean or git push. Returns outcome (ran, refused or stopped), behind_before and behind_after, the rescue_ref, local_commits, updated, removal_entries, kept and skipped (each with why).

values.title: Keep the words a person gave
values.job: Work out the row that keeps the words a person gave in reply, with the consent they gave and the words that gave it, as a received row of the list
values.description: Answers the row that keeps words with one of the consents the list declares and consent_note, the person's own words that gave it (or where they are). With row_id it fills the row that asked them (found among the `rows` handed in); without it, `who` is required and the words become their own row, the same words from the same person always the same row. The row is received and any approval is taken away, so changed words are reviewed again. A withdrawn row takes no more words. The same call again changes nothing. Nothing is written by this tool: `keep` holds the records the caller's AI keeps in its store, conditional on the row as handed in. Returns row_id, status, changed and keep.

values.title: Keep what I said to an AI and what it answered
values.job: Keep the messages of a turn with an AI that keeps its chats on its own service (Muse, Grok Bot), my words and its replies, as my messages
values.description: Takes one conversation's messages from an AI that keeps its chats on its own service and has no store on this computer (Muse, Grok Bot: set-up-my-account harnesses.json turns.roads mcp-record), as old Trillion's record_messages did: app (the AI as it calls itself), conversation_id (its own name for the conversation), title?, and messages [{id, speaker: person | ai, text word for word, at?, model?}]. Each is kept as the person's message record through the same message owner every other place uses, with its original time, so sending a turn again adds nothing; the conversation's row of the AI conversations list is kept. Answers conversation_id, messages, added and already_kept.

values.title: Keep what my devices report about themselves
values.job: Keep the facts a new person's devices report about themselves (which cameras a computer sees, whether a phone's switches are on), each report replacing that device's facts, so a setup checklist can tick itself from them
values.description: Give reports (each { device, facts: { name: text }, and device_id, source and generation together for a device that reports from several sources }), devices (the devices the last run answered; omit the first time) and optionally now (an ISO time stamped on what changes). Applies each report in order with device-facts.mjs deviceFacts: a report replaces that device's (or that source's) facts whole, a report that changes nothing changes nothing, an older generation is answered stale, and at most 20 devices are kept, the least recently heard dropped first. Answers answers (one per report: device, changed, and for an identified report device_id, source, stale, current_generation) and devices (every device as kept). It refuses a report with no device name, facts that are not short lowercase names with text values within device-facts.json's bounds, and an identified report missing its id, source or generation, naming the report. It keeps nothing after the run, reads no device itself and writes nothing. It does not tick setup steps from the facts (that needs the account's checklist rules and the formula engine) and does not show the Get started, plan, account, security or business pages: those are the app's screens.

values.title: Keep where you stand on something
values.job: Write down whether a person agrees, disagrees or partly agrees with something made for them, such as a title, a take, a plan or a file, in their own words
values.description: Give kind (what the thing is: a title, a take, a plan, a file), the thing (artifact_ref, its identity: 1f: and 64 hex digits, or file: and that identity; or the thing itself: text, contains for a part of a text, or view for any JSON, with fold, how its owner says two texts are the same), stance (agree, disagree or partly, or null to take a stand back), why (the person's own words, kept exactly) and answered_by "person": only send what the person said. Returns the stance record, one per kind and identity (stance:<kind>:<identity>), for the caller to keep where the person keeps stances: a change of mind is a new version and every earlier stand stays in its history. Text is identified folded, so the same title typed again finds the same stand. A name instead of an identity, or a stand not answered by the person, is refused.

values.title: Keep who appeared in a recording
values.job: Work out the rows that link each person whose voice was heard or face seen in a recording to that recording, the seconds and the place, for the person's list of where people appeared
values.description: Reads and keeps nothing. Takes what tool:who-is-in-this answered (heard) and what tool:find-faces answered (seen) about one recording and answers one row per stretch (rows) for the person's Where people appeared list, for you to keep: who, heard or seen, recording, start and end seconds, the words said, the place it was recorded, and the person's own row when given. A person is named only when the answer named them, and only while their voice-print or face-print is handed in with consent words (consents, read from the prints without their numbers): a person with none refuses the answer. An unsure stretch keeps the people it could be and an unknown voice keeps its number, so enrolling that voice later names what was kept; a face nobody enrolled is not answered. The same answer again is the same row ids; a changed answer answers the rows it replaces as superseded_rows (earlier, the appearance records already kept for this recording, tells which) and deletes none. list is the list definition to make if it is not there yet. No row holds a print's numbers.

values.title: Label a person
values.job: Give a person in the network one label (unwanted-requests, unsafe or vouched) in the database named in the input.
values.description: Gives a person in the network a label: unwanted-requests, unsafe or vouched. It writes one label row for the labeler, once, and one history row, in the database named by `database`, through the connection the person's vault holds under that name. Enough different labelers hide a listing; this tool only records the label.

values.title: Label frames of my videos with a small model on my computer (runs on your computer)
values.job: Label sampled frames of my videos with a small model on my computer, from my own shot vocabulary: an image-text model, a vision decider or a vision-language model, and rank free-text places
values.description: Give shots (with frames), vocabulary ({field: {value: plain definition}}) and the model. label_frames_with_image_text_model asks each value two ways (bare word, plain definition) of an open_clip model; label_frames_with_vision_decider asks a decider-vision snapshot one lettered question per field (questions, context, mode bare | defined), as a two-round tournament past ten values; label_frames_with_vision_language_model asks an mlx-vlm model for one JSON answer per frame (instruction, phrases for free text); rank_free_text_places ranks every distinct reference phrase per frame two ways. Each answer has meta (load seconds, time per frame, memory) and one row per frame. Steps: label_frames_with_image_text_model, label_frames_with_vision_decider, label_frames_with_vision_language_model, rank_free_text_places.

values.title: Lay out a calendar view
values.job: Arrange time blocks for a day, week, month or agenda view, split overlapping blocks into columns, and name the blocks that clash
values.description: Takes time blocks and the views the person keeps (each a record naming a geometry: a time grid with a number of day columns, a month grid, or an agenda list, and the numbers it reads) and gives back the days to show with the blocks on each. In a time grid, blocks that overlap in time share the day column in equal parts, and every set of blocks that overlap is listed as a clash. Days are the person's own: give utc_offset_minutes and every time moves by it before it is cut into a day; an all-day block is a date and is not moved. There is no clock: the day comes from the anchor, the selected block, the first block or the range start. A view whose geometry is not known is answered with a notice.

values.title: Lay out a diagram of boxes and arrows
values.job: Lay out a diagram of boxes and arrows so few arrows cross, and give me the positions, the arrow routes, how many arrows cross and a picture of it as SVG
values.description: Takes the boxes (an id, and optionally a label, a size, a lane and a style) and the arrows between them (from, to, an optional id and label). Breaks cycles by reversing the arrows that close them (reported, and drawn in their real direction), puts every box in a layer, orders the boxes inside each layer to cut crossings (counted exactly, before and after), places them without overlap, spreads the arrow ends along each side of a box and routes each arrow as a list of points. Optional lanes (a list of lane ids in order) keep every box of a lane in its own band with the same layers lining up across lanes; direction "right" lays layers out left to right. Answers each box's position, size, layer, order and lane, each arrow's route, the drawing's width and height, quality numbers (crossings before and after, reversed arrows, layers, virtual points) and, unless draw is false, a standalone SVG whose colours are page variables (--diagram-background, --diagram-ink, --diagram-node-fill, --diagram-node-stroke, --diagram-edge) with fallbacks. A box's style may hold only fill, stroke, stroke-width, stroke-dasharray, font-weight, font-style and opacity, with plain values. The same request always gives the same answer. Takes no diagram text: send the boxes and arrows as data. An arrow to an unknown box, two boxes with one id, a lane not in lanes, a style outside the list and a request over the limits (1000 boxes, 5000 arrows, 200 characters in a label) are refused with a sentence saying what to send.

values.title: Lay out a person's profile
values.job: Lay out one person's profile page from their record: name, fields with values, related lists such as their activity or deals, and the actions that apply
values.description: Give layout (what the profile shows: surfaceId; identity {titlePath, subtitlePath, fallbackTitle}; fields [{id, label, sourceId, valuePath, fallbackValue, editable, visibleWhen}]; relationships [{id, label, sourceId, itemPath, fields [{key, path}], emptyLabel}]; actions [{id, label, enabled, intent, visibleWhen}]) and sources (the records it reads by name; record is read when a field names none). Returns the profile's title, subtitle, each visible field with its value, each related list with its items, and each visible action.

values.title: Lay pictures over a video
values.job: Put a logo, a photo, or a picture-in-picture or b-roll video over a video at chosen times, with position, size and opacity
values.description: Draws each picture or video from `start` seconds for its length, `size` wide, its centre at `x`,`y` (0..1 across and down), at its opacity, later ones over earlier ones; a video plays its `from`..`to` stretch. Saves the new video in your files.

values.title: Leave a shared pursuit
values.job: A person leaves a pursuit they share with other people: their own membership of its space is marked left, what they put there stays, and the pursuit ends for them
values.description: Give the pursuit's id, the person, and the rows read from the store ([{ id, type, value }]: the pursuit, its space, the space's member rows). Refuses a pursuit that is not theirs or has ended, and refuses the person who runs the space (hand it over first). Answers the membership change and the pursuit ended, under `keep` ([{ id, type, value, expected }]) for the caller to store. It changes only the caller's own rows. The network's room leave is not a row change and is not done here.

values.title: Leave a space
values.job: Work out a member leaving a shared space and answer their member row marked left; what they put there stays
values.description: Answers the person's record:space-member row marked left, stamped when, under `keep` for the caller to store. Leaving a space the person is not in answers nothing to keep. The person who runs the space cannot leave it: hand it over first. They may join again later by the space's join rows.

values.title: Show device steps only when they apply
values.job: Leave waiting rows about an unowned device out only when the caller reports complete, successful evidence; keep them visible when evidence is unknown.
values.description: Leave waiting rows about an unowned device out only when the caller reports complete, successful evidence; keep them visible when evidence is unknown. All opinion settings arrive as input rows; the tool reads no records. No old Worker store is imported.

values.title: Let go of a site address
values.job: Stop a website answering at one of its addresses
values.description: The site stops answering at host (a name or your own domain), and every earlier name that sent visitors to it goes too. Another account may take a name once it has been let go.

values.title: Line up two movements by their phase, whatever their speed (runs on your computer)
values.job: Match each moment of one movement to the same part of another movement, even when one is slower, starts later or has more frames
values.description: Takes two pose tracks (from tool:read-peoples-poses-from-a-video, or any file in the pose.keypoints.v1 shape) and writes the pairs of frames that show the same phase of the movement: dynamic time warping over each frame's posture, with the joints centred on the hips and scaled by the torso so camera framing and body size do not count. It uses the most confident person in each track. Gamma 0 is hard warping; above 0 is soft warping with a smoother path. The path is monotonic (time never runs backwards), starts at the first pair and ends at the last pair. It also gives a distance (the posture cost along the path divided by both frame counts) so several references can be ranked against one clip. An empty or torso-less track, or a joint that is not a number, is refused with the reason; nothing is written. The cost grows with the product of the two frame counts: a 10 second clip at 30 frames a second takes seconds, a 10 minute clip does not.

values.title: Link Signal on this computer
values.job: Link my Signal account to this computer so my messages can be read here
values.description: Links this computer to your Signal account as one of its devices, once, so tool:read-my-signal-messages-on-this-computer can read your messages here. The computer fetches signal-cli and the Java it needs itself. It runs as a session: as soon as Signal gives the link it prints { state: "scan", link, qr_text, qr_svg }, the code to scan, and keeps waiting; on your phone open Signal, Settings, Linked devices, Link new device, and scan it. It then answers { state: "linked", self_id }, or not_linked with why (a code is good for about a minute: run it again for a new one). Signal's keys for this device stay in a folder on this computer that only this tool's runs are given. Already linked, it answers linked and asks nothing.

values.title: List a channel's latest videos (runs on your computer)
values.job: Get the latest videos of a creator's channel: their titles, dates, lengths and links
values.description: Runs on the person's own computer with yt-dlp, which lists a channel's videos without downloading them: the answer is the channel's name (source) and its latest videos (30 unless --limit says otherwise), each with item_id, title, duration, published (as the site writes it), url and the first 500 characters of the description. The channel is a link, a channel id (UC...) or a @handle. Nothing is sent to Trillion and no key is needed.

values.title: Look inside a folder on a drive
values.job: List the files and folders in one folder on a drive connected to this person's computer, a page at a time
values.description: Runs on the person's computer. hidden "1" includes hidden files; offset and limit page through a long folder. Returns path, name, parent, mount, entries (name, path, kind, file_kind, bytes, modified_at), total and has_more.

values.title: List the inputs a repository needs from this computer
values.job: Find named environment and place-report inputs read by tracked code, without revealing their values
values.description: Scans tracked Python, shell and JavaScript source for the original environment and place-report patterns. Lists names, reader files, presence, and run switches. Does not execute repository code.

values.title: List a space's members
values.job: List who is in a shared space, by the name each chose to show, with their type; only members may ask
values.description: Lists the space's record:space-member rows handed in as `records`: each person's id, the name they chose to show (never a contact), their member type and its label, and whether they count now (the same reader as tool:check-someone-is-in-a-space, over one read of what people hold). Only a current member may ask; anyone else is refused in the space's words. include_ended true also lists people who left, were put out or lapsed.

values.title: List a space's posts
values.job: Read the posts a member who counts there now sees in a shared space, newest first
values.description: Answers the space's item rows (record:space-item) the caller handed in, newest first. Only a person who counts as a member of the space now may read them; anyone else is refused in words. It replaces the old read-items of create_group_post.

values.title: List the clips that say they are part of a series (runs on your computer)
values.job: Find my clips that are part 1, part 2, part 3 of a series, from what is said in them
values.description: Reads one or more moments files (one JSON row per spoken moment of a clip, as a transcript cut into moments gives) and lists every clip whose joined words say "part <n>" (a number, or one to fifteen in words) within its first 300 characters, the window changeable. Each line is the clip's name, path, source, the part words it said, and the clip's whole text, ordered by path so each clip reads once. Words like "partly", "parts 5" or "department 4" do not count. Moments of one clip may come from several files and in any order; they are joined by their number.

values.title: List the comparisons a rule can use
values.job: List the comparisons and the all-of and any-of groups a rule can use, for one kind of field or every kind
values.description: Answers each comparison's id, its label, what it takes (nothing, one value, a list of values, words, text, a day or a range) and the field kinds that offer it, the group combinators, and the field kinds known. Send operators to list a person's own comparison rows instead of the built-in ones.

values.title: List completed Stripe checkouts
values.job: List every completed Stripe checkout since a time, payment links included, so each buyer can be followed up once
values.description: Give created_after_unix, and offer_id to keep one offer. Returns each checkout oldest first (session id, time, buyer email, offer and price option, amount, currency, subscription id), complete, and next_created_after_unix for the next read. The same checkout can come back in two reads: keep each one once by provider_session_id. Uses the Stripe key of the seller connection that seller_connection names (service_connection:stripe is your own).

values.title: Drives on my computers
values.job: List the drives connected to this person's computer: each drive's name, where it is mounted, its size and free space, its kind (USB, disk image, internal) and whether it can be ejected
values.description: Runs on the person's computer with the drives they granted it to see. Returns devices: each with name, mount, size_bytes, free_bytes, kind, internal, ejectable and state.

values.title: List connections
values.job: List the services this account is connected to, with each connection's status and when it was last checked
values.description: List the services this account is connected to, with each connection's status and when it was last checked. Returns connections: one row a connection in connection id order, { connection_id, service, vendor, account_label?, status?, can_send, connected_at?, grant_scopes_known, grant_scopes?, capabilityChoices?, last_checked?, connected_by? }, from the person's own connection records, which you hand in as connection_records (read them from the person's store: records of type connection, each { id, value }), and from the connections the account's vault holds, which you hand in as held_connections (read from the vault's names, each { connection_id, fields }, never a value); a connection whose values the account holds and that has no record yet is listed from what its held names say (its id, service and vendor), its other facts left out as unknown. Reads only; it reads no store itself, keeps nothing and writes no row; it connects, checks and sends nothing, and shows no secret.

values.title: List email sending domains
values.job: See which domains my email-sending account can send from and whether each is verified
values.description: Reads the domains of the person's connected email-sending account (Resend) with the key they connected, and answers each domain's name and status and how many there are. It never shows the key and sends no email.

values.title: List ended Stripe subscriptions
values.job: List every Stripe subscription that ended since a time, so each customer record can be marked ended once
values.description: Give ended_after_unix. Returns each ended subscription oldest first (subscription id, when it ended, its metadata) and complete. Uses the Stripe key of the seller connection that seller_connection names (service_connection:stripe is your own).

values.title: List everything I can connect, services and my computer's places together
values.job: Show every service I can connect to Trillion and every place on my own computer it can read (notes, voice memos, messages, photos, downloads), in one list grouped by kind
values.description: One list of every connection a person can make: each service (how it connects: a key, a sign-in, or carried by their computer, with the steps for one carried) and each place on their own computer (what it arrives as, and the switch it needs). Optionally give category (one group, such as Messages or Pictures) and looked, the answer of tool:look-for-the-places-on-this-computer, so each place says whether it is on the computer (found, needs_switch, could_not_check, not_here); without it a place is not_looked. Reads rows only: it connects, looks at and sends nothing, and shows no secret. Returns said and connections ({ id, kind: service | computer-place, label, category, how, ... }), sorted by category then label.

values.title: Ideas for what to ask an AI on a screen
values.job: Show the written ideas for what to ask an AI on one screen, each with the request a Do this for me button would hand over
values.description: Give screen (a screen key: calendar, marketplace, home, files, spaces and the others in workspace/examples.json). Answers heading, count_words, words (the strip's words) and examples, each { id, title, detail, do_this, from: 'written' }: the ideas written for that screen (or for the screen it reuses), do_this being the request an AI would be handed. It reads only workspace/examples.json and writes nothing. It never hands a request to an AI (the screen's Do this for me button is the app's), never adds published stories or ideas from the account's current tools (those need the person's account), and refuses a screen with no written row, naming the screens it has.

values.title: List drafts
values.job: List the person's drafts, one page at a time: each draft id with its message id and thread id. Read one with read-a-mail-draft.
values.description: List the person's drafts, one page at a time: each draft id with its message id and thread id. Read one with read-a-mail-draft. Takes provider (an id of read-data/mail-providers.json) and connection (the person's account of that provider, by its handle only: {connection_id}). Runs as that account with the key the person's vault holds for it; the engine hands the key to this run alone and it is placed only in the request to the provider's own host, never shown. Answers the provider-neutral rows of read-data/neutral.mjs, never the provider's own payload. A provider that does not offer it says so in words.

values.title: List my automations
values.job: Show everything my account does by itself on the signed-in page: each trigger, schedule and kept-running program with what sets it off in plain words, what it does, whether it is on, its last run and a switch, each workflow with the words of the conditions it fires on, and one of them opened as a when-then graph with the input of what it runs
values.description: Give wakes (the rows wake:list answers), optionally recipes (my workflow rows; fields kept as JSON text are read back), tools (descriptors of the tools the wakes run: id, label, input_schema) and open (an id the list gave). Returns automations (id, open_id, kind trigger|schedule|running, name, when, does, starts, enabled, state, red, last_run_at, last_problem, switch), workflows (workflow_id, label, job, steps, fires_when words, enabled) and counts of red, on and off; with open, that one automation or workflow: says, does, then, input_schema, last_run and graph {steps, edges}. Reads only; the switch is the engine's wake:switch.

values.title: List my connected accounts in Composio
values.job: Find which Composio account each connected app belongs to, and the user id that owns it, so a tool can run as that user
values.description: Asks Composio, with the vault's Composio key, for the connected accounts that key can see (of one app when a toolkit is named): each account's id, the user id that owns it, its app, alias and status. It reads only: nothing is created, changed or removed. The key goes only to Composio's own host and appears in no answer.

values.title: List my conversations newest first
values.job: List every conversation with AIs and in spaces newest first, found by words, participant or project, grouped Today, Yesterday, This Week and Older, as the messages screen's list shows them
values.description: Give conversations (rows of { recordId, sessionId, participantRef, lastActivityAt, title?, projectSlug?, projectName? }; other fields are kept as given) and optionally search (words matched, ignoring case, against title, sessionId, projectSlug and recordId), participant (a participantRef) and project (a projectName). The rows are sorted by lastActivityAt newest first, filtered and grouped by date with the Messages screen's own list helpers (show/build-chat-conversation-list.ts, run by Node's type stripping); groups follow the clock of the machine the run is on. Answers groups ([{ label, conversations }]), shown, total, and participants and projects (every one named across all rows, for the filters). Refuses conversations that is not a list and a row missing recordId, sessionId, participantRef or a readable lastActivityAt. Reads no records, keeps nothing and sends nothing: the screen itself (reading the person's conversations, transcripts and the composer that sends) is not part of this run.

values.title: List my recordings and media
values.job: List a person's recordings and the videos, sounds and pictures their tools made or they saved, newest first, each with what is known about it, as the Media screen shows a page
values.description: Give files ([{ name, identity, byte_length?, modified_at_ms? }], names starting with /), results kept about them ([{ identity, kind, value }]: kind library-entry makes a recording row from its value { name?, path?, media_kind? }; title, summary, organization, facts, transcript and the other kinds media-library.json joins add to a row), optionally set_aside (files or folders to delete first, as Recently Deleted does) and page ({ limit? (1 to 60), origin? (recording, made or file), unused? }). The files are named in the namespace (namespace-store.mjs, from tools/recently-deleted-and-storage) and the results laid in a namespace_results table as old trillion's namespace-results.mjs made it, in an in-memory SQLite database; then media-library.mjs's own mediaLibraryPage reads the page. Answers rows (identity, origin, name, path, media_kind, media_type, stored, captured_ms, title, duration, facts, edits, words), next_after, origin_labels and revision. A file that is not video, sound or a picture is no row, and a file set aside with no name left is none either. No bytes are held, so every row says stored: false; nothing is kept after the run, no file is written and nothing is sent. Refuses no files, a result without identity, kind and value, and what the page refuses. The screen also plays a row, suggests the next edit and searches for a spoken or seen moment; this run does none of that.

values.title: List my spaces and events
values.job: Show a person the spaces they count in now, and the events in them between two times, soonest first
values.description: Answers the spaces this person counts in now, with their type, and the events in those spaces: posts whose fields hold a starts_at, between from and to when given. Nothing is decided here: the member rows answer whether a person counts. It replaces the old community reader and my_events.

values.title: List my stays
values.job: List a person's own stays, inactive ones included, from their own database
values.description: Lists this person's own stays, newest first (up to 100), each with its title, city or area, price and whether it is active. Give database and person. Reads only the person's own stays; it does not read other people's.

values.title: List my YouTube videos
values.job: List the videos of the person's own YouTube channel, public, unlisted and private as the connection allows, with each video's title and privacy status
values.description: Lists the videos of the channel the person's youtube connection signs in as, from the channel's uploads playlist (give the playlist_id that tool:check-a-connection returns for place youtube), page by page. Each video comes back with its id, title, privacy status (public, unlisted or private) and publish time; unlisted and private videos come back when the sign-in has read access to the channel, and a refusal means it does not. It posts nothing and changes nothing.

values.title: List mail that arrived since a point
values.job: List the mail that reached the inbox since a point in its history (since: the cursor find-my-mailbox or an earlier list-new-mail answered).
values.description: List the mail that reached the inbox since a point in its history (since: the cursor find-my-mailbox or an earlier list-new-mail answered). Takes provider (an id of read-data/mail-providers.json) and connection (the person's account of that provider, by its handle only: {connection_id}). Runs as that account with the key the person's vault holds for it; the engine hands the key to this run alone and it is placed only in the request to the provider's own host, never shown. Answers the provider-neutral rows of read-data/neutral.mjs, never the provider's own payload. A provider that does not offer it says so in words.

values.title: Paired senders and waiting codes
values.job: List which senders are paired and which pairing codes are waiting, for one source or all
values.description: Optional source_id narrows to one source. With source_id and sender, also answers is_paired for that sender. Returns waiting [{ source_id, sender, code, expires_at }] (expired codes left out) and paired [{ source_id, sender, paired_at }]. It changes nothing. It reaches no database: give the pairing facts the person keeps as facts, and keep what the answer's keep lists.

values.title: Where a post can go
values.job: List the accounts this person can post to, each ready or not and why, and each place they have no account for yet
values.description: Reads the person's connection records handed in as `records`. Returns destinations: each account_id (the connection id), platform, label, name and ready, with said when it is not ready (a field the place needs that the connection lacks); not_connected: each place with no account yet; and said. Use the account_id values as tool:draft-a-post destinations. It changes nothing.

values.title: List public prediction markets
values.job: See which prediction markets are open right now, what each asks, its outcomes, their prices and its trading volume
values.description: Reads the public prediction-market list (no account, no key) and gives each market's question, outcomes, outcome prices (the market's own odds), outcome token ids, volume, liquidity, whether it is open and when it ends. The busiest markets come first. Give limit (1 to 100, default 20). The answer's status says live or error with the HTTP status; an error returns no markets and never invented ones. Use a market's token id with tool:read-prediction-market-order-book.

values.title: Programs running on my computer
values.job: List the programs running on this person's computer and how much memory each one uses, the largest first, optionally only the programs whose name has some words
values.description: Runs on the person's computer with the right they granted it to see the programs running there. Returns total, programs (each with pid, name, footprint_bytes and resident_bytes, parent_pid, session_id, started_at_ms and cpu_ms, the processor time it has used; null for what the person may not read; and command, its command line, when commands is true) and complete (false when the list was cut at `most`).

values.title: List the addresses a mailbox sends as
values.job: List the addresses the mailbox can send as, each with whether it is the primary one and the signature the provider holds for it (null when the provider holds none).
values.description: List the addresses the mailbox can send as, each with whether it is the primary one and the signature the provider holds for it (null when the provider holds none). Takes provider (an id of read-data/mail-providers.json) and connection (the person's account of that provider, by its handle only: {connection_id}). Runs as that account with the key the person's vault holds for it; the engine hands the key to this run alone and it is placed only in the request to the provider's own host, never shown. Answers the provider-neutral rows of read-data/neutral.mjs, never the provider's own payload. A provider that does not offer it says so in words.

values.title: List sending keys
values.job: See the keys my email-sending account has: each one's id, name and when it was made
values.description: Lists the keys of the person's email-sending account (Resend), with the key they connected: each key's id, name and when it was made, never a key itself (the provider shows a key only once, when it is made). It only reads.

values.title: List tasks and what blocks them
values.job: Read the facts kept about tasks into one entry per task, and see for each task what it blocks
values.description: Takes the facts about tasks, one row per fact ({ subject_id, property_id, value }, the property named like prop:task:title). Returns one entry per task with its number, title, project, status (default pending), priority (default MEDIUM), objective, acceptance criteria, what blocks it, what it blocks (worked out from what blocks the others), attachments (opaque references, never followed) and dates.

values.title: List the conversation sources on this computer
values.job: Find every app's conversations on this computer (AI chat exports, Google Takeout activity, and the sessions local AI apps keep) and say how many files of each there are
values.description: Runs on the person's computer over the folder they granted it to read (their home folder), and reads only inside it. For each kind of source (read-data/conversation-sources-on-this-computer.json: ChatGPT, Claude.ai and Grok account exports, Google Takeout activity for Gemini Apps, Assistant and AI Mode, and the sessions of Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Hermes) it answers how many files are here, their bytes and the first of them. more_places adds folders to look for exports in. Keeps nothing and reaches no records.

values.title: List the courses a learner is on
values.job: Show the learner their courses as a list: each course, how many lessons are done, and each lesson complete, active or locked. Opening a lesson opens it in the lesson screen.
values.description: Give the courses (each with its id, title, about and lessons with id, title and body) and the lessons this learner has finished as { course_id, lesson_id }. Returns each course with how many lessons are done, and each lesson with its status: complete when done, active for the first lesson not done, locked for the rest. Nothing is read or written here; the course list screen runs the same read in the page.

values.title: List the Facebook Pages a sign-in reaches
values.job: Read which Facebook Pages the connection's sign-in manages, keeping each Page's own token sealed in the vault
values.description: The facebook-messenger descriptor's acquire.choose.list: GET graph.facebook.com/v23.0/me/accounts (id and name only, at most 100 Pages) with the connection's user token, placed from the vault only as the request leaves. The answer is each Page's id and name; no Page token is read or kept here. Run by tool:connect-an-account-by-signing-in-to-the-service at the sign-in callback, which connects the Page the person named beforehand (or the only one reached) and then runs tool:keep-a-facebook-pages-token for it.

values.title: List the file formats an export can be written in
values.job: Show every format a document can be exported to, with its file ending, its media type and the block kinds it writes itself
values.description: Takes nothing. Answers formats: one row each with id, label, extension, mime and draws (the block kinds the format writes itself; the others are written as tables or refused), and finished_by when a page must do the last step (png). The ids are what tool:export-a-document-to-a-file takes as format.

values.title: List the items in a list saved on your computer (runs on your computer)
values.job: Read a list the person saved in a file (bookmarks, a source list, an exported set of rows, a browser's saved tabs) into items to research
values.description: Runs on the person's own computer and reads one JSON file: an array of rows, or an object holding rows under sources, bookmarks, items, records, rows or data (shape list, the default), or the sidebar file of the Arc browser (--shape browser-sidebar: pinned and current tabs of its default profile with their folders; an address that looks like an account, admin or sign-in page, or carries a token, is kept as Private page with no address). Each row becomes an item with item_id, title, url, published, description, source_family, source_type, container_path, license_status (unknown when the row says nothing) and lifecycle_status; at most 5000 (--limit cuts it). Nothing leaves the computer.

values.title: Kinds of conversation export I can read
values.job: List the kinds of conversation export that can be read (chat apps, email, the Messages database, AI assistant logs, captured web chats), what each one's files look like and what the run must say for it
values.description: Returns said (the count and the ids, in a line) and sources: each { id, label, format, reader, needs, app, files_look_like }. id is what source takes in tool:read-an-export-of-my-conversations; needs lists the choices the run must make for that kind (mailbox_address for mail, expected_provider for a captured web chat); app is the name its conversations are kept under; files_look_like is what a file of that kind holds, which is how a file is matched to its kind when none is named. A kind not listed is a new row in a file of the person's own.

values.title: List the latest items of a feed
values.job: Get the latest posts, videos or episodes of a creator or a topic from their Atom or RSS feed
values.description: Reads one public Atom or RSS feed (at most 2 MB, 15 seconds) and returns its title (source) and its items, each with an item_id (the id the feed gives it, else its link), title, published, url and description. Give limit (1 to 200, 50 when left out) to cut the list. It reaches public sites only and does not sign in. The address of the feed is the person's own: this tool knows no creator and no site.

values.title: List where my video holds still longest (runs on your computer)
values.job: Show me where my video holds still the longest, and the second each of those holds starts, so I can find it and fix it
values.description: Reads a video with the same frame-difference measure as tool:check-a-videos-motion-against-a-reference (every frame as a small grey picture; a frame moves when it or a neighbour changed by more than the still level and less than a cut) and lists its longest holds, longest first, each with its length and the second it starts. The still level is the one the person gives (for example a reference's still_threshold from the check, so the list matches what the check counted) or, left out, the one read from this video. The person can measure only the first seconds of the video (up to its end card) and say how many holds to list. It names no bar and judges nothing: it says where the stills are.

values.title: Make the spans file to grade from my edit plans (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn my edit plans into the list of recorded stretches whose speech should be graded, with their words and word times
values.description: Reads a folder of edit plans (JSON files with a segments list; a segment with a clip is a cut of that recording from one second to another, with the words said) and writes the spans file tool:grade-and-repair-speech-audio reads: each cut with its media file (the plan's sources, else the source the clip's word file names) and the words inside it, timed in source seconds from a whisper result for the clip when there is one, else from the clip's word file. It also lists each plan's span ids as groups, so the grade writes one grades file per plan as well. Segments that are not cuts of a recording (a generated voice line) are left out. The plans, word files and recordings are only read. It runs on the person's own computer, never on Trillion.

values.title: List the videos a site plays
values.job: List video files, streams and frame addresses across a public site
values.description: Source-first port of the original site-media crawler. Opens at most 25 same-origin pages in Chromium, scrolls each ten times, records video requests and video/source/iframe addresses. Returns unique video addresses, visited pages and pages left by the bound. Does not sign in. Frames are reported as addresses, without claiming every frame is a player.

values.title: List the tours waiting to show
values.job: Show me the tours waiting to start by themselves, and which my show rules are holding
values.description: Every tour that would start by itself on an event (opening Trillion, by default), with the facts your show rules decide it over (reason, urgency, hours since one like it) and how your show-rules record leaves it now: held, the rules holding it (held_by) and until when. The same trigger choice, facts and rules the tour host asks before it starts one, so this list and what shows agree. Give own_tours, progress and show_rules (the values of your tour records and your show-rules record, read from the store that holds them; each left out when you have none). It changes and keeps nothing.

values.title: List every caption line a character says, with the second it starts (runs on your computer)
values.job: List every caption line spoken inside a character's turns, with the video and second, for quoting
values.description: Reads every <data_folder>/voice/<id>.turns.json (find-when-a-character-speaks) and the video's captions (the first of <youtube_folder>/captions or videos/<id>.en.json3, .en-orig.json3, .en*.json3, then <data_folder>/../raw/<id>.en.json3); a caption line counts when at least half of it lies inside a turn. Writes <data_folder>/character-lines.tsv (id, date, format, second, turn, text). Lines are auto-captions: the spelling is YouTube's.

values.title: List what is due for review
values.job: See which of the things a person is learning are due for review now, soonest first, from the grades they have given them
values.description: Give the items being learned (each with an id and optional text; anything else on an item is handed back), the grades given so far (the item id, the grade word and when) and the person's own spacing policy. Each item's due time is folded from its grades, oldest first, so the grades are the only record and the queue cannot drift from them. Returns every item with whether it is due now, when it is next due, its state to keep, how many grades went into it and how many of them lapsed (lapse_count). Items never reviewed are due at once. Due items come first, soonest due first, then by text and id. Pass learner to count only that person's grades. The policy may be given as policy or found among rows by policy_kind. There is no default policy: a missing policy or field is refused with its name.

values.title: List what my AIs did
values.job: Turn the tool calls an AI made on a person's account into the activity rows the AI activity screen lists: what it did, the item it made or touched, whether it worked and why not, newest first
values.description: Give calls ([{ tool, at, input?, result?, error?, app?, description? }]), one tool call each in the order they happened. Each becomes the row activity.mjs's activityRow makes from activity-marks.json (a call whose tool has no mark leaves a row only with an execution receipt or work it was done for), is read through recordableActivityRow and keptActivityRow (access, the person's access names, decides which linked ids are kept), and is kept with keepActivity in an in-memory SQLite database laid out by activityTable. Then readActivity reads them back newest first (read: { limit?, app?, failed? }). Answers kept, left (each call that left no row, and why), items (seq, at, app, tool, label, item, title, uses, for, ok, reason), next_before and coverage. Nothing is kept after the run, no file is written and nothing is sent. Refuses no calls, more than 50 calls, and a call without a tool or an at. The screen also traces one item through the calls that made and used it and draws each app by its sign-in picture; this run does neither.

values.title: List the workspace tours
values.job: Show me every tour in my workspace and which ones I have finished
values.description: Given the tours your AIs wrote (own_tours, the value of guided-overlay::own-walkthroughs) and your tour progress (progress), both read from the store that holds them, and the app's own tours when the caller passes them as tours, answers each tour in its order: tour_id, title, summary, steps, finished, the event that starts it by name (start_event), when the change it shows landed (changed_at) and whether it is one of your own. It changes and keeps nothing.

values.title: Writing recipes and instruction blocks
values.job: List the ready writing recipes (summarize, translate, rewrite, critique and more) and the instruction blocks a recipe can use
values.description: Give words (every word must be in a recipe's or block's id or label) and section to narrow the list, or nothing for all. Returns recipes, each with id, label, section, needs (the work item fields it must have) and fields (the answers it asks for, with choices and defaults), blocks (id, label, body) and sections. Use a recipe's id as recipe_id in tool:compose-a-writing-instruction.

values.title: Listen
values.job: Turn listening on or off on this person's computer, or say whether it is on: while on, everything said near the computer is heard, split into moments, each part named by who said it, and sent to the person's AIs as it is said
values.description: Runs on the person's computer. on true starts listening (macOS shows its microphone light the whole time), on false stops it, and no on only says how it is going: since when, pieces heard, turns sent and left out, the last one sent. Saying "stop listening" also turns it off. Each turn arrives as a message from its speaker in the moment's conversation (route Listening), so read_messages with speaker finds what someone said.

values.title: Listen to the microphone until a time, and tell me who said what
values.job: Listen in on a meeting or a room until a time I give, and tell me each person's turn
values.description: Records the microphone on this computer until `until`, hears each short piece of it on this computer with the Whisper model the person names, names each turn from the voices people enrolled (`voice_prints`: the person's voice-print rows, read by their AI; tool:enrol-a-voice-or-face; unknown voices keep the same number for the whole listening when the last answer's `voice_session` is handed back), and answers one heard row per turn: the listening, the device, when it began and ended, the words, who said it, whether it is the person, the voice and how sure the match was. It keeps nothing: it reads no row of the person's and writes none, so the person's AI takes the `heard` rows from the answer and keeps them where it chooses. The sound never leaves this computer: pieces are kept in the run's own folder and deleted once heard, and only the words and the names are in the answer. It stops at `until` by itself and answers then; a run cancelled before that answers nothing, so the person's AI asks for the stretch it wants in `until`. Pause is real: while `listening_switch` says { on: false, since }, nothing said after `since` is kept, however far behind the hearing is, and the run ends at the first piece recorded after it. The person's own recording rules (`recording_rules`) are asked for every piece, over the facts in `recording_facts`; a piece recorded while they say blocked is let go unheard. `transcriber` ({ device, until }) says which device holds the hearing; a piece another device's live role covers is let go. Every answer lists what leaves this computer and what stays. The run lasts as long as `until` is from now, up to the row's longest run.

values.title: Listen to a generated voice take word by word (runs on your computer)
values.job: Find the words in a generated voice take that sound least real or most like a glitch
values.description: Asks the local listening package earshot, for every word of the take, how real the voice sounds and how well the word matches a glitch and the voice the person wants (described in their own words), then ranks each word against the take's own median so one odd word stands out. Writes one row per word. It runs on the person's own computer, never on Trillion.

values.title: Listen to music excerpts against my film's sections (runs on your computer)
values.job: Judge each music excerpt by ear against my film's section words and a reference stem
values.description: Per excerpt: per-section mood match against the film's section words (against alternatives), typicality against a reference music stem cut into its sections, realness and the top describe tags.

values.title: Rank sound effects in folders by ear and find each one's cleanest trim (runs on your computer)
values.job: Rank my sound-effect folders against a description and find the cleanest trim of the best ones
values.description: Per category (folder, query, kind, top, alternatives: the person's CATEGORIES.json), earshot ranks the folder, finds the best segments of the top candidates, moves each trim edge outward in 5 ms steps until it is at or below -30 dB of the trim's peak, then describes, judges realness and measures that trim. Merges into OUT.json.

values.title: Look at my screen
values.job: See what is on the person's Mac screen right now: a picture of every display, the main one first, each with its size in pixels so an AI can point at an exact spot. Looks only when run; nothing is captured in the background or kept on the Mac. Says plainly when Screen Recording is off.
values.description: Runs on the person's own Mac. Asks the system whether Screen Recording is allowed and, if it is not, answers needs_access with the words that say what to turn on; nothing is captured. Otherwise it captures every display with the system's screen capture (the pointer too when `cursor` is true), shrinks each to at most `long_edge` pixels on its longest side, and answers one picture per display, the main display first, each with its width and height in pixels, its media type and its bytes as base64. The pictures are made smaller together until the whole answer fits what one run may return; the sizes in the answer are those of the pictures sent. The folder the pictures are made in is removed before the run ends, so nothing is kept on the Mac. The run needs the screen-recording capability granted to this tool.

values.title: See what is on the person's computer screen
values.job: Read the person's computer screen: the app in front (or one named), its controls from the accessibility tree and the text on its windows from the pixels, with where each is
values.description: Returns the app, the displays, and the things on the screen (role, label, centre and size, and the actions each offers) in points from the top left of the main display, never coordinates guessed from a picture. Text from the pixels is kept to the app's own windows. Read-only. Uses this Mac's existing Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions. The person can turn on an optional grant policy in their screen-driving settings folder; calls cannot change that policy.

values.title: Look for the places on my computer Trillion can read
values.job: Find which places on my computer (notes, voice memos, messages, mail, calendar, photos, downloads, AI apps, browsers) are there for Trillion to read, and which need a switch turned on first
values.description: One look under the folder the person granted for reading (their home folder), checking each place the computer's place rows list by whether it is there and whether it may be opened, never what it holds. Optionally give places (row ids, such as messages or downloads) to look at only those, and services ({ vendor, domains }: the services the account offers) so a browser's store of sites answers only which of those services it is used for, never a cookie's value. A place that is not there is left out; one this program may not open is needs_switch with the switch it needs (gate); a place outside the granted folder (an app in /Applications, a plugged-in drive) is could_not_check with the reason. Returns said, sources ({ id, label, category, state, detail?, gate? }) and browser_sites.

values.title: Look up a Stripe checkout
values.job: Read a Stripe checkout and the subscription it made: whether it was paid, who by, the metadata set when it began and the real recurring amount
values.description: Give provider_session_id. The amounts and status come from Stripe, not from the buyer browser, so a success redirect cannot forge them. Uses the Stripe key of the seller connection that seller_connection names (service_connection:stripe is your own).

values.title: Look up instruments at my live broker
values.job: Find the instruments my broker lists for trading, such as option contracts, from my live account
values.description: Give route (one broker route with mode "live" and its lookups), lookup (a lookup's name) and query (by the names the lookup allows; the lookup's own defaults fill the rest). A lookup is any read the broker answers: its listed instruments, the account (a lookup with one_item reads the one object as one item, for example equity and buying power) or the positions held. Answers the listed items the lookup keeps (for example only tradable ones), numbers read as numbers, sorted as the lookup says, with the next page token. An error answer carries no items. The held live-broker-credentials reach only the request.

values.title: Look up instruments at my paper broker
values.job: Find the instruments my broker lists for trading, such as option contracts, from my paper account
values.description: Give route (one broker route with mode "paper" and its lookups), lookup (a lookup's name) and query (by the names the lookup allows; the lookup's own defaults fill the rest). A lookup is any read the broker answers: its listed instruments, the account (a lookup with one_item reads the one object as one item, for example equity and buying power) or the positions held. Answers the listed items the lookup keeps (for example only tradable ones), numbers read as numbers, sorted as the lookup says, with the next page token. An error answer carries no items. The held paper-broker-credentials reach only the request.

values.title: Make a calendar invite
values.job: Make an invitation file that any mail client turns into a calendar event, or into a cancellation
values.description: Writes a standard calendar file (.ics): a request that creates or updates an event, or a cancel that removes it. The host is the organizer, so the host's own calendar shows it, and everyone else is an attendee. The same uid with a higher sequence updates the event. Times are instants, written in UTC. It sends nothing: attach the text to a message.

values.title: Make a contact sheet of pictures or video frames (runs on your computer)
values.job: Lay my pictures, or frames of my video at chosen times or at a steady rate, out as one labelled sheet so I can choose or check them by eye
values.description: Three kinds of sheet, each from one JSON request. pictures: the given pictures in a grid, each cell the same width and shape (16:9, any w:h, or the first picture's), each picture cut to the cell's middle or stretched into it, labelled below or above with its own words or its file name. frames-at-times: one frame of a video at each given time, or every 1/fps second between two times, stamped with its time, a set number to a row, split over several sheets when asked. frames-at-a-rate: ffmpeg's tile filter over a stretch of a video, frames at a steady rate stamped with their time or frame number, columns x rows a sheet, every sheet or only the first. Every size, colour, font and JPEG quality is a field of the request; nothing is kept between runs.

values.title: Make one picture of the frames of a short part of a video (runs on your computer)
values.job: Take a short part of a video, from a link or a file, and lay out one frame every few seconds on a single picture so I can see what happens in it
values.description: Cuts at most 300 seconds of a video and makes a contact sheet: one frame every `step` seconds (4 unless given), 320 pixels wide, `cols` frames to a row (4 unless given), as one JPEG. A link is fetched with yt-dlp, only that section, at 360p or less, into the folder's clips/ and used again on the next run; a video file on the computer is read directly from start to end. Every command and its output go to a log beside the sheet; a failure says which program failed with what exit code and shows the log's last lines. Each heavy program runs alone at the lowest priority (nice -n 20), so the computer stays usable.

values.title: Make a fresh-viewer review pack of a preview: contact sheets and a transcript (runs on your computer)
values.job: Make the contact sheets and the timed transcript a fresh viewer reviews a preview from
values.description: For one preview (the option's working preview unless the request names video): contact sheets of a frame every every_s seconds, per_sheet frames a sheet at width px (tool:make-a-contact-sheet-of-pictures-or-video-frames), and transcript.txt, a line per sentence led by its mm:ss, heard with the place's Whisper engine (tools/audio-transcription whisper_here; model and language from the settings), into work-round-<n>/review-pack/<id>/; a rules.txt already there is kept. The input of tool:check-a-rendered-video's fresh-viewer review.

values.title: Make a colour lookup table that fixes flat log footage from any camera (runs on your computer)
values.job: Make a LUT file so my flat, grey-looking log camera footage looks like normal colour
values.description: Writes a .cube 3D lookup table that maps a camera's log footage to display colour. The camera is not built in: the person passes a profile (a record of kind log-to-display-profile) holding the camera's log curve (a straight-line toe under a cut code, a log segment above it), its gamut matrix, luma weights, video range, the soft shoulder that rolls highlights off and the display gamma, with optional look settings (exposure, saturation, size, red and blue white-balance gains). The table expects the colours ffmpeg gives after it decodes limited-range video to full-range RGB, so it first undoes that expansion. Flags override the profile's settings. The same profile and settings always give the same file, byte for byte. Do not apply a table to footage from another camera or curve: it makes that footage washed out or blown out.

values.title: Make a searchable set of what my videos show (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn a folder of my videos into a set of picture vectors, one frame every few seconds with its time, so I can find moments by what they show
values.description: Reads every video in a folder the person names (only reads it) and keeps one frame every few seconds (2 by default), decoding key frames only, small, with an optional 3D LUT for log footage and an optional smaller proxy copy on the same timeline to decode instead. Each frame becomes a CLIP ViT-B-32 picture vector (OpenAI weights, the model tool:words-as-picture-vector uses for words, so they compare). Writes the two files of a vector set, frames.npy (float16, normalised) and frames.jsonl (video, path, t in seconds, the file decoded), with done.json so a run that stops goes on where it stopped and a new card adds only its videos, and vector-set.json: the vector_set member to put in the person's semantic-index-descriptor record so tool:search-everything-with-one-question can search it. It runs on the person's own computer, never on Trillion.

values.title: Give a job a short plain title
values.job: Give a piece of work a short plain title from its own words, so a person sees what it is at a glance
values.description: Give the job's words (job), and optionally the title someone already said (said) and the words to show when the job holds no sentence a person reads (fallback). A nonblank said is kept, trimmed. Otherwise the first sentence a person would read becomes the title: links keep their words, web addresses, folder paths, record ids, long hex ids and markdown marks are taken out, a leading 'Label:' is dropped, a sentence holding a program word (like list_items) or a short heading is skipped, the first letter is put in capitals and the title is cut at a word to at most 80 UTF-16 units with an ellipsis. Returns title and from (said, job or fallback).

values.title: Make a referral code
values.job: Make a referral code that earns what my referral reward rules give, and give back the event to save
values.description: Makes a short readable code (letters and digits, no I, L, O or U, so it survives being read aloud) or checks the one you chose, and gives back the event that makes it live once the person saves it. You say what the code points at: the sale attribute and the value it must have. A code may point only at an attribute one of the person's active referral reward rules (given in `rules`) names, because a code no rule applies to earns nothing; with no active rule it says to add one first. A code someone else already made stays theirs when the events are read. Nothing is kept by the tool.

values.title: Make a sales contract's terms, export request and approval link
values.job: Make the terms of an accepted sales contract ready to give out: what the buyer must accept, the terms as rows, the request that turns them into a PDF, Word, spreadsheet, Markdown or text file, and a link the buyer opens to accept
values.description: Give a contract (its name, currency, total in cents, customer, offer and a list of rules such as Commitment and GrantAccess) and which file forms you want (pdf, csv, xlsx, md, txt; all by default). Returns acceptance_requirements (always the terms; the payment obligation when a rule is a Commitment; the installment authorization when it has a payment schedule), terms_rows (the contract's facts and one row per rule, money in the locale you name, en-US by default), export_request (the document, the file stem and the format ids that tool:export-a-document-to-a-file turns into the files) and output_forms. With a base_url it also returns approval_link: a link that carries the whole request, so the buyer can open it on any computer and see the same contract. The forms a contract can be made in are the rows of data/contract-output-targets.json. Nothing here knows what is being sold, who the parties are or what anything costs.

values.title: Make a sending key
values.job: Make a new key that can only send email from my email-sending account, kept under its own name
values.description: Asks the person's email-sending account (Resend), with the key they connected, for a new key that may only send email (from one domain when domain_id names one), and keeps the new key in the person's vault under keep_as. The new key is never shown: the answer holds its id and the held word in its place. A keep_as already held is never replaced, and then nothing is asked. Give the new key's name as Resend should show it.

values.title: Make a sound-effect palette from trimmed sources and read each sound back (runs on your computer)
values.job: Render my sound-effect palette from its sources and trims, and check each finished sound by ear
values.description: Each sound of PALETTE.json: decode its source at the palette's rate and channels, cut the trim, fade in and out, scale to the sample peak, write 24-bit WAV; then earshot reads the final file (match z, describe, realness, measure) into palette_readings.json.

values.title: Make a searchable set from picture vectors another program kept (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn picture vectors my programs already kept (an asset index of CLIP matrices, a folder of timed frames, an app's results store) into sets I can search by what the pictures show
values.description: Reads, only reading, the stores the person names: an asset index of CLIP matrices (video frames with no time, images, and readable names from assets.jsonl), a folder of timed frames (frames.npy and frames.jsonl), and an app's SQLite results store of timed frames (base64 float16 vectors, each item's path from its library entries), with the id a namespace store keeps each of those videos under. Each store becomes its own set in --out: items.jsonl (path, kind, t or null, and name, or id and b2), vectors.npy (float32 source-compute precision: assets and app results normalized once as the source did, kept timed frames unchanged) and vector-set.json, the vector_set member of a semantic-index-descriptor record with points_to.carry naming the extra fields. Last line: {"result": {"sets": {name: items}}} or {"error": ...}.

values.title: Send only what changed in an answer
values.job: Turn the next JSON answer a screen will read into just the changes from the answer it already holds, when that is smaller
values.description: Give previous and next, each the JSON text of one answer. Returns the next answer as { status, content_type, identity, patch: { from, to, ops } } (ops are RFC 6902 add, remove and replace; from and to are the BLAKE3 identities of the canonical JSON before and after) when the patch is under 0.6 of the whole; otherwise the whole answer with its text (and its identity). An answer under 2000 or over 400000 characters, or one that is not JSON, is answered whole without an identity. Text that is not a string is refused.

values.title: Turn something I made or copied into a word-for-word template (runs on your computer)
values.job: Keep the exact words of a script, post, slide set or page as a template where only the specifics (numbers, names, the product) can change
