values.description: Reads a spec (sources, lines, slots with their rule, keeps with their reason) or one bare measurement it recognises (a word-timed transcript, a caption file, a post, a table of units, a folder of images) and writes a template: every word and every other measured value of the piece, each marked KEEP, with only the author's own specifics marked SLOT, each slot naming the rule that made it one. Works for any medium the registry lists (spoken scripts, posts, threads, slides, articles, newsletters, pages, audio). Writes TEMPLATE.json and a readable TEMPLATE.md beside it with the slot table, every region, and the dimensions it could not measure with the reason and how they would be measured.

values.title: Make a working preview of a stitched opening with ffmpeg (runs on your computer)
values.job: Make a quick working preview of a stitched opening from a render of my cut, to judge its timing and sound while FilmCraft cannot export
values.description: For an option whose spec stitches an opening (edit.prepend, an optional hold at 0:00, the overlay at 0:00): cuts the same frame-snapped ranges, in the same order, out of a render of the person's cut with ffmpeg, holds the first frame for the hold, mutes the cut's sound where edit.a1_mute says, lays the overlay and its sound over it and masters the sound the way the real export is mastered. Not the delivered preview (no grade layer): it goes to work-round-<n>/working/ and is never published.

values.title: Make every A/B take of one narration line, master them the same way and measure them (runs on your Mac)
values.job: Make my narration line in every voice model I am comparing, mastered the same way, and measure them all
values.description: Runs the takes the settings list (Kokoro voices and clone engines) one heavy job at a time, puts each through the same clean and master commands, moves a take already there into work/replaced/ before making it again, runs the ticks command, and measures every take into <out dir>/work/measure-final.jsonl.

values.title: Make examples from the options a person picked
values.job: Make labelled examples for calibrating a small model from which options of a piece a person picked or rejected, and the lines they named
values.description: Give films (each piece: name, gate (its pick settings: picked_verdicts and pick_labels with spec_globs using {option}, and optionally words, exclude, rejected_lines, text_keys, spoken_lead_s), decisions (its pick rows: option_id, verdict, lines, reason_verbatim; the last row of an option governs), files (the piece's file paths) and units ({ <spec path>: [{ text, kind, context }] }, the lines of each spec read so far)), and optionally rulings with real and needs (a text ruled directly is left out: the ruling wins), bad_label and rejected (the pattern a rejecting verdict matches, default ^rejected). Units of a picked option are good except the lines its row names; a rejection labels bad only the lines it names. Returns items, left_out (excluded, ruled_directly, both_labels, no_spec, several_specs) and units_needed: the specs whose lines to read and send again. Any of these may come from settings_record, the person's setting for this tool (their row of list:settings as the person's store gives it, read by tools/settings); the input's own fields win. It writes nothing.

values.title: Make examples from rulings on lines
values.job: Make labelled examples for calibrating a small model from the rulings a person gave on lines of copy, and from lines they said themselves
values.description: Give rulings (the person's ruling rows of list:checks, type record:check with id prefix record:check:ruling-, as records or values), real (who counts), needs (fields a ruling must carry to count), and optionally speech (lines they said, each with sets), speech_set, exclude (lists of lines a model was trained on), bad_label (the label a bad example carries in bad_for), contexts ({ text: context }) and verdicts ({ bad, good }). Returns items ({ text, good, bad_for, split, source: ruling or speech, context }) and left_out (texts ruled both ways, texts in exclude). Only rulings by the people in real count. Any of these may come from settings_record, the person's setting for this tool (their row of list:settings as the person's store gives it, read by tools/settings); the input's own fields win. It writes nothing.

values.title: Make labelled examples from where a person stands
values.job: Turn the verdicts a person already gave into good and bad examples, to tune a model that answers their reading rules
values.description: Give the person's rule document (verdict_rules) and their stands. Every thing of a reading row's kinds whose current stand is their exact agree is a good example; a stand a reading row names in pairs[].rejected is a bad example for that row. A pair naming no current exact stand is refused.

values.title: Make Marketplace tiles with their icons (runs on your computer)
values.job: Make tiles of my Marketplace tools and workflows, each with its own icon drawn, for a page or a film to show
values.description: Reads the tools and workflows as the shelf's readers answer them (two JSON files of { items: [{ id, kind, title, job, steps?, icon? }] }) and the icons folder of an installed lucide-react, and answers one tile per item: id, kind, title, job (cut to 90 characters), steps, icon and svg, the icon's own shape elements (the item's icon, else its kind's icon from marketplace-kinds.json; an alias icon file is followed). Titles that read as machine names are left out. With --out it writes window.<global>=<tiles>; for a page (global TILES unless --global names another). The icon files are read as data, never run. Last line: {"result": {tiles, counts}} or {"error": ...}.

values.title: Make the plain-text copy of every source my claims cite, from the files I saved (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn every source I saved for fact checking (a web page, a FoodData Central food, an edit plan, a text) into the plain text my claims are checked against
values.description: Reads a sources file ({"sources": {id: {raw, extract, text}}}) and writes each source's plain-text extract beside it: html (scripts and styles dropped, tags removed, entities decoded, spaces joined), fdc-json (a FoodData Central food as one line per nutrient amount per 100 g), new-order (an edit plan's new_order rows as one line each) or copy. A kind made by its own tool (a word-timed transcript, a text) keeps its extract and is refused when it is missing. Run it after adding or re-fetching a source; tool:check-every-claim-against-its-facts-and-sources checks quotes against these extracts.

values.title: Make quiz questions from text
values.job: Make fill-in-the-blank quiz questions from a piece of text, such as notes, a lesson or an article
values.description: Splits the text into sentences and turns each into a question by blanking its most telling word, with the answer kept beside it; a sentence with no such word becomes a recall prompt. The same text always gives the same questions with the same ids, ready to ask with the form tools.

values.title: Make the candidates of a spoken line, one slot varying at a time (runs on your computer)
values.job: Make candidate versions of a spoken line where each slot's other options are tried one at a time against my base picks, each with its script, shot file and a claim for every sentence
values.description: From a request of slots (each with a base pick and candidates, each candidate with the words it adds and the claim it makes) and sentence templates ({SLOT} where a slot's words go), writes the base variant, then every other candidate of each slot with all other slots at their base pick. Each variant gets a script line, a shot file naming that script and a claims file with one entry per sentence taken from the candidate that formed the sentence (a sentence whose filled words are empty is left out with its claim), plus a manifest of the variants and a list of their lines. A picked candidate that has words but no claim is refused. The words, claims, ids and file shapes are the person's own and come in the request (one file, or several laid over each other key by key); the tool names no film, speaker or claim.

values.title: Make the decision
values.job: Record what my AI decided, why, what to do next and how we will know it worked
values.description: Once every row of the decision's method has an answer: decision is { option_id (one of the options), reason, next_action, success_measure, evidence_refs, move?, and every decision field the decision asks for }. A decided decision changes only after a failed result: the decision it had moves to decision_history. Returns what to do now and how to say it.

values.title: Make a tracked link
values.job: Make a tracked link with UTM fields for a post, ad, email or bio, so visits and sales can be traced to it
values.description: Adds the project, source and campaign (and optionally the medium and a content tag for one post) to a web address as UTM fields, replacing any already there. Refuses an address that is not a web page or carries a user name or password. Use the same project, source and campaign names when breaking visits down later.

values.title: Make the planned public playlists on YouTube (runs on your Mac)
values.job: Make the YouTube playlists my Watch Later sort plan names, adding videos and removing none
values.description: Creates each playlist of a plan from tool:plan-sorting-youtube-watch-later-into-playlists as a public playlist on the same channel, with its description, and adds its videos in batches. It never removes a video and never changes Watch Later. A playlist already on the channel with the same title is reused, never duplicated. What was made is kept in applied_file and each playlist is read back before adding, so running it again adds only what is missing; a recorded playlist that reads back empty stops the run, so a lost sign-in cannot add videos twice. Then verify_sort.py checks each playlist holds the planned number of videos and anyone can see it, that each Watch Later is unchanged, and writes verification.json, INDEX.md and a table of every Watch Later video with its playlists.

values.title: Set up an AI harness on a computer
values.job: Inspect, apply or remove the account's hooks for one chosen AI harness on an exact owned computer
values.description: Runs the shared signed-app harness installer on the exact recorded computer. Inspect is observational; apply and remove require authorization. Preserves other settings, disabled hooks, managed policies, models and permissions. A configured hook is not evidence of execution. Codex trust requires explicit review of all current definition hashes and refuses changed definitions before writing. Returns the original typed report with computer attribution. Requires the installed computer host to advertise this tool and its exact computer scope; old or offline hosts remain unavailable. No shell, arbitrary module, download, model launch or personal-file import can be selected. After apply, run inspect again to obtain current evidence.

values.title: Manage my API descriptions
values.job: List the API descriptions my tools come from, add one for my account, edit it or remove it
values.description: An empty request lists current default sources and this account's own sources. Change one source with add, edit or remove and keep the same request_key when retrying it. Your source definition stays in this account's original tool-source record; edits keep its added_at and removal keeps a tombstone. Defaults come only from the native task's current source configuration. Source reads still pending are named as pending. Connection fields are references, never keys or tokens. This manages source definitions; it does not sign in to a service, fetch a tool list, or grant permission to execute its tools. An unavailable native source owner refuses without writing.

values.title: Manage usage pricing
values.job: Read, list, set, supersede, retire or delete my resource pricing rules, with effective dates, resource, plan and client overrides, without changing purchased terms
values.description: Read or list my resource pricing rules from the rows the caller hands in, or save, retire or delete a rule as its next immutable version. The answer holds the rows to keep (the rule head, its new version row and the receipt row): the caller writes them in its own store, in one transaction, while the head is still at the version it read. With action list and versions true it pages the rule versions it was given, the rules price-resource-usage takes as input. Purchased terms are never changed. Keeps nothing itself.

values.title: Map an app's screens and controls
values.job: Find the screens of my app and what a person can do on each, so journeys can be written to check it
values.description: Opens the app at app_url in a headless Chromium on the person's own computer and follows its links within the same origin, at most most_screens screens (20 at most). For each screen: its address, title, headings, the same-origin links, every visible control with its role and accessible name, the actions it offers as `do` objects ready to paste into a journey for tool:walk-through-an-app-like-its-users, a picture, and the console errors and failed requests seen while it loaded. not_opened lists links that were found but not opened.

values.title: Match a video's colour to another
values.job: Make one video's colours match another video's, so clips from different cameras or light look like one shoot
values.description: Measures the colour of both videos (this one at its start, the other at match_at seconds) and shifts this video's colours to match, then saves the new video in your files at its own size and length.

values.title: Match rows from two places
values.job: Pair rows from two places that describe the same thing: a bank or card line and its receipt, both sides of a transfer between accounts, a payment and the invoices it paid, a statement line and a bookkeeping row, a calendar event and a timesheet entry. You say which fields to compare (amounts, dates, words, exact values), how close counts and how much each matters. Returns confident matches, suggestions with their alternatives and why, and what is left unmatched on each side. Never auto-confirms when two candidates are nearly as good. Changes nothing; write the pairs you accept.
values.description: Every left row is scored against every right row, field by field: a number agrees by being the same (or the same ignoring sign, or the mirror image, as the field says) within its tolerance; a date by being within its tolerance in days; words by the share of the smaller side's words they have in common (the rules' ignore_words never count); `same` by equal text ignoring case and spaces. A field marked required that disagrees or is missing on one side rules the pair out. A pair's confidence is the weighted share of the fields' scores. A pair at or above `confirm_at` is matched only when no other unused row is within the rules' `clear_lead` of it for either side; otherwise, and for pairs between `suggest_at` and `confirm_at`, it is suggested with up to the rules' `alternatives` other candidates. Each row is used once (`one_to_one`), or each right row goes to its best left row (`many_to_one`, many bills for one payment). Pairs in `already` are kept and their rows are not offered again. Each pair carries the reason for every field. With no `fields` the rules' defaults compare amount (ignoring sign, weighted most and required), date and description. A row without an id, or two rows on one side with the same id, is refused by name.

values.title: May this spend go ahead
values.job: Just before my AI pays, check that the spend still holds its one current budget reservation
values.description: Reads the latest budget check and the reservation for one operation and answers available only when the check approved this operation, idempotency key and spend authority, has not expired, and exactly one current reservation matches it. Answers the reason, the reserved amount in whole cents and the reservation's fencing token. It changes nothing.

values.title: Measure how much of a checklist is done
values.job: See how much of a packing list or other checklist is done and group its items, for example by category
values.description: Give the items (id, status, and optionally group) and which statuses mean done and which statuses leave the count (an item no longer needed). Returns how many counted items are done, how many are counted, the share done (0 when nothing is counted), and the items grouped by their group with a count and a done count for each. An item with no group goes under ungrouped_label (default uncategorized). Both status lists must be given, and may be empty. An item with no id is refused. Optionally give containers (id, label, parent) and name each item's container: the answer then holds container_paths, each item's bag path from the outermost bag in. Optionally give what an item waits on, as depends_on (item ids) on the item or as a dependencies list of { item, depends_on, reason }: the answer then holds blocked, each not-done item that waits on something not done, with what it waits on and the reasons. A thing waited on that is not in the list counts as not done. Without these the answer is unchanged.

values.title: Measure a reference video into frame sheets, a cut scan, its motion rhythm and a sound timeline (runs on your computer)
values.job: Measure a video I want to learn from: its probe, a frame a second, the first five seconds closely, where it cuts, how it moves and what is heard, as files I can review
values.description: Runs the programs the person names (hf-media for frame sheets and the cut scan, a motion-rhythm script, a Python with earshot for the sound timeline, ffprobe) over one video into a new folder, checking every program before any media work. A film longer than 120 seconds gets small labelled review pages instead of one contact sheet. It records evidence; it does not certify viewing or meaning. Answers one JSON line.

values.title: Measure what ad spend brings back (CAC, LTV, payback)
values.job: Measure return on ad spend per source, campaign or keyword: cost per sign-up, CAC, customer lifetime value, LTV to CAC ratio and payback months, flagging what meets 5x
values.description: Joins ad spend with the visitors each source, campaign or keyword brought (first touch, the same counting as the visits breakdown), their sign-ups, paying customers and revenue. Spend is given as rows ({ amount, source or utm_campaign or utm_term: value }) or as the answers of the Meta Ads and Google Ads spend tools (spend_answers with shape meta-ads-campaign-spend, google-ads-campaign-spend or google-ads-keyword-spend), whose campaign names fill utm_campaign and campaign ids utm_id. Each row and the paid and all-visitor totals give spend, visitors, sign-ups, customers, revenue, cost per sign-up, CAC, revenue per customer per month, LTV (needs gross_margin and monthly_churn or customer_lifetime_months), LTV:CAC, payback months and whether LTV:CAC meets the target (5x unless target_ltv_to_cac says). Payment values are the revenue of revenue_months months (1 when left out). A figure the numbers cannot give is null and unknown says what would give it. Spend in another currency than the project is refused.

values.title: Measure how fast a video starts
values.job: Measure how fast a video that is read by byte ranges starts and seeks for a real browser: first frame, Play to a moving frame, seek and bytes fetched, fresh and returning, against the speed the old files path set
values.description: Give url (the address of a video a browser can play by Range: a share link, a file's byte route) and optionally samples (1 to 20, default 3), seek_fraction (default 0.6), timeout_ms and browser_path. Opens a real Chromium on this computer, plays the video in a blank page and answers per-sample first_frame_seconds, play_to_moving_seconds, seek_seconds, bytes and responses for a fresh visit and a returning one, their medians, and each median against the bar (warm first frame 2.9 s, cold 5.9 s, 17 MB, seek 204 ms) with within true, false or null when a number was not measured. The address is never answered (a share's key is in it); the answer names the host.

values.title: Measure funnel stages
values.job: Count how many visitors reached each stage of a funnel, how many converted and the revenue each stage brought
values.description: Reads the facts a person recorded (one per visit or per sale) and counts, for each stage you list, the visits, the conversions, the conversion rate to one decimal and the revenue in cents. You say which field of a fact holds the stage and which holds the amount; a fact is a conversion when it is marked converted or carries an amount. Facts that name none of your stages are counted separately, not hidden. It reads and counts only.

values.title: Measure how a video stages a character's turns: cuts, shot lengths and music stop-downs (runs on your computer)
values.job: Measure how a video is cut and scored around a character's turns: whether a cut lands on the turn, how short the shots are inside the exchanges, and whether the music stops just before
values.description: For each id: from <youtube_folder>/measure/<id>/rhythm.json (shots) and earshot-timeline.txt (GAP drop lines) and <data_folder>/voice/<id>.turns.json: the share of turns with a picture cut within 0.5 s of their start against chance, the median shot inside the character's exchanges (turns within 8 s, padded 2 s) against elsewhere, and the share of turns with a music stop-down in the 2 s before against chance. Adds or updates one row per id in <data_folder>/staging.tsv.

values.title: Measure a video's loudness
values.job: Measure how loud a video or recording is and whether it is ready to publish
values.description: Measures integrated loudness (LUFS), loudness range and true peak, and says whether it meets the target (-14 LUFS by default) without clipping.

values.title: Measure narration takes: pace, pauses, pitch, words heard, same voice and accent (runs on your computer)
values.job: Measure my narration takes side by side so I can compare voice models with numbers as well as my ear
values.description: For each take of one line: every pause of 120 ms or more (10 ms RMS below -45 dBFS) with the words on each side, words per second over the speech and over voiced time only, F0 5th-95th percentile and span in semitones, onset F2 and length of one vowel_check word, the words whisper heard and the word errors against the script, the cosine of a WeSpeaker speaker embedding to the line's voice_reference take, and the mean accent probability from a wav2vec2 accent classifier. Writes each take's word times to <words dir>/<take>.words.json. Every level, model and length is a setting.

values.title: Measure exact page citations across planned questions and answer engines
values.job: Compare every planned page × question × answer engine cell against recorded answer observations, keeping exact page citations, unavailable answers and unasked cells distinct
values.description: Builds the complete page × question × engine matrix from a plan and supplied observations. A citation counts only when its parsed HTTP(S) URL exactly matches the page URL, its supplied checked canonical URL, or an explicitly supplied verified redirect URL; a path prefix is never enough. Query strings remain significant and fragments are ignored. Original answers and citation links are preserved. Missing/not-run and unavailable cells stay unknown; only an observed answer with an explicit citations array can be cited or not cited. This tool measures supplied observations and does not query engines, establish who observed them, or prove why an engine cited a page.

values.title: Measure source-piece instruction coverage
values.job: Report exact uncovered source pieces, stale provenance and broken links in caller-supplied source, piece and instruction readbacks
values.description: Pure structural coverage. Every current source piece needs a structurally explicit linked step or a nonblank source-pinned no_check reason. Returns every gap by source/piece/step. Preserves original BLAKE3 identities and separately checks exact piece text. Does not read an account, infer completeness of the supplied inventory, establish semantic correctness or prove execution. No private defaults.

values.title: Measure the speech in my recordings, without grading or changing it (runs on your computer)
values.job: Show me how loud, noisy, hummy, windy, echoey or clipped the speech in each part of my recordings is, before I choose what counts as good
values.description: Takes the same spans file as tool:grade-and-repair-speech-audio and, for each unique span, cuts it exactly from its start to its end and measures it: loudness and true peak, noise floor read from the pauses between words (or the quietest frames when there are no word times), signal to noise, clipping, mains hum and its frequency, wind rumble and room tail. It needs no settings and grades nothing: it is for seeing what a set of recordings is like before the person chooses the settings the grade is judged against. Writes probe.json (per span: the measures and how many words it has) and the cuts; show_probe.py prints probe.json one line per span. The source recordings are only read. It runs on the person's own computer, never on Trillion.

values.title: Cost measurements
values.job: Review provider and operation usage, forecasts, unknown coverage, and billed history in my account
values.description: Shows the account's saved measurement Lists with a live overview, run history, provider and operation filters, versioned forecasts, billed records, source revisions, retries and errors. It keeps units, currencies, scenarios and measured, assumed and unknown values distinct. It includes no private measurements in the screen code.

values.title: Find the moments in my videos, pictures and talks that match a phrase (runs on your computer)
values.job: Find which of my recordings show or mention something, and at what second
values.description: Builds a local index of what a person's videos and pictures look like (frames sampled every few seconds, embedded with a CLIP model) and what their talks say (transcript chunks embedded with a sentence model), then answers a phrase with the best moment in each recording, picture lane and speech lane apart. The script reads one JSON request per line on standard input and prints one reply per line: embed_picture and embed_speech return a value the AI keeps (vectors by the identity it gave), add brings kept values back in so nothing is embedded twice, search takes a phrase. Model names, sampling interval, frame cap and the near-duplicate cut are fields of the request or the config file; the script holds none of a person's recordings, words or settings. Models are read from the local cache and never downloaded by the script, and nothing leaves the computer.

values.title: Eject a drive
values.job: Eject one drive connected to this person's computer safely, so it can be unplugged
values.description: Runs on the person's computer. check true only names anything still using the drive and ejects nothing.

values.title: Where else a file is
values.job: Find every other place one file on this person's computer also is (a duplicate): on their other connected drives and in their Trillion space
values.description: Runs on the person's computer. path is the file on a connected drive.

values.title: Copy or move files between drives
values.job: Copy or move files and folders to one or more folders on drives connected to this person's computer, as a long job that can be paused and stopped
values.description: Runs on the person's computer. sources are full paths; destinations are folders on connected drives; mode is copy or move. check true previews what would be copied and changes nothing.

values.title: Drive work in progress
values.job: List the long file jobs running on this person's computer drives (copies and moves): how far each has got, and whether it can be paused, resumed or stopped now
values.description: Runs on the person's computer. Returns work: each job with its id, what it is doing and the controls it takes now.

values.title: Pause, resume or stop drive work
values.job: Pause, resume or stop one long file job on this person's computer drives (a copy or a move), optionally resuming it at a chosen time
values.description: Runs on the person's computer. id is the job from tool:media-work; action is one of the controls it lists; check true only says whether that control is ready.

values.title: Merge a streamed answer's parts
values.job: Merge the events of a streamed answer into keyed parts: text that appends, sources and related questions as parts of their own, patches to parts already sent, and a snapshot to pick up an interrupted stream
values.description: Give events, each { seq, type, key?, ... } as the stream sent it (types and how each merges are src/keyed-parts.json), and entry when continuing one an earlier call answered. Answers entry (seq, order, parts, drift, stalls) and resume ({ seq, identity }), the token a re-attach continues from. An event at or below the entry's seq is already held and adds nothing; a patch that does not apply is kept under drift and as a part of its own, never losing the answer.

values.title: Mix sounds under a video
values.job: Lay music, voice-overs and sound effects under a video at chosen times, each trimmed, with its own volume and fades, music lowering itself under speech
values.description: Plays each sound from `start` seconds into the video, trimmed to `from`..`to` of its file, at its volume with fades; a sound with duck drops while the video's speech or a voice-over is heard. Optionally evens out the whole video's loudness (loudness_lufs, -14 suits most sites). Saves the new video in your files.

values.title: Move a booking on my calendar
values.job: Move a booking's event on my own calendar to a new time
values.description: Moves one event on the person's own Google calendar to a new start and end, with the person's own calendar account (the held value calendar-account); Google tells the attendees. Answers changed, or error and why.

values.title: Move a group of files from one code tree to another, with everything they import
values.job: Move groups of code files from one repository to another byte for byte, with every file they import and their tests, delete the originals so one copy remains, and prove the moved files are the same bytes and still load and pass their tests
values.description: Give step (plan, apply or check), the move row (row, or row_file such as move-rows/older-repository-to-workshop.json), source_folder and destination_folder (git working copies on this computer). The row is data: the two trees, which owner rows go to which folder (its groups, or groups_from an owner index whose rows name a destination), keep (paths that must stay; a group importing one is held), provider_calls (calls that must not be left in a moved file) and calls (find/replace rows that swap a provider call for a records door call). plan changes nothing and answers each group with its owner files, import closure, tests and why it is held; every file with where it lands (its group folder, or shared_folder when more than one group imports it) and how its imports change; and the files that stay and import a moved file from the destination package. apply carries the plan out on both working copies (apply_groups carries out some groups only, placing shared files as the whole plan would), moves owner-index rows whose files all moved, and writes moved-from.json in each destination folder. check proves a move from those receipts on a clean checkout: each file is its source commit bytes but for import paths and swapped calls, every import reaches the same file, the source no longer holds it, every module loads, and its own tests pass.

values.title: Move static items into a space
values.job: Move the static items a space held into its own posts, once: the owner moves them and asking again keeps nothing
values.description: Each item of the static projection becomes a record:space-item row keyed by where it came from. Only the person who runs the space may move them. It replaces the one-time migrate-static-projection-items.

values.title: Time each word of a voice take from where the voice really starts, for graphics on the word (runs on your computer)
values.job: Make the word times of my voice take start where each word is actually heard, so on-screen graphics land on the word and not early in the pause before it
values.description: Reads a voice take and its word times (a Whisper word list) and moves each word's start to the first 10 ms window inside the word whose level is above a silence line (default -45 dBFS); each end stays. Whisper puts part of a pause into the next word's start, so a graphic timed to it lands early. Given the take's line file (its script), each word takes the script's spelling when the script and Whisper give the same number of words, and a word Whisper split at a hyphen is joined into one; otherwise Whisper's spelling stays and the answer says why. Writes {source, timing, words: [{text, start, end}]} and answers how many words moved.

values.title: My browser push application key
values.job: Get the public key browsers need to register for notices
values.description: Returns only the base64url P-256 public applicationServerKey derived from the web_push field of the held notification-signing-keys bundle. The private signing scalar and contact stay on the credential pipe.

values.title: How I chose to be notified
values.job: Show the options a notification setting offers this person and which one they chose
values.description: setting is the name of a setting the person described in their own records. Returns { setting, heading, explanation, options: [{ id, label, description, current }], current, status, said }. status is ready, empty (the setting describes no options), missing (the person has described no such setting; said tells how) or invalid (the saved choice is not one of the options; it is reported, not corrected). It changes nothing.

values.title: My notification devices
values.job: List the devices registered to show or read my notices
values.description: Returns each registered device by opaque device_id, route, label and status. Push tokens and addresses are never returned.

values.title: Notices recorded for me
values.job: List the notification events recorded for one audience, newest first
values.description: audience is the reference the events name in audience_refs; limit is optional (up to 100, default 20). Returns { audience, events, said }, each event exactly as it was recorded. It changes nothing.

values.title: Requests taken and who owes an answer
values.job: List the requests taken, newest first, with their receipts and the ones still waiting on an owner
values.description: records: the intake-request and intake-receipt rows, each { id, type, value }, as the store that holds them returned them (this run reads only what is handed in and keeps nothing). Optional owner (only that owner's requests), waiting true (only requests handed to an owner that has given no receipt) and limit (up to 100, default 20). Returns { requests: [{ request_id, text, at, status, disposition, reason, owner_ref, owner_request, receipts, waiting_on_owner }], said }.

values.title: Name a voice heard before it was enrolled
values.job: Put a person's name on what they said in a listening before I enrolled their voice, and tell me which turns changed
values.description: After tool:enrol-a-voice-or-face names a voice heard in a listening (its heard_as), answers that listening's heard turns still under "Someone (voice-N)" for those voices with the person's name on them, keeping the former label on each row. Turns a person already named, unsure turns and other listenings are left as they are. It keeps nothing: the heard rows come in with the request (`heard`) and the renamed rows (`rows`) go out in the answer, for the person's AI to keep where it chooses.

values.title: Name a voice
values.job: Attach a person's name to one voice cluster after identifying that voice
values.description: Keeps your explicit person name for an existing voice cluster. Later analysis shows that name on matching voice segments; the model itself never guesses a name.

values.title: Name my next commitment for the menu bar
values.job: Say what is happening now or next on my calendar, with a countdown, as the line the Mac menu bar shows
values.description: Give the timed calendar items (each with its title, its start and end, whether it is all day, and the calendar it came from) the caller read from the person's own records, and optionally the time to count from, how many hours ahead counts (0 for the rest of today) and how each calendar counts (within, always or never). Returns the one line the menu bar shows ("Design review · in 12 min") for the commitment now or next inside the reach, or null when there is none, the reach's end, how far ahead the calendar is read (look_ahead_minutes) and how often the line refreshes. Only timed items count; an item with no title is skipped; nothing is read or written here.

values.title: Name the open rows a message names
values.job: Given the person's own message and the open list rows it names, make the classifier question for each row, with the settle values and the hand-off words
values.description: Pure. Takes the message and the open rows the caller read (each with its list and settling field). Refuses AI words, someone else's words and history brought in (brought_in true) by returning no asks. Each ask carries its question (state and questions for the classifier), the values a settle would write, and the words a hand-off needs. It asks nothing and settles nothing.

values.title: Name the voices from the call app
values.job: Name the unnamed voices of a recorded call from who the call app showed as speaking on screen, only where the screen evidence is enough, one name to one voice
values.description: Give turns ([{ start, end, who }] in seconds, such as tool:who-is-in-this answered) and samples ([{ at, names }] or [{ at, elements }] in milliseconds from the start of the recording, elements being the call window's accessibility elements), and app (the call app's name) when known. Only voices whose label is still unnamed (Someone (...), Unsure (...)) are laid over. Returns assignments ([{ voice, name, share, overlap_ms }]) and unnamed ([{ voice, candidates }]). With apply, returns writes (each a name_speaker call's arguments, evidence included) for the caller to send; nothing is written here.

values.title: What is using a drive
values.job: Name the programs on this person's computer that are using one drive right now, which would stop it from ejecting
values.description: Runs on the person's computer. Returns mount and processes (each pid and name): the programs with files open on that drive.

values.title: Name a site
values.job: Give a published website its own readable address, or rename it so old links still work
values.description: Gives the site (installation) the address https://<name>.<suffix>/: name, or one made from title. A site renamed keeps its earlier names, which send visitors on to the new one. A name is 3 to 40 lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens; reserved words and code-like names are refused. Your computer hands the address to the forwarder and the site answers there while your computer is on.

values.title: Set how people can find me
values.job: Change how this person shows in the Network: the name, handle, what they offer and seek, whether they are findable, their pursuits and their meaning vectors
values.description: Saves the person's network_records profile row in the database named (or the held connection named), changing only the fields sent. A field a person wrote is listed under written. A handle is 3 to 30 letters, digits or underscores and is unique among the profiles. A contact is kept on the person's own row and is never answered by the search or path tools; read-a-network-contact answers it only while an introduction is released.

values.title: Notice each message on this Mac, and tell the engine
values.job: Watch the Messages database on the person's own Mac and tell their engine one fact for each iMessage or text message that arrives, is edited or is unsent, the moment Messages writes it, so the workflows that hear messages start. It only reads: it never sends a message.
values.description: The noticer's program (tell-the-engine.mjs) run on the person's own Mac with one capability, read-messages, which the person grants to this tool and which macOS allows only once the app that runs the engine has Full Disk Access. Its one wake, keep-noticing-one-source, names no waiter: the person switches it on with their own input (wake:switch input {waiters}), naming the imessage-chat-database leaf, so which Messages database is watched and from when (history_since) is their own DATA. Each message is told as a something-changed fact at place message, with the same eight fields every message source tells (where, place, change, at, key, by, after, kinds), so the router and the history keeper take it as they take WhatsApp. A Mac that refuses the database is told once at place access with the setting to change.

values.title: Notice what needs attention
values.job: Decide whether an arrival opens work or stays as context from caller rules, voice confidence and history facts, using the current formula tool without a metered model.
values.description: Decide whether an arrival opens work or stays as context from caller rules, voice confidence and history facts, using the current formula tool without a metered model. All opinion settings arrive as input rows; the tool reads no records. No old Worker store is imported.

values.title: Notice when something shows up, and tell the engine
values.job: Keep watching for things outside (a stretch of time passing, a drive attached or removed, files someone finished putting in a place, a delivery over the network) and tell the person's engine one fact each time, so any tool whose wake hears that kind of fact starts
values.description: Give waiters: the standing orders the noticer keeps (notice-when-something-shows-up.waiter-descriptor rows, each naming one mechanism in do-work/mechanisms, its settings and the kind of fact it emits). It runs as a kept-open program: while its wake is on, each waiter waits, and each time something shows up or goes away it tells the engine one fact at wake:arrive, of the waiter's kind, with the change's fields as text. A tool hears it by declaring a wake {fact: {kind, from: ["run"], match}}. This row may tell only the kinds its rights name. Each fact told or refused is one line of the program's output. Given for_seconds, it watches that long and answers {told, refused}. A second wake, keep-noticing-row-changes, watches one database's changes (the row-changes leaf) over the connection the person keeps under own-rows-postgres-connection; it is off until the person switches it on, and only then does the run hold that connection and reach its host. A third wake, keep-noticing-one-source, names no waiter and no credential: the person switches it on with their own input (wake:switch input {credential_name, waiters}), so a source of theirs (a booking service's list, their sent mail) is watched from their own DATA and never from a shared row; one source per switch, because a run reaches only the hosts every value it holds may go to.

values.title: Observe my live usage
values.job: Turn my account's own usage day rows (stored bytes, work time, source bytes the person's files program counted) into one usage observation per billed resource for each closed day, ready to settle
values.description: Turn my account's own usage day rows (stored bytes, work time, source bytes the person's files program counted, handed in as usage_days as its usage_days answered them) into one usage observation per billed resource for each closed day, ready to settle. This run reads only the rows it is given and keeps nothing; the caller keeps the observations it is answered and gives them to settle-shared-resource-cost.

values.title: Observe something I watched or read
values.job: Turn one thing a person watched, read, used or saved (a page they visited, words they selected, an app they spent a while in, a feed item) into one observation with a stable identity, so seeing the same thing again is recognised and a changed page is a new revision
values.description: Give source_ref (what to call the source) and content (an object saying what was seen: url, text, title, app, window, whatever applies). Optional: native_ref (the item's own id; else its url, else the identity of its content), observed_at (ISO-8601 UTC; else now), metadata. Returns observation { id, source_ref, native_ref, observed_at, content_revision, payload } and said. A url adds its host and, where none was given, a title. content_revision is the BLAKE3 identity of the payload without the time, so the same words seen at another time are the same revision and the same id. Reads nothing and keeps nothing: hand the observation to whatever keeps the person's records.

values.title: Who is on my path
values.job: Show people whose shown pursuits are close in meaning to one of this person's pursuits
values.description: Answers the people who chose to show their pursuits and whose pursuit is at least on_your_path.min_similarity close, by cosine, to one of this person's pursuits (each pursuit carries its embedding), each with both pursuits beside each other. Open pursuits: spaces you are not in whose join rows let anyone in (a free row) and whose embedding is close to one of your pursuits, at most the settings cap (6).

values.title: Open a paid file for a buyer
values.job: Check, each time a buyer opens a paid file link, that they still hold access, and say which sealed bytes to stream
values.description: For a link's token and the account presenting it: refuses a malformed or expired token, then checks the file's paid-file row against what the presenter holds now (from the access rows the request carries), so a refund or an ended subscription stops the very next open and a link passed to someone else does not open. On authorized it answers the sealed copy's identity, the cipher, the nonce and the NAME of the key the door decrypts with; never the key.

values.title: Open a prompt in a local AI app
values.job: Hand one prompt (an issue, a task) to a coding AI app the person already has on their computer, such as Claude Code or Codex
values.description: Opens the prompt in the app named by `app`, one of the rows of read-data/open-in-ai.json (the rows are the allowlist; an app not in them is refused). A url row opens its URL with the prompt percent-encoded, an argv row runs its list as it is with the prompt as one argument; nothing goes through a shell. `folder` must be a folder that exists; the app's own config is never read or written. The outcome is launched, app_missing or refused; the prompt is never echoed, only its length. `dry_run` shows the launch without running it.

values.title: Open a meeting link
values.job: Open a meeting link in the meeting app that owns it on the person's computer, after reading it through the declared routes; a refused link is never opened
values.description: Give link. The link is read first (as tool:read-meeting-link); only an allowed link is handed to the system to open. Returns opened, route, action and redacted; never a secret parameter's value.

values.title: Open the billing page for one purchase and show its card
values.job: Open the billing page of one purchase, where the buyer can change or cancel it, and show the card that pays it
values.description: Give subscription_id (the sub_ id of one purchase), return_url (an https address the billing page returns to) and subject_email (the signed-in buyer's verified email; the purchase must be theirs, or nothing is opened or read). Reads the purchase with the card that pays it, opens a Stripe customer billing-portal session for the customer that bills it, and gives back the redirect address and the card (brand, last four, expiry only). flow opens the page on one step: payment_method_update (change the card), subscription_update (change the plan) or subscription_cancel (cancel); leave it out for the page itself. The configuration is the account default unless configuration names one; an account with none is refused, never given a made-up one. It changes no subscription and moves no money: the buyer confirms the change on Stripe's page. Uses the Stripe key of the seller connection that seller_connection names (service_connection:stripe is your own).

values.title: Open the document a pursuit edits together
values.job: Say which document each page of Write opens, so everyone in a pursuit edits the same document together and a personal page stays personal
values.description: Give pages: what each page of Write is opened with ({ space_id?, scene_address?, ... }). A page opened in a pursuit (space_id) opens that pursuit's one shared room (space-room:<pursuit>/package::documents::documents, from show/write-screen.json) unless it names a document of that same room; a page with no pursuit keeps its own address. Answers pages (each { opened: true, input: what the screen opens with, shared } or { opened: false, refused }, in the screen's own words: an empty pursuit name, one that is not text or holds '/', or a document of another room) and shared_rooms (each room once). It runs show/write-screen-input.mjs writeScreenInput, the rule the Write screen opens with. It reads, keeps and sends nothing; the editing itself (blocks, merges, undo, presence) is the Write screen's and is not run here.

values.title: Order my goals under the goals they serve
values.job: Keep my goals in the order they are shown, each one under the goal it serves, so a goal with several parents is shown once and none is hidden by a missing parent or a loop
values.description: Give goals ([{ id, title?, parents?, children? }]; parents and children name other goals by id or { id }). The goals are ordered by the reader the app's goal list used (read-data/pursuit-hierarchy-view.mjs): each top goal in the order given, then the goals under it, depth first; a goal with several parents is one row, indented under the first parent reached; a goal whose parent is not among those given, or that is in a cycle, is still shown. Answers rows ([{ id, title, depth, shown_under, parents }]) and count. Refuses goals that is not a list and a goal without an id. Reads no records, keeps nothing and sends nothing. The Home screen did more than this run does: it saved goals, marked the one needle mover, focused the app on one goal or space, and greeted the person with the next step and their AIs' work in the words of home-words.json; none of that is here, and this run does not read home-words.json.

values.title: Add or remove labels on a conversation
values.job: Add or remove neutral labels on every message of one conversation: remove inbox to archive the whole conversation.
values.description: Add or remove neutral labels on every message of one conversation: remove inbox to archive the whole conversation. Takes provider (an id of read-data/mail-providers.json) and connection (the person's account of that provider, by its handle only: {connection_id}). Runs as that account with the key the person's vault holds for it; the engine hands the key to this run alone and it is placed only in the request to the provider's own host, never shown. Answers the provider-neutral rows of read-data/neutral.mjs, never the provider's own payload. A provider that does not offer it says so in words.

values.title: Add or remove labels on a message
values.job: Add or remove neutral labels on one message: remove inbox to archive it, add or remove unread to change its read state, add or remove starred to star it. Answers the labels it has now.
values.description: Add or remove neutral labels on one message: remove inbox to archive it, add or remove unread to change its read state, add or remove starred to star it. Answers the labels it has now. Takes provider (an id of read-data/mail-providers.json) and connection (the person's account of that provider, by its handle only: {connection_id}). Runs as that account with the key the person's vault holds for it; the engine hands the key to this run alone and it is placed only in the request to the provider's own host, never shown. Answers the provider-neutral rows of read-data/neutral.mjs, never the provider's own payload. A provider that does not offer it says so in words.

values.title: Sort my saved browser tabs into folders by my rules
values.job: Sort the tabs a person pinned in their browser into folders by rules they wrote, keep every tab and a backup of the file, and undo it
values.description: Works on the browser's sidebar file (the Arc layout) inside the folder the person granted for change; close the browser first, because it rewrites the file while it runs. Give file (the sidebar file's plain name) and rules: space (title of the space), root_folder (title of the pinned folder that holds the sorted tree), folders ({ top: [sub, ...] }, the tree to make; the root folder must already hold exactly one folder for each name, because the browser makes folders and this reuses them), fallback ([top, sub?] for a covered tab no rule places), and optionally skip_hosts, relevant_hosts, relevant_words (what covers a tab outside the root folder) and rules ([{ put_in: [top, sub?], hosts, words }], first match wins; words are matched anywhere in the tab's title, address and folder path, ignoring case). Tabs already in the root folder are always covered; a split view moves whole. Without apply: true it only reports every tab's decision and the counts, and writes nothing. With apply: true it first copies the file to a backup beside it, checks that every tab is still reachable and no item appeared or went, then replaces the file in one step. To undo, give file and restore_from (the backup's name): the file is put back and what it replaced is kept. Reads no history, cookies, passwords or page content. Returns the counts, each tab's decision and folder, whether it was applied, and the backup's name.

values.title: Read the files I keep for my other AI apps
values.job: Read the instructions, commands, skills and MCP servers the person already keeps for their other AI apps (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Claude Desktop, Gemini CLI, Windsurf), in place, without copying them
values.description: Lists every entry the rows of read-data/other-ai-files.json name that exists under the folder the person granted (their home folder), as source/kind/name with its app label and size and no contents; `source` and `kind` narrow the list. `read` names entries to return whole, up to most_chars, each labelled with its app and kind. Read only: nothing is written into those folders or imported, a link inside a folder is never followed, and an MCP server another app lists comes back as its command or address with the NAMES of its environment variables and headers, never their values; nothing switches a server on.

values.title: Pace sends from an inbox
values.job: Say when each address on a list may be emailed from one sending inbox, so a new inbox warms up slowly, sends only on chosen days and hours, and stops when its mail bounces
values.description: Give time_zone (the inbox's), recipients and a pacing row (pacing: new-inbox-warmup or saturday-local from read-data/inbox-pacing.json, or your own pacing_row): a ramp of sends a day by the inbox's day number, the least gap between sends, weekdays, local hours, how many days to leave an address after it was sent to, and when to pause (a share of hard bounces or any complaint among the last sends). Add history (every send this inbox made), outcomes (from tool:sort-bounces-and-replies) and suppressed addresses. Returns due_now (send these now, through a send tool), schedule (a slot for every address that may be sent to, in local time with its ramp day), held (each address left out and why: suppressed, bounced, unsubscribed, replied, sent to recently, listed twice, not an address, or the inbox is paused) and paused. It sends nothing and keeps nothing; every number, day and hour is a row you can change.

values.title: Pack my device copy's settle upload
values.job: Work out what my device's copy of my records would send when it settles with my account: where the account's copy is kept on the device and the exact upload for one batch, compressed when that makes it smaller
values.description: Give account (the signed-in account name, 1 to 256 characters) and request (one settle batch as a JSON object, the shape record-sync.mjs sends: copy, root, took_through, rows). Answers location (the private-file-system directory the account's copy is kept under, the account name's bytes in hex so two accounts never share one, and the file name records.sqlite3), sends (frame or plain), headers (content type, the x-trillion-device-account header, and for a frame its dictionary BLAKE3 id and exact expanded size), plain_bytes, sent_bytes, body (plain text) or body_base64 (the deflate frame, compressed against the sample of settle JSON in do-work/frame-dictionaries.json) and expands_back (the frame expands to exactly the batch). A batch under 1024 bytes, or one that would not shrink, goes plain. Refuses an empty, non-text or over-long account and a request that is not an object. It reads only its input: it opens no database, keeps nothing on any device, sends nothing and settles nothing. The screen's other work (the SQLite copy in the browser's private file system that survives reloads and reads offline, the outbox of small writes, the settle itself with the hosted store and sealed records) needs a browser worker and @sqlite.org/sqlite-wasm and is not done by this run.

values.title: Give an unknown sender a pairing code
values.job: Hold a message from a sender the person has not paired yet and give that sender a short code the person can approve
values.description: Give source_id (the event source the message came in on) and sender (the sender's own id on that source). Returns { paired: true } when the sender is already paired; otherwise code (8 characters with no 0, O, 1 or I), expires_at (an hour from now) and said. Asking again for the same sender gives the same code; a source with 3 codes waiting gives no more ({ full: true, said }). It reaches no database: give the pairing facts the person keeps as facts, and keep what the answer's keep lists.

values.title: Read fields out of a screen snapshot
values.job: Turn the accessibility elements of one app's window ({ role, label }) into fields through that app's declarative parser row, with emails, card numbers and tokens removed before anything is returned
values.description: Give app (its name) and elements ([{ role, label }], as the Mac app's reader takes them). The first parser row whose app_contains matches the app is used, else the generic one; it selects elements by role and label pattern and cuts fields out with regular expressions. Every field is redacted with the redact patterns. Answers rows: [{ field: value }]. Triggers, throttle, parsers and redaction: read-data/snapshot-triggers.json; the governor that decides when to take a snapshot is createGovernor in the same file, used by the Mac app's reader.

values.title: Pay someone a share through Stripe
values.job: Pay a share of what I took on to a person I pay, out of my own Stripe balance
values.description: This pays real money out. Give amount_cents, currency, destination (their Stripe account id), optionally source_transaction, and confirm_moves_money: true in the same request, or nothing is sent. Uses the Stripe key of the seller connection that seller_connection names (service_connection:stripe is your own).

values.title: Pick the screen for what I am typing
values.job: Pick, as a person types, the screen that already does what their words ask from the screens they are offered, the interfaces made for them and the screens they kept, with no model, and keep the shown screen calm
values.description: Give words (what is typed so far) and the catalog: rows (offered screens, each { id, label, description?, asked?, source? }), made (interfaces, each { interface_id, title, intent }) and asks (kept screens, each { id, words, screen, input? }). memory is the last call's memory (omit it the first time). Answers picks (ranked, each with its entry and score) and memory: shown is the screen to show, which a challenger replaces only after winning twice in a row or with a certain score. Weights, thresholds and bounds are src/instant-screens.json; it names no screen.

values.title: Pick the small good moment to play
values.job: Pick the small good moment to play when something good happens or a phrase is typed: its words and motion, from the moment rows I give, so once-only moments play once and the words change each time
values.description: Give moments (the moment rows, tried in order: each { id, on: { event_kind, match?, starts_with? } or { typed }, words (one line or a list that rotates), motion?, mark?, once?, count_at? }) and exactly one of event (what happened, { event_kind, ...fields }) or typed (the text typed so far, matched by the phrase it ends with, any case); memory is the remember of the last pick (leave it out the first time). A row answers an event when its event_kind is the event's, every match field equals the event's and every starts_with field starts it; a once row is due only if it never played, a count_at row only at those running counts; {count} in words is the running count. Answers moment ({ id, motion, mark, words } or null when no row is due) and remember ({ counts, played }), the whole next memory. Nothing is played, shown, stored or sent and no clock is read. Refuses moments that are not rows with ids, neither or both of event and typed, an event without event_kind and memory that is not an object. The screens (show/mount-delight-moments.tsx, show/mount-feel.ts, show/FeelSettings.tsx, show/ambience-screen.tsx) also play the moment's motion, give it a feel in touch, sound and motion on each device under the person's show rules and move lights with music; this run does none of that.

values.title: Pick a cover frame for a video
values.job: Choose the best frame of a video for its cover or thumbnail and save it as a picture
values.description: Scores frames across the video for sharpness and exposure, saves the best one (or the frame at `at` seconds) as a JPEG in your files, and returns its time.

values.title: Pick the progress rules that fire
values.job: Pick which of my progress rules fire for my current numbers and give the adjustment each carries
values.description: Takes one value per metric (signals) and the person's rules. A rule fires when its metric has a number and the number lies in the rule's half-open band [min, max) (an omitted min is minus infinity, an omitted max is plus infinity). Answers the fired rules with the value that fired them, their adjustments in rule order, and whether any fired. Rules may overlap, so several can fire. Metrics, bands and adjustments are the person's; the tool knows none.

values.title: Find the cleanest stretch of someone's speech to use as the voice to clone from (runs on your computer)
values.job: From a person's own recordings, pick the cleanest ten seconds of continuous speech to clone their voice from
values.description: Takes a list of recordings of the person who agreed to be cloned, each with its word times. In each recording it takes the first run of words with no pause over 0.4 s that lasts the window length (ten seconds by default), cuts it to a wav (the recording is only read), measures it, drops windows that are too quiet, too loud or clipped, and ranks the rest by signal to noise. Writes reference-candidates.json with each window's wav, text and measures, and prints the best few. It runs on the person's own computer, never on Trillion.

values.title: Pick the release a host version runs
values.job: Tell which release of a published tool a given Trillion version runs, or which version it needs
values.description: Give row (a published tool row, optionally with minimum_host_version and earlier_releases, newest first) and host_version (the version of the Trillion that will run it, like 2026.10.1). Versions compare part by part, missing parts are zero. Returns release: the row itself when its minimum is met, else the first earlier release whose minimum is met (without its earlier_releases); when none runs, release is null and oldest_needed names the oldest version any release runs on. A missing host_version is refused.

values.title: Check or update the pins of a folder of DATA files
values.job: Check that a pin file records each DATA file's exact byte count and BLAKE3, or bring the pins up to the files, so a program that reads them can refuse a file that changed after it was pinned
values.description: Reads every file under a folder (skipping folders whose names start with a dot, and the files named as never pinned), hashes each with BLAKE3 and compares it with its entry in the pin file. check answers which pins are added, changed or gone; write rewrites only the entries, keeping every other key of the pin file and the order of the entries it keeps. The pin file's shape is DATA (read-data/pin-shape.json or the caller's own).

values.title: Pin a video's frames into labelled contact-sheet pages (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn a manifest of extracted video frames into labelled page images, with timestamps, that an AI can look at and cite
values.description: Projects a frame manifest into the form the pages need, then tiles the frames into labelled page images (optionally pairing adjacent candidate frames with their frame number and time). Each page is bound to the identity of the frames on it. Sizes, quality and font are options.

values.title: Put a section into a markdown document
values.job: Put one named section into a markdown document without repeating it: replace the section with the same heading, or add it at the end
values.description: Give the whole markdown document as text and the section as text. The section names itself by its own first heading line. When the document already has that heading, the section from there to the next heading of the same or a higher level is replaced (its deeper subsections go with it, its sibling sections stay); otherwise the section is added at the end. A heading-looking line inside a fenced block never ends a section, so a document that quotes markdown is safe. Placing the same section twice gives the same text. A section with no heading is refused, because it could never be replaced later. Returns the new document text, whether the section was appended or replaced, and its heading.

values.title: Place live orders from a trading policy
values.job: Place the orders of my trading policy at my broker's live (real money) account
values.description: Give policy (its version, its orders, and its own limits: risk.max_order_notional, risk.max_daily_notional and risk.day_time_zone; risk.allowed_symbols, when given, is the only symbols it may trade), routes (how your broker takes an order, each route with mode "live") and prices for market orders. Every order is checked first and skipped with its reason when it is malformed, says live: false, has no live route, was already sent for this policy version, names a symbol outside risk.allowed_symbols, or would pass a limit; nothing is resized. Give records too (the trade-order and trade-day-spend records of earlier runs, read from the store that holds them): they say what was already sent and how much of the day's limit is used. Nothing is kept here: the answer's records are the trade-order, trade-order-event and trade-day-spend records this run would write, for you to keep; a 4xx answer is a refusal, and no answer is "unknown" and is never sent again once its record is handed back. With no policy nothing is sent and the answer says what to give. The held live-broker-credentials (a JSON object of named fields) reach only the request and are never kept or shown.

values.title: Place paper orders from a trading policy
values.job: Place the orders of my trading policy at my broker's paper account
values.description: Give policy (its version, its orders, and its own limits: risk.max_order_notional, risk.max_daily_notional and risk.day_time_zone; risk.allowed_symbols, when given, is the only symbols it may trade), routes (how your broker takes an order, each route with mode "paper") and prices for market orders. Every order is checked first and skipped with its reason when it is malformed, says live: true, has no paper route, was already sent for this policy version, names a symbol outside risk.allowed_symbols, or would pass a limit; nothing is resized. Give records too (the trade-order and trade-day-spend records of earlier runs, read from the store that holds them): they say what was already sent and how much of the day's limit is used. Nothing is kept here: the answer's records are the trade-order, trade-order-event and trade-day-spend records this run would write, for you to keep; a 4xx answer is a refusal, and no answer is "unknown" and is never sent again once its record is handed back. With no policy nothing is sent and the answer says what to give. The held paper-broker-credentials (a JSON object of named fields) reach only the request and are never kept or shown.

values.title: Place a cue plan's sound effects into one effects track (runs on your computer)
values.job: Lay every sound-effect cue of my cue plan at its time and gain into one effects-only track
values.description: Every cue [seconds, sound, gain dB] placed at its whole millisecond, with its gain, summed, as a mixer that delays by whole milliseconds places it, with no music and no voice; prints its integrated loudness.

values.title: Places left out of screen capture
values.job: List, check and turn on or off the categories of places (banking, health, social and more) the person's screen capture must leave out, and take new coverage as a cursor diff
values.description: Runs on the person's own Mac. action list gives each category, whether it is on and how many domains it holds; check says which category on an address is in, or null; set turns one category on or off in the person's own file; diff applies a cursor diff of added domains and tombstones only when it starts at this Mac's cursor. A subdomain belongs to its domain's category, a look-alike does not, and a removed domain stays gone after a seed reload.

values.title: Fill a column by asking my sources in order
values.job: Fill one column of my list row by row by asking my sources in my order until one gives an answer that passes my check, paying only for the sources each row needs: tell me the next calls to run, and turn what they answered into values
values.description: Takes rows, where each row's id is, the column (field), the sources in the order to ask them (each a Workshop tool, its input built from the row's fields or fixed values, where the value is in its answer, its cost and its source kind), an accept check (a tools/formulas rule tree over the answer as field value), an optional run_if rule tree over the rows, and the attempts already made with what each answered. Answers the next calls to make, one source at a time per row, each with a request key (the content identity of row, source, tool and input, so a retry is never paid twice); the values found, each as an offer settle-field-values reads; the rows skipped (run_if does not hold, already has a value while keep_existing holds) and the rows out of sources with what each source did. Run it again with the new attempts until done. stop_after_same_failure stops a row whose sources keep giving the same rejected answer; most_calls bounds one run.

values.title: Work out the ffmpeg commands that premix a motion film's soundtrack
values.job: Show me exactly how my film's soundtrack will be mixed: the music bed and how loud it is when, every voice line and every sound effect at its time, before anything is rendered
values.description: Reads a motion film's cue sheet (its length, voice line offsets, the stretches where a voice is heard, and every sound effect as [time, palette sound, gain in dB]) and the film's settings, and answers the ffmpeg commands that premix its soundtrack: the music bed trimmed from its start and shaped over time (ducked while a voice is heard, set or lifted in named windows, faded out), each voice line delayed to its offset, each effect delayed to its time at its gain, all summed, then the film's loudness pass (in the graph, a measured gain and a limiter, or a linear two-pass loudnorm). Nothing is read or written: it is the plan tool:premix-a-motion-films-soundtrack runs where the recordings are. The film's choices are its settings row; the tool holds only the format's file layout.

values.title: Plan a side-by-side video of two movements, each framed on its person (runs on your computer)
values.job: Make the edit for a video that shows two movements next to each other, each cropped to the person doing it, with labels and an optional slow-motion pass
values.description: Takes two clips with their pose tracks (from tool:read-peoples-poses-from-a-video), the second of each clip to centre on, and the look as data: labels and corners, side by side or stacked, a mirror for a clip filmed from the other side, the passes (a full pass and a slow-motion pass, each with its own window), the picture size and an optional narration to replace the sound. It writes an edit for the media-composition tool: for each pass one split segment whose cells are crops of each clip around the joints it found in that window, padded and cut to the cell's shape and kept inside the clip's frame; with no confident joint a centred crop. The window is cut to the shorter clip so both cells stay in step. It renders nothing: hand the edit to the media-composition tool.

values.title: Plan moving kept stands into stance records
values.job: Turn stands a person took that were kept somewhere else into their stance records, with every earlier stand as an earlier version, and show what would change before anything is written
values.description: Give stances (rows: kind, text, contains or view, stance, why, by, at, earlier as [{stance, why, at}], and the old ref if there was one) and fold, how the owner of the rules says two texts are the same. Returns writes, the record versions to send one at a time in order (each record's earlier stands first, oldest first), and summary: rows, records and versions by kind, refs_changed (rows whose identity differs from their old ref) collisions (records two or more rows became under the fold, with each row's text and time), already (versions in kept, not written again) and unverified (rows whose words are not in their source, never written). A row may name a rule (a waiver stand) and a source with after_line, and so may each of its earlier stands; every stand naming a source is checked against sources, and a row any of whose words are not there is listed in unverified by the id of the record it would have been. summary_only true leaves the writes out. It writes nothing.

values.title: Plan the write that accepts an evaluation of a learner's step
values.job: Accept the result of judging a learner's work on a step: the receipt to keep and the learner's next progress state, without applying one twice
values.description: Give the evaluation receipt, the learner's current progress state (leave out if none) and the revision you expect it to be at, and the receipt already stored under that evaluation id if there is one. Returns the keep rows: the receipt and the next state, each with the value it expects to find in your store (the receipt not yet stored; the state as you gave it), so your store keeps each one only where it still holds that value. The step is finished only if the receipt's decision says so. The same receipt again returns idempotent with no keep rows; a different receipt under the same id, a stale revision, a state that belongs to another learner or track, or an unsound receipt is refused with the reason.

values.title: Plan an event
values.job: Turn my draft of a gathering into its session, its catalog entry, the places to open and the link people will use
values.description: Checks an organizer's draft (a retained 128-bit hex id, the owning group, labels in any language, a primary time and an optional alternate in the zone given, a place, a mode and a visibility word the organizer chooses, a capacity of 1 to 1,000,000, the host's web address and the workflow to run) and answers the session, the catalog entry that offers it, the capacity ledger to open for its places (the input of workflow:hold-places-in-a-finite-pool), and the preview and share addresses. The same draft always gives the same plan. It plans only: nothing is kept, published or sent. Refuses a half-given alternate, an end before a start, an unsafe route or a web address that is not https (except this computer's own).

values.title: Plan choosing and saving files on my computer
values.job: Make the requests the Mac's local files target gets when a person chooses files on their computer or saves a copy back, and read what the picker answered into the files chosen, without touching any computer
values.description: Give operation choose with picker_reply (what the picker answered: { cancelled?, files: [{ path, name, byte_length, content_type, bytes_base64? }] }) and, if wanted, prompt, multiple, include_bytes, allowed_extensions and allowed_content_prefixes: chooseLocalFiles (do-work/choose-local-files.ts) makes the choose_files request and reads the reply into files, each with its content type worked out from its name when the picker said only application/octet-stream, and refuses a file not of an accepted type. Or give operation save with file_name, content_base64, copy_id and directory (a full folder path; or home, for its Downloads folder): saveLocalFileCopy (do-work/save-local-file-copy.ts) names the copy <name>-<copy_id><ext> so it never replaces a file and makes the write_new_file request and the read_file request that checks the bytes came back the same. Answers operation, requests (every request, in order, a save's bytes named by their length) and files (choose) or path (save). The workspace's sender is stood in (run/requests-kept-here.mjs): nothing is sent, no picker opens, no file is written or read, and a save's replies are the ones a Mac that saved it would give. Refuses an unknown operation and what the part refuses (a name with a slash, a folder that is not a full path, more than 16 MB).

values.title: Plan clock-aligned recording pieces
values.job: Plan how recording every camera and microphone without end is cut into clock-aligned pieces that line up across devices: when each input's pieces begin and end, what each is named, which day folder it goes in, and the list that ties them together
