values.description: Give started_at and until (ISO times), segment_seconds (piece length, 300 when left out), folder (Recordings when left out), inputs ([{ label, kind: camera | microphone, extension?, with_sound? }], the device's own label with browser bus numbers dropped), device, list_name and time_zone (the device's own IANA zone; the run's own when left out). Pieces are cut every segment_seconds counted from the start of the device's day, never from when an input started, so every input on every device cuts at the same instants; the first piece runs from started_at to the first cut and a new day starts a new window. Answers time_zone, list (where the session list is kept), first_cut_at, piece_count, pieces (each input's { input, folder, name, file, start_ms, end_ms, seconds }) and session_list (the list kept beside the pieces: inputs and moments, each moment the files recorded together). Refuses unreadable times, until not after started_at, no inputs, an input without a label or of another kind, an unknown time zone and a plan of more than 5000 pieces. It reads only its input: it opens no camera or microphone, records nothing, keeps nothing on a device and sends nothing to Files. The screen's other work (opening each input, recording the pieces, keeping them on the device first, sending them while recording, reopening an input that stops and pausing by rule) needs a browser and is not done by this run.

values.title: Plan my time
values.job: Plan the person's tasks into their free time and judge their meetings against their pursuits, like an auto-scheduling calendar: ASAP first, then hard deadlines, then what serves their most important pursuit, then due date; tasks wait for their blockers, long tasks split into pieces, hard deadlines may use time outside working hours. Returns each task's placed times, whether it fits (on track, past due, will not fit) and when it finishes, and proposes declining meetings that serve no pursuit when they keep more valuable work from meeting its deadline. Changes no calendar; apply the result with the calendar actions. Also reports each day's planned work against a daily cap with which tasks to move to tomorrow first, keeps fixed-time tasks exactly where they are, uses a task's own named schedule (theme days, a pursuit's hours), keeps a gap around work, flags tasks that keep rolling over for a decision, and ignores declined, all-day and free calendar events.
values.description: Free time is the weekly schedule in the person's time zone, minus busy events, blocks and work already placed. Tasks are placed in this order: a fixed-time task at its exact time, then ASAP, then hard deadlines, then value (the weight of the pursuits it serves times its priority), then due date; a task waits until the tasks that block it end. A task shorter than the rules' first chunk is never split; a longer one is split only into pieces of at least the rules' minimum block. A hard-deadline task that cannot meet its deadline in working hours may use time outside them, and says so. Each task comes back as on_track, past_due, unfit_past_due, unfit_later, needs_decision (it has moved `rolled_over` days in a row), conflict (its fixed time is taken), blocked or not_planned (no length, already done, or a deadline long past), with the words that say why. A meeting that serves no pursuit and is not required is proposed for decline, lowest value first, only while declining it lets more valuable work meet its deadline; nothing is declined here. Each day's planned minutes come back against the rules' daily cap with the lowest-value movable tasks to move first. Every policy number is the rules file's (read-data/rules.json) and any of them can be overridden in the request's `rules`.

values.title: Plan future recurrence windows
values.job: Enumerate a bounded set of future recurrence slots from generic schedule data, including local-time daylight-saving policies and explicit coverage.
values.description: Give an explicit replay-stable now, recurring schedules, and max_occurrences_per_schedule. Returns future_occurrences in start order, rejected_schedules, skipped_resolutions, and per-schedule coverage showing count and calendar-scan limits. Recurrence is open-ended; a bounded plan never claims the schedule itself is exhausted. This is a pure plan: it writes no occurrence state, creates no materialization intents, and runs no action.

values.title: Plan which playlist each Watch Later video goes in
values.job: Sort my YouTube Watch Later into playlists: plan which playlist each video goes in
values.description: Places each video of one or more channels' Watch Later into the playlists the person's sort settings name, and writes nothing to YouTube. A channel is sorted by rules (a channel-name expression scores 3, a strong title expression 3, a weak one 1; a video goes to every playlist scoring 3 or more, at most max_per_video, else to its best weak match marked low confidence; titles matching hold_back are kept off public playlists with hold_back_reason) or by hand-made lists kept in their order. Within a rules playlist, videos are ordered by views, highest first. The answer is the plan and a summary per channel; with out_dir it also writes sort-plan.json and SORT-PLAN.md, the page to show the person before anything is made.

values.title: What leaves when, by my release rules
values.job: Say which deleted items give their storage back now and when every other one will, by the person's own release rules and keep-for, for the items the AI read
values.description: items are what list_recently_deleted answered, each with byte_length (the bytes of its names); kept_bytes is the bytes the person's files use now (files_summary bytes); now is the ISO time to judge at (left out: now). rules, if given, decide this run only and are not saved; left out, the person's saved rules (setting:release_rules, handed in as stored) decide. Answers now (ids that leave now), items (each with leaves_at, because: a rule id or keep-for, and when_storage_above), leaving (bytes per day for the next days), kept_after, the rules and what a rule can name. It changes nothing: to give the storage back, forget those items for good and run the files tool's queue_release and release_gone_bytes.

values.title: Plan the address a live camera streams to
values.job: Work out how a live camera's stream would be received: the address this computer listens on for the camera's own key, the FFmpeg listener it is taken with, and a public RTMPS address through Tailscale Funnel that never takes a port serving something else
values.description: Give key (the camera's stream key), port (1935 when left out), app (live when left out), output (the destination's FFmpeg arguments after the input, [] when left out) and optionally funnel ({ name: this computer's Tailscale name, ports: the public ports its tailnet allows, status: what tailscale funnel status --json printed }). Answers listening_address, camera_server_address, ffmpeg ({ program, arguments }: exactly what the shared listener do-work/take-a-stream.mjs starts FFmpeg with, captured from a stand-in that is never run) and, with funnel, public: the port picked the way the Funnel way in picks it (one already forwarding here, else the first free one of stream-settings.json tailscale.public_ports the tailnet allows), the rtmps:// address, whether it already forwards here and the trust anchor a camera imports for it (RTMPcert.pem, the public ISRG Root YE certificate), or why no port is free. The key is shown as <key> in every answer. Refuses a key, port or app of another shape, an output that is not a list of text and a funnel without a name or ports. It reads only its input and stream-settings.json: it starts no FFmpeg or Tailscale, opens no port, changes no Funnel setting, reads no saved login and sends nothing. The receiver's other work (taking the stream, showing the live picture, cutting it into pieces sent into the person's files, relaying it, following the person's stream rows) needs FFmpeg, a camera and the account and is not done by this run.

values.title: Plan what a sent deal sets up
values.job: Turn a sales contract's follow-ups into the rules and schedules that run them once the deal is sent: a paid follow-up for this deal only, a dated one at its time, with the deal's own words filled in
values.description: Give contract ({ id, name } of the deal being sent), facts ({ to, contract_name, contract_id, address }: contract_name and contract_id default to the contract's) and follow_ups (each { label, on: "paid" | { once_at }, then: { tool_id | workflow_id, input } }). Answers set: one { kind: "rule", input } per paid follow-up, its when the folder's paid-deal trigger (sales-contract-builder.json after_payment.trigger) with this deal's contract_id added, so one deal's payment never runs another's steps; one { kind: "schedule", input: { once_at } } per dated one. Words in braces in a step's input are filled only from the facts; any other brace stays as written. Also answers offered: the follow-ups the builder offers (after_payment.steps). It sets nothing itself (the person's automations owner keeps each rule and schedule) and reads no offer, customer or list: building the contract on the screen, reading the person's offers and customers, and sending the deal are not run here.

values.title: Point editor projects at clips' new places
values.job: On the person's own computer, point their Premiere Pro projects and DaVinci Resolve's open project at clips that moved to a new place, such as their Trillion files connected as a drive
values.description: Runs on the computer where the editors are. Rewrites each Premiere Pro project that names a moved clip so it opens the clip from its new place, keeping the original project beside it, and relinks the clips in the project DaVinci Resolve has open through Resolve's own scripting. A project that is open is left alone and reported. On a computer every Premiere project is found by Spotlight; elsewhere name the project files.

values.title: Post entries whose lines add to zero
values.job: Check an entry of signed lines adds to zero and answer it to keep, once per entry id, answer its undo as a new entry with every line negated, and list every entry in the lists that does not add to zero
values.description: action post takes lines { amount_field, group_field }, entry_id and rows [{ values }] (two or more); lines that do not add to zero are refused and nothing is answered to keep; the same entry_id posts once. reverse takes entry_id and reverse_id and answers the negated lines to keep; the original lines stay. Both answer the rows under `keep` for the caller to store; give the lists in `lists`. balance reads every line and answers the entries that do not add to zero and the lines with no amount or no entry (unplaced, never counted as zero). It reads only.

values.title: Post in a space
values.job: Share one item into a shared space as a member who counts there now, as its space item row, for the caller to store
values.description: Answers the new record:space-item row under `keep` for the caller to store. Only a person who counts as a member of the space now may post. Asking again with the same idempotency_ref answers the post already there and keeps nothing. The fields hold what the post says; author, space, time and revision are set by the run. It replaces the old create_group_post.

values.title: Post to Slack
values.job: Post a message to a Slack channel from a note, or anything picked
values.description: Posts your note, and a link to what was sent, in the Slack channel you name (channel: its name like #general, or its id). Uses your Slack connection, so connect Slack first and invite the app to a private channel. Returns what Slack answered; Slack saying no (a channel it cannot find) is told in its words.

values.title: Pour a kit's example rows into a list I already keep
values.job: Put the example rows that come with a workflow or tool into a list I already keep for the same job, matching its fields to mine
values.description: Reads one kit list (its fields, each with the names it goes by, and its example rows) and the person's own list (its id, row type and fields), both handed in by the caller from its own store. Reads and writes no store. Matches each kit field to one of theirs by the map they give, the same id, the same label or a name it goes by. Under the least share of matched fields (0.8 unless they ask for more) it pours nothing and names the fields with no home. Otherwise it answers keep: the example rows to add to their list, each { id, type, value, expected: null }, with ids <row type>:kit-<example id> so pouring twice changes nothing, leaving out rows already there and naming any choice value their field does not offer (not_an_option). The caller stores them; a store refuses a row that appeared since the list was read.

values.title: Predict how a viewer's brain responds to a video, second by second (runs on your computer)
values.job: See, second by second, where a video should hold a viewer's attention and where it goes flat, by predicting the brain's response to it
values.description: Runs a published brain-response model (TRIBE v2 by Meta FAIR) on one video on the person's own computer and writes curve.json and curve.png: the mean predicted cortical response for each second of the video, scored against the video's own average (z), the seconds where it spikes and the stretches where it stays flat. It is a prediction for an average viewer, not a measured view count or retention: use it to compare two cuts of the same video, never two different videos. Every model name, which of picture, sound and words to use, the device, and the spike and flat thresholds are fields of the request. The model's weights are licensed for non-commercial use only (CC-BY-NC-4.0); the person must be using it that way. The video is only read: the script works on a copy. Nothing leaves the computer.

values.title: Premix a motion film's soundtrack from its cue sheet (runs on your computer)
values.job: Mix my film's soundtrack: the music bed ducked under the voice, every voice line and every sound effect on the frame of its picture event, at the loudness I chose
values.description: The same premix as tool:plan-a-motion-films-soundtrack-premix, run with ffmpeg where the film's recordings are: writes the film's soundtrack wav (by default <film>/assets/soundtrack.wav), measuring the premix first when the film's loudness method is two-pass, and removes its work file. Answers where it wrote, the counts and the loudness it measured and reached. The film's choices (music, start, gain windows, fades, filter chains, loudness) are its settings row in list:settings.

values.title: Prepare a match pick prompt, a pick or a result to keep
values.job: Make the record for a free match pick prompt (a label and two or more choices), one person's pick, or a match's result, checked and trimmed, with a new id and the time, ready to keep
values.description: Give what (prompt, pick or result) and that record's fields. prompt: label, choices as [{ choiceId, label }] (at least two, each with its own id), startsAt?, matchId?. pick: matchId, pickerId, choiceId, pickId?. result: matchId, winningChoiceId, summary, resultId?. An id you leave out is made new; now is the time to stamp (else the clock). Give banned_terms (the person's own list) to refuse a prompt label, a choice label or a result summary that uses one of them. Returns { id, record }: the record to keep in the person's own store, in the shape tool:tally-match-picks reads. Nothing is written here. Refuses a missing field, a choice id given twice, an unknown what or a time that is not a time, saying which.

values.title: Prepare the notes a match plan is made from, and record the plan
values.job: Plan a match against an opponent: gather what the trusted notes say about both sides into the brief a plan is written from, then check and record the plan that was written
values.description: Calls no model: the AI that reads the brief writes the plan. context takes the person's records, who is self and who is the opponent, who asked, and plan_shape { strategies, tactics_per_strategy } (how many of each the person wants; both required). It returns a plan-request record whose promptText asks for exactly that shape and then lists what only the usable evidence says of each side, one line per fact: names, facts, style, strongest, weakest, strategies that worked and did not work (earlier tactic outcomes included), ratings out of 100 and any other fact in the profile. Missing facts are left out, never written as unknown. It also lists the ids of the public, private and to-be-reviewed reports, the profiles and the tactic results behind the brief. A report is usable only if the confidence policy allows it (confidence_policy, or an evidence-confidence-policy record in the rows); with no policy none is, and every report is listed for review. record-plan takes the written strategies (each { strategyId, name, tactics: [{ tacticId, label, reason? }] }) and returns the match-plan result record only if it has exactly the strategies and tactics asked for. Records come back for the caller to write; nothing is kept here.

values.title: Prepare sign-ups and payments to send back to Meta Ads and Google Ads
values.job: Send sign-up and payment conversions back to Meta Ads (Conversions API) and Google Ads so their bidding learns which clicks became customers
values.description: Off until a destination is turned on (on: true) with its account (Meta: pixel_id; Google Ads: operating_account_id, the customer id without dashes) and which outcome is which event (Meta: an event name like CompleteRegistration or Purchase; Google Ads: a conversion action id). Each conversion (visitor, outcome, at, value, event_id, email, phone) becomes one event carrying the click ids of the visitor's first touch (gclid, gbraid, wbraid, fbc, fbp; fbc is made from fbclid when absent) and the email and phone hashed with SHA-256 after each platform's own plain-form rule; the plain values never appear in the answer. The answer lists the sends, each a send to Meta Ads or Google Ads with its exact input, batched to the platform's limit, and the conversions skipped with why. Event ids are the conversion's event_id or project:visitor:outcome, so sending again is counted once; give each repeat payment its own event_id.

values.title: Prepare public content for people and discovery tools
values.job: Prepare one explicitly authorized public source page as consistent HTML, Markdown, structured data and discovery-feed data, with exact source versions and continuation state.
values.description: Takes a site identity, one bounded page from the existing current-public-view owner, its real source version and observation time, public document citations and one origin-relative route per document. A customer’s existing public List/share read enforces current visibility; this pure projector does not authenticate caller strings or create rights. Imported or model-written text is parsed as safe blocks and rendered through the existing structured page renderer. The complete flag, requestedCursor and nextCursor must match the owner’s actual paged result. Preparation never publishes or caches content.

values.title: Price a sale
values.job: Work out what a buyer would pay for one of my offers and one of its prices: what is due today, what repeats and when, with a trial, a per-unit count, a code or an amount they choose
values.description: Give offers (your offer rows), offerId, priceOptionId, checkoutAttemptId and checkoutStartedAt, and optionally adjustments (your code-adjustment rows), suggestions (your suggested-amount rows), checkoutCode, unitCount, customerSelectedAmountCents or chargeDimensions. Your AI reads the rows from its store and passes them; this tool reads and keeps nothing. Nothing is charged; the quote is the answer.

values.title: Price resource usage
values.job: Price measured resource costs from my versioned resource, plan and client rules or purchased snapshots, and keep one total with expandable detail without charging rollups twice
values.description: Give at (the pricing time) and either resource_id, with plan_id and client_id when they have their own rules, or a tree of measured costs, and the pricing rules to price from as rules (the rule versions manage-usage-pricing lists) or a purchased snapshot as pinned_terms. The answer is the one resolved set of terms, or the priced tree. This run reads no rows and keeps nothing.

values.title: Print a file
values.job: Print a file from the person's Trillion files on a printer their computer already has (paper size, fit to page, two-sided, colour, copies), so the person never opens a print dialog
values.description: Give file (its name in the person's files, such as /Projects/sample-card.pdf, or its identity); printer (from tool:printers; the computer's default when left out), copies, paper (the print system's size name, such as Letter, A4, Tabloid), fit (true to fit the page), sides (one-sided, two-sided-long-edge), color (color or monochrome), orientation and title when wanted. Returns printed, the printer, the job id and said. Large-format or many copies belong to a print shop (workflow:print-and-deliver).

values.title: Printers I can use
values.job: List the printers the person's computer can print to, and which one is the default

values.title: Turn one channel's rows of my packaging ledger into source DATA a word template can read (runs on your computer)
values.job: Make one channel's titles, thumbnail words, descriptions and hooks from my packaging ledger into a source I can build a word-for-word template from
values.description: Reads the ledger rows of one source key and writes an HTML file holding one inert application/json script block (id packaging) of records: a unit per video, then its title, description, each thumbnail word, the thumbnail analysis, caption source references (file identity, event range and time span, no caption text) and the opening and internal hook evidence and analysis. It also writes a spec (schema word-template-spec@1) whose html_json_records source points at that block, so tool:make-a-word-template can measure it. With --previous-html and --replace-video-id it refreshes only the named videos: every other record stays exactly as it was, the named videos' record ids and order are kept, records it does not own are kept, and an existing spec's lines, slots and custom fields are kept.

values.title: Publish a checked option preview, then put it in my watch folder (runs on your computer)
values.job: Move a finished option preview into its previews folder, and put it in my watch folder only after it was checked
values.description: action publish: moves work-round-<n>/pending/<id>.mp4 and its still into previews-round-<n>/ by a rename (a file the person can open is never written in place), only once ffprobe reads one video stream of the settings' frame size and one audio stream and the picture is as long as the spec's preview range. action watch: hard-links the published preview into the round's watch folder under the spec's watch name (a temporary link renamed over the old one, never left behind), only when the rendered-video check has measured that very file after it was made and the settings' content gate passes for the option; no content gate in the settings refuses it. The person's rule: never show an unfinished preview.

values.title: Publish what a saved view of my list shows into a file my site shows (runs on your computer)
values.job: Put the rows one saved view of my list shows (a changelog, the articles I marked public) into a file my website renders when it is next deployed, without opening my account to the internet
values.description: Takes the read of one saved view that my AI takes directly from my own store (one page holding the whole view: the rows its rules keep, in its order, with the list's fields) and a config naming the view's record id, and writes { schema, source: { view, list, blake3 }, fields, rows: [{ id, values }] }. With media in the config, the pictures and recordings the rows name are copied into the site's own static files under the BLAKE3 of their bytes (never twice) and the rows name the site's address. The BLAKE3 of the fields and rows is the file's key, so publishing the same rows again writes nothing. A read that holds only part of the view publishes nothing. It names no list, view or field.

values.title: Publish a post now
values.job: Work out queuing an approved post for immediate sending through each destination's existing send row and answer the post row to keep
values.description: Give post_id and expected_values (the complete approval_values snapshot reviewed for this action). It is refused if the post changed, is not approved, or is not ready for every destination. When ready, it sets the post's time to now and queues the existing at-its-time wake; this action itself sends nothing and does not say the post was published. The queued post row comes back under `keep` for the caller to store, and each destination's send row answers its own outcome. Repeating the same request while it is queued returns the existing state without arming another send. A destination whose outcome is not known is never sent again automatically. Give records: the post and the person's connection records. Returns post_id, status, post, ready, said and keep.

values.title: Publish a saved tool
values.job: Publish one of my saved tools as my listing, so anyone can find it in the marketplace
values.description: Lists one saved tool as this maker's listing in the database the request names. Only the saved version is listed, with its price (price_ref or a usage_price) and show_on_public_site (default false, so it is not on the public site). A saved tool with no sample-run check, or one that changed since it was checked, is refused.

values.title: Publish a site
values.job: Publish a website's pages and files so it can be given its own address
values.description: Keeps a site's files (files by path, index.html first, text or data: URLs; or site, the name of a site.json in your files such as copy_a_site leaves) under a new installation in your files, or a new version of one already published (installation). Returns the installation id, how many files and bytes, and a name its page title suggests. Give it an address with name_site or attach_domain. A site that already has an address also gets llms.txt, the list of its pages AI apps read, unless it ships its own.

values.title: Get one stretch of sound, or one picture, from a camera file in my cloud storage without downloading it
values.job: Get the sound of a few seconds, or one still picture, out of a big camera video I keep in cloud storage, reading only the small part of the file that holds it
values.description: Reads the MP4's box headers and its index (moov) by byte range, builds a sparse local copy with the same layout, asks ffprobe which byte ranges hold the audio packets inside the window (or the one key frame at or before the second asked for), reads only those ranges through the person's own reader program and decodes them with ffmpeg. Camera files run about 13 MB per second of footage, so this takes seconds where a whole-file pull takes hours and costs a few megabytes of storage reads instead of the file. The wav starts with silence up to the window's start, so second N of the wav is second N of the camera file. The request names the stored file's identity, the mode (window with from and to, or frame with at) and out (a file in the folder the person let this tool change). The person's own storage, kept in their list:settings row for this tool (settings_record) or given as settings: store (the store the reader is pointed at), account (the storage account id), reader {argv, cwd, env, ok_marker, retries, retry_seconds} (argv is a template filled with {store} {account} {identity} {out} {offset} {length}), credentials (names of environment variables the reader needs, set from the person's vault), gap (bytes; audio reads closer than this are joined). A key at the top of the request wins over the same setting. The tool never reads, prints or keeps a key; the reader program reads the storage itself.

values.title: Pull the messages from the Discord text channels my bot can read
values.job: Pull the messages from the Discord text channels my bot can read and hand them back
values.description: Reads the text and announcement channels of every server the bot is in (only those the bot may view and read the history of), newest messages first, and answers them folded into held: a message pulled twice appears once, an edited message replaces the older copy, and a renamed channel takes its new title. The bot cannot read anyone's personal direct messages, and a message's text is empty unless the bot has the Message Content setting. Give account (a name for this account, default "default"), and optionally limit, most_pages, most_threads. The held Discord bot token (name discord-bot-token) reaches the one process on a private pipe; it is never shown, printed or stored. Answers status (pulled; partial when some requests failed; needs_login when Discord did not accept the token; unreachable), the conversations (threads) and saved items (collections) that are new or changed, each exactly as the service sent them, how many new messages or items arrived, the cursor to hand back as held.cursor, and any failed requests in errors. It keeps nothing: hand in held (what earlier pulls answered) to fold into it, and keep the answer where you keep such things.

values.title: Pull the comments on my Instagram posts
values.job: Pull the comments on the posts of my Instagram professional account and hand them back
values.description: Reads the posts of the Instagram professional account the token belongs to, then each post's comments (through the Instagram Graph API, not by logging in as a person), and answers each post as a thread of its comments. Each conversation carries the service's own description of it (its participants) in source. A message pulled twice appears once. Give account (a name for this account, default "default"), and optionally limit, most_pages, most_threads. The held Instagram messaging access token (name instagram-access-token) reaches the one process on a private pipe; it is never shown, printed or stored. Answers status (pulled; partial when some requests failed; needs_login when Instagram did not accept the token; unreachable), the conversations (threads) and saved items (collections) that are new or changed, each exactly as the service sent them, how many new messages or items arrived, the cursor to hand back as held.cursor, and any failed requests in errors. It keeps nothing: hand in held (what earlier pulls answered) to fold into it, and keep the answer where you keep such things.

values.title: Pull the direct messages of my Instagram professional account
values.job: Pull the direct messages of my Instagram professional account and hand them back
values.description: Reads the conversations of the Instagram professional account the token belongs to (through the Instagram messaging API, not by logging in as a person) and the newest messages of each, and answers them. Each conversation carries the service's own description of it (its participants) in source. A message pulled twice appears once. Give account (a name for this account, default "default"), and optionally limit, most_pages, most_threads. The held Instagram messaging access token (name instagram-access-token) reaches the one process on a private pipe; it is never shown, printed or stored. Answers status (pulled; partial when some requests failed; needs_login when Instagram did not accept the token; unreachable), the conversations (threads) and saved items (collections) that are new or changed, each exactly as the service sent them, how many new messages or items arrived, the cursor to hand back as held.cursor, and any failed requests in errors. It keeps nothing: hand in held (what earlier pulls answered) to fold into it, and keep the answer where you keep such things.

values.title: Pull the Messenger conversations of my Facebook Page
values.job: Pull the Messenger conversations of my Facebook Page and hand them back
values.description: Reads the Messenger conversations of the Facebook Page the page access token belongs to and the newest messages of each, and answers them. Each conversation carries the service's own description of it (its participants) in source. A message pulled twice appears once. Give account (a name for this account, default "default"), and optionally limit, most_pages, most_threads. The held Facebook Page access token (name messenger-page-access-token) reaches the one process on a private pipe; it is never shown, printed or stored. Answers status (pulled; partial when some requests failed; needs_login when Facebook Messenger did not accept the token; unreachable), the conversations (threads) and saved items (collections) that are new or changed, each exactly as the service sent them, how many new messages or items arrived, the cursor to hand back as held.cursor, and any failed requests in errors. It keeps nothing: hand in held (what earlier pulls answered) to fold into it, and keep the answer where you keep such things.

values.title: Pull my Pinterest pins and boards
values.job: Pull my Pinterest pins and boards and hand them back
values.description: Reads the pins and boards of the account the token belongs to (needs a token with pins:read and boards:read) and answers each. It stops at the first page held already (held), so a pull after the first reads only what is new; a pin or board pulled again has its fields refreshed. Give account (a name for this account, default "default"), and optionally limit, most_pages. The held Pinterest access token (name pinterest-access-token) reaches the one process on a private pipe; it is never shown, printed or stored. Answers status (pulled; partial when some requests failed; needs_login when Pinterest did not accept the token; unreachable), the conversations (threads) and saved items (collections) that are new or changed, each exactly as the service sent them, how many new messages or items arrived, the cursor to hand back as held.cursor, and any failed requests in errors. It keeps nothing: hand in held (what earlier pulls answered) to fold into it, and keep the answer where you keep such things.

values.title: Pull the Signal conversations my client printed
values.job: Pull the Signal conversations my client printed and hand them back
values.description: Answers the conversations a Signal client on your computer printed (signal-cli output, handed in as conversations) as conversations, folded into held, with who the account is (self_id). It asks no one and holds no token: the Signal client holds its own login and the transport that runs it is a different row. A message pulled twice appears once, an edit replaces the older copy, messages stay exactly as printed in time order, and the cursor is the greatest message time seen, which the transport asks the client from next time. Give self_id and conversations, and optionally account (a name for this account, default "default"), held and most_threads. Answers status (pulled), the conversations that are new or changed (threads), how many new messages arrived, the cursor to hand back as held.cursor, and anything that failed in errors. It keeps nothing.

values.title: Pull the messages from the Slack channels my bot is in
values.job: Pull the messages from the Slack channels my bot is in and hand them back
values.description: Reads the public channels the bot is a member of, only the messages newer than the last pull (the cursor is the newest message time seen, and moves only when no request failed), and answers them folded into held: a message pulled twice appears once and an edited message replaces the older copy. Channels the bot has not joined cannot be read. Give account (a name for this account, default "default"), and optionally limit, most_pages, most_threads. The held Slack bot token (name slack-bot-token) reaches the one process on a private pipe; it is never shown, printed or stored. Answers status (pulled; partial when some requests failed; needs_login when Slack did not accept the token; unreachable), the conversations (threads) and saved items (collections) that are new or changed, each exactly as the service sent them, how many new messages or items arrived, the cursor to hand back as held.cursor, and any failed requests in errors. It keeps nothing: hand in held (what earlier pulls answered) to fold into it, and keep the answer where you keep such things.

values.title: Pull the messages my Telegram bot was sent
values.job: Pull the messages my Telegram bot was sent and hand them back
values.description: Reads the updates waiting for the bot (messages and edited messages in chats, groups and channels it is in), answers each chat as a conversation and moves the offset past what it read so Telegram does not send it again. A message pulled twice appears once and an edit replaces the older copy. A bot cannot read your own private chats. Give account (a name for this account, default "default"), and optionally limit, most_pages, most_threads. The held Telegram bot token (name telegram-bot-token) reaches the one process on a private pipe; it is never shown, printed or stored. Answers status (pulled; partial when some requests failed; needs_login when Telegram did not accept the token; unreachable), the conversations (threads) and saved items (collections) that are new or changed, each exactly as the service sent them, how many new messages or items arrived, the cursor to hand back as held.cursor, and any failed requests in errors. It keeps nothing: hand in held (what earlier pulls answered) to fold into it, and keep the answer where you keep such things.

values.title: Pull the posts I bookmarked on X
values.job: Pull the posts I bookmarked on X and hand them back
values.description: Reads your bookmarks (newest first; needs a token with the bookmark.read, tweet.read and users.read scopes) and answers each. It stops at the first page held already (held), so a pull after the first reads only what is new, and a bookmark pulled twice appears once. Give account (a name for this account, default "default"), and optionally limit, most_pages. The held X OAuth 2.0 user access token (name x-access-token) reaches the one process on a private pipe; it is never shown, printed or stored. Answers status (pulled; partial when some requests failed; needs_login when X did not accept the token; unreachable), the conversations (threads) and saved items (collections) that are new or changed, each exactly as the service sent them, how many new messages or items arrived, the cursor to hand back as held.cursor, and any failed requests in errors. It keeps nothing: hand in held (what earlier pulls answered) to fold into it, and keep the answer where you keep such things.

values.title: Put a booking on my calendar
values.job: Make the event for a booking on my own calendar and invite the people booked
values.description: Makes one event on the person's own Google calendar, with the person's own calendar account (the held value calendar-account), and has Google invite the attendees. A video call is made only when video_call_request_id is given, and is an error when Google made none. It keeps nothing: the AI notes the event's id and call link on the booking where the person keeps it. Answers created and the event's id and link, or error and why.

values.title: Put the option I picked into my FilmCraft project (runs on your computer)
values.job: Put an option I picked for my film into my protected FilmCraft project, and refuse any option I have not picked myself
values.description: Reads, from the rows the person's AI read from their own store and handed over as --stored (JSON {records}), the film's settings row (list:settings, record:setting:put-picked-options-into-a-filmcraft-project~film~<film folder name>, or the id --settings-record names: the protected project patterns, the option folders agents may edit freely, which stands count as a pick, the option kind and its text fold, the filmcraft-cli command and the apply log), laid over the script's defaults by tools/settings, and the person's stand on each option (the stance records tool:keep-where-you-stand keeps, named by tools/where-a-person-stands' own code). check says whether the option is picked: only the person's own stand that is one of picked_stances counts, the newest stand wins, and a recommended flag, a brief or a review note never counts. rows lists where the person stands on every option of the kind. apply checks, then runs `filmcraft-cli --project P --save run OPS` headless on the project (never the live app's control port; --print shows the command and runs nothing) and appends what it did to the film's apply log. The ops file must be inside the film's folder. A stand missing from the rows is no stand; a stand is a row the person's AI keeps, so the rows must be handed over exactly as the store holds them. A refusal says why on standard error and exits 1.

values.title: Work out which of my prepared records my account lacks (runs on your computer; writes nothing)
values.job: Take the records I prepared and the target records my store holds now, and say which to write, in small commands, and whether my store matches after the writes
values.description: Takes the result of tool:build-records-to-write and the target records (one record type and id prefix) that my store holds now, which my AI reads directly from my own store and hands in as held. It plans the writes: only the records the store lacks or holds with another value, or, when keep_held is true, only the records it lacks; or, with an optional previous-import baseline, source-field merges that keep live edits and deletions and report each conflict by id and field path. It returns commands of bounded size, each with a request key made from the BLAKE3 of its records. A record of a baseline refresh carries the value the store must still hold: the store's write has to check it and refuse any other value. The tool writes nothing: my AI writes each command into my store, then calls again with mode readback and the target records the store holds afterwards. A readback that differs is never all_equal. It reads no file, config file, keychain item or credential.

values.title: Quote a stranger's words safely
values.job: Make someone else's words safe to quote into what an AI reads, so hidden characters or a fake tag cannot sneak instructions in
values.description: Give text (another party's words: mail, an imported chat, a web page, a title) and, optionally, max (the most code points the quote may hold, ellipsis included; 8000 when left out). The text is normalised to NFC; control and format characters are removed (bidi overrides, zero-width characters, the byte order mark), except newline and tab; '<' and its full-width and angle-bracket lookalikes become '<'; then it is cut by code points, never inside a surrogate pair or an escape, ending with an ellipsis. Returns quoted and code_points. Never give the person's own words: only the copy handed to an AI is quoted, the original is not changed.

values.title: Make the private bit for a result
values.job: Turn whether something worked into the one noisy yes or no that may leave my account to teach everyone, so nobody can tell my real result
values.description: Randomized response in the person's own store: returns worked as the truth with probability e^epsilon/(1+e^epsilon) and the opposite otherwise, drawn from the platform's cryptographic random source. rules.epsilon is the pool's privacy loss (the pool's own settings). Keep the bit you got with the result it is for, so the same result is never sent with a new draw.

values.title: Rank candidate clips for each slot of my video with a small model (runs on your computer)
values.job: Rank the candidate clips for each slot of my video with a small model on my computer, and see how often its best is the one I would pick
values.description: Give slots (each with its candidates' frames and library text), method (siglip, decider-vision, decider-text, bge-text or qwen3vl) and model; optional reference ({slot: [candidate, best first]}) and reference_name give top1 and top1 within the reference's first three.

values.title: Match every video format I have collected to every idea I could film, and keep the best fits
values.job: For every idea I could make a video of, find which of the formats in my library suit it best, and record the best few per idea with why
values.description: Two steps. catalog lists every candidate format (each analysed item in the library's index, the title templates in a bank that name a form, and the person's own formats) and every concept (each concept heading with its beats and how many of its moments were found, and how many of those are on this computer or in cloud storage) as tab-separated lines for judges to read; the concept lines never name a format. apply reads judged files ({concept id: [{format, fit, material?}] best first}), refuses a format key the catalog does not hold and a concept nobody judged, and writes format_options (each judged option with its type, medium, library path, fit and the concept's moment counts), format_palette (every format some concept's options use, plus each plan's pick) and format_ranking_about into the titles file. The ranking is a reading of the whole catalog per concept by judges, not a model score: a cross-encoder scores topic, not form. Everything that belongs to the person (their form templates, stable format keys, their own formats, the package ids, which concepts to skip, the material wording and the about text) is their settings: a row of their list:settings (record:setting:rank-library-formats-against-concepts~<scope_kind>~<scope_id>, named by settings_record) read through tools/settings, with the run's own settings laid over it. Paths are inside the folder the person let this tool change (apply rewrites the titles file there). Run catalog, read every candidate against every concept (yourself or with judges), write each concept's best three to five formats with why to a judged file, then run apply; never pick a format by a model score, and never change the person's titles file without their say.

values.title: Rank my title ideas with a small model on my computer (runs on your computer)
values.job: Rank my video title ideas by how strongly a small decider model on my computer answers yes to my question about each
values.description: Give titles ({ref: title}), question (your yes/no question) and model (a decider snapshot). P(yes) is used only as a ranking.

values.title: Rank what is still open on a trip
values.job: Plan a trip: list everything still open across its schedule, packing list and bookings in the order to deal with it, with the one thing to do first and a count of open things per lane
values.description: Give the trip's lanes, each a list of rows (id, title, status, and optionally kind, group, day_order, day_date, starts_at, ends_at), and the person's policy: priority_order (the priority names, most urgent first, the last one meaning closed) and, for each lane, default_priority, priority_by_status (which status has which priority) and sort_by (the row fields that order things of the same priority, for example day_order then starts_at). A row with no status takes the lane's default_status. Returns every row with its priority, then the first open one as focus, the other open ones as later, and for each lane how many rows it holds and how many are open. Things of the same priority come lane by lane in the order the lanes were given. A row with no id is skipped and named under skipped. The tool knows no status and no urgency: a lane the policy does not cover, a priority name outside priority_order and a missing policy are refused.

values.title: Rank people by activity
values.job: Rank people by the points their activity earns, all time or over the last days, and give each person their level, like a leaderboard
values.description: Give each thing people did ({person, kind, at}), the points each kind is worth (weights), the counts to keep (metrics: {key, label, lookback_days}, null for all time), the levels ({level, name, min_points}) and which count ranks them (rank_by). Returns each person with their rank, points, every count and level, best first.

values.title: Rank poker hands and name the winner
values.job: Rank poker hands against a board of community cards and say which hand wins
values.description: Give the community cards (none to five) and each player's own cards (up to two), every card as its rank then its suit: ranks 2 to 9, T, J, Q, K, A and suits S, H, D, C, for example AS or TD. Each hand is ranked on its best five cards out of its own and the board, from high card up to a straight flush (an ace plays low in the lowest straight, five high). Returns the hands best first with the category and the five cards that make it, a place (hands that tie share a place) and the winners: every hand in first place. A hand with fewer than five cards in all cannot be ranked yet and comes last with no place. Refuses a card written wrongly and a card given twice.

values.title: Move events to where their words now play (runs on your computer)
values.job: After I rewrite the script, move every transition, graphic, caption or section break that was tied to a phrase to where that phrase now plays
values.description: A token in a piece can carry bound_to: the word or phrase it responds to, an edge (start or end of the phrase), an offset in seconds, optionally a slot (so an event tied to a swapped specific follows the new specific) and which repeat of the phrase. Given the word-timed transcript of the rewritten script, every bound token moves to where its words now play and keeps its length when it has an end time. Words missing from the new transcript leave the time unchanged and are listed as unmatched, never guessed. The binding names no medium, so it works for any timed piece.

values.title: Read a Codex run on this computer
values.job: Read a Codex run's output after a byte position and its state (harness/codex-runs.mjs readCodexRun)
values.description: Answers the run's state (running, exited with exit_code, ended or cancelled), the output bytes after the given position (whole UTF-8 characters only), and next, the position to read from next time. Refuses a run id that is not a codex run.

values.title: Read a computer
values.job: See whether a computer's machine is running and its health page answers
values.description: Reads the saved lease, the machine's state at the provider and the health page's HTTP status at the computer's public name.

values.title: Read a computer's price
values.job: See what a machine for a computer would cost each month before renting it
values.description: Reads the monthly price of the request's machine size at its location from the provider description's price request. Rents nothing.

values.title: Read a conversation
values.job: Read the messages of one conversation as headers, previews and labels, with no message text; read one message with read-a-mail.
values.description: Read the messages of one conversation as headers, previews and labels, with no message text; read one message with read-a-mail. Takes provider (an id of read-data/mail-providers.json) and connection (the person's account of that provider, by its handle only: {connection_id}). Runs as that account with the key the person's vault holds for it; the engine hands the key to this run alone and it is placed only in the request to the provider's own host, never shown. Answers the provider-neutral rows of read-data/neutral.mjs, never the provider's own payload. A provider that does not offer it says so in words.

values.title: Read a field's history as lines
values.job: Read one field's history of one row as lines a person reads: each value it held, from when until when, who changed it and by which road
values.description: Send list ({ id, fields }, the field naming keeps_history: true), row_id, field_id and kept (the row, with its _history). Answers steps [{ value, from, until, by, said }] oldest first, said being who changed it and by which road in plain words ("You via <app> over MCP"), and complete: false when older steps were let go or the first step's start is not known.

values.title: Read a funnel definition
values.job: Read a funnel that is written as stages pointing at workflow steps, offers, price options and measures, and see each stage's title, versions, price and conversion
values.description: A funnel definition is a list of stages; each stage points at records kept elsewhere (a workflow step that gives its title, a selection surface holding the versions being tried, an offer with the price option the stage shows, and measures that count who entered and who converted). This joins them: each stage's title, its versions with the decided one marked live, its price, its measures with where they came from, and the conversion percent from entered to converted. A stage whose record is missing stays in the answer with what could be read. A stage with several price options and no named option gets no price rather than a guessed one.

values.title: Read a link
values.job: Read one public link into a card: its title, picture, description, site and the words on the page
values.description: Reads one public http or https page (at most 2 MB, 6 seconds) and returns its title, picture (image, and every picture in images), videos, description, site name and icon from the page's own tags and structured data (data, its schema.org JSON-LD), and its readable text. A link that is itself a picture or video is that picture or video. A page that does not answer or says nothing about itself returns the bare address with unread saying why. It does not sign in.

values.title: Read a page of one of my lists or saved views, or refresh its row sources
values.job: Read one page of what one of my lists or saved views shows, from records handed in, or refresh a list's row sources (a folder of documents, for one) into keep rows for the caller to write
values.description: Reads a list (or the saved view and its list) from the records the caller hands in as stored.records: the list's rows are the records of its row type, and each row source's rows are among them, written there by an earlier refresh (row id <source>~<its id>), so a read reads no folder. A refresh reads each row source's folder on this computer and answers keep rows (id, type, value, expected) for the caller to write back: a store refuses a row whose expected record has moved. A page holds limit rows (read_page_rows when left out, never more than rows_per_read) and answers next as the record id to pass as after.

values.title: Read a whole message
values.job: Read one whole message: its headers, its plain text, the web links in it and the files it carries (names, kinds, sizes).
values.description: Read one whole message: its headers, its plain text, the web links in it and the files it carries (names, kinds, sizes). Takes provider (an id of read-data/mail-providers.json) and connection (the person's account of that provider, by its handle only: {connection_id}). Runs as that account with the key the person's vault holds for it; the engine hands the key to this run alone and it is placed only in the request to the provider's own host, never shown. Answers the provider-neutral rows of read-data/neutral.mjs, never the provider's own payload. A provider that does not offer it says so in words.

values.title: Read a draft
values.job: Read one draft as a neutral message (needs_original says whether editing it as plain text would lose attachments, formatting or a Bcc line).
values.description: Read one draft as a neutral message (needs_original says whether editing it as plain text would lose attachments, formatting or a Bcc line). Takes provider (an id of read-data/mail-providers.json) and connection (the person's account of that provider, by its handle only: {connection_id}). Runs as that account with the key the person's vault holds for it; the engine hands the key to this run alone and it is placed only in the request to the provider's own host, never shown. Answers the provider-neutral rows of read-data/neutral.mjs, never the provider's own payload. A provider that does not offer it says so in words.

values.title: Read one of my methods
values.job: Read the rows of one of my methods, a saved view over my method rows, a page at a time, each row with how strictly an answer to it is checked
values.description: A method is a saved view over the person's method rows (their files and the sections of their files, each row whole): the view's rules keep the rows, its sort orders them, and any mix of rows is a method. Reads the saved view `method` (the id of a record of type list-view) and answers a page of its rows in the view's order, each with its whole values and the strictness an answer to it is checked by (its own `strictness` value, else the method's, else the default cheap check), and `next` to pass as `after` for the following page, null on the last. A page holds at most `limit` rows (25 when not given) and at most the bytes read-data/method-rows.json allows. Reads only; it writes nothing. The rows are those of the list the view is over, read by the list reader's own rule filter, so the method means what the person's own view of the list shows. Answer what you read with tool:record-method-answers.

values.title: Read a network contact
values.job: Give a person another person's contact, only once an introduction between them is released
values.description: Answers the contact of the person named by `of`, to the person named by `subject`, only while an introduction between the two is in a released state: accepted, waiting for AIs, introduced or talked. Proposed, one yes, sent, declined, passed and expired are refused, and so is a stranger.

values.title: Read a page in my browser
values.job: Open a page in the person's own browser, signed in as they are, and read what it shows
values.description: Opens the page at url in a window of its own that is not brought forward, in the browser the person is signed in to, waits for it to load, reads it and closes the window. Answers { url, title, text, links } as the loaded page shows them, so a page that needs the person's sign-in or refuses requests from servers can still be read. Refused in words when no browser is connected to this computer.

values.title: Read a conversation summary
values.job: Read the summary kept of this conversation and whether newer messages have come since it was written
values.description: Give conversation_id (and app) and message_times: the times of the conversation's newest messages as the messages owner shows them (its newest page, like the last 100, is enough). Returns summary (null when none is kept yet), newer_messages (how many of message_times come after the message the summary covers through), stale (newer_messages above 0) and said, so a stale summary is never taken for the conversation's present. Give records: the summary's record. Changes nothing.

values.title: Read the settings a person keeps for a tool, for one person, film, piece or their whole account (runs on your computer)
values.job: Read the settings a person keeps for one of their tools, choosing the row for this piece, else this film, else this person, else their whole account, or make the settings row to write
values.description: A tool's settings are rows of the person's list:settings (record:setting:<workshop-folder>~<scope_kind>~<scope_id>; fields name, tool, scope_kind, scope_id, settings as JSON, from, status). read: give the records your AI read from the person's own store (or the path of the file holding them), the tool's folder and the scopes to try, most specific first; the answer is the settings of the first scope that has an active row, or the default given when none does. A row id given as settings_record is looked up in the rows handed in stored.records; with settings_record left out, the setting rows in stored.records are read. make: give the folder, scope, settings, name, tool and where the values came from, and the current rows in stored.records when they exist; the answer is keep: the row your AI keeps in the person's own store, with the list:settings row when asked, each with expected (the row as handed, or null when it was not there), so the store refuses a write made from a stale read. The same reader is a library for Python (read-data/settings.py) and JavaScript (read-data/settings.mjs) tools.

values.title: Read one treg call by its id
values.job: Read one of the person's treg calls by the id it answered: what it cost, and how an asynchronous task it started is going and where its result is
values.description: Give call_id, the x-treg-call-id header of a tool:call-a-treg-endpoint answer. Answers treg's own record of that call (GET /calls/<call id>): call (its endpoint, status and cost_charged_micro), async_task when it started an asynchronous task (status pending, settled, released or timed_out; reserved_micro, settled_micro, error, and once settled its result_url, which expires, or fetch_command), ledger (the money entries) and charged_micro. This is how a task is followed: treg itself polls the provider, so after a call answered 202 with _treg.outcome pending (its x-treg-async header says which statuses are final), read the call about 60 seconds later, then every 30 to 60 seconds, until async_task.status is no longer pending. Never send the call again or try another provider while it is pending: the task may still finish and charge. Reads only; spends nothing; the token is never shown.

values.title: Read a treg endpoint and its price
values.job: Read one paid endpoint in full before calling it: its price, the inputs it takes, how it is called, and the other providers that do the same job
values.description: Reads one endpoint of treg's public catalog by its id: endpoint.method and endpoint.input (its query or body fields, which are required, their notes), endpoint.cost (usd per unit, per call or per success, and a note on per-row charges), endpoint.async (a task that is polled, when not null), endpoint.observed (how often it worked, over how many calls, when it last worked) and siblings (other providers of the same job with their prices). An id it does not know answers 404 with near misses in detail.did_you_mean. Free and needs no token. Quote the price to the person before the first call of an endpoint, and pass a max_cost_usd to tool:call-a-treg-endpoint that the quoted price fits.

values.title: Get the words spoken in a video from its captions (runs on your computer)
values.job: Get the words spoken in a video as text, from the captions the video site holds for it
values.description: Runs on the person's own computer with yt-dlp, which fetches a video's captions (the automatic ones when there are no others) without downloading the video. The answer is { video_id, url, has_captions, char_count, transcript, status }: status ready with the words, or empty (has_captions false, with the reason in stderr_tail) for a video with none. The original spoken language is read first, then plain English. The video is an id or a link; --watch-base sets the address an id is put after. Nothing is sent to Trillion and no key is needed.

values.title: Read my AI apps and keys
values.job: Say which AI apps are connected to my account and what each one can reach, how long it may go unused and how many calls a minute it may make, my personal keys by their last four characters, my pursuits an AI can be given, and my webhooks
values.description: Give the account records: keys ([{ id, name, ending, created_at }]), grants (the sign-ins: [{ id, clientId, userId, createdAt, metadata: { clientName, reach, ceiling } }]), idles ({ sign_in: idle days }), calls ({ sign_in: calls lately }), spaces ([{ space_id, title }]) and hooks ([{ id, url, name, created_at, delivered }]). A part you could not read: send null. Returns apps, keys and webhooks_section, with every word and count the screen shows.

values.title: Read other AIs' setups
values.job: List, read only, the instruction files, slash commands and skills other AI apps keep on the person's computer, each with its text, so the person can bring them in as saved instructions
values.description: Give sources (ids from read-data/ai-setups.json: claude-instructions, claude-commands, claude-skills, codex-instructions, codex-prompts, cursor-rules) to read only those; all are read when left out. The places are under the person's home folder, which the person grants for reading. Nothing in those places is created, changed or removed. Returns items (each { id, source, kind, name, path, text, cut }, or unreadable with the reason when a file is refused: a link out of the home folder, a protected name, too big, not text) and sources (a count per source). Each text is cut at 2000 characters and says it was cut. To save them, hand the items to the account's saved_instructions with add_instructions and imported_from: ai-setups; that adds and never replaces.

values.title: Read a run of my AI command line as live events (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn the JSON event stream of my own AI command line's run into the same text, thinking, tool started, tool done and reply events, whichever command line it is
values.description: Reads one run's JSON event stream (Claude Code's stream-json, Codex's --json) on standard input and prints one normalised event per line: { kind: text | thinking | tool_start | tool_done | reply, text?, name?, id? }. Which line is which event is a row of read-data/ai-command-lines.json per command line; a line that is not JSON or matches no row is ignored. Nothing is started or changed: it only reads what the run wrote.

values.title: Read an email sending domain
values.job: See whether a domain of my email-sending account is verified, and the state of each DNS record it needs
values.description: Reads one domain of the person's email-sending account (Resend), by its id, with the key they connected: its name, status and each DNS record it needs with that record's own status. It only reads.

values.title: Read an export of my conversations
values.job: Read an export of the person's conversations (a chat app's saved messages, a mailbox page or email file, the Messages database, an AI assistant's logs or a captured web chat) from a folder they chose, and give each conversation's messages in order, ready to be kept as the person's messages
values.description: Runs on the person's computer over the folder they granted it to read, and reads only inside it. Give file (a path inside the folder). source names the kind of export (tool:list-the-kinds-of-conversation-export-i-can-read gives them); left out, the file is matched to a kind by what it looks like and a file two kinds could read is refused with their names. sources_file is a file in the folder holding the person's own kinds ({ sources: [row] }): a kind is a row of field names, so a new export is a new row, not new code. descriptor holds the run's own choices: mailbox_address (which address is the person's, for mail), expected_provider (for a captured web chat), source_ref (what to call this source), app (the name the conversations are kept under). mode all (the default) returns the whole export a page of atoms at a time (limit, cursor); threads returns the list of threads, newest first; page returns one thread's newest messages first from before_cursor, for a very large single log (session_id, limit). Returns threads and atoms (the canonical contract: each atom has a stable atom_ref that does not change when its words are edited), conversations ({ conversation_id, title, app, messages: [{ id, speaker, text, at }] }, speaker person, ai or the name the source showed, only what was said, a time only where the source gave one) in the shape the owner that keeps messages takes a chat read off its page, rejections (one structured entry for each thing the export could not give), next_cursor where there is more. Keeps nothing: hand conversations to the owner that keeps messages.

values.title: Read a spreadsheet, document or presentation as data (runs on your computer)
values.job: Read a spreadsheet (xlsx), a Word document (docx) or a presentation (pptx) into plain data: the sheets with their rows and typed cells, the document's paragraphs and tables, or the slides' text in presentation order
values.description: Reads one Office file without opening Excel, Word or PowerPoint. A workbook gives its sheets in their declared order, each with rows of cells (what is shown, and with --formulas also what was typed); a document gives its paragraphs, each with a selector like paragraph:3 that counts empty paragraphs too, and its tables; a presentation gives each slide's paragraphs in the order the deck declares, never file-name order. Which kind of file it is comes from the parts inside it, not the file name. The file is never changed. Flags: --formulas, --sheet NAME (other sheets come back as skipped), --max-rows N.

values.title: Answers over time
values.job: Show one person's answers to a form across every time they answered, in order, and the trend of one numeric answer, from the answer facts in the database
values.description: Give form_id, respondent_id and field_map (the name you want for each answer, to its questionId), and optionally trend_field (which mapped answer to chart; default the first that is numeric). The answer facts are read from the table answer_fact. Returns one row per time answered, oldest first, with the mapped answers and when; the numeric series for the trend; the latest row; and the count. A person who has not answered gets no rows. It reaches no database: give the person's form rows it reads as rows.

values.title: Read an app's TestFlight availability
values.job: Check with Apple which TestFlight and App Store routes a released app can be installed from right now, without changing anything
values.description: Give source_id (a configured release source, such as native-ios), the app's bundle_identifier and its testflight_groups. Reads App Store Connect with the release owner's held team key (app-store-connect-key: {key_id, issuer_id, private_key}) and answers the short-lived public observation: source_id, checked_at, expires_at and routes (each with its state, distribution_state, eligibility_state, reason, check and, when ready, action links on testflight.apple.com or apps.apple.com only). It never answers a tester email, the key or Apple's raw reply, and changes nothing at Apple. publish true is refused until the engine lets a tool save the release owner's device-distribution record.

values.title: Check by listening that every cleaned-up or re-voiced span still says the right words (runs on your computer)
values.job: Read back every span in a graded folder with a speech transcriber and count the words that differ from what should be said
values.description: Reads the part of each audio file between its handles with whisper large-v3-turbo and counts word errors (edit distance after lower-casing, dropping punctuation and spoken contractions) two ways: against a read of the untouched cut (same decoder, so only the audio differs) and against the span's text. A kept or remastered span passes with zero on either count; a cloned span, which speaks the text, passes with zero against the text. Writes work/verify.json with what was heard and lists every span under the bar. Single-word filler flips between two reads of nearly the same audio are listed, not hidden. It runs on the person's own computer, never on Trillion.

values.title: Read this account's business this month
values.job: Read what this account's business took in this month on the payment services it connected
values.description: The one read of the Business screen (tool:business). Returns since_words (the first of this month), service_names (the payment services whose money can be read), connected ([{label, state: read | none | unread, currencies: [{currency, code, multi, service_label, money_in, fees, refunded, net}] written in each currency, payments, more, at_most}], one per payment service, each read with the person's own account of it by running its money read, tool:stripe-events-read_money_since; a read that fails is unread, with no number) and operator (null: the operator's part has no owner here). Which services this account connected is read by running tool:list-connections with the connection_records and held_connections it is handed: a service it did not connect is not read and is drawn as not connected; when either list is not handed in or the listing cannot be read, no account is known to name, so each service says its money could not be read. A person who holds more than one account of a service is refused, with the accounts named. Reads only.

values.title: Read events from my calendar
values.job: Read the events in a time range from one of the person's own calendars, on whichever provider it is on, and give them back as time blocks
values.description: Asks the person's calendar provider (a row of read-data/calendar-providers.json: Google Calendar or Outlook Calendar today; a new provider is a row and an adapter file) for the events of one calendar between two times, every occurrence of a repeating event in start order, as the person, through their connected account, and gives them back as time blocks that read-time-blocks and lay-out-a-calendar-view understand. A cancelled event is marked cancelled; an all-day event is a date. It reads only: it never creates, changes or removes an event. The account's key arrives on a private descriptor and goes only to the provider's own host; no answer or error carries it.

values.title: Read my current screen look
values.job: Read this person's current worn screen look, look rules and day plan as the device token payload native screens draw
values.description: Reads this person's current worn screen look and returns the token payload native screens draw: every wearable look, the look now (including a scheduled blend), upcoming changes for twelve hours, and when to read again. `app_data` is the calling app owner's current look DATA: its starting look and themes, plan anchors/presets, and rule facts. Those values are supplied at runtime, never chosen by this generic reader. time_zone is required and must be an IANA zone. host, device, device_id and place are the facts this native screen says about itself; only saved rules matching those facts select another look. The person's own saved values (the worn choice, own themes, look-over-time plan and look rules) come in `saved`, read by the caller from wherever the person keeps them; it reaches no database. A missing personal choice uses `app_data.looks.start_with`. Returns `{ worn, worn_record, now, ahead, looks, read_again_at }` in the DeviceLooks token format.

values.title: How long deleted files are kept
values.job: Read how many days this person's Recently Deleted and Archived keep things before they move on
values.description: Takes keep_for, the person's own choice (your AI reads it from your setting:keep_for), or nothing for the defaults. states: each with its id, label, after_days (null: until put back), default_after_days and what happens when its time ends; choices: the usual numbers of days.

values.title: Show a folder of my documents as the rows of a list
values.job: Read the markdown documents in a folder I granted as rows: each document's frontmatter is its fields, with the file's name, folder, size, dates, links, tags and identity, a page at a time
values.description: Reads every .md, .markdown and .txt document under the granted folder (or `folder` inside it), skipping folders whose names start with a dot and links that point outside it, in name order, and answers one page of rows: { id (its path under the folder), title, identity (1f: and the BLAKE3 of its bytes), values } where values holds its frontmatter as note.<key> and its file facts as file.<key>. A page holds up to `limit` rows (200 by default, 2,000 at most) and answers `next` while more remain; pass it as `after` for the next page, so any number of documents is read. `match` keeps the documents whose path fits a glob such as */SKILL.md. `backlinks` adds file.backlinks, worked out over the whole folder. Nothing is copied: the documents are the rows. Optional content:true adds exact complete UTF-8 text including frontmatter in bounded linked pieces, keeping the original parent ID and metadata. Child pieces name their parent, part number and total; pass the opaque next cursor unchanged. No body is silently truncated.

values.title: Read how each version did
values.job: Sum what visitors did on each version of an experiment and work out the rate that decides the winner
values.description: Takes the recorded outcome facts for one experiment (views, clicks, conversions or any metric you track, per candidate version) and returns each version's totals. A rate you name (converted over views) is worked out per version, left out where either number is missing or the denominator is zero, and the version that leads on it is named.

values.title: Form results
values.job: Show who answered a form, the score each earned and the segment each was sorted into, with a count per segment, from the segment assignments in the database
values.description: Give optionally a form_id to see one form, or nothing to see every form in the table segment_assignment. Returns rows (respondentId, formId, segmentId, score, decidedAt), newest decision first, and a summary with the total and a count per segment. No assignments gives an empty list, never an invented one. It reaches no database: give the person's form rows it reads as rows.

values.title: Read how AIs are told to act
values.job: See the standing instructions every AI is given when it first connects, or read one of them whole
values.description: Answers the rows an AI is told on first connecting: with no id, each row's id, order, whether it is on, where it reaches and its size; with an id, that row whole. It changes nothing; a person switches a row off or adds a rule of their own with their own setting records.

values.title: Read Internet Archive item metadata
values.job: Inspect one Internet Archive item's original metadata, license, rights, collection and available file listing before deciding whether it fits an objective
values.description: Free, read-only lookup at Internet Archive's metadata endpoint. Accepts only an item identifier and returns the original metadata and available file listing, including creator, dates, collection, license/rights statements and access details when present. No media bytes are downloaded. Record the returned identifier and its canonical item page, https://archive.org/details/<identifier>, as provenance. Archive hosting or an available file does not establish permission to reuse. Missing or ambiguous rights stay unknown; independently check the item and collection against the intended use. The George Blood 78rpm collection states research, teaching and private study only and says copyright was not transferred; concert recordings need item-specific review too.

values.title: Latest answers as lines
values.job: Give the latest answers to a form as plain lines, each starting with the question it answers, ready to hand to a writer or a summary, from the database
