values.description: Give form_id and optionally respondent_id. The form is read from the table question_sequence and its answers from answer_fact. Returns lines: the most recent time the form was answered, one "Question: answer" line per non-empty answer (the bare answer when the question's label is not known). It reaches no database: give the person's form rows it reads as rows.

values.title: Read my link in bio page
values.job: Say what my link in bio page shows: whether it is on, its address for each place, my links, the posts it lists, and what people opened
values.description: Give page ({ on, code, name, title, about, links: [{ link_id, label, url }] }, null for no page yet), counts (the visit and open rows the page keeps), posts (my posts: [{ post_id, status, caption, link, destinations }]) and origin (the address the page is read at). Returns the page facts: on, address, addresses, links, posts, counts and the words the screen uses.

values.title: Show live matches, their scores and a tournament board
values.job: Show the current score of live matches for the scorer and for spectators, and a board of matches with their schedule, bracket, standings and leaderboard
values.description: Give the records of the matches (match records, score events, context links and board rows) and get every match, newest first. Each match has the scorer's view (every event counts) and the spectator view (no actor ids, and no tap that is still pending-offline). Events with one sequence number, such as an offline tap and its confirmation, count once: reconciled beats confirmed beats pending-offline, and the same state keeps the later one. The board lists each match with its score line and its linked schedule, bracket, standing and leaderboard rows; a finished match without standing or leaderboard rows of its own gets one row per side (win 3 points, loss 0). With match_id the answer also holds that match's view and the sequence number the next event takes.

values.title: Read who a message is from and its subject
values.job: Read who sent a message, to whom, its subject and when, with its labels and preview line. Its text is not included: read it with read-a-mail.
values.description: Read who sent a message, to whom, its subject and when, with its labels and preview line. Its text is not included: read it with read-a-mail. Takes provider (an id of read-data/mail-providers.json) and connection (the person's account of that provider, by its handle only: {connection_id}). Runs as that account with the key the person's vault holds for it; the engine hands the key to this run alone and it is placed only in the request to the provider's own host, never shown. Answers the provider-neutral rows of read-data/neutral.mjs, never the provider's own payload. A provider that does not offer it says so in words.

values.title: Read a meeting link
values.job: Read a meeting link through the declared meeting-app routes: which app it is for, what it asks (join, start, schedule, launch) and its parameters, with the host checked first and secret parameters hidden
values.description: Give link. Returns route, action, params (secret ones left out), secret_params (their names) and redacted (the link for logs). A link whose host is not on the route's list, whose action is unknown, or whose parameter is not in its form is refused with the reason.

values.title: Read my API descriptions
values.job: Read the tools my connected API descriptions currently offer
values.description: Reads the current native-selected source definitions and templates, derives OpenAPI tools, and retains conditional-read/backoff metadata in the current account. A source that is pending, unreadable or needs an unavailable connection is named with that state. Tools are DATA, never privately installed copies. The current native owner supplies and rechecks source/configuration, account and connection authority; request input cannot choose them.

values.title: Read my matches in a community, my profile, and the score job I owe
values.job: See who a community's matchmaker proposed for me and where each introduction stands, what my profile still misses, the shortlist my AI still has to score, and fellow members who share my categories
values.description: Reads one member's view (person): on (their switch), cadence_label, next_at, matches (each match_id, status and the community's words for it, answered, answer_by, consent: what to answer a yes with, with, why: the scoring AI's cited reasons, topics, space_id once they are in the one-to-one), profile (answers, categories, complete, missing questions), waiting_for_your_scores (the open round's shortlist with citable claims), discover (members sharing a category, with what they offer and seek), waiting_tasks (this person's own To do tasks, for their AI to pull: nothing is ever written into another person's account), wake_at (when the community's clock next acts, so the member side wakes then and pulls once), and for the community's owner experiments (each arm's introduced and talked counts and the shown and converted events an experiment owner reads). It writes nothing and keeps nothing: the caller's AI reads the community's records from a store and hands them in as `records`.

values.title: Read my groups and everything inside them
values.job: Show what is in my groups, lists or collections, with the groups inside them, in their order
values.description: Give roots: the addresses of the groups to start from, each { family, parts: { name: text } }. Each group is found among the records handed in (type group) and every member that is itself a group is followed, so the answer holds those groups and everything inside them at any depth. Returns groups (each { groupRef, memberOrder, members: { memberId: { memberId, nodeRef, role?, presentation? } } }, members in memberOrder), count, and skipped: the ids of records that were not a well-formed group or claimed another group's address. A root that is not a group yet is simply not in the answer. It changes nothing and reads no store: the caller hands the records in.

values.title: Read my saved bookmarks and pins
values.job: Read the bookmarks or pins a person saved on a social site (an export file of X bookmarks or Pinterest pins and boards) from a folder they chose, and give each saved item with its words, author and time, ready to be kept and found like anything else they read
values.description: Runs on the person's computer over the folder they granted it to read, and reads only inside it. Give file (a path inside the folder). source is x-bookmarks or pinterest-saved; left out, the file is matched to a kind by what it looks like. sources_file is a file in the folder holding the person's own kinds of saved-items export ({ sources: [row] }): a kind is a row of field names, so a new site is a new row, not new code. descriptor holds the run's own choices (source_ref: what to call this source). mode all (the default) returns the whole export a page of atoms at a time (limit, cursor); threads returns the list of saved items, newest first. Each saved item is one thread with one atom: the atom has a stable atom_ref that does not change when its words are edited. Also returns rejections (one structured entry for each thing the export could not give) and next_cursor where there is more. Keeps nothing.

values.title: Read my saved X posts
values.job: Read the posts I bookmarked or liked on X, newest first, with their full words, links and quoted posts
values.description: Reads the posts the person bookmarked or liked on X through X's API with the access token of their connected X account, newest first: each post's full words, who wrote it, when, its pictures, every real link it carries (not the short t.co form) and the post it quotes. Give already_kept (post keys the person already has) to stop at the first posts they already have. It reads only: nothing is posted, liked, followed or changed on X, and the token is never shown. When X refuses (expired token, a plan or credits that do not allow the list, a limit), it says so and gives no empty list.

values.title: Read my Signal messages on this computer
values.job: Read my Signal messages on this computer
values.description: Runs the Signal client (signal-cli) on your computer, which reads the messages Signal holds for this computer as a linked device, turns them into conversations (a group by its name, a person by the name their messages came with; your own messages sent from your phone are yours) and answers them the way tool:pull-my-signal-messages does, folded into held: a message read twice appears once, an edit replaces the older copy, calls stay calls, and receipts, typing, reactions and group changes are left out and counted. The computer fetches signal-cli and the Java it needs itself, the first time, from their publishers, checked against pinned hashes; nothing is installed and you do nothing. It must be linked once first (tool:link-signal-on-this-computer); until then it answers needs_link and starts nothing. Signal hands each message to a linked device once, so what arrived is written down on this computer before it is answered and handed in again if the run failed before answering. Give account (a name for this account, default "default"), timeout_seconds (how long to wait for messages, default 5), most_messages, most_threads and held, all optional. It keeps nothing.

values.title: Read my trading account board
values.job: Show my trading account: its value, today's change and goal, its own figures and what I hold, from the trading agent's last cycle
values.description: Give cycle: the fact the trading agent keeps as its last cycle (agent:trading-momentum.last-cycle), as the store holds it (its value_json) or the cycle object itself. It only reads what you give: nothing is kept, sent or read from a broker. It answers live (true when the cycle was given and reads), headline (value, deltaValue, deltaPct, deltaTone, goalLabel, goalProgressPct, equitySeries), account (the cycle's own scalar figures) and positions (one record per holding; an option contract carries its label, such as AAPL $150 Call · Jan 16 '26). Without a readable cycle it answers live false and says nothing about the account.

values.title: Read my treg balance and recent charges
values.job: Read how much is left on the person's treg balance and what recent calls were charged, to keep a run inside its budget
values.description: Reads the treg team's prepaid balance (balance_micro, in millionths of a US dollar), its credit blocks, amounts held for tasks still running, and its most recent charges. The balance is the hard limit on what any call can spend. Read it before a run's first paid call and after each step: what the run spent is the balance at the start less the balance now. Reads only; spends nothing; the token is never shown.

values.title: Read which treg team my saved key pays from
values.job: Read the treg team the saved key belongs to, with the team's number that its balance is read by
values.description: Asks treg who the held token is (GET /auth/me, the request the treg command line makes when it needs the team's number). The answer's org_id is the team number tool:read-my-treg-balance takes. Reads only; spends nothing; the token is never shown.

values.title: Read my YouTube Watch Later, subscriptions and playlists (runs on your Mac)
values.job: Read my YouTube Watch Later, subscriptions and playlists from my signed-in channels
values.description: Acts as each signed-in channel the request names (brand channels too, by page_id) through YouTube's own web API, with the browser login tool:export-browser-login-cookies-for-yt-dlp wrote, and writes <out_dir>/<slug>/watch-later.json, subscriptions.json and playlists.json. A channel naming sign_in_as (its account's email or channel handle) is found by it each run, since the account number a browser gives an account changes as accounts sign in and out. Reads only; never changes YouTube. Also tells which accounts the login holds (list_signed_in_accounts.py) and whether it is still signed in.

values.title: Show a folder of my account's documents as the rows of a list
values.job: Read the markdown documents in a folder of my account's files as rows: each document's frontmatter is its fields, with the file's name, folder, size, dates, links, tags and identity, a page at a time
values.description: The same rows as tool:read-documents-as-list-rows, read from the Namespace files the caller hands in as stored.files (every name under /, as text or {base64}) instead of a folder on their computer. A page holds up to `limit` rows and answers `next` while more remain; `match` keeps the documents whose path fits a glob; `most_bytes` ends a page at the last row whose answer fits. It writes nothing. Optional content:true adds exact complete UTF-8 text including frontmatter in bounded linked pieces, keeping the original parent ID and metadata. Child pieces name their parent, part number and total; pass the opaque next cursor unchanged. No body is silently truncated.

values.title: Read objects in an S3-compatible store
values.job: List the files in one bucket of the person's connected object store, or read one file, such as the pages of a site kept there
values.description: Lists one page of the objects of the bucket the person's connected S3-compatible store holds (Cloudflare R2 is one), or reads one object by key and answers its bytes as base64. The store's key, its endpoint and its bucket reach this run on private pipes; each request is signed and goes to that endpoint only. It writes and deletes nothing. A refused key means the person connects the store again.

values.title: Read the Panes and Feel settings
values.job: Show the Panes settings (how panes size and snap, with the rows a person edits) and the Feel settings (each moment and the feel it plays on touch, sound and motion)
values.description: Reads the starting pane sizes and their settings rows from tools/arrange-screens-in-panes/pane-sizes.json and the feels from tools/feel/records/feel-moments.json. Refuses a moment that names a feel the DATA does not define. Keeps nothing.

values.title: Read where each person's joints are in a video, frame by frame (runs on your computer)
values.job: Find the people in a video and where their joints are in every frame, so two movements can be compared
values.description: Runs a pose model on a video on the person's own computer and writes one file in the pose.keypoints.v1 shape: for each person (kept as the same id through the clip) and each frame, 17 joints (nose, eyes, ears, shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees, ankles) as x and y in pixels with a confidence from 0 to 1. A joint that is not found or is not a finite number is written as absent (0, 0, 0). A track already written for the same video bytes and the same pose model is reused. The model weights are the person's: a downloaded pose checkpoint passed by path; the script names and fetches none.

values.title: Posting calendar
values.job: Show what this person is posting between two times, and which drafts have no time yet, so a post can be given a time or moved to another
values.description: Give from and to (dates and times with their zone) and records (the person's post records). Returns posts: each post whose scheduled time falls in between (or, sent without a time, when it was sent), earliest first, with at, status, words and can_move; and unscheduled: the drafts and approved posts with no time yet. A post gets a new time through draft_post with post_id and scheduled_for, which makes an approved or scheduled post a draft again to approve. Its screen is the month and hour calendar, where a post is dragged to its time.

values.title: Read a prediction market's order book
values.job: See the buy and sell offers on one prediction market outcome: the best prices, the gap between them and how much is offered
values.description: Reads the public order book (no account, no key) of one outcome token and gives every bid and ask as price and size, the best bid and best ask, the spread, the midpoint and the total size on each side. Give token_id (one of a market's token_ids from tool:list-public-prediction-markets). The answer's status says live or error with the HTTP status; an unknown token or an empty book is an error with no levels, never invented ones.

values.title: Read price bars from my market-data account
values.job: Read recent price bars (open, high, low, close, volume) and the latest price for symbols from my own market-data account
values.description: Give feed (how your market-data account is read: url, its default query and the query names it allows, where each held field goes as credential_injections, where the bars are as bars_at, and what each bar field is called as fields with at least timestamp and close) and query (such as the symbols and the bar size, by the feed's own names). Answers bars (symbol, timestamp in milliseconds, open, high, low, close, volume), latest (each symbol's newest close, ready as the prices a trading policy's market orders need) and status (live or error with the HTTP status). An error answer carries no bars, never invented ones. The held market-data-credentials (a JSON object of named fields) reach only the request and are never shown.

values.title: Read a public web page
values.job: Open one public web page and return its title, readable text, links, the card it describes itself with, every picture and video it declares and its structured data; or walk an outlet's archive from a start address, following its older pages and reading a chosen, dated sample of its entries
values.description: Reads one public HTTP or HTTPS page and returns its title, readable text and links, and the card it describes itself with: its picture, description, site name and icon (each null when the page does not say), every picture (images) and video (videos) it declares in its tags and structured data, and that structured data (data, its schema.org JSON-LD objects). It reaches public sites only (the engine judges every address, every redirect and every address a name resolves to), follows a small number of redirects, limits the response to 2 MB and returns at most 30,000 text characters and 100 links. It does not sign in or reuse browser cookies. With walk it also walks the start address's archive: it reads the site's robots.txt first and obeys it and its crawl delay, follows the listing's next or older links (or a sitemap and its child sitemaps) for at most walk.max_listing_pages listing pages, collects the entries they list with the day each was published, chooses entries by walk.window (a first and last day) or by walk.eras (some of early, middle, recent: equal thirds of the time between the oldest and newest day the listings showed) with walk.count entries from each era or in all, and reads those pages one at a time with at least walk.delay_seconds (2 or more) between requests. Every request stays on the start address's own site. The answer is the start page's read with a walk object: the listing pages read, how many entries were seen and dated, whether the oldest listing page was reached, the eras, the pages read (title, text, day and where the day came from, era) and why the walk stopped. A count of 0 only measures the archive. With walk.source wayback the url is a page, not a listing: the walk asks the Wayback Machine's public index (web.archive.org, no login) for the snapshots of that page that were answered normally, one per walk.collapse period (year, month or day; default month) and inside walk.window when given, picks them by window or eras exactly as above, and reads each chosen snapshot as it was archived (the answer's pages carry snapshot_of, the address that was archived; their day is the snapshot's). Its robots.txt, delay and own-site rules apply to web.archive.org.

values.title: Read resource usage report
values.job: Read a usage report and distinguish provider acceptance from actual payment collection
values.description: Read a usage report and distinguish provider acceptance from actual payment collection. Takes the report row the caller read from its own store and answers it as the caller may show it; keeps nothing.

values.title: Read a resource usage settlement
values.job: Inspect a supplier-cost settlement and its original or corrected version, including exact customer amounts, company expense and unresolved funding, without moving money
values.description: Inspect a supplier-cost settlement and its original or corrected version, including exact customer amounts, company expense and unresolved funding, without moving money. Takes the settlement row and its allocation rows the caller read from the person's own store, and pages the allocations; keeps nothing.

values.title: Read rows as Marketplace shelf items
values.job: Show rows of one kind (tools, workflows, looks, layouts and more) as the Marketplace shelf shows everything my AI can use: title, what it does, who made it, its price and runs, whether it is mine and published, and whether I can use, publish or withdraw it
values.description: Give kind (one of the kinds in marketplace-kinds.json: tool, workflow, studied-screen, design-component, look, layout, configuration), rows (the source rows of that kind, as their own owner answers them) and published (the ids of that kind this account has published to the shared shelf). Answers items, one shelf item per row: id, key, kind and its label, icon, title (a row's own title when it reads as words, else the action its id names, with the service), job, made_by in the person's words, price and its key value and unit, runs, mine, published and its badge, facts, picture, preview, a link only when it is a web page, open_target, action_input and can (use, publish or withdraw); plus kind ({ id, one, icon }) and kinds (every kind). Which fields are read and how they read is the kinds file's DATA. It reads, publishes and withdraws nothing: reading each kind's rows from the person's store and the shared shelf, paging and searching across kinds, and publishing or withdrawing are the hosted Marketplace's routes and are not run here.

values.title: Read rows from a REST database service
values.job: Read the rows of one table in the person's connected database service, such as a Supabase project, with filters and an order
values.description: Reads one page of rows from one table of a project of the person's connected PostgREST service (Supabase is one): the columns asked for, filters, an order and a limit. The service key reaches this run on a private pipe and goes only to a project under a domain the tool's hosts file names (supabase.co), at that project's REST path. It only reads. A refused key means the person connects the service again.

values.title: Read my setup
values.job: Gather what my account's setup is made of and draw the Get started screen from it
values.description: The one read of the Get started screen (tool:get-started). It is handed this account's setup facts as setup_facts (sign-ins and their app grants, notification devices, the AI connection, computers, the setup runtime, device releases, the last setup snapshot: what the caller can read of them, since no one owner answers them now), is handed the account's own show rules (show-rules) and setup context (setup-context) as the caller read them from the person's own store, in stored.workspace, and draws the screen with tool:see-what-is-left-to-set-up's own function from them and the page's account id, in the same run. The setup run is handed in as setup_run (the status tool:run-workflow-definition answered and the answers so far), since no tool keeps a run. A source it could not read is left unknown, so the screen is not ready rather than opened on a guess. It writes nothing.

values.title: Read the anonymous shared entry of a decision
values.job: Read back the anonymous entry a decision was shared as, with the review it was checked under
values.description: Reads the anonymous shared entry tool:share-a-decision kept on a decision: its five shared fields and the review identity it was checked under. No goal, evidence or person field is read or returned. A decision that was never shared is refused. The caller hands in the decision's records as records.

values.title: Read my sharing and stories
values.job: Say whether my decisions are shared anonymously and my stories published, whether each is my own choice or the default and the day the default began, and how many decisions everyone has shared or published so far
values.description: Give the person stored choices and pool counts: share ({ anonymized: true|false } or null), stories ({ on: true|false } or null), sharedCount (number, or null when the pool could not answer), storyCounts ({ career: n, ... } or null) and storyRows ([{ name: story:<case>, value: { published, id, title, at } }]). Returns sharing { on, chosen, from_day, shared_so_far } and stories { on, chosen, from_day, published_so_far, stories }. A count the pool could not give is null, never zero.

values.title: Read spend rails
values.job: See which ways my AI may pay (card, bank, x402 and others) and which rail rows are refused
values.description: Reads the rails shipped with this tool and the person's own payment-rail records (a person's row replaces a shipped row of the same id). Answers each valid rail's id, label, whether it is turned on, the spend authority it spends from, the name of the credential it settles with and its settlement tool, and the rows refused because they do not go through the budget reservation and the spend record. It never shows a key.

values.title: Read the promotion codes in Stripe
values.job: Read the promotion codes and the coupons they give in your Stripe account, to see whether a code is active, how often it was used and what it takes off
values.description: Reads the promotion codes of your own Stripe account. Give code (one promotion code as the buyer types it), active (true or false) and limit (1 to 100), all optional. Answers each promotion code with its id, code, whether it is active, how many times it was redeemed and the most allowed, when it expires (Stripe's own time in seconds), its restrictions (first order only, minimum amount and its currency) and the coupon it gives (id, amount off or percent off, currency, duration and months, whether it is still valid, its own redemption counts), and whether Stripe has more beyond the list. A field Stripe did not send answers null. Only reads: nothing is created, changed or used up, and the key is never answered. Uses the Stripe key of the seller connection that seller_connection names (service_connection:stripe is your own).

values.title: Read the promotion codes in Stripe test mode
values.job: Read the promotion codes and coupons in your Stripe test account, to see a read work before it is run on the real account
values.description: Reads the promotion codes of your Stripe test account. Only a Stripe test key is accepted (it must start with a test prefix, checked before anything is built); it is the test key of the seller connection that seller_connection names. Give code (one promotion code as the buyer types it), active (true or false) and limit (1 to 100), all optional. Answers each promotion code with its id, code, whether it is active, how many times it was redeemed and the most allowed, when it expires (Stripe's own time in seconds), its restrictions (first order only, minimum amount and its currency) and the coupon it gives (id, amount off or percent off, currency, duration and months, whether it is still valid, its own redemption counts), and whether Stripe has more beyond the list. A field Stripe did not send answers null. Only reads: nothing is created, changed or used up, and the key is never answered.

values.title: Read everything one record is connected to
values.job: Read everything one of the person's records is connected to: its relations by side and role in order, everything that happened with it and when they were last in touch, and the records a few steps away
values.description: Give any record id (or me). relations groups what it is related to by side (subject: the relations it is the subject of; object: the ones naming it as the role) and role, each group in that end's own order with its order keys; side and role narrow it, ended adds ended relations. history is everything that happened with it, newest first, each saying the roles it took (as), with last_contact; history { with, kinds, role, since, until, limit } narrows it, false leaves it out. hops (1 to 4) adds every record within that many steps through relations and activities, nearest first, each with the step that reached it. complete false means a bound cut a part, so what is not shown is not known yet. It works from the rows given as records and reads and keeps nothing.

values.title: Read the Mac menu bar's own settings
values.job: Say the Mac menu bar item's own settings (on or off, how far ahead meetings count, how long its title may be, its app icon), each with the value it shows, and whether a change I ask for is one its setting allows
values.description: Give the Mac menu bar item's settings (enabled, how far ahead meetings count, the title's length, the app icon) from this tool's own row definitions: each setting with its value (the held answer's when the answer has the right shape, else its default), whether an answer was held, and the change when one is given and the setting allows it; a change it does not allow is refused. Reads nothing and writes nothing: the definitions are this tool's DATA.

values.title: Read records as time blocks
values.job: Turn any records that have a start and an end (bookings, scheduled work, reservations, events) into one ordered list of time blocks, and say which rows could not be shown
values.description: Reads each kind of record through a lens the person wrote: which field is the identity, the start, the end, the title, the colour, the state, and which fields point at other records. A new kind of record that happens in time is one more lens. Rows may be records or lists of cells (column N is the Nth cell). Gives back the blocks ordered by start, how many rows were read and skipped, and an issue for every lens that could not be used or has no rows. It can also read account records through account lenses, and show changes waiting to be written and changes that clashed as blocks of their own. It reads and shows only; it never writes a calendar.

values.title: Read transcript and caption files into timed words, and check quotes against them (runs on your computer)
values.job: Read a folder of transcript files (srt, vtt, txt, json) or a channel's downloaded YouTube captions into one timed-words shape, and check that quotes really are in the transcripts at the times they cite
values.description: Five readers on the person's own computer, none of which hears audio or reads the network. pick_transcript_files.py picks, from an asset index (JSON lines with root, ext, name, display_path, sha256), the files of one drive or library that look like transcripts (srt or vtt, or a name with transcript, _raw., _clean., _cleaned_up or _rag.), names each one's kind, and joins each to the person's file store by its sha256 (the person's file store's answer given as a JSON file, or a namespace sqlite copy opened read only), listing one the store does not hold as missing. read_transcript_files.py reads each listed file's bytes (or one file) into a words.json: srt and vtt cues, '## h:mm:ss.fff - h:mm:ss.fff' txt blocks with their source line, 'hh:mm:ss:ff' timecode txt at the frames per second given, or a recognizer's json with its words; it says whether the timing is per word, per segment or none, and keeps the whole text of a file with no times. caption_transcripts.py turns a channel download (raw/json3 caption files, raw/meta and raw/flat-videos.jsonl, as yt-dlp leaves them for tool:keep-channels-latest-videos-and-captions) into one [m:ss] paragraph transcript per video, preferring a video's manual English track, and an index of every listed video. find_whisper_quotes.py checks each quote cited from a whisper transcript: it finds the quote's exact words among the word times and says whether it starts inside the cited window. show_segments.py prints a transcript's segments between two seconds. Each prints its account and a last line {"result": ...}.

values.title: Read what a running app really shows
values.job: Drive my running app through some steps and report what is actually on the screen after each: which controls exist, what a click would land on, errors, timing
values.description: Opens the app at app_url in a headless Chromium on the person's own computer, does each step's `do` (the same actions as a walk: goto, click, fill, press, upload, wait, on a control named by role and name), then reads what the page holds as the step's `observe` asks: `elements` (for each match of a selector: its box, cursor, stacking, opacity, whether it is disabled, what a pointer aimed at its own centre would land on, and `pointer_is_self`, which tells a control that is missing from one a layer covers), `count`, `attributes` (named attributes and the form value), `text`, `global_path` (whether a dotted name exists on the page and its kind) and `media_ready` (milliseconds until a video or audio can play). It asserts nothing and fails nothing: a step that cannot complete comes back with `completed: false` and `blocked_by`, its readings are still taken, and the run goes on. The page is never intercepted or stubbed; requests reach the real server. Page errors and failed requests are listed. Use tool:walk-through-an-app-like-its-users to check that people can do what they came for, with expectations and a verdict; use this to see why something is not working.

values.title: Read what is on my screen
values.job: Read what the person is doing on their Mac as text from the front window (app, window title, page address and visible words), when they switch apps or windows and every minute, for a short watch, so their AIs keep continuity across the day. Never reads password managers, Keychain, Settings or private browser windows, and removes passwords, keys and card numbers on the Mac before anything leaves it. After a window's first read, later reads carry only the lines that changed. Uses no screenshots.
values.description: Runs on the person's own Mac for `watch_seconds`. It reads the front window's accessibility text (never a picture) when the front app or its window title changes and again after `tick_seconds` of the same window, and answers one capture per read: when, app, bundle id, window title, page address and `reason` (changed or tick). A window's first capture in the run carries its whole `text`; later captures of it carry only the lines `added` and `removed`. An app listed in the rules' never-read apps, a window whose title holds a never-read word, and a page whose address holds a never-read word are skipped before any text is read. Text matching the rules' secret patterns (private keys, API keys and tokens, card numbers, `password:` values) is replaced with [removed] on the Mac before it is returned. When Accessibility is off the answer is needs_access with the words that say what to turn on. Every list in this behaviour is the tool's rules file, read-data/rules.json. The run needs the accessibility-reading capability granted to this tool.

values.title: Read what is waiting on me
values.job: Gather every configured waiting source's cards from the records and reader results handed in
values.description: Reads the person's record:waiting-sources rows over declared source DATA and gathers each source's cards from what the caller hands in: stored (the person's record:waiting-sources rows and the records of each kind a source reads, each { id, type, value }, read by the caller from the person's own store) and pages ({ [reader tool id]: [result, ...] }, each reader tool a source names run by the caller, in order, following its cursor). Uses the same source-row aggregator as what-is-waiting-on-me. A source whose records or pages were not handed in, a store query the handed-in records cannot answer, and a failed, partial or bounded read stay unread; complete is true only when every declared source is read whole with no skipped cards. Answers sections, finishes, source coverage and problems. The tool reads and writes nothing.

values.title: Note new releases or commits from a repository (runs on your computer)
values.job: Read a person's release mark or commit branch, stage each new entry once with its source identity, and let their mapping make list rows
values.description: Reads settings the person gives: a program in the repository that prints JSON naming a release, a git ref for the newest release, or a commit branch where each commit is one entry. In commit mode, each entry has the commit identity, date and its own subject; the first run may start after an explicit commit, and skip_subjects are filters in the settings. The staged file is what the person's mapping turns into rows. The planner with keep_held plans only the rows the list lacks, so an existing row or a person's edits are preserved. The tool does not infer push boundaries or group commits by day, and knows no product, list or road.

values.title: Read where you stand on things
values.job: See whether a person agrees, disagrees or partly agrees with one thing made for them, in their own words, with every time they changed their mind
values.description: Two steps. First read the thing's stance record's history from the store the person keeps it in (id stance:<kind>:<identity>, newest version first, up to 100 versions a page, each page from the next of the one before, until next is null); this tool cannot read the person's store itself. Then give the versions of every page together and next from the last page, as the store gave them. Returns stand: its stand now (the newest version), said, why in the person's own words, by, at, version, earlier (every version before it, oldest first, a tombstone as deleted) and complete (false while next is not null: earlier stands not yet read are unknown); and choices, the stands a person can take. No version, a tombstone or a stand taken back reads stance null with taken_back: silence is not agreement.

values.title: Read Wikimedia Commons file metadata
values.job: Read one Commons file's original license, author, title, source URL and rights metadata for any objective before selecting it for use
values.description: Free, read-only lookup of one Commons File page. Supply its exact File: title from search or another trusted source. The request places the title in an encoded query parameter, follows MediaWiki redirects, and asks for the canonical file page, original media URL, dimensions, MIME type and full extmetadata. No media bytes are downloaded. The extmetadata may contain untrusted HTML; retain it as data and do not render it. A Commons page or media URL does not grant permission to reuse. Run the file-level assessor; BY-SA, NC, ND, missing, ambiguous or conflicting rights are ineligible for selection.

values.title: Read the words that may be shown
values.job: Read the words of a list that may be shown on a page: approved, consented to be shown, and unchanged since approval, as items for a page's proof section
values.description: Takes the list's rows and returns only those whose state is approved, whose consent allows showing and whose pin still matches the speaker, words and consent now in the row, as items {heading, body, row_id} that a sales page takes as a proof section's items (heading = the name as the consent says: whole, first name only, or the list's own anonymous heading). Every other row is counted in held_back by its reason (not_approved, changed_since_approved, consent_does_not_allow_showing) and never returned. limit keeps the first items. Returns items, shown, may_show_total and held_back.

values.title: Read the comments on a YouTube video
values.job: Read the top-level comment threads of one YouTube video, with each comment's text, like count, publish time and the commenter's channel id
values.description: Reads the top-level comment threads of one video (give its video_id), newest first, 100 to a page; give the nextPageToken the page before returned as page_token for the next page, until none comes back. Each thread carries the comment's text, like count, publish time, reply count and the commenter's channel id; YouTube is asked to leave out the commenter's display name and picture. A video with comments turned off comes back as a refusal from YouTube. To read many videos, run it once per video id: YouTube's comment threads are asked for one video at a time. It posts, rates and moderates nothing and changes nothing.

values.title: Rebuild a screen recording from its chunks
values.job: Keep a screen recording's chunks in order as they are recorded and rebuild the finished recording from them, with the file reference it is published with
values.description: Give chunks ([{ base64 } or { text }] in the order they were recorded; at most 1000 and 8 MB in all), and optionally recording_id (screen-record:<words>; one is made when left out), media_type (video/webm when left out) and observed_at (the ISO time each chunk is stamped with). Each chunk is kept through the folder's own store (do-work/recorded-file-store.ts) under the key the browser uses (<recording_id>:chunk:<sequence>), in a stand-in IndexedDB held only in this run's memory; then the file reference a finished recording is published with (kind local-playback.indexeddb-chunks, database, store, chunk_refs, media_type, byte_length) is built and the recording read back in order. Answers file, kept_keys and rebuilt ({ byte_length, media_type, identity: 1f: and the BLAKE3 hex of the rebuilt bytes, matches_chunks }). Refuses no chunks, a chunk with neither base64 nor text, too many chunks or bytes, and a recording_id or media_type of another shape. It captures no screen, keeps nothing in any browser once the run ends, and saves, names, removes or publishes no recording. The screen's other work (asking for the screen through getDisplayMedia, the recording panel, and publishing through the workflow actions in screen-recording-requests.ts, which needs the workspace's request sender) needs a browser and is not done by this run.

values.title: Rebuild the files derived from my records, or list which are stale (runs on your computer)
values.job: Rebuild the files that are computed from my source record files, or tell me which of them are out of date, without changing anything
values.description: Runs the builders a person's schema declares for files derived from other files (counts, merged lists, tab-separated tables). With --check it writes nothing and lists the stale files, exiting 1 if any; otherwise it rewrites them, or writes them under a folder the person names. Which files, builders and formats come from the schema.

values.title: Receive files pushed by a camera, scanner or printer over FTP (runs on your computer)
values.job: Receive the files a device pushes over FTP, such as a scanner, camera, drone or printer, into a folder on my computer, with nobody there
values.description: Starts a receiver on the person's own computer that speaks FTP (passive mode, and explicit TLS when a certificate is given) for devices that can only push files that way. Each file is streamed into the folder; when it is whole, a note named like the file plus .finished.json is written next to it with content_identity (BLAKE3 of the bytes on disk), byte_length, media_type, finished_at_ms and handed_over_by, and only then is the device told the transfer is done, so a half file is never seen as finished and a device that did not hear the answer sends it again. Only the senders the person puts in the settings file can push (a login, a password and the opaque name written in the notes); there is no built-in sender, and the receiver listens on 127.0.0.1 unless the settings give an address. A path outside the folder, active mode and deleting or renaming a finished file are refused. It runs until it is stopped.

values.title: Count how often the same kind of thing has been flagged, even in different words (runs on your computer)
values.job: When something is flagged again, file it under the earlier flag it repeats, or as a new kind, and say how many times and in how many sessions it has come up
values.description: Give memory_file (where the flagged shapes are kept), rubric_id (which question it was flagged under), excerpt (the flagged text), keep_characters (how much of a new flagged text to store) and optionally session and providers. Once an earlier flag exists you also give plainly_the_same_at (the word overlap, above 0 and at most 1, at which two texts are the same without asking anyone); with providers you also give pass_when_share_correct (the share of the earlier flags a model must file back under themselves before it is trusted) and same_at_least (the confidence at which a model's pick counts as the same kind). None has a default. The same kind in different words is a closed choice over the earlier flags put to a small model, which cannot invent a kind that is not on the list; at most 40 earlier flags, each shown as its first 300 characters, are offered in one question, because that is what fits a small model's reading window. With no providers only text at or above your overlap is a repeat, so shapes are overcounted rather than a repeat count inflated. Returns the shape, times, sessions, first_seen and repeat. The count, not louder wording, is what to tell the person.

values.title: Reconcile lines against a statement
values.job: Work out closing a set of cleared lines against a statement with any difference explained in words, answer a receipt of each close, find lines changed or removed after they were closed, and answer the undo of the last close
values.description: action close takes lines { amount_field, closed_in_field? }, row_ids, period, opening_balance, statement_balance, request_key and residual_reason when the lines do not add up to the statement; it answers each line marked closed and the receipt for "<lines>-reconciliations" under `keep`, for the caller to store. The same request_key returns the same receipt; a line already closed elsewhere is refused. check lists every line that changed or was removed after its close (record: true answers each as a discrepancy row to keep, once). undo answers the lines of the latest close reopened and its receipt marked undone; the receipt stays. Give the lists in `lists`.

values.title: Reconcile resource usage report
values.job: Recover an unknown usage charge by reading the exact provider invoice item without sending it again
values.description: Recover an unknown usage charge by reading the exact provider invoice item without sending it again. Give the frozen report an earlier answer returned (report), the cash and applied it was prepared from, and the provider invoice item id; the answer carries the next cash and applied to keep. This run reads no rows and keeps nothing.

values.title: Record a step with a customer
values.job: Write down a step with a customer, such as outreach, a reply, a booked call, a purchase, onboarding, a follow-up or feedback, as a record
values.description: Builds the step record, with a new id, its time, a label (a plain default for the kind when none is given), the outcome and each piece of evidence once, and returns it as step_record; it keeps nothing, so your AI writes the record to your store, where see-where-each-customer-is is given it.

values.title: Show me once
values.job: Record, for a short bounded time, what the person does on their Mac (clicks, typing, shortcuts, with the app and the control each was in) and give it back as a draft workflow in words an AI can keep after the person has looked at it
values.description: Give seconds (1 to 300; 30 when left out). The recorder listens only: it posts, blocks and changes nothing, and the stop key (Escape) ends it early. Text typed in a secure field is never recorded; the draft says a secret was typed. Answers draft ({ id, label, job, steps: [{ id, title, do, submit }], dropped_steps }), events_seen, secrets_skipped, ended (time, stop_key, most_events) and said. Without the Mac's Input Monitoring for the recorder the run is refused in words. Bounds and every step's words: read-data/demonstration.json.

values.title: Record a notice for someone
values.job: Record one notification event for the audience the caller names, so it is kept and can be read back; nothing is delivered
values.description: Pass the event: notification_id, kind, conversation_ref, privacy_class, title, body, occurred_at (words) and audience_refs, source_refs, proof_refs (each at least one reference). Optional actions are preserved in the told notice as its offered action definitions, including post:{path,body}, open:{surface_id,...} and press. operationId, transitionId and idempotencyKey are optional. No audience is inferred and no field has a default. If the person saved a notification-event-rules record (kinds, privacy_classes), kind and privacy_class must be among those it lists; with none, any words are accepted. The same event again changes nothing; a different event under the same notification_id is refused. Returns { notification_id, recorded, said }.

values.title: Record a decision I made myself
values.job: When I have already decided, keep my own verdict as the decision, with my exact words and when I said them, without my AI walking the method's questions
values.description: The person decided; this keeps their verdict as the decision. Only the person's own word is taken: person.message_id names the message row they sent (type message, speaker person) and person.said must be their exact words in it, or the run comes from their own signed-in page, which the engine attests as the task's origin and no input can set. An AI saying the person decided, with neither, is refused and told to answer the rows of the method (tool:read-a-method, tool:record-method-answers, then tool:make-the-decision), which every decision an AI makes still needs. The person's words are kept as an evidence row (person-verdict-<generation>) with where and when they said them; the decision and its root say decided_by person and method_walked false. A decision already made moves to decision_history. next_action and success_measure are what the AI will do now and how it will know it worked. The same verdict again replays.

values.title: Record a step on the work waiting to be published
values.job: Record a step on the finished work waiting to be published: change a field, link its proof, add a receipt that it was sent, correct it, or hand an action to whatever tool does it
values.description: Give graph (the queue as data; its actions are the person's own) and steps. Each step is { operationId, descriptorId (an action of the graph) or method (update-field, create-record, link-record, unlink-record, append-receipt, correct-record, archive-record or restore-record), recordId, fieldPatch, relationshipPatch, receipt, correction, expectedBasis, actor, observedAt, sources }. An action's patch, params and bindings apply; the record the step is about is offered to its bindings as the source named selected. A step on a local method becomes an operation and is folded into the queue: records get their fields and relationships added to, receipts and corrections are only ever added. A step whose action names a target or a definition is not done here: it comes back in handoffs with its inputs bound, for whichever tool does that job (for example the one that posts). A step that cannot be recorded (no operationId, an action the graph lacks, a method nobody declared) comes back in refused with a code and what was wrong; the other steps are still recorded. Returns operations, handoffs, refused and the queue as it now stands. The queue keeps no state of its own: read it with the tool that sees what is ready.

values.title: Record a spend
values.job: After my AI has paid, work out the new today's and all-time totals and the payment record
values.description: Adds one paid spend (whole cents) to the spend authority's total for today and for all time, read from the person's records, and answers the new totals and the payment record as `write` for the caller's AI to put in a store (this tool keeps nothing; the authority write is conditional on the totals as read). One payment is added once: sending the same payment_ref again (the operation_ref when left out) answers the record already kept and nothing to write. It records what was paid; it never authorizes a spend.

values.title: Record a demo of a web page
values.job: Record a web page as a demo video with a large clear pointer, click ripples and zoom, plus marked screenshots of each step for an article or post
values.description: Opens the address in a browser in the cloud and plays your steps on it the way a person would: the pointer travels to each target, clicks, types, scrolls. Returns an MP4 and a GIF with a large drawn pointer, a ripple at every click and the view easing in toward each step, a cover picture at the first click, and one picture per step with its target ringed, an arrow pointing at it and the step's caption. Pauses longer than a second are shortened. Works on any public page, and on a signed-in page when cookies are given; nothing needs installing.

values.title: Record an introduction state
values.job: Record one introduction's state (proposed, sent, accepted, declined, passed, expired, and the rest) in the person's own database, with the consent it was shown.
values.description: Records one introduction's state move in the person's own database named by `database`: a move the lifecycle allows, from the state it is in now, and a move to sent or one_yes only with the consent the introduction was shown. It records states only: it sends nothing to any person and sets no route, wake or notice. Live sending waits for the owner's word.

values.title: Record a checklist answer or run its checked steps (runs on your computer)
values.job: Record a checklist answer or run a declared checker or gate, with the required folder change grant
values.description: Uses the same checklist consumer as the read-only gate, but only after the person grants this tool permission to change one folder. It records the person's answer, imports a checker report under the reviewed checker pins, runs the schema's sweeps or gates, holds files only when requested, writes the checklist generated from the person's text, or records and removes source assessments in the existing applications DATA through `library-assess` and `library-remove`. Assessments require current source and work-context pins and preserve other contexts. The existing consumer still checks criteria definitions, BLAKE3 file pins, checker pins, scopes and stale rows; this tool adds no alternate answer or bypass.

values.title: Record my answers to a method
values.job: Record my AI's answers to any number of the rows of a method in one call, each with the rows it cites and the decision's evidence it rests on
values.description: Records answers to a method's rows for a decision: input { decision_id, method, answers: [{ row, answer, cites?, evidence_refs? }], by? }, any number of answers, each about one row of the method (tool:read-a-method). An answer is recorded only when its row is a row of the method, every row it cites is a row of the method, every evidence ref it cites is evidence of the decision (or one of the person's current pursuits), and it passes its strictness: an open value on the row, else on the method, else the default (the answer says something and cites a row or a piece of evidence), a rule tree in the vocabulary of the person's view rules. A review by an AI is asked only where the strictness says review: that answer is kept with review asked. Nothing asks a judge. An answer that fails is named with why and nothing of it is written; the others are recorded, so one wrong answer never holds up the rest. The same answer again is unchanged; a different one is the row's next version. Answers are records of their own, one per decision and row. Returns recorded, unchanged, refused, how many rows of the method the decision has answered and how many the method has.

values.title: Record my screen
values.job: Record one display or one window of the person's Mac as a movie the person chose, pause, resume and stop it, note the pointer (positions and presses, never keys) beside it, and save it only to a place the person's allow-list names
values.description: Runs on the person's own Mac. action start needs a source ({ kind: display | window, id }) that is there now; the first capturer row that this Mac has, that can take that kind of source and that can leave out the apps and window titles the person listed records it (a ScreenCaptureKit helper, then the system's screencapture). pause and resume reach it as its row says, or are refused in words. The recording ends by itself, saying so, when its source goes away. It is written as a 0600 file in a fresh 0700 folder; save moves it, and the pointer sidecar, to a path under the allow-list, never through a link and never over a file. prefs and exclude edit the person's own settings and leave-out list. status says what is recording.

values.title: Reframe a video to a new shape
values.job: Make a video vertical, square or any other shape, with the frame following the person or action
values.description: Crops the whole video to a new shape (9:16 for a reel by default) with the window following what moves in the picture, and saves the new video in your files.

values.title: Keep measurement history current
values.job: Collect configured operation evidence and return the observation and forecast rows to keep, on a timed or record wake without an AI
values.description: Takes the source configuration (config) and the forecast rows the caller read from its store (forecasts) in the request, runs the canonical collector and ledger checks directly, and returns checked observation and forecast rows with real OS CPU, wall and peak-memory measurements of this refresh. It creates no task and reads and keeps nothing; the caller writes the returned rows through its store. Missing or stale measurements remain incomplete; monetary cost remains unknown.

values.title: Refresh provider price book
values.job: Read the current version of the declared provider price DATA and return provider-qualified unit prices with source revisions
values.description: Reads the dated provider-price-source DATA through its owner. It returns only scalar prices explicitly marked eligible for unconditional evaluation, preserves provider, meter, currency, source and revision, and lists conditional rates as excluded. It does not infer account plans, invoices, usage or billed amounts.

values.title: Put Trillion in my AI apps' MCP settings, or take it out (runs on your computer)
values.job: Add Trillion's MCP server entry to the config file of each AI app I name, preview exactly what changes first, or take the entry out again
values.description: mcp-inspect answers what each named app has now (absent, registered, outdated, custom, blocked or not_installed). mcp-preview writes nothing and answers each file's exact before/after lines and a review_hash of the whole plan; mcp-register with --reviewed <hash> refuses every write when the plan changed meanwhile. An entry under the same name that matches none of Trillion's signatures is the person's own and is never changed or removed; every other key in the file is kept. An app not on this computer is answered not_installed and nothing is created for it. Writes are locked, backed up beside the file, refused for a symbolic link or a file changed meanwhile, and read back. The address is https, or http at the literal loopback host only. An entry is not a signed-in connection: each result names the sign-in still to do in that app. Each app's file, format and entry is a row of read-data/mcp-registration.json.

values.title: Register or end my Live Activity
values.job: Keep this iPhone Live Activity token so this account can update or end it
values.description: Pass board_key, the activity push token, app bundle id and environment. ended=true removes the token when the activity ends. Tokens stay private in your own records; the answer never returns them.

values.title: Register my notification device
values.job: Register this device to receive or read my notices
values.description: Pass route (web-push, apns, apns-activity or live) and the address its app received. For web-push, address is {endpoint,keys:{p256dh,auth}}; APNs routes use a hex token. Apple routes also need app (the bundle id); apns-activity also requires attributes_type, the receiving app’s exact Swift ActivityAttributes type and may set environment (sandbox or production). Optional label, can_show, turn_on and present describe this device. The stable device_id is returned; its private address is kept in your records and never returned. Repeating the same registration keeps its id. At most 40 devices are kept.

values.title: Regroup the segments of my plans (runs on your computer)
values.job: Rearrange the pieces of my video plans into groups: a new line to open each group, then the recordings I pick for it in the order I pick, each with an on-screen label if I want one
values.description: For each plan the person names, builds new segments from a shape: head segments kept as they are, then each group's lead segment (given whole, such as a voiced line) followed by existing segments in the order given, each taking the group's segment kind and its label, then tail segments. Indices are the plan's current segment positions (the outline step prints them). Every segment with a recording must be used exactly once, so no recording is dropped by accident. Writes the plans back and returns the seconds of recording in each group. Also: outline, each plan as a numbered list of its segments.

values.title: Regroup a folder tree the way I say, or turn it into groups
values.job: Move folders under other folders by their names, the way I describe it, or turn a tree of folders into groups
values.description: records is the tree as flat records { node_id, parent_id (null for a root), ordinal, role, title, external_identity, attributes }; a node with role group holds others. operation nest-by-intent takes intent { nest: [{ parent_title, child_titles }], scope?: { root_node_id?, applies_to_role?, depth? }, materialize_missing_parents?: { kind } }: titles are matched without case or outer spaces, only the named nodes move, two nodes with one title are a refusal for that row and never a guess, a missing parent is made only when materialize_missing_parents is given (its id from new_parent_ids[title] when you give one), and a row that would put a group inside itself is refused; every other row still applies. Returns records (the tree after), moved, created, refusals ({ row, reason, detail }) and untouched. operation tree-to-groups takes family and returns groups, unplaced (with why), group_count and member_count. It writes nothing: tool:change-my-groups keeps a tree as groups.

values.title: Rehearse a billing page in Stripe test mode
values.job: Make a test subscription in Stripe test mode and open its billing page, to see the billing page comes back before a real buyer needs it
values.description: Give product_name, amount_cents and return_url (an https address the billing page returns to). Only a Stripe test key is accepted (it must start with a test prefix, checked before anything is built); it is the test key of the seller connection that seller_connection names. Makes a test customer, product, price and subscription, then opens the billing page of that subscription the way the billing-page tool does, and gives back the subscription, the page's address and the card that pays it (none until a card is added). It never opens the address. Makes test objects only; no real money moves.

values.title: Rehearse a payment schedule in Stripe test mode
values.job: Build a payment schedule in Stripe test mode and see what Stripe says it will charge and when, before a real buyer meets it
values.description: Give payment_schedule and product_name. Only a Stripe test key is accepted (it must start with a test prefix, checked before anything is built); it is the test key of the seller connection that seller_connection names. Makes test objects only; no real money moves.

values.title: Free a held device again
values.job: End a hold on the person's computer now: apps can open again and Focus turns off
values.description: Give id to end one hold, or nothing to end every hold.

values.title: Release a host of the public door
values.job: Remove the server and SSH key one of my public door's host leases rented, and only those
values.description: Removes the exact server and SSH key the lease handed in as `lease` names, through the requests of the hosting row it was rented from (handed in as `hosting`), after reading each one back and checking it still carries this lease's label, and answers the removed lease. It keeps nothing: the person's AI stores the answered lease. A server relabelled to someone else is left untouched. Handed a lease already removed, it answers the removed lease. A box the person already runs is only forgotten, never touched. The hosting key comes from the vault by the row's vault name and is never shown.

values.title: Remove a sending key
values.job: Turn off one key of my email-sending account, by its id, so it can never send again
values.description: Removes one key of the person's email-sending account (Resend) by its id (the id tool:make-a-sending-key or tool:list-sending-keys answered), with the key they connected. Anything still holding the removed key can no longer send. The vault's copy is removed with the vault's own remove.

values.title: Remove my notification device
values.job: Stop sending or queueing notices for one of my devices
values.description: Pass the opaque device_id from my-notification-devices. The private address is removed from this person’s records. A device that later registers again receives its own id.

values.title: Draw a motion-graphics overlay for a video from a timed list of paper cut-outs, type, cards, charts and marks
values.job: Draw the animated graphics that go over a piece of my video (paper cut-outs, typed words, cards, charts, marker marks) as a see-through overlay with its sound, from a list of what appears when
values.description: Draws one spec, a list of timed events ({type, at, ...}: torn paper strips and cards, typed and kinetic words, count-ups, charts and labels, marker circles and underlines, cut-out photos, footage insets, endcards and many more, one module per event type in do-work/overlay/events/), into overlay.mov (ProRes 4444 with alpha), its sound stem sound.wav (every placed sound, plus the voice when the spec mixes one; sfx-only.wav then holds the sounds alone) and timeline.json (every element, sound and placed box with its time), or, with stills, single frames over the spec's still background. The look (colours, faces, paper textures, motion, sound table, title-safe margin) is the person's settings: a row of their list:settings named by settings_record, or settings, or settings_files. The spec is the request's spec (a piece row's settings.spec, which your AI reads from your list). Times are seconds from the overlay's first frame, or [word, offset] against the voice's word times. A render stops, saying where, when an element leaves the title-safe area or the last frame still shows something. The crumple exit needs Blender; a citation card read by OCR needs tesseract.

values.title: Render one frame of a square-grid pointillist film (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn a film script of square-grid pictures, a grid and a time into one packed frame of coloured cells
values.description: Takes a request file: the grid (columns, rows, gap), the limits and style bounds, the script (target pictures, one style per cell, and timeline segments whose weights are small expressions over time) and a time in seconds. Writes one packed frame file: the cells at that time, each with its colour, opacity and scale, in a fixed little-endian layout that begins PFCF. The same request always gives the same bytes. A request that breaks a limit or names a missing target is refused with a message and nothing is written.

values.title: Pack a square-grid pointillist film as one target-animation file (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn a film script into one compact file of its pictures and timeline at a frame rate, for a viewer that works out the frames itself
values.description: Takes an animation request: the grid, limits, style bounds, the script and a frame rate. Writes one target-animation file, whose first bytes are PFAT, holding the target pictures and the timeline (when each picture shows and by what weight) with the frame rate, in a fixed layout a viewer reads directly. The same request always gives the same bytes. A request that breaks a limit is refused with a message.

values.title: Render an edit
values.job: Render a video from an edit decision list: cuts, speed changes, reframing, captions, music and layouts of your files
values.description: Renders one edit in the media-composition edit format (spine.segments of clips with in, out, speed, speed_ramp, reframe, crop, fades; split layouts; subtitles.ass; audio_graph.music_bed; encode width and height). Every source is a file identity from your files. Saves the video in your files.

values.title: Render a correction insert for a film cut: its overlay, the voice and music stems, freeze plates and a preview in context
values.job: Make everything I need to cut a narrated correction into my film: the overlay, the narrator voice and the music and sound stem lined up with it, freeze frames from the camera clip and from my graded export, and a preview with a few seconds of my cut before and after, after checking its claims
values.description: For each shot (a spec with plate {source, frame}, graded_frame {export, cut_frame}, cut_insert_s and optional preview_before_end_s / preview_after_start_s), first runs tool:check-every-claim-against-its-facts-and-sources on it and refuses a shot whose claims fail; then writes into out/<shot id>/: <id>-overlay-prores4444.mov (ProRes 4444 with alpha), <id>-narrator.wav (the voice padded so 0 s is the overlay's first frame), <id>-sfx-music.wav (the music bed from the look's recipe.sound.music and every placed sound effect, same alignment), <id>-plate-slog3-prores422hq.mov (the camera frame held, ungraded), <id>-plate-graded-prores422hq.mov (the same moment from the graded export, held, to sit above the editor's adjustment layer), <id>-preview.mp4 (3 s of the graded export, the insert, 3 s after) and <id>-timeline.json. mode quick writes only the two stems and a 540p preview with the overlay piped in; audio_only re-renders the stems and preview against the existing overlay; stills writes frames over the shot's cut-out picture. A shot without duration_s lasts until its exit's light leak and its last word are done. specs renders a batch one after another under one lock; copy_previews_to copies each preview into a picker folder under a given name. The look is the person's look row (as for tool:render-a-motion-graphics-overlay); its insert section can give claim_check and preview_encoder.

values.title: Play back a music model's note transcription as a plain test WAV (runs on your computer)
values.job: Hear what a music transcription model wrote down: turn its notes into a test audio file I can measure
values.description: Test-only. Renders a music transcription's JSON note events (start events with a MIDI pitch, end events, drum hits) to a plain 48 kHz 24-bit stereo WAV: three sine partials per note with a short attack and slow decay, a noise burst per drum hit, peaking at half scale and lasting one second past the last note. The same events always give the same file. An audio meter such as earshot can then measure the playback beside the original, to compare transcription models. Code-made audio for comparing models, never a sound for a finished piece.

values.title: Render a run of frames of a square-grid pointillist film (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn one film script into a numbered file of packed frames, one for each time I list
values.description: Takes a sequence file: one frame request (grid, limits, style bounds, script) and the list of times in seconds. Writes frame-0000.pfcf, frame-0001.pfcf and so on into a folder, one for each time in the order given. Each is the packed frame the single-frame tool writes for that time, so the same file always gives the same frames. A request that breaks a limit is refused with a message.

values.title: Rent a host for the public door
values.job: Rent one server for my public door from my hosting service, or adopt a box I already run, and give me its lease
values.description: Rents one server from the hosting row handed in as `hosting`, through that row's own requests only, and answers the lease: the provider, the server and SSH key identities, the address, size and place, and the cleanup deadline of a test host (within one day; a retained service has none). It keeps nothing: the person's AI stores the answered lease. Handed that same lease back as `lease`, it answers the lease it already holds. A server with the same name that this lease does not own is left untouched. When the provider's answer is lost, it removes only the server labelled with this lease's name. A row with no provider API (a box the person already runs) is adopted at the address given and is never deleted. The hosting key comes from the vault by the row's vault name and is never shown.

values.title: Rent a machine
values.job: Rent a machine (or take one I already run) with a public name pointed at it, for another tool to set up
values.description: Rents a machine from the provider description the request names (or adopts a Linux machine the person runs, at its address), points a public name at it through the name provider description, waits until it answers SSH, and answers the lease, the public name, the machine's architecture and the monthly price. It sets nothing up on the machine: another tool (an engine builder, a computer) does that. tool:give-back-a-computer gives it back from the same lease file. Running it again resumes from the saved lease.

values.title: Change one piece of text in a file
values.job: Change one exact piece of text in a text or code file without sending the whole file: give the words to find and the words to put there
values.description: Give file (a path inside the folder the person granted for change), find (the exact text, as it is in the file, newlines and quotes included) and replace (what to put there; empty removes the found text). The find text must occur exactly once: no match or more than one is refused and nothing is written, so a change that did not happen is never reported as done. Bytes are compared as they are: no pattern, no case folding, no whitespace tolerance. The file is replaced in one step after the full new text is written, keeps its permissions, and is left alone if it changed while the edit was prepared. A path that leaves the folder, goes through a link, is a folder or is not UTF-8 text is refused. Returns the file, its size before and after, and replaced: 1.

values.title: Change several pieces of text in files, all or nothing
values.job: Make several exact text changes across one or more text or code files in one go, so either every change is made or none is
values.description: Give edits: a list of { file, find, replace }, each as in tool:replace-one-piece-of-text-in-a-file. They apply in order, and a later edit to the same file sees the text the earlier ones made. Every find must occur exactly once at the moment its edit applies; if any edit is refused (no match, more than one, a path that leaves the folder, goes through a link, is a folder or is not UTF-8 text) nothing is written to any file and the refusal names the edit by its place in the list. Every changed file is written beside itself first and all are put in place only when none of them changed while the edits were prepared; each keeps its permissions. Returns each file changed with its size before and after and how many edits it took, and the number of edits. A person can also keep the edits in a JSON file and run the script with that file after the folder.

values.title: Report how a decision turned out
values.job: Tell Trillion how a decision actually turned out, in my words
values.description: Keeps the person's result of a decided decision: result (met, failed or unknown), summary, answered_by "person" (ask them). A failed result opens the decision for a new one. The same words again are kept once; source_ref and supersedes correct an earlier report. A claim is kept as the caller's claim; nothing here marks it verified.

values.title: Report on an accrual or a cash basis
values.job: Read the same rows on an accrual basis (by the date each row is due) and on a cash basis (by the date of each allocation to it) for a period, each figure naming its basis and the rows behind it
values.description: action basis takes targets { amount_field, date_field }, allocations { list_id }, from, to and basis (accrual, cash or both; the list's saved report_basis, else both, when left out). Answers each basis asked with its total, count and the rows behind it (capped, with truncated said). It reads only the `lists` handed in.

values.title: Report resource usage
values.job: Report exact reconciled usage once to its purchased subscription, and answer the retained fractional carry and, when the outcome is unknown, the frozen report to retry or reconcile
values.description: Report exact reconciled usage once to its purchased subscription, and answer the retained fractional carry and, when the outcome is unknown, the frozen report to retry or reconcile. Give the confirmed purchased billing agreement (agreement), the settlement and allocations a settlement answered (settlement), payer_id and seller_connection, with the cash and applied the last report for this agreement answered (cash, applied; leave them out for the first). The answer carries the next cash and applied to keep and the frozen report to give back as prior_report when the outcome is unknown. This run reads no rows and keeps nothing; it sends one invoice item to the person's own Stripe account.

values.title: Request a booking
values.job: Check a requested time is open and make the booking record for it
values.description: Checks that the start asked for is an open time (same rules as tool:find-open-times, with the existing bookings given in `bookings` counted), then answers one booking record; it keeps nothing, so the AI keeps the record where the person keeps bookings. It starts waiting for payment, waiting for the host to confirm, or booked, as the request says. When `bookings` already holds a booking with this idempotency_key, that booking is answered and no new one is made. A time that is not open is refused with the open times that day; a person who already holds a seat at that time is refused a second one.

values.title: Reserve a spend within budget
values.job: Before my AI spends money, check the spend against my budget and work out the reservation, or refuse it
