values.description: Checks one spend (whole cents) against the person's spend authority, read from their records: it must be turned on and active, and stay inside the daily limit and the per-spend limit. Answers approved and the reason, and the check and the reservation the spend carries as `write` for the caller's AI to put in a store (this tool keeps nothing); a refused spend is answered too, with its reason. A zero-cost operation is checked and fenced without using the budget. The same idempotency key while its reservation is current answers the first reservation again and nothing to write, and counts nothing twice. No authority record means every positive spend is refused. The limits are read from the person's own records, never taken from the caller.

values.title: Reset today's spend
values.job: When a new day starts (UTC), work out setting my AI's spend today back to zero
values.description: Answers the spend authority's total for today set back to zero the first time it runs on a new UTC day, and that day, as `write` for the caller's AI to put in a store (this tool keeps nothing); every later run the same day answers nothing to write. Answers whether it reset, the day and today's total. Meant to run on a schedule each day.

values.title: Resolve a brand
values.job: Pick the logo variant (wordmark or mark, SVG or PNG) a light or a dark page draws, from a brand kept as list rows
values.description: A brand is the rows of the person's brand list: one row per logo variant (name, brand, family, role wordmark or mark, format svg or png, background such as "black on transparent", url) and one selection row (role selection) naming the family in use. Give a request file: rows (as the list or the record store answers them), tone (light or dark) and, optionally, files_at (a folder with a copy of each asset under its address's file name). Answers the family in use and, for both tones, each role and format's variant (url, row id, and the local file when a copy is there). Making or changing a brand is writing those rows in the person's list; this tool only reads them.

values.title: Resolve a look
values.job: Turn a look's colour, size and font tokens into concrete values and the stylesheet a document carries, with the person's own font faces
values.description: Give a request file: look (the look record as its owner keeps it: tokens of {key, value, css_variable?}) and faces (the person's own font files: family, weight, style, file, relative to the request). Answers the look's concrete values by variable name (--accent-primary, --font-display and the rest), the font families the look names, which faces were written and which files were missing; with --css it writes one stylesheet: a @font-face for each named face, then the look's variables. Nothing about a colour or a font is in the tool: the look and the faces decide.

values.title: Judge cited code lines against their repositories at the cited commit
values.job: Check each citation (root/path:line-line@commit) against its repository: the line, or range, holds the quoted text, read at the commit the citation names, or at the root's ref when it names none. One verdict per citation, with the reason when refused.
values.description: The citation resolver (read-data/citation-resolvers.mjs with citation-resolvers.json) as a tool, so a workflow check can refuse a wrong citation with its reason. It reads only the repositories the resolver names, through git in their checkouts on this computer; a repository not here answers ok null, never true. The answer is { result: [{ cite, ok, why, against }] }.

values.title: Restore a conversation from the trash
values.job: Restore every message of one conversation from the trash.
values.description: Restore every message of one conversation from the trash. Takes provider (an id of read-data/mail-providers.json) and connection (the person's account of that provider, by its handle only: {connection_id}). Runs as that account with the key the person's vault holds for it; the engine hands the key to this run alone and it is placed only in the request to the provider's own host, never shown. Answers the provider-neutral rows of read-data/neutral.mjs, never the provider's own payload. A provider that does not offer it says so in words.

values.title: Restore a message from the trash
values.job: Restore one message from the trash.
values.description: Restore one message from the trash. Takes provider (an id of read-data/mail-providers.json) and connection (the person's account of that provider, by its handle only: {connection_id}). Runs as that account with the key the person's vault holds for it; the engine hands the key to this run alone and it is placed only in the request to the provider's own host, never shown. Answers the provider-neutral rows of read-data/neutral.mjs, never the provider's own payload. A provider that does not offer it says so in words.

values.title: Resume importing all my conversations
values.job: Bring in every conversation from every app found on this computer, continuing each source from where its last run stopped, until all of them are in my records
values.description: Runs on the person's computer over the folder they granted (their home folder). Every source tool:list-the-conversation-sources-on-this-computer finds here (or the ones sources names) is imported in turn the way tool:import-my-conversations-from-a-source imports one, each file from its cursor row. A run stops at time_box_seconds and answers more: true; run it again until more is false.

values.title: Retire a copied AI reply
values.job: Retire an AI reply a person recorded by hand when the transcript already kept the same reply, and keep the transcript's reply with its links
values.description: Give the copy's id and the reply's id, the evidence, and the rows read from the store ([{ id, type, value }]: the two messages and the thread index row when there is one). Answers the correction under `correction` and the rows that change under `keep` ([{ id, type, value, expected }]) for the caller to store. Nothing is retired unless the copy and the reply have the same text, app and conversation, are within two minutes of each other, and the reply has a source_ref.

values.title: Make a raw control byte in my source files searchable again
values.job: Rewrite a raw control character hiding in source files (which makes search tools skip the file as binary) as the escape that means the same character, so the file stays exactly the program it was
values.description: Give files: the paths, inside the folder the person granted for change, of the files to rewrite (names, never a search: finding them is the caller's job, with grep -a). A file is rewritten only when putting every escape back reproduces the original byte for byte and, for a file Node can parse, Node still accepts the result; otherwise it is left alone and the answer says why. Tab, newline and carriage return are never touched. A path that is a link, special file or leaves the folder is refused. Returns rewritten, left_alone and each file's outcome.

values.title: Roll up how much work is finished
values.job: See how much of a body of work is really finished, which items were said done with no proof, and what is blocked
values.description: Counts a work tree from its items' states: an item marked done with nothing anyone can check is counted apart as said done, never as finished, and a percentage typed into the tree is refused rather than trusted. Returns finished out of all items, the share finished, what was said done without proof, what is blocked and by what, and the open items nobody has decided how to build; as "checklist" it also returns the tree as a checklist.

values.title: Route buttons for a trip
values.job: Give one-tap buttons that open the route to a place in each maps app, from a start and through stops on the way
values.description: Give destination, and optionally origin, stops (places on the way) and mode. Answers one button per maps app, each { id, label, url }. Pure: it reaches no network. A new maps app is a row in read-data/get-there.json.

values.title: Pick which of my places holds the answer to what I am looking for (runs on your computer)
values.job: Given something I am looking for and a list of places an answer could live, say which place most likely holds it, how sure that is, and which to try next
values.description: Give looking_for (the text), owners ([{id, holds (what that place keeps), ask (how to look there), for_example: [texts that belong there]}]) providers (the models you can ask) and your three settings: pass_when_share_correct (the share of the owners' own examples a model must file back under the right owner before it is used, above 0 and at most 1; below 1 lets that share of mis-filed examples through), confidence_bands ([{at_least, then}], what to do at which confidence) and band_when_confidence_unknown (what to do when a model gives an answer with no probability). None has a default. The examples are the calibration: a model that files fewer of them back under their own owner than your share is refused, and one that meets it is used even if it mis-files a few. Returns go_to, confidence, what_to_do (the then of the band that confidence falls in), how to look there and then_try, the close seconds, so a near tie is looked at in both places. The model only chooses among the owners you listed, so its worst mistake is the second-best place to look.

values.title: Run one Composio action for a connected account
values.job: Do one thing in an app the person connected through Composio, as that account: run a Composio tool by its slug, or send one request to the app's own API for a field Composio's tools do not carry
values.description: Runs, with the vault's Composio key, either one Composio tool for one connected account ({action, arguments}) or one request to the connected app's own API that Composio sends with the account's held sign-in ({proxy: {endpoint, method, body, parameters}}), for example a post's trial settings that Composio's named tool has no field for. The account is named by its connection id, with the user id that owns it and, for a person's own user key, the project the connection lives in. Nothing here names an app, a tool or an account: the caller names them. The key goes only to Composio's own host and appears in no answer. What the action does is the action's: a publish publishes and a send sends, so a caller puts its own checks in front.

values.title: Run a game of Texas Hold'em at a table
values.job: Run a game of Texas Hold'em poker for a table of players: open a table, seat players, deal a hand, take each player's action, and deal the next hand
values.description: Keep the table's saved state (the room) and send it back with one operation each time. open-table makes a table in its lobby from a list of player names and optional settings (starting chips, blinds, blind mode and increase, most players). seat-player adds a player (only in the lobby) or reconnects one by id or name. configure-table changes the settings. start-game posts the blinds and deals every player two cards and the board. player-action is the turn of the seat to act: fold, checkCall, raise (with an amount) or allIn; a round that is over moves on by itself to the next street and then to the showdown, and the answer says in words what happened. next-hand moves the dealer on, raises the blinds by the table's mode and deals again. kick-player removes a player and deals again if a hand was in play. Every deal takes a seed (any whole number), so the same table and seed always deal the same cards. The room holds every player's cards: give a player only what view-a-poker-table-for-a-player returns. One pot is kept per hand: when a player who is all in has put in less than the others, the showdown still pays the whole pot to the best hand. Refuses an action out of turn, a request that does not fit the table's phase, and a room that is not a saved table.

values.title: Run a session step
values.job: Create, change, reschedule, fork, merge, cancel, supersede, confirm, close or ask feedback of a gathering I organize, keeping who came from where
values.description: Applies one named step to a coordination session and answers the next session (or, for supersede, the old one and its successor). The session carries its purpose, candidate times, places and modes, capacity plan, who may see and join it, and a lifecycle state, all as open descriptors the person names. Every step keeps lineage (which sessions it came from) and the provenance of who took part and what they preferred. Steps: create, update, reschedule, fork, merge (two or more sessions), cancel, supersede, confirm, record_no_show, close, request_feedback. A step that is not named is refused. Nothing is saved or sent: keep the answer as a record.

values.title: Run a workflow on the workflow engine, one step at a time
values.job: Run one of my workflows from its definition: walk its steps with the answers held so far, start the tool each next step names, tell every other step as waiting, and run again when an answer is told
values.description: The workflow engine as one WebAssembly component (tools/workflows/crates/workflow-component), run with no network, no secret and no door. A run is handed its definition by whatever started it, from where the person keeps their workflows: in its input, in its wake's switch input, or in the fact that woke it (definition and start_at). The engine walks it from the start with the answers held. A step that names a tool starts that tool as a wake effect, whose result (or why it failed) is told back as the fact workflow-step-answered, which runs this again with the answer. Any other step is told as the fact workflow-step-waiting with what it asks, whom, and told_as, the envelope its answer comes back in; the person's own wakes decide what it becomes (its wake a-step-is-waiting runs the definition its switch input carries, such as one that gives the step to its answerer as a task). A step that asks wake:arrive, the engine's own operation, is answered at once and told as the fact it gives ({kind, event_id?, payload}) when the run ends; a step inside a loop or a used workflow waits under its place in the run, so each item is a step of its own. Nothing is kept here and no store or tool is named. A walk that failed ends the run failed, in the engine's words. Its wake a-workflow-was-picked hears the chooser's workflow-chosen facts (a message seed, a matched condition) and a-kept-workflow-is-due the times a noticer tells for kept workflows (kept-workflow-due, a due-time waiter's change_kind); the definition their switch input carries decides which kept workflow, if any, each fact starts.

values.title: Run the command line an installed app keeps inside itself (runs on your computer)
values.job: Run the command-line tool that came inside an app I installed, without installing it again
values.description: Some desktop apps ship their own command-line program inside the app bundle (for example a Node script under Contents/Resources/app.asar.unpacked/node_modules/<name>/bin/) but never put it on the PATH. This launcher runs that entry as if it were installed: Node runs a .mjs, .cjs or .js entry, any other entry runs as itself. Every argument after the entry is passed through unchanged and the app's own exit code and output come back. Nothing about any app is built in: the person passes the installed app's path and the entry path inside it. A missing app or entry, or an entry that is not a program, is refused with exit code 2 and {"error"} on standard error saying what to pass.

values.title: Run the Better Auth sign-in server (runs on your computer)
values.job: Start the sign-in server: email and password, passkeys, and JWTs that anything can verify against its public keys
values.description: Starts Better Auth (better-auth-rs, the documented axum setup) on the port in settings.json. It serves sign up, sign in, sessions and passkeys under the base path (default /api/auth), GET /api/auth/token for a JWT (EdDSA, claims sub, iss, aud, exp, iat and the user's email and name) and GET /api/auth/jwks for the public keys. Sessions travel as the __Host-trillion_session cookie or as an Authorization Bearer token. Port, base URL, issuer, audience, passkey relying party, trusted origins and the SQLite file are all in settings.json; the secret comes from the BETTER_AUTH_SECRET environment variable and is never printed.

values.title: Run the official Better Auth sign-in server (runs on your computer)
values.job: Start official Better Auth: email and password, passkeys, two factor, email codes, magic links, API keys, JWTs, and the OAuth server MCP clients sign in through
values.description: Starts official Better Auth (the TypeScript library, set up as https://www.better-auth.com/docs shows) on node with a shared Postgres store (Better Auth's Kysely PostgreSQL adapter), so any number of these processes serve one sign-in. Plugins: email and password with password reset, passkey, two factor (TOTP and backup codes), email OTP, magic link, multi session, API keys, JWT (EdDSA, keys at {base_path}/jwks), MCP (the OAuth 2.1 authorization server for MCP clients, with Client ID Metadata Documents; discovery at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server and /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource) device authorization, and bearer (so a device's session token works as Authorization: Bearer, as the device docs require). MCP access tokens are EdDSA JWTs with header typ at+jwt, the JWKS kid, and aud naming settings.json mcp.resource (the MCP door's address). As the JWT docs require with MCP, settings.json disabled_paths turns off the session /token route by default; OAuth clients get tokens from {base_path}/oauth2/token. Port, base URL, issuer, audience, passkey relying party, trusted origins, MCP resource and pages, the SQLite file, the session cookie name (__Host-trillion_session) and where email goes are all in settings.json; the secret comes from BETTER_AUTH_SECRET and is never printed.

values.title: Run SQL in my database
values.job: Run one SQL statement in my own database and see its rows
values.description: Runs exactly one SQL statement as written (sql, with params for $1, $2 and so on) in the person's own database, as the login the connection string names: the server refuses text holding more than one command, and a login that may only read (the read connection) cannot write, because the database says so. Give database, the name of one of the person's databases (the computer opens it with the login its vault holds as that name and -connection), or credential_name, the vault name the person saved the connection under (a login that may only read, for a share that may only read), and optionally statement_timeout_ms. Answers columns, rows and row_count, or the database's own error text. It adds no shape, no list names and no record types. With recipe instead of sql it runs a role recipe (read-data/role-recipes.json, the SQL that makes, grants and takes away a kind of login) as the owner login, in one transaction unless the recipe says otherwise: create with role_credential_name makes that standing login with the password the person holds under that name; create with recipe.valid_until mints a login that stops working then and answers its connection once; drop takes a role away. The connection may name any server that speaks the Postgres wire protocol that this computer reaches on a local port it reports as own-rows-postgres.

values.title: Run a workflow definition (workflow engine)
values.job: Workflow engine: run a workflow definition of steps (asks, branches, loops, parallel steps, checks) with an input, using the answers known so far, and say where it finished or which steps are waiting for an answer
values.description: Give definitions (workflow-core definitions: id, name, kind "workflow", is_active, version, steps [{id, kind, config}], edges [{from, to, kind}]), the workflow_id to run, its input and answers keyed by step id (an ask's config.context.step_id) or ask name. Returns the run (status completed, failed or paused, each step's output) and waiting: the asks with no answer yet, each with the input the engine gave it. Call again with those answers added and the run goes on from there. Or give a recipe (or the person's record:workflow-recipe row with its record:workflow-step rows) instead of definitions: it becomes one definition, each step an ask of the tool it runs or, when it runs none, of the run's own actor (the binding context.actor.user_id), followed by the steps that judge its checks, and a recipe holding its own definition runs as that definition, from the step start_at names when one is named. A check fails the run with the engine's own words, naming the value. A listed workflow row (source:workflow-recipes) runs as this tool: given its id as row, the shipped recipe runs, the row's other fields (a wake's input) are the run's input, start_at there is the step the run starts at, and the answer carries the recipe's kit. Nothing is kept: the caller keeps the answers and calls again.

values.title: Sales contracts in my database
values.job: Save, list and read sales contracts as rows of a sales_contracts table in one of my pursuit databases
values.description: Saves a sales contract (contract with a name and optional primitives), lists one page of them newest first, or reads one by contract_id, in the sales_contracts table of the named pursuit database (the tool makes that table if it is missing). Nothing here fixes a price, a term or a billing period; a removed contract is not read and not revived by a save. Answers the saved or listed contracts with their times, or the database's own error text.

values.title: Sample shots and their frames from my format library (runs on your computer)
values.job: Sample shots from my format library spread over creators, or candidate shots for described slots, and cut each one's frame with the frame tool I already use
values.description: sample_shots_across_groups takes up to N videos round-robin over creators and evenly spaced shots of each (seeded); sample_candidates_for_slots takes, per described slot, candidates of the right kind from different videos; cut_sample_frames and cut_candidate_frames cut each frame at its middle second with frame_tool (an `evidence frames` command) and copy it beside the others. The library is formats/<creator>/<video>/shots.tsv with videos/<video>.mp4. Steps: sample_shots_across_groups, sample_candidates_for_slots, cut_sample_frames, cut_candidate_frames.

values.title: Make a form record
values.job: Check a form, a list of questions people answer, and keep it in the person's own database, so it can be asked and its answers checked
values.description: Give a form_id, an optional title and presentation, and the questions. Each question needs a questionId and a questionTypeId (a row in the question-type list: text, long text, number, rating, choice, a reference to a file) and may carry a label, required, options, its own validation rules laid over its type's, and an afterSaved hand-off naming an owner and an action. The form is kept as one row of the table question_sequence (the same form_id replaces the same row) and answered with how many questions it holds. It reaches no database: it answers the row to keep as keep.

values.title: Save a draft
values.job: Keep a plain-text draft: a new one, or the one named by draft_id replaced. Give from (the mailbox address), to (addresses joined by commas), subject and text; thread_id, in_reply_to and references make it a reply where the provider takes them. Nothing is sent. Run with the same request key to repeat a save safely.
values.description: Keep a plain-text draft: a new one, or the one named by draft_id replaced. Give from (the mailbox address), to (addresses joined by commas), subject and text; thread_id, in_reply_to and references make it a reply where the provider takes them. Nothing is sent. Run with the same request key to repeat a save safely. Takes provider (an id of read-data/mail-providers.json) and connection (the person's account of that provider, by its handle only: {connection_id}). Runs as that account with the key the person's vault holds for it; the engine hands the key to this run alone and it is placed only in the request to the provider's own host, never shown. Answers the provider-neutral rows of read-data/neutral.mjs, never the provider's own payload. A provider that does not offer it says so in words.

values.title: Save a stay
values.job: Offer or change a place a person hosts, in their own database
values.description: Saves one stay the person offers: a city or area (never a street address), a price (free, ask, or a per-night amount in cents with a currency) and whether it is active. Give database and person; stay_id changes one of their stays. A person can have at most 6 active stays; an inactive one is always saved. The stay is kept in this database's stays table. Refused when the stay is not the person's.

values.title: Save someone's interest in one email update
values.job: Keep the consent of a person who asked for one email if a course becomes available, without sending anything
values.description: Give email, consent (true only when the person agreed in the words of course.consent_text) and course ({ id, public_origin as an https site root, consent_text, consent_version, capture_only: true }) and source (optional). Works out the address's pending row with the words, version, time and source of the agreement and answers it in keep for the caller to write (records: the person's email-course-interest rows). Sends nothing, queues nothing; saving the same agreement again changes nothing. Answers { status: interest_saved, already_saved }.

values.title: Save a tool
values.job: Save a tool I built, so any AI signed in to this account can find it and run it later
values.description: Saves one tool (its descriptor and its code files) as a row of the saved_tools table in the database the request names. The table is made when missing. The descriptor is checked the same way a catalog tool is.

values.title: Save how someone writes
values.job: Save what you learned about how this person writes, for one kind of writing
values.description: Shapes what you learned into the voice profile of one kind of writing (kind, like post or email; leave out for a general one). earlier is the voice-profile the person's store holds for that kind (null when none), profiles_kept how many it holds. fields are named by voice.json's profile_fields; a field you give replaces that field, an empty one removes it, and the rest are kept. builds_on names the kinds of the profiles this one sits on, earliest first. Pass expected_set_at (the set_at you read) so a profile saved since is not overwritten. by is person only when the person saved it themselves. Returns profile, said and keep: the row the store writes, with the version it was read at.

values.title: Save your X bookmarks to your files
values.job: Keep the posts the person bookmarked on X in their files, newest first, so their AI can use them
values.description: Reads the posts the person bookmarked on X, through the person's X account that Composio holds: Composio's X bookmarks action, run as the person. No X token is kept in the vault for this. It keeps them as one file in their files. Give since (the newest key the last read answered) to read only the new ones; the answer says how many were read, how many are not kept yet, the newest key and the file's name. It reads only: nothing is posted, liked or changed on X.

values.title: Save the posts you liked on X to your files
values.job: Keep the posts the person liked on X in their files, newest first, so their AI can use them
values.description: Reads the posts the person liked on their connected X account through X's API (the reader in save-what-you-watch-and-read) and keeps them as one file in their files. Give since (the newest key the last read answered) to read only the new ones; the answer says how many were read, how many are not kept yet, the newest key and the file's name. It reads only: nothing is posted, liked or changed on X.

values.title: Say one narration line in a voice-cloning model, best of N per sentence (runs on your Mac)
values.job: Try a voice-cloning model on my narration line: keep the best of a few takes of each sentence
values.description: Evaluation take of one narration line in a voice-cloning model mlx-audio loads (Qwen3-TTS, Chatterbox Turbo, Pocket TTS, or another the settings name), cloned from a reference recording. Same units, pauses and inner-pause cap as the Kokoro take. Each unit is made N times and heard by whisper; the one kept has the fewest word errors against the unit's words, then the length nearest the median of the N. Writes the take and <take>.units.json (what each kept unit was heard as).

values.title: Say one narration line in a Kokoro voice, the natural way (runs on your Mac)
values.job: Say my narration line in a Kokoro voice with natural pauses, so I can compare voices
values.description: Evaluation take of one narration line in Kokoro-82M through mlx-audio: one generation per unit (a unit never splits a sentence), pronunciation fixed in the text as misaki [word](/IPA/) markup with the G2P language of the voice's accent, a silence the model makes inside a unit (an ellipsis) kept but capped at inner_most seconds, each unit's own edge silence trimmed, and units joined by the line's set pause_after silences. Speech is never slowed or stretched. Writes a 24-bit WAV.

values.title: Say a tool's hints in its description
values.job: Make a tool's description say in words what its read-only, destructive, idempotent and open-world hints say
values.description: Give tool (an MCP tool entry with description and annotations: readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint). Returns the same tool with one sentence added after its description for each matching rule (reads only; confirm with the person before removing; adds or sets only; reaches outside), in rule order. A sentence the description already says is not added again, and a tool with no annotations comes back as it is.

values.title: Say how this device stands
values.job: Work out how this device of mine stands (caught up, offline or still holding changes) as the device list to keep
values.description: Reads and keeps nothing. Takes one device's report: device_id (the id the device keeps for itself), state, waiting (the changes it still holds), at (when its writes last reached your store), title, kind and copy_id (the copy of your records it keeps), with your device rows as devices. Answers the report as the next device list (devices) for you to keep, and written: true; the list changes only when what you would see changed, or when the device's last catch-up moved by more than an hour; at most 40 devices are kept, newest first. When nothing changed it answers written: false and no list.

values.title: Say some lines in a voice model I am trying out, cloned from my reference recording (runs on your Mac)
values.job: Try a new text-to-speech model: say these lines in my cloned voice so I can compare it with the voice I use now
values.description: Evaluation only. Loads a voice-cloning text-to-speech model with mlx-audio on Apple silicon (for example a Fish Speech S2 Pro conversion), clones the voice from a reference recording and its transcript, and says each line given as <line id>=<text>, writing <line id>.wav (24-bit, the model's sample rate) per line into a folder, with how long each took. The same line ids said by the voice already in use can then be scored side by side (tool:score-how-alike-lines-sound-to-a-reference-voice) or played blind. Some models allow non-commercial evaluation only (the Fish Audio Research License among them): read the model's licence before using what it says.

values.title: Say what got worse since the last reading
values.job: Compare a reading with the one before it (this day and the day before, this week and last) and say which numbers got worse, so a schedule tells the person only when something did
values.description: Give measures, each { label, now, before, worse_when: "higher" or "lower" }. now and before are a number, a list of numbers (added up) or a list of items: value is the path to each item's number and key the path to its name, so a total also says which parts moved. missing: "zero" counts nothing found as none (for counts); otherwise a side that was not read is left uncompared. at_least is the smallest change that counts, scale divides both before they are shown (1000000 for microseconds to seconds) and unit is shown after each number. Returns worse (true when any measure got worse), measures (each with now, before, change, worse and the parts that moved), lines and said, the reading in words. Use it in a workflow after a tool that reads two periods, with an edge on worse to tool:tell-the-person.

values.title: Say what the Mac menu bar mark shows
values.job: Say what the Mac menu bar item shows right now: how many things are running, the newest one and how far along, the unread count, or the next calendar line when nothing runs
values.description: Give the person's records (each with title, kind, running, updatedAt and an optional progress value), the unread count and, optionally, the next calendar line. Returns the mark's message: its count, whether anything is working, how many are running, the now line (the newest running record with its progress rounded to two places, or the next line when nothing runs, or null) and the first eight running titles. Nothing is read or written here.

values.title: Say what was done about a decision
values.job: Tell Trillion my AI did the next step of a decision, or the exact wall it reached
values.description: Keeps, with the decision generation it carried out, that its next action was done (state done) or the exact wall reached (state wall: the file, field, refused command or missing credential), in what_happened.

values.title: Say where file sync stands
values.job: Say where the sync of a person's files on one computer stands: starting, synced, syncing, offline, conflict or error, why Trillion was not reached, and how many saves are still moving
values.description: Gives one typed sync status record from what the computer's change feed and write journal observed. The state is the first DATA row (sync-files.json sync_status) whose every condition holds; a failed ask is filed under the cause its answer status names (no_network, signed_out, storage_full, busy, trillion_unavailable, else refused). A feed that was never answered is starting, never read as empty or synced. Names, file identities and keys never enter the record: only counts, a cause and a status.

values.title: Say why each technique works, in words every other technique shares (runs on your computer)
values.job: Describe each technique I kept by why it works, what it changes, what it needs and what it produces, in shared words that let it combine with every other technique whatever medium it came from
values.description: For each technique row, a writer model proposes its mechanism (why it works, never naming a medium), the properties it changes (operates_on), its needs and what it produces, and the medium it came from, shown the nearest existing terms so it reuses them. Every proposed term then goes through the vocabulary's admission rule: the same words, or a term at least reuse_at close in meaning, is the same term (kept as an alias); a term below new_below is new; in between the writer judges. Each need is tagged with its closest property so one technique's change joins another's need. Returns the rows' fields with the writer's own proposal, the vocabulary to keep for the next call, what merged into what, and any row not read. Without a vocabulary it starts one from the measured lines.

values.title: Say words in my chosen voice with a speech model on my computer
values.job: Say words out loud in my own cloned voice or a natural neutral one, made on my own computer, and keep the sound in my files
values.description: Makes a sound of `text` with a speech model on the person's computer (read-data/speak.json programs and engines: mlx-audio with Qwen3-TTS for a voice cloned from a reference recording, Kokoro for the neutral voice), in the voice asked for, else the voice chosen for `place` or the chosen voice, else the shared voices in order; a voice that cannot be made is passed over with why. The sound is made at its natural pace and handed to the engine's declared Files output owner. Completion returns its exact byte identity only after persistence; retry an unavailable or unknown result with the original request key so generation is not repeated. The answer carries the place's speed for the player to apply with the pitch kept. The person's voices and places are their own list rows, which their AI reads from a store and hands in as `voices` and `places`; a voice row's `reference` is a file on this computer. This tool reads and keeps no records. Scratch is removed; the private output remains until delivery succeeds. Nothing is sent to a paid service and no system voice substitutes. It plays nothing: the sound is a file.

values.title: Schedule the next review of something being learned
values.job: Work out when a flashcard, drill, passage or any other thing being learned should come back, from how well the person just recalled it
values.description: Give the grade the person just gave, the item's state from its last review (leave it out the first time) and the person's own spacing policy: the starting ease, the ease floor, the gap after the first and the second success, the recall quality below which an item lapses, and a map from each grade word to a recall quality between 0 and 1. Returns the item's next state to keep and hand back at the next review, when it is due (a time and a date), whether it lapsed and the quality the grade mapped to. The grade is an open word the policy defines. A grade the policy does not list counts as a total lapse and is marked grade_in_policy false. With prompt_id and schedule_id it also returns the next schedule record to keep (the state, the day it is due and state due). The policy may be given as policy or found among rows by policy_kind. There is no default policy: a missing policy or field is refused with its name.

values.title: Schedule the later payments in Stripe
values.job: After a buyer has paid at the door, set up the payments that come later (a week on, a month on, then every month) in Stripe
values.description: Give payment_schedule (charges with amount_cents as text and days_after_signup, and an optional repeat), customer_ref, product_name and signed_up_at_unix_seconds. The first payment is taken by the checkout, not here. Uses the Stripe key of the seller connection that seller_connection names (service_connection:stripe is your own).

values.title: Keep score of a match point by point
values.job: Keep the score of a match (tennis, pickleball, padel or any game whose scoring a person writes as a rule): start a match, give a point to a side, undo the last point, type in a score, and link a match to a tournament, schedule, bracket, standings or leaderboard
values.description: Every answer is records for the caller to write; nothing is kept here. A game's scoring is a rule row (scoring-rule: ruleId, label, scoringModel with scoreUnit game or point, setsToWin, gamesToWinSet, tiebreakAt, pointsToWinTiebreak, winBy and, for a labelled ladder, pointLabels and advantageLabel). Rules for tennis, pickleball and padel come with the tool; pass scoring_rules to use the person's own. start-match takes a rule id, singles or doubles and the players of each side, and gives the match record and its first score event. score-point takes the match's records (rows) and the side that won the point, replays the log, and gives the next score event with the right sequence number: a game is won on the rule's points with its lead, a tiebreak counts to the rule's target, games make a set, sets make the match, and a point after the match is won is refused. undo-point writes the score before the latest event as a new event, because the log only grows. record-score writes a score the scorer typed in (whole numbers at or above 0). link-context writes a context link for a tournament, schedule row, bracket match, standing or leaderboard. A tap made offline is written with local_state pending-offline; spectators do not see it until it is confirmed or reconciled.

values.title: Score answers and pick a segment
values.job: Score a lead's or respondent's answers with your rules and pick their segment and follow-up, such as hot, warm or not ready
values.description: Adds up points for each answer by your rules (a value worth points, at least or at most a number, equal to a value, long enough, answered at all, one of a list), keeps subtotals under labels you name, picks the segment whose starting score the total reaches, and returns that segment's title, meaning, next step and follow-up steps. Every weight, threshold and follow-up is yours to set; nothing about a good lead is built in.

values.title: Measure how well a small model judges my rules on lines it never trained on (runs on your computer)
values.job: Check how well my trained model catches lines that break each of my rules
values.description: Scores the held-out test lines, the never-trained lines and the held-out set with a decider model, with or without a LoRA adapter, and reports per law: AUC of the probability of the failing answer on bad vs good lines, recall at the thresholds that fail 1%, 2% and 5% of good lines, the same with only written good lines, the share of other laws' bad lines it also fails, the held-out set's good lines failed (by kind) and bad lines caught, and each never-trained line's verdict. A line is scored per sentence and takes its highest probability. Given scores_from, it reports again from an earlier run's kept scores without a model. Fit the lines a gate uses with tool:fit-pass-and-fail-lines.

values.title: Score how much each line sounds like the voice it was cloned from (runs on your computer)
values.job: Check which voice model sounds most like the real speaker: score each line against the reference recording
values.description: For one or more folders of line recordings (one folder per voice model), scores how alike each line sounds to a reference recording of the speaker: the cosine of WeSpeaker ResNet34 voice embeddings (256 numbers), where same-speaker pairs typically score well above 0.5. Prints each line's score and the folder's mean, so two models saying the same lines can be compared. A score says how alike the voices are, not how good the lines sound.

values.title: Score a questionnaire's answers
values.job: Score the answers to a questionnaire, flipping reverse-keyed items and filing each item under its subscale
values.description: Takes a questionnaire (its id, the response scale, the subscales and their item ids, which items are reverse-keyed) and a person's responses. Answers one scored fact per response: the response, the scored value (a reverse-keyed item is reflected on the scale: min + max - response), its subscale and whether it was reversed. A questionnaire not marked validated, or marked banned, is refused: it will not be scored.

values.title: Score small models' frame labels against the labels I already have (runs on your computer)
values.job: Score the frame labels my small models gave against the labels I already have: agreement per field, the top mix-ups, how often a model is right when it is sure, a prior-corrected reading, and the always-the-most-common-value baseline
values.description: Give shots (the sample, each with reference labels, width and height), vocabulary, labels (the files the label steps wrote), reference_name, unknown, list_separator, thresholds, and optionally shape_field with shape_ratios (the field whose reference is the named ratio nearest the frame's own). Standard library only.

values.title: Score soundtrack variants of a film by ear at every cue (runs on your computer)
values.job: Score my film's soundtrack variants with earshot: critique, sync to the picture, and how well each sound effect reads at its cue
values.description: Each variant: earshot critique against the launch profile with the picture, timeline sync to the picture's cuts and the cue frames, realness, and a match z at every cue on the effects layer alone and in the full mix; merged into the scores file.

values.title: Score voice takes against the voice I want and recordings of it (runs on your computer)
values.job: Compare voice takes for pitch, realness, how well they match the voice I want and how close they are to my reference recordings
values.description: For every take in a folder and every reference recording: median pitch and its spread, realness, how well it matches the voice the person wants (in their own words) and, for a take, how typical it is of the references (three nearest), plus words per second when a <take>.words.json lies beside it. Writes one JSON file of scores, to choose a voice and a speed. It runs on the person's own computer, never on Trillion.

values.title: Score labelled or unlabeled passages, or one draft, with a writing-voice adapter
values.job: Score passages with a trained writing-voice adapter and report every probability, with the exposure of the passages to the training rows, or score one draft paragraph by paragraph
values.description: Runs on the person's computer that holds the decider model snapshot. Validates the challenge with the maintained validator before weights load, binds the adapter and its receipt by BLAKE3, keeps every row's probabilities and the audit of what the adapter was trained on, and never invents accuracy for unlabeled rows. Draft mode (mode "draft") scores one draft text instead: its settings come from the person's own settings row (settings_record, the row record:setting:train-and-evaluate-a-writing-voice-classifier~person~<them> as selected from their database; its settings.draft gives adapter, base_model, criterion, min_paragraph_chars and bar) or the request itself, and it loads the Workshop's own decider frame. It splits the text at blank lines, keeps paragraphs whose words (web addresses left out) are shorter than min_paragraph_chars as skipped, scores every other one with the same request a v3 row gets, and answers paragraph_scores and body_min (the lowest p_pass) with no decision, and hands on the person's bar when their settings give one; the caller's check compares body_min with it.

values.title: Scout an opponent from the notes on file
values.job: Look up an opponent: list the people scouted, and pull together everything on file about one (what they are good and weak at, what worked and failed against them, their style and ratings) and which notes are trusted enough to plan from
values.description: Give the person's records and an operation. search lists every subject that is not the person themself, with how many reports and profiles are on file and how many tactics worked and failed against them. profile (with subject_id) joins the subject's reports (player-report evidence), profiles (profile-projection) and tactic outcomes into one view: strengths, weaknesses, strategies that worked and failed, style labels, ratings (any name, numbers 0 to 100; a value outside that is left out, not guessed), public and private reports apart, and the outcomes of tactics from earlier plans. It also says which reports a plan may use: the confidence policy is { minimumConfidence, missingConfidenceIsUsable }, given as confidence_policy or as an evidence-confidence-policy record in the rows, and with none no report is usable (every one waits for review). A report's confidence is its source's, else its own. Nothing here names a sport: the words for ratings, styles and facts are the ones in the records.

values.title: List what can be done on the person's computer screen
values.job: List the actions this computer keeps for operating its screen, what each needs, and how to describe a target
values.description: Read-only and needs no permission; it reads the computer's own list.

values.title: Seal a paid file
values.job: Put a file I sell (a book, an audiobook, a course video) behind paid access so only buyers can open it
values.description: Encrypts one of the person's files with their paid-files key (AES-256-CTR, a fresh nonce per file), keeps the sealed copy in their files, and answers the file's paid-file row: the name buyers ask for it by, the sealed copy's identity, how it is sealed, the key's NAME and the access refs a buyer must hold (any one of them opens it). The key is handed to this run on a private pipe and is never in the row or the answer. This tool keeps no record: store the row it answers, and hand it back as paid_file to tool:give-a-buyer-a-paid-file-link and tool:open-a-paid-file-for-a-buyer.

values.title: Search everything I keep with one question (runs in a small container)
values.job: Search every list, record and file name I keep with one question, in one ranked list, without my own computer
values.description: Searches the records and file names the caller hands in (`records` and `files`, read by the caller from the person's own store) with one question, as a Workshop run: every kind of record (each kind ranked as its own lane) and the file names, merged by reciprocal rank into one list, best first. Each result has found_in (written for a record's text, name for a file's name), said (the text it was found in), score and address (the person's own record by id and kind, or a file by path). The run reads no store and changes nothing. unavailable names a lane that was not handed its input and why; pending names one still working.

values.title: Search everything I keep
values.job: Find anything in my account with one question across every list and file, by what was said, seen, named or written
values.description: One question over every record and file name the caller hands in, and each installed semantic index among them. The caller reads the person's records and files from the person's own store and gives them as `records` and `files`; this run searches them and reads no store, and changes nothing. Results are fused by rank, never by scores across models, with addresses (the person's own record by id and kind, or a file by path), places (said, seen, name, written), timed moments and their original evidence scores. Semantic-index-descriptor records are discovered automatically; no index choice is needed. places and sources narrow the requested search. unavailable names every source or model that could not answer (a source not handed in too); pending names work still in progress. A missing model leaves literal words usable. A model with an encoder in the settings (a picture model) is asked with the query vector handed in as query_vectors; without one this row runs that encoder (the one other tool it may run).

values.title: Search Freesound for free-licence sound effects (runs on your computer)
values.job: Find CC0 and CC BY sound effects on Freesound for each kind of sound I need
values.description: Freesound's public search pages, CC0 and Attribution only, within each category's length, most downloaded first; each item once per category. One request every 1.5 s; pages are read as text.

values.title: Search Internet Archive
values.job: Search Internet Archive for books, articles, audio, concerts, films, images and other primary sources, with license and collection filters and source provenance for any objective
values.description: Free, read-only Internet Archive Advanced Search. Supply Archive's query syntax; the request always adds NOT access-restricted-item:true and returns a bounded page with identifier, title, creator, date, year, media type, collection, licenseurl, rights, description and access-restriction metadata when indexed. Query examples: (title:tennis AND mediatype:movies); (creator:Example AND collection:georgeblood); (mediatype:audio AND licenseurl:*creativecommons.org*). A license URL or unrestricted access is evidence to inspect, not proof of permission for your intended use. Preserve the item identifier and source metadata; missing or ambiguous rights remain unknown. The Archive's George Blood 78rpm description limits use to research, teaching and private study and says copyright was not transferred; concert recordings also need item-specific rights review. Search results only; this does not download or save media.

values.title: Search Mixkit for free sound effects (runs on your computer)
values.job: Find Mixkit sound effects on its tag pages for each kind of sound I need
values.description: Mixkit tag pages per category, each item once, within the category's length. One request every 1.5 s; a missing tag page is reported and skipped.

values.title: Search one of my lists with one question
values.job: Find the rows of one of my lists that hold the words I ask, best match first, however far down the list they are
values.description: Searches the records of one kind (one list) the caller hands in as `records` (read from the person's own store, that kind only) with one question: the rows holding every asked word, best first, each with said (the text it was found in), score and address (the person's own record, by id and kind). The whole list handed in is searched in one call, never one page at a time. This run is given that one kind only; to search every list and the files together, use tool:search-everything-with-one-question. The run reads no store and changes nothing.

values.title: Search the public web
values.job: Search the public web for a creator, a topic or a question, and get back at most ten results with the address each one cites
values.description: Sends one query (1 to 500 characters) to a public web search and reads the one results page. Returns at most ten results, each with title, url (the page the result points to, never the search engine's own address), a snippet in description, and a citation { url, retrieved_via }. It follows no result and signs in nowhere; to read a result, read its page with the tool that reads a public page.

values.title: Search treg's catalog of paid endpoints
values.job: Find the external endpoints that can do a job (backlinks for a domain, a company's job openings, a brand's ads, a channel's posts) and what each costs, before spending anything
values.description: Searches treg's public catalog by the job in plain words and answers its matches, each with its id, what it does, its method, its inputs and its price (cost.usd per cost.unit, and whether it is billed per call or per success). Free and needs no account or token: nothing is spent. Read one match in full with tool:read-a-treg-endpoint-and-its-price, then call it with tool:call-a-treg-endpoint. A job usually has several providers at very different prices; choose by the inputs you actually hold first, then by how often each works, then by price.

values.title: Search Wikimedia Commons files
values.job: Find real images and other source files on Wikimedia Commons for any objective by searching for the exact place, object, event or subject
values.description: Free, read-only Commons File-page discovery for real media needed by any objective. Returns a bounded page of file titles and canonical file-page URLs, without downloading media or requesting expensive license metadata for every search result. Search Commons first when the task needs a real place, object or event. Read exact file metadata for a candidate, then run the file-level reuse/credit assessor before reuse selection. Only explicit public-domain/CC0/CC-BY metadata under the requested policy is eligible; BY-SA/NC/ND/unknown or conflicting rights are excluded. Source metadata remains a qualified assertion, not blanket permission.

values.title: See how one file changed
values.job: See the difference between one file in a project on the person's computer and the last commit
values.description: Give folder (the full path of the project folder the person has let this tool use) and file_path (the file, relative to the folder). Returns diff, git's text of the difference from the last commit. A project with no commit yet has no last commit to compare with, and git's own words say so. Changes nothing.

values.title: See a pursuit through my lens
values.job: Tell an AI how to look at what I am pursuing: where to look, the parts to read what it finds by, and what to look for and do, from my own pursuit lens
values.description: Answers the paragraph every AI reads when it connects (the lens's opening, each part in one sentence, its closing) and the setup (every part with each of its rows whole: what to look for and what to ask or do, plus the joining interview: the rows marked joining_interview and where its answers are kept). The lens is the person's own, handed in as lens: its rows are the rows of their pursuit lens list and its opening, parts and closing the row of their content settings, which their AI reads from a store. Nothing is read or kept here; the answer is the result.

values.title: See what changed in a project
values.job: See every file that changed in a project on the person's computer and where each one stands: staged for the next commit, changed but not staged, or new
values.description: Give folder, the full path of a project folder the person has let this tool use. Returns the branch, how many commits it is ahead of and behind its upstream, and one row per changed file per place it stands (bucket staged, unstaged or untracked, with git's one-letter status). Changes nothing.

values.title: How each post did
values.job: Show how each of this person's published posts did in each place it went: that place's own counts, the visitors its link brought and what they bought
values.description: Give observations (each place's own counts for a post, read with that place's tools: { post_id, account_id, metrics: { name: number }, observed_at } or { platform_post_id, account_id?, metrics }), visits and conversions (as tool:break-down-visits-and-sales takes them: { visitor, project?, signals: { utm_content, ... } } and { visitor, project?, value? }) and optionally post_ids. Reads the person's post records handed in as `records` and returns posts: one row per place a post was published to that has a count, a visit or a conversion, with post_id, account_id, title, platform_post_id, url, metrics, observed_at, brought ({ visits, conversions, value }, only what was counted) and evidence. A visit counts for a place only when its utm_content is exactly that post's post_id (the post went to one place), the place's own post id, or post_id::account_id; a token that could name several places counts for none. Nothing missing is shown as zero.

values.title: See if my copies are in step
values.job: Show me whether every copy of my things is in step, and which records two of my devices changed apart
values.description: Reads and changes nothing: the device rows, the records kept apart and the records they name come in with the request. Answers devices (each device's state, waiting changes and when it last caught up; a copy of your records you send in positions is shown once, as the device that named it or as a copy of its own) and versions (each record kept apart of the kind you name as thing_type: the record as it is now first, then one side per other version, with the words of its keep button). other_kinds names the kinds of other records kept apart, to ask about next.

values.title: See my decisions
values.job: Show my decisions, what I am working toward, my plans and what has helped me decide
values.description: Reads your own rows and answers the Decisions screen: your newest decisions (at most 100) as summaries with the pursuits each cites, where each stands and how far it has got (decided, next action carried out, result checked); your current pursuits as the tree they nest into (from your record-scope choice rows); your newest plans; and what has helped you (which questions changed your answers and how those decisions turned out). With native_collection_page it answers one bounded page instead: the facts what helped is counted from (helped_items, your method check questions and your AIs' recorded work), collection_coverage saying whether more decisions, pursuits or plans exist, and next_before to send as before for the next page. access and allowance are what your computer reports: when your access limits deciding and does not keep decisions, the answer is free with nothing listed; none reported is no limit. metadata_only answers only access, allowance and the words for no pursuits, and reads no row. It changes nothing.

values.title: See tasks: one task by its id, or the newest that match
values.job: Show me tasks: what is waiting, who holds what, and what each finished with
values.description: With id, reads that one task. Otherwise reads the tasks, kept to those whose status (a status word of the rules, such as To do or In progress), sent_by or taken_by equal what is given, or whose assignees name assignee, and answers the newest limit of them by when they were sent (task-moves.json tasks_shown), with more true when more matched. A task comes back whole: its status, title and words, who gave it, who may take it, its priority, outcome, who took it and when, what is stuck, who released it and why, and its result and summary. Nothing is written. The caller hands in every record it reads as input.records; this tool reads no store and names no store method. Each write it makes comes back as keep, for the caller to keep in the person's own store.

values.title: See the ink marks drawn on a page or picture
values.job: Work out which ink marks are showing on one page, picture or other space, after later marks hid, restyled, reordered, copied or merged earlier ones
values.description: Give the mark operations (every drawing step ever recorded, in any space), the mark styles they name and the space to look at. Marks are only ever added; a later operation changes what shows by naming an earlier mark in its effects (hide_refs, style_ref_by_ref, order_by_ref, copy_ref_by_ref, merge_refs). The answer lists, in drawing order, each visible mark with its points, whether its shape is closed and its style (the style it names, with any fields the mark carries itself laid over it), plus the refs that are hidden and the operations that drew nothing. Operations for other spaces are left out. Rows may be bare, wrapped as { payload } or stored as { value_json } text. Nothing is written.

values.title: See what holds me
values.job: Tell me whether my setup still has to be finished before anything else opens, and which one thing I must do now
values.description: Reads and keeps nothing. Everything it works from is in the request and everything it makes is in the answer. From your setup steps (setup_steps: record:setup-steps rows, or the Get started answer you send as setup), your must-do list (must_do: record:waiting-on-you rows, or the whole waiting answer as things) and your hold setting (state), it answers cover { covered, key }: true while any required step is not done (the page draws only setup until then), null when nothing says, and key, the name your gate row gives the cover (required-setup when it gives none, so a missing key never leaves everything open). Beside it, hold: the one row that unblocks the most by your rank rules, every row that may hold in that order, how many times it can still be set aside today, the ways to hand it back and the stakes for turning the hold off. While the cover stands nothing else is held. Also answers what to keep: tasks (calendar-task records for the AI-doable work it removed from the hold, each under a stable id so the same trigger is one job), held_fact ({ key, title } or null, the held thing to keep) and device_runs (the declared device tools to start when the held thing changed from kept_held, the one you last kept).

values.title: See what is left to set up
values.job: Show me what is left to set up in my account, who does each step and what to do next
values.description: Draws the Get started screen from your setup facts: which setup steps apply to your account (picked by the setup show rules, yours and the operator's), which are done, which only you can do, whether your workspace is ready, and the steps for connecting your AI. A step whose facts were not sent is unknown, never done, and a rule set or setup context the request leaves out is unknown too, so the screen stays not ready rather than opening on a guess. It reads and changes nothing.

values.title: What is on a drive
values.job: Tell what is on one drive connected to this person's computer by kind of file (videos, pictures, sound, documents), with how many of each and how much space they take
values.description: Runs on the person's computer. Reads the drive once, inside one run's time; a drive with more files than that is answered as far as it was read (complete false). Returns mount, files, bytes, complete, kinds (kind, label, files, bytes) and largest (path, bytes).

values.title: See what runs on its own
values.job: Show everything my account runs on its own (due times, facts it hears, programs it keeps running): what each waits for, whether it is on, its last run, which ones should have run and did not, and a switch to turn each off or on
values.description: Give wakes, the rows wake:list answers ([{tool, id, on, switched_on, mark}]). Returns one row per cause: what it waits for in plain words (a due time as its schedule), its state (on, running, off, last run failed, outcome unknown, came with no budget left, not picked up yet), red when it needs the person, why (a failed run says its cause), its last run and outcome, and the switch that turns it off or on; red rows first, then switched-on ones, with counts of red, on and off.

values.title: See what finished work is ready to publish
values.job: See the finished work waiting to be published as a changelog: which group each piece is in, what can be done with it, what stops it (for example no proof yet) and what was already sent
values.description: Give graph: the queue described as data. Its groups ({ id, label, empty_copy, order }), fields, relationships, views ({ selected, density_threshold }), rules ({ id, message, requires_relationship or requires_field, blocks_actions }), actions ({ id, label, method, target }) and surface_copy are the person's own words and rules; this tool knows none. Records come in graph.records or in recordAtoms ({ id, title, group_id, fields, relationships, action_ids, receipt_ids, issue }), receipts in graph.receipts or receiptAtoms. Optional selectedRecordId, status and issues. Returns status (empty, sparse, dense, loading, error or blocked, with where it came from), each group with its records, the selected record with its actions, the rules that block it and its receipts, and the ids the data names that the queue does not declare. A record with no proof is shown with the rule that asks for it; nothing is sent.

values.title: See when things show
values.job: Show me the rules that decide when things show, hide or stay quiet for me, and the types I keep
values.description: Reads your show-rules record and answers every rule in force (the starting rules, your own, and those of the types you have switched on), the subjects a rule can be about with their facts, the moment facts, the effects, the quick choices and the operators a rule's when can use, the types you keep and which are on (in_use). It reads and changes nothing.

values.title: See where each customer is
values.job: See where each customer is: their latest step, every step so far, and how many customers each product has against its target
values.description: Reads the customer records you send (read them from your store): customer-contact ({contactId, displayName}), customer-product-target ({targetId, productId, productLabel, targetCount}) and customer-step ({stepId, contactId, productId, stepKind, label, createdAt}) rows, in records or as a JSON file from your files. It reads no store itself and keeps nothing. Returns each customer with their steps newest first and latest step (most recently active first), each product's customers, target, how many remain and percent, and the customer you name in contact_id (or the most recent).

values.title: See where the public door runs
values.job: See where my public door runs now and which hosting services it can move between
values.description: Takes the person's Service connections rows as `connections` (the caller reads them from the person's own store and hands them in) and answers where their public door runs now (its hosting row, its address and what proves it) and each hosting row with whether the door can move there and why not. It never reads or shows a key, reads no store and changes nothing.

values.title: See which of my models can judge each of my questions (runs on your computer)
values.job: Score every model I can ask against every question in my rubrics file and show who agrees with the answers I already know, how long it took and who did not answer
values.description: Give rubrics_file ({providers: [...], rubrics: [...]} on your computer) and optionally passes (default 2). Every model on offer is asked every calibration case of every rubric. Returns, per rubric, one row per model: cases right out of cases asked, time, wrong answers, cases with no answer (a connection or time-limit problem, not a wrong answer) and whether it can judge that question. A model that is excellent at one job can be a coin flip at another; this is how you find out which. It changes nothing.

values.title: See who can take my work: which people, AIs and other records are live, what each can do and how many tasks each holds
values.job: Show me who I can hand a task to: which are live now, what each can do and how many tasks each is doing
values.description: Reads every record handed in that is not a task (a person, an AI, a raccoon, anything with a record) and answers each with its id, its whole stored value (every cell as kept: a caller names it from those cells by its own formula; no name is made here), whether it is live (seen within the minutes its record names as live.minutes, else task-moves.json live_minutes_default), when it was last seen, and how many tasks it holds as taker. Live ones come first, then by the order cell. `can` keeps only those that can do every word given (one that can do any can do all); `live_only` keeps only the live ones. Nothing is written. The caller hands in every record it reads as input.records; this tool reads no store and names no store method. Each write it makes comes back as keep, for the caller to keep in the person's own store.

values.title: See who holds paid access
values.job: Work out which paid access one buyer holds right now: what they bought, what renewed, what ended or was refunded, and what I gave them by hand
values.description: Folds the buyer's payment events (the payment-event records the payment tools keep, which your AI reads from your stores and hands in) through your access-effect-rule rows into effects, folds those into purchase episodes (a purchase starts one, a renewal keeps it, a cancellation or refund ends it) and answers the access refs of the offers they hold now, with every offer that asks for no money held by everyone, plus the access-grant records you wrote for them (a gift, a pass with an end date). Returns held_access_refs (the one list every gate here asks), the episodes behind it, any allowance limits, and problems (events that gave no effect, and why). Give the buyer the way your rules name them; the starter rules read the buyer's email address from the payment event. Without your own rules or lifecycle row it reads the event kinds the payment tool writes. It reads and keeps no records and sends nothing: the rows come in the request, the answer is the whole result.

values.title: Send a draft
values.job: Send an existing draft. Sending consumes the draft, so the same draft id cannot send twice; the same request key answers the first send.
values.description: Send an existing draft. Sending consumes the draft, so the same draft id cannot send twice; the same request key answers the first send. Takes provider (an id of read-data/mail-providers.json) and connection (the person's account of that provider, by its handle only: {connection_id}). Runs as that account with the key the person's vault holds for it; the engine hands the key to this run alone and it is placed only in the request to the provider's own host, never shown. Answers the provider-neutral rows of read-data/neutral.mjs, never the provider's own payload. A provider that does not offer it says so in words.

values.title: Send a message in Messages on this Mac
values.job: Send a message to one person or a list from the Messages app on the person's own Mac
values.description: Give recipients (phone numbers or Apple ids Messages knows; to for one) and text. Each recipient is sent to on their own and answered on their own: sent holds { recipient } or { recipient, error }. The text goes to Messages as its own argument, never inside the script. If the Mac has not allowed this to control Messages, nothing is sent and the answer says what to allow in System Settings, Privacy and Security, Automation.

values.title: Send a post
values.job: Send one of the person's approved posts to one of their accounts at a place once its time has come, and answer where it went as the post to keep
values.description: Give post_id (an approved or scheduled post whose time has come), place (the slug of one of the places in read-data/post-places.json, as tool:list-post-destinations names them) and account_id (one of the post's destinations: a connection of that place's kind, service_connection:<vendor> or service_connection:<vendor>:<account>). The engine hands this run only that account's held values, chosen by place; they reach only that place's hosts, as each request leaves. A destination the post carries as not known is never sent again by itself: give resend: true only after looking at the place. This run reads the post and the connection from the rows it is given as `stored` and stores nothing: the post as it ends (each destination's outcome) comes back under `keep`, and the place gets an idempotency key made from the post, the account and the attempt. A destination that already has the post is not sent it again. A post with a file needs media_url, an address the caller made of that file where the person keeps it (a share such as a signed link, valid until the place has fetched it): the place is handed that address, or the bytes streamed from it, never a copy kept here; with no address, nothing is sent. Returns post_id, status, post (with each destination's status, url and error in plain words), said and keep. This posts publicly on the person's account: run it only with the person's yes for this post.

values.title: Send a reply on Instagram
values.job: Send one chosen automatic reply to one Instagram message or comment, once, while its place's window, if it sets one, is still open
values.description: Give account_id and one decision from tool:decide-the-replies whose action is send. The place row's request for the decision's channel is sent (read-data/reply-places.json), the window is checked again at the moment of sending: a closed window sends nothing. The reply's reply-kept row is in the answer (`keep`: sent, failed or not-known) for the person's AI to keep, and the rows already held are given in `kept`: a key in them is never sent again; if no answer comes back the reply is not-known for a person to look at, and it is not retried. The account's held token is placed only on the request, only to the place's own hosts, never kept or answered. It posts publicly on the person's account: run it only for replies the person's rules chose.

values.title: Send a reply on YouTube
values.job: Send one chosen automatic reply to one YouTube message or comment, once, while its place's window, if it sets one, is still open
values.description: Give account_id and one decision from tool:decide-the-replies whose action is send. The place row's request for the decision's channel is sent (read-data/reply-places.json), the window is checked again at the moment of sending: a closed window sends nothing. The reply's reply-kept row is in the answer (`keep`: sent, failed or not-known) for the person's AI to keep, and the rows already held are given in `kept`: a key in them is never sent again; if no answer comes back the reply is not-known for a person to look at, and it is not retried. The account's held token is placed only on the request, only to the place's own hosts, never kept or answered. It posts publicly on the person's account: run it only for replies the person's rules chose.

values.title: Send a text message
values.job: Send a text message, to one number or a list, through the text provider I connected
values.description: Give recipients (phone numbers with country code; to for one), provider (the id of the text provider row in read-data/message-providers.json that the person's text connection is), the settings that row asks for (for twilio-sms: from, a number on the account, and account_sid, the account's id) and text (or subject when there is no text). Each number is sent to on its own and answered on its own: sent holds { recipient, messageId }, { recipient, error, unknown: false } when the provider confirmed a rejection before the message was made, or { recipient, error, unknown: true } when it may have gone and must not be retried blindly. The held key of the provider named reaches the one process on a private pipe; it is never shown.

values.title: Send an email
values.job: Send an email, to one person or a list, through the email provider I connected
values.description: Give recipients (a list of addresses; to for one), provider (the id of the email provider row in read-data/message-providers.json that the person's email connection is), the settings that provider's row asks for (region for Amazon SES, such as us-east-1) and the words: subject and text (drawn as an email in the look the person wears, in the person's saved screen look, which the caller hands in as `saved` (the shipped look until they choose one; an email whose look cannot be read is not sent), with its mark from the mail row's site and made_with) or your own html, markdown for a written email (it also goes as a BCC to the account's own address, and answers sent_copy), or template (a template name from read-data/message-templates.json, or your own templates) with variables; kind names what it is for the account's limits (sign-in-code, message ...). Every email comes from the account's own mail row, which the caller hands in as mail_settings (read from the person's `mail-settings` row `settings:mail`; with none the shipped row names no sender and nothing is sent), never from the request; each address may be sent only so many emails of a kind (per_person, counted from the mail_sent rows handed in), the day keeps room for sign-in codes (daily, counted from the mail_day row handed in), a proof address is never sent, and every email is written down under its address: nothing is kept here, the answer's keep holds the mail-sent and mail-day rows as the send left them, each with the row it expected, for the caller to write.
