Each recipient is sent to on their own and answered on their own: sent holds { recipient, messageId } or { recipient, error } with limited, unknown (it may have gone; it is not sent again) or suppressed. The held keys of the provider named reach the one process on private pipes; they are never shown.

values.title: Send the email lessons that have come due
values.job: Send each email-course lesson whose time has come to the people still signed up, once each, and retry a failed one later
values.description: Give records (the person's queue, subscription, token and contact rows, read from their store), optional limit (up to 50 per run), provider (the id of the email provider row in read-data/message-providers.json that the person's email connection is) and region when that row asks for one. Finds the queued lessons whose time has passed, sends each to a subscriber who is still signed up and has not had it, works out the subscription's sent mark and the queue entry's removal, and answers them in keep for the caller to write. A failed send queues its own retry (up to three, each later than the last). Answers results [{ lesson_index, status: sent, already-sent, unsubscribed or failed, why? }] and said.

values.title: Update my Live Activity
values.job: Start, update or end the one Live Activity board for running work
values.description: Pass a stable update_id, board_key and up to four items, plus what the caller read from its own records: activities (the registered activity tokens), devices (the push-to-start iPhones, each with its registered attributes_type) and last_start_at (the started_at of an earlier start). Running items update the passed tokens or push-to-start when none has returned yet; an empty running set ends them. Apple acceptance does not prove the person saw it. Nothing is kept: the answer names retired_activity_ids (tokens that are gone, ended or past iOS's update window, for the caller to forget) and started_at (when a start was sent). An uncertain state means the outcome is unknown; check before sending again.

values.title: Send a notification to my devices
values.job: Send one notice to the registered Apple and browser devices the caller passes, and answer what each provider said
values.description: Pass notification (the event as recorded: notification_id, kind, title, body, audience_refs, optional conversation_ref, open and actions), audience (a reference the event names) and devices (the registered devices to try, each with device_id, route, address and for Apple app and environment; the caller reads them from its own records). Sends through APNs and browser push; accepted is never treated as read, and an unknown network result is stage uncertain. Nothing is kept: the answer names each device's result, gone_device_ids (providers that said the device no longer exists) and live_device_ids (devices that read notices themselves); the caller decides what to send again, and sends only the devices that failed definitely.

values.title: Send to a webhook
values.job: Send a note, or anything picked, to a web address as JSON
values.description: Posts { title, link, words, things } as JSON to address, a public web address you give, and says what the address answered. Takes things (what is being sent), note (your own words, sent as words), title and address. It refuses an address that is not public, waits at most 10 seconds, and does not follow a redirect, so what was posted stays at the address you gave. A refusal says what the address answered.

values.title: Serve my task pages on this computer
values.job: Show my pursuits' task pages on this computer, read from their own databases each time the page asks
values.description: A kept session this computer's own door serves as a page on its loopback address (invoke.pages: the page folder, task-page/pages, built by task-page/do-work/build-served-page.mjs). The page signs the person in with their own sign-in and calls this session through the door: `pursuits` {dbs, pages_database} answers [{id, label}], the rows of task_pages (pursuit, label, database, tables, place) whose database the session holds; `data` {dbs, pages_database, p} answers those pursuits' task pages joined (the task page's own read-only SELECT, read-data/read-task-page.mjs). Start input dbs is [{database}]: each database's login is handed by name for the owner alone (secret_name_from_database), element i on descriptor 3 + i, and each is opened once and kept. Nothing is written, copied or kept; the page's address names the databases (?dbs=a,b&pages=a).

values.title: Set a product's customer target
values.job: Set how many customers I want for a product, so progress toward that target can be tracked
values.description: Builds the target record (one per product, its id made from the product's) and returns it as target_record; it keeps nothing, so your AI writes the record to your store, replacing the earlier target of that product. see-where-each-customer-is counts the product's customers against it.

values.title: Set a mailbox signature
values.job: Set the signature of one address the mailbox sends as (address from list-send-as-addresses), as the HTML the provider takes; an empty signature clears it. The answer is what the provider saved.
values.description: Set the signature of one address the mailbox sends as (address from list-send-as-addresses), as the HTML the provider takes; an empty signature clears it. The answer is what the provider saved. Takes provider (an id of read-data/mail-providers.json) and connection (the person's account of that provider, by its handle only: {connection_id}). Runs as that account with the key the person's vault holds for it; the engine hands the key to this run alone and it is placed only in the request to the provider's own host, never shown. Answers the provider-neutral rows of read-data/neutral.mjs, never the provider's own payload. A provider that does not offer it says so in words.

values.title: Set a post to go at its time
values.job: Work out setting an approved post to go out at its scheduled time, once it is ready for every place it is going, and answer the post row to keep; nothing is sent now
values.description: Give post_id of an approved post whose scheduled_for is still ahead. It is checked for every destination (as tool:check-a-post does); when ready, its status becomes scheduled and it waits for its time, and when not, it stays approved and said gives what each place is missing. Nothing is sent by this tool and nothing is stored: the scheduled post row comes back under `keep`. Give records: the post and the person's connection records. tool:take-back-a-post makes a scheduled post a draft again. Returns post_id, status, post, ready and said.

values.title: Change how long deleted files are kept
values.job: Change how many days this person's Recently Deleted or Archived keep things before they move on
values.description: after_days is { state: days } (a whole number from 0 to 36500, or null to keep until put back). It applies at once to everything already there, so a shorter time can make things move on, or be gone for good, at the next sweep. A state left out keeps its days. Your AI reads your setting:keep_for and hands it in as stored; the answer's keep is the new setting for it to keep. Answers the keep-for now in force: states (each with its id, label, after_days, default_after_days and what happens when its time ends) and choices.

values.title: Set fields on the rows my rules match
values.job: Set fields on the rows my rules match, like coding transactions by merchant and amount: my rule groups in order, the first matching rule sets each field, never over a value I set myself, with a preview of what each rule would change
values.description: Takes rows, the fields (an id, a kind and a path into each row), and groups of rules in the order they are tried. A rule is a tools/formulas rule tree (when; left out matches every row) and the fields it sets, each to a value or to another field of the row. For every row the first rule that matches and sets a field decides that field; rules that set different fields all apply, and a later rule setting the same field is listed as shadowed. A field already holding a value from a stronger source (a person, or a source the rows do not record when the precedence says unknown sources hold) is not changed and is answered as held, naming who holds it. When the rows keep who wrote each field (provenance: where, and the keys for the kind and the writer), each change carries the rule as its writer, and a field a rule set that no rule sets now goes back to empty. Nothing is written: the answer holds the changes, each changed row as it would be, and per rule the rows it matches and how many it changes, finds already set, cannot change and shadows. An unfinished rule sets nothing and is named in incomplete.

values.title: Change when deleted files give back storage
values.job: Change the rules that give back the storage of deleted files sooner than keep-for: by where it was, kind, size, days since deleted, or while storage is above a size
values.description: rules replaces the whole list; each is { id, label, on, when, after_days, storage_above_bytes, order }. when is a formula-engine rule tree over label (text), kind (choice), where (choice), size (bytes), days_deleted (number), state (choice), by (choice), count (number), or null for everything; after_days gives matching items back that many days after they were deleted; storage_above_bytes gives matching items back (order oldest or largest) while the files kept are above that many bytes. Keep-for stays the longest anything waits. Left out, nothing changes. Your AI reads your setting:release_rules and hands it in as stored; the answer's keep is the new setting for it to keep. Answers the rules now in force and what a rule can name.

values.title: Set up Trillion's hooks in an AI app on this computer
values.job: Read, add or take out the hooks that keep an AI app's sessions on this computer as the person's records (Claude Code or Codex)
values.description: Runs harness/setup.mjs with --action inspect, apply or remove for one AI app on this computer (claude-code or codex). inspect writes nothing and answers a report: status, ready, checks (each with id, status and reason), changes it would make and boundaries (what this installer never does: write an MCP entry, open a browser, grant notification permission). apply writes the hooks named in harness/setup.json into that app's own settings, keeping the person's existing settings and permission choices; remove takes them out again. The full hook suite needs the Trillion Mac app and macOS Keychain: on another platform the platform check answers unsupported and nothing is written. Exit 0 means ready, 2 means not ready (the checks say why), 1 means the request was wrong (standard error says what to change).

values.title: Set up someone I pay in Stripe
values.job: Make a Stripe account for a person I pay, or check one, and get their Stripe onboarding page and what Stripe still needs from them
values.description: Give settings ({ country, controller, capabilities }), owner, payee_ref, refresh_url and return_url, or an existing account id. Returns the account, whether it can be paid and what is due, and the onboarding address. Uses the Stripe key of the seller connection that seller_connection names (service_connection:stripe is your own).

values.title: Set up Stripe payment links
values.job: Make Stripe hold one lasting payment link for every priced option of my offers, with the buyer plan page and my discount codes
values.description: Give owner (a name that marks the Stripe objects as yours) and after_payment_url (where a buyer lands after paying: an offer row with post_purchase_route_path lands at that path under it, any other at its root). A trial, a part of the first month taken today, and a quantity the buyer picks come from each price option. Takes your offers and code adjustments (the rows your AI reads from its store) in the request, and keeps nothing. Safe to run again: prices, links, codes and the plan page are found, not made twice; links for options you no longer sell stop taking payments. Webhook endpoints are not made here (Stripe shows a signing secret only once); add yours in the Stripe dashboard and keep its secret in your held values. Uses the Stripe key of the seller connection that seller_connection names (service_connection:stripe is your own).

values.title: Settle a triage of one incoming item
values.job: Keep the decision made about one incoming item only if it holds up against the person's priorities and dispositions, and otherwise hold the item back
values.description: Give the same item, priorities, dispositions and least confidence you were briefed with, and answers: a list holding your one answer ({disposition_ref, confidence, rationale, target_ref, and objective with acceptance_criteria where the disposition needs them}). Returns and keeps one decision record per item and version. If there are no priorities, no answer or more than one, the confidence is not a number, is outside 0 to 1 or is under the least, the rationale or objective has more words than max_words allows, the disposition is not listed, or a needed objective is missing, the decision is the fallback disposition, blocked, with each reason in words. blocked is false only where the disposition's row says blocked_default is false. It does nothing else; whoever owns the disposition acts on the decision.

values.title: Apply an amount across rows of another list
values.job: Work out how the amount one row holds (a payment, a credit, a grant) goes across the open amounts of rows of another list (invoices, bills, budgets) as allocation rows, propose it first, answer allocations to take back, or read what is applied and open on a row
values.description: action propose works out, writing nothing, how the source row's amount would go across the targets in an order (oldest_first by default, or as read-data/list-settlements.json orders say) and what is left unapplied as a credit. apply answers one allocation row per target (source, target, amount, date, request) for the allocations list "<source>-to-<target>-allocations" under `keep`, for the caller to store; give items [{ target_id, amount }] or leave them out to apply the proposal; request_key makes it apply once. Every item is answered done, already_done or refused with why, and the outcome says all, some or none. remove answers allocation_ids as rows to take away under `keep`, reopening exactly those targets once stored. position reads one row ({ row: { row_id, amount_field }, role, allocations: { list_id } }): its amount, applied, open and the allocations behind it. A row with no amount is refused: empty is not zero. Body: lists (the rows read), source { row_id, amount_field }, targets { list_id, amount_field, order_field?, row_ids? }, order, allocations { list_id?, *_field? }.

values.title: Say who set each value and which source wins
values.job: Say which value each field of my rows keeps when several sources offered one, who set it, and why the others lost: what I typed beats my rules, my rules beat imported sources, and those beat an AI's guess, with the AI's reasons and confidence kept beside its value
values.description: Takes offers, each a value for one field of one row with its source (kind, by, at, confidence) and optionally its basis (reasoning, citations). Each field keeps the offer the precedence puts first: source kinds strongest first (person, rule, source, ai by default, or the person's own precedence), then inside one kind the newest, then the most confident, then the order handed in. An offer below its kind's confidence floor never wins and is set aside with the reason. An offer with withdraws: true takes back what that same source offered earlier, so the field falls back to the next offer. as_of answers the value a field held at that time. Every other offer is kept beside the winner with why it lost, and a field whose two best offers tie with different values says contested.

values.title: Settle shared resource cost
values.job: Allocate one verified supplier invoice among its attributed excess users under purchased limits, with separate platform expense, explicit funding gaps and exact subcent amounts; answers the settlement and every allocation and sends nothing to a payment provider
values.description: Allocate one verified supplier invoice among its attributed excess users under purchased limits, with separate platform expense, explicit funding gaps and exact subcent amounts; answers the settlement and every allocation and sends nothing to a payment provider. Give observations (as keep-resource-usage-observation or observe-live-usage answered them) to count each payer's excess from them, or each payer's excess_units directly. This run reads no rows and keeps nothing; the caller keeps the answer.

values.title: Settle two versions
values.job: Work out how to settle a record two of my devices changed apart: keep one version, keep both, or keep a merged one
values.description: Reads and keeps nothing. Works out what you chose for one record kept apart (id, from see-if-my-copies-are-in-step): keep one (side, the id of the version to keep), both (each other version is kept as a record of its own, named after it with -kept- and a number that no record in records holds yet), or merged (value, the merged record). thing_type is the kind of the record; records are the kept-apart record and the records it names, as you read them. Answers writes: the chosen record first and the kept versions removed after it, for you to keep in one write, each standing on the record as it was handed in (expected, null for a record nobody had), so every copy takes it like any change.

values.title: Make a decision safe to share
values.job: Make a decided decision safe to show strangers: the plain privacy pass with the person's own private terms, then a second model's re-identification check bound to the exact words
values.description: In three turns. With decision_id and never_publish (the words of the person's never-publish list, which the caller reads from its own rows; an empty list when there are none; a call without it is refused): the decision's facts with every private term already redacted, and how to rewrite them in general terms. With rewrite: the plain privacy pass (tools/learn-from-everyones-results) runs on it with the person's own private terms (the never_publish words and the proper names in the decision) and must find nothing; then reidentification, the whole answer tool:ask-a-small-model-for-a-verdict gave for the rubric and content this tool names, must be accepted and bound to exactly this rewrite. Only then is the entry kept on the decision as shared and answered with the pool tool to send it to (tool:add-a-shared-situation). Nothing leaves the person's records here.

values.title: Share a kept show type
values.job: Share one of my show-rule presets with people so they see Trillion that way
values.description: Shares a type you keep with one person or account (principal), as the Account visibility screen does: answers two records to keep, in order, the preset's copy show-types-shared:<id> = { label, types } (the preset with every preset it inherits) and its grant sharing:<that label> = { record, people: [{ principal, key_blake3 }], changed_at }. It makes the share key and answers it once as key, to hand to that person; the grant keeps only its BLAKE3. Someone it is already shared with is refused, and nothing is kept.

values.title: Share anything
values.job: Share anything of mine read-only, from one record or one piece of text to a whole list or any mix of records, with a person, an AI or anyone holding a link, or let named people and AIs run some of my tools at my door with no copy on their computer; show who has access; and stop it
values.description: op share (the default job): give grant (sharing: plus the thing's label; read-data/share-label.mjs grantOf makes it, and the answer of any earlier call names it), thing (one of { type, id }, { list } for a list and all its rows, { text, title? } for a piece of text, or { items: [{ type, id? | prefix? }], title } for any mix) and who: with (a list of names of people or AIs, each given a key of its own) and/or link: true (one key anyone can hold). Optional until (a future ISO time the view share ends) and origin (https:// address that opens a link: url is then origin/share/<key>). A view share only lets people view (can: ["view"], the default). It keeps the share as one record of yours and answers each key once: the key itself is not kept anywhere, only a digest of it, so lose it and share again after stopping. A person or AI presents the key at your door, and the engine reads what was shared there; a person opens the url in a browser. op stop: give grant, and principal to stop one person (principal "link" stops the link), or leave principal out to stop everyone. op access: give grant; answers who can open it now (people with when added, the link, until when, whether it is open, stopped or ended), never a key. To let people run tools instead: can ["run"] with grant (sharing: plus a name you choose), tools (Workshop tool ids, tool:...), with (names of people or AIs: letters, digits, _ or -), an optional end rule you choose (until, a future ISO time; unused_days, whole days with no use; or both, the earlier ends it; by default it has no end and stands until you stop it), identity (none, the default: your side learns nothing of who runs; self: the tool's input gets their name) and journal (input, the default, or none). Each person gets a key of their own, answered once; they or any MCP client of theirs present it at your door and can list and run only those tools there. op stop and op access take can ["run"] and grant the same way; stopping a person or everyone ends their next call. op end with can ["run"] and grant sets the end rule again (until and/or unused_days, or neither for no end), and the people keep their keys. The rule is kept beside the share and the engine never reads it: tool:end-shares-whose-condition-failed, given the run shares the store lists, returns the withdrawal of each whose rule says it has ended.

values.title: Show how far my conversation import is
values.job: Show how far bringing in my conversations has got: for each source, files done, conversations and messages kept, and whether it stopped
values.description: Reads the import's cursor rows (conversation-import-cursor) from the cursor rows handed in and answers, per source, the files seen and done, conversations kept, messages added and already kept, files the messages carried that were not copied, its state (done or more) and when it last moved. Reads nothing else.

values.title: Show one purchase's plan, card and receipts
values.job: Show the buyer the plan of one of my purchases, when it renews or ends, the card that pays it and its receipts
values.description: Give subscription_id (the sub_ id of one purchase) and subject_email (the signed-in buyer's verified email; the purchase must be theirs). Reads the purchase from Stripe: its plan, status, renewal date (or end date when it is set to end), the card that pays it (brand, last four, expiry only) and its latest receipts (up to 12, with a receipt address when Stripe gives an https one). It changes nothing and opens no billing page; the buttons that change the card, the plan or cancel open tool:open-the-billing-page-for-one-purchase-and-show-the-card with a flow. Uses the Stripe key of the seller connection that seller_connection names (service_connection:stripe is your own).

values.title: Show the courses a learner is on, lesson by lesson
values.job: Show the learning page for one learner: each course as its lessons in order, how many are done, the lesson they are on now, and each lesson's words
values.description: Give the courses (each with its id, title, about and lessons with id, title and body) and the lessons this learner has finished as { course_id, lesson_id }. Returns each course with how many lessons are done, and each lesson with its status: complete when done, active for the first lesson not done, locked for the rest, plus its words. A lesson with an interactive module is marked interactive. Nothing is read or written here.

values.title: Show what a tool would give members
values.job: Before I add a tool for my space's members, tell me what it would give each member beyond what they already hold, what it reaches or could cost, and whether I must decide it myself
values.description: Give descriptor (the tool's row: id, placements, needs, price_ref...), toolVersion (the content identity of that definition, so exactly one immutable version is judged), members ([{ member_id, name }]), held ({ member_id: [operations their grants already give] }), and when wanted operations (some of discover, describe, run, read; all when left out) and memberId (one member; * for everyone now and later). Returns per member gains and already, reaches (what the descriptor says it does: runs on a member's computer, sends data off the device, can cost money, keeps results), needs_owner and says. Read-only: it grants nothing.

values.title: Show which offers a buyer may see
values.job: Work out which of my offers to show a buyer given what they already hold, with my upsell and already-owns rules
values.description: Give offers and rules (your offer and eligibility rows, read by your AI from its store; an offer with no rule is always shown) and held_access_refs (what the buyer holds now). A refund that shrinks what is held reverses every decision.

values.title: Sign a Mac app update record
values.job: Sign the Mac app's update record text with the release key in my vault, so installed apps accept the update
values.description: Signs the UTF-8 text it is given (the update record's signed lines) with the Ed25519 key held under mac-app-update-signing-key, through the engine's secrets:sign operation. The key never leaves the vault; the answer is the signature in base64, as the app reads it. Only a run reaches the operation; the run's right names that one key and that one operation.

values.title: Sign someone up for an email course
values.job: Sign a person up for an email course after they agreed to it, keep their consent in my records, send the first lesson now and queue the others
values.description: Give email, consent (true only when the person agreed in the words of course.consent_text), course (id, public_origin as an https site root, checkout_url, from, mailing_address, consent_text, consent_version and 2 to 12 lessons { delay_hours, subject, article_url, text_lines, html_lines } where every lesson carries {{unsubscribeUrl}} and {{mailingAddress}} and the first has delay_hours 0), source (where they signed up, optional) records (the person's rows listed in its schema, read from their store) and provider (the id of the email provider row in read-data/message-providers.json that the person's email connection is; region too when that row asks for one). Nothing is sent without consent, a sender and a mailing address. Works out the consent row with its words, version, time and source and each later lesson's queue row at its time (tool:send-due-email-lessons sends them), and answers them in keep for the caller to write; nothing is kept here; sends lesson 1 with List-Unsubscribe headers; signing up again sends nothing twice. Answers { status: enrolled, already_enrolled }.

values.title: Silence the ticks and hiss in a generated voice take's pauses (runs on your computer)
values.job: Clean the clicks and hiss a text-to-speech engine leaves in the pauses of a voice take
values.description: Every stretch of the take quieter than -50 dBFS (20 ms windows) for at least 60 ms, bridged across a tick of up to 40 ms, becomes digital silence with 5 ms fades, and a sentence that stops at full level gets a 25 ms fade-out instead of a hard edge. The take is only read; the cleaned copy is written where the person says (24-bit). It runs on the person's own computer, never on Trillion.

values.title: My site addresses
values.job: List the addresses my published websites answer at
values.description: Every address your sites answer at: each host, its https address, the installation it shows, and for an earlier name the address it sends visitors on to. told says what the forwarder last answered: answering, or refused and why.

values.title: Sort bounces and replies
values.job: Sort the bounces, complaints, unsubscribes and replies that came back from emails I sent, and say which addresses never to send to again, which to retry and which people wrote back
values.description: Give events as your provider or mailbox gave them and event_source (plain, resend-webhook, amazon-ses-notification or mailbox-message from read-data/inbox-pacing.json, or your own event_source_row naming where the recipient, type, status, subject, text and time sit). Each event is read into those fields and the first outcome row whose every condition holds (a field equals one of its values, contains one of its words, or matches its pattern) names its kind (hard-bounce, soft-bounce, complaint, unsubscribe, reply, auto-reply, delivered) and action (suppress, stop-sequence, retry-later, hand-to-person, none). Returns outcomes (hand them to tool:pace-sends-from-an-inbox), suppress, stop, retry (with when), replies and the unmatched events. It sends, deletes and keeps nothing; your own outcome_rows replace the shipped ones.

values.title: Sort mail into my built-in task lists
values.job: Say which built-in to-do list (calendar, email or other) each email would become a task in when I turn my mail into tasks
values.description: Give messages (at most 50, each { subject?, from?, labels?, list_unsubscribe?, has_invite? }). Each is tested against the email_split rows of calendar-tasks.json in order (an invite or invitation subject goes to calendar; a list-unsubscribe header, a promotions, updates, social, forums or spam label, or unsubscribe in the subject goes to other; anything else to email), and the first row that matches names its list. Answers messages ({ index, subject, smart_list }) and counts per list. It reads only the messages it is given: it reads no mailbox, makes and saves no task, and sends nothing. The Calendar task screen (calendar-tasks.mjs, kept in this folder but not run here) does the rest of the old job: it keeps named task lists with counts, groups and sorts them, schedules a task onto a day or time, and saves each email as a task with its title, priority, duration, deadline and repeat rule. That needs the records store and the timed-action parts, which this run does not have.

values.title: Split a long document of many items into one document per item
values.job: Turn long markdown documents that hold many numbered items (rules, lessons, questions) into one document per item with its fields in frontmatter, so each item is a row of a folder list
values.description: Reads the documents a mapping names and finds the items by the mapping's heading and table-row patterns, merging pieces of one item from several documents. Each item becomes `<id>.md`: frontmatter (id, then the fields the mapping captures, groups and flags) and its parts under headings. Text that belongs to no item is kept in one leftover file per document. Every line read is placed (the report counts both), and pieces with the same words are written once. It refuses a folder that is not empty. It knows no item kind: everything comes from the mapping.

values.title: Split a document into its pieces
values.job: Split a document into its smallest self-contained pieces, a page per call, so every check can name the piece it came from
values.description: Give one of the person's files by name (as /folder/file.md, read through their files door page by page, so a file of any size up to 4 MB is never sent in one request body), or the text of a short document (Markdown), and optionally its file name and its identity. Each paragraph, list item, table row or fenced block (``` or ~~~, as CommonMark fences them) under its headings is one piece; titles, rules and table headers are not. The answer holds the pieces and keeps nothing: each is a row shaped for the person's Checks list (id piece- and the first 24 hex of its identity, kind piece) with says (its lead), text, identity (1f: and the BLAKE3 of its whitespace-folded text), key (its heading path and lead), sources (the file, the piece's key there as section, the file identity and the line where it starts), and empty tags, kinds and checked_by; the same text twice is one piece with two sources. Pieces come a page per call within most_bytes (the door carries an answer twice in one 64 KiB message): send the answer's next as after to read the next page. A piece too large for one answer is named in too_large. The person's AI keeps the pieces in the store of its choice; tool:check-every-piece-is-covered then says what each kept piece lacks.

values.title: Choose files for the next commit
values.job: Add chosen files in a project on the person's computer to the next commit
values.description: Give folder (the full path of the project folder the person has let this tool use) and paths (the files to add, relative to the folder). Returns the project's changes after it, as tool:see-changes-in-a-project does. The files themselves are not changed.

values.title: Start a Codex run on this computer
values.job: Start one fresh Codex run in a folder on this computer and get its run id (harness/codex-runs.mjs startCodexRun)
values.description: Starts `codex exec` detached in the given folder, with the prompt read from the message file (never on the command line). Answers the run id and state running. Read the run with tool:read-a-codex-run-on-this-computer; end it with tool:cancel-a-codex-run-on-this-computer. Codex uses the person's own login; nothing here reads a credential.

values.title: Start a computer
values.job: Make a machine into a computer that runs what its own row says: rent one or use one I already run, set it up, build its programs from source there and read back its health page
values.description: Rents a machine from the provider description the request names (or adopts a Linux machine the person runs, at its address), points a public name at it through the name provider description, and applies the computer's own row (record:computer, `runs`) over SSH: set-up (packages, toolchains, users, folders, keys), each unit with a `source` fetched by the machine itself from the git address the row names and built there (no release, no feed, no copied program), the files the row renders, the restarts and each unit's boot check. Answers the lease, the machine's architecture, the monthly price, what the apply wrote, built and restarted, and the public health page's HTTP status. Running it again resumes from the saved lease.

values.title: Start a decision with my method
values.job: Start a decision my AI will make with my method: what is being decided, the facts and constraints, and the options only if I already hold them
values.description: Opens a decision in the person's own records from a source_id (the same source always opens the same decision; the same input again is that decision, different input is refused), its goal, its evidence ({ref, claim}, each ref unique: the facts and every non-negotiable constraint) and the options ({id, label}, at least two). The decision is answered by the rows of one method, a saved view over the person's method rows (the one named, else their default view): read it with tool:read-a-method and record answers to any number of its rows in one call with tool:record-method-answers. Returns case_id.

values.title: Start a Stripe checkout
values.job: Make the Stripe hosted checkout page a buyer is sent to, for one of my offers, with my own Stripe account
values.description: Prices the sale as price-a-sale does from the offers (and adjustments, suggestions) your AI passes in the request, needs the buyer agreement in consent (billing and legal), and success_url and cancel_url for where the buyer lands afterwards (they only land the buyer; they never grant access). Returns the address to send the buyer to. Uses the Stripe key of the seller connection that seller_connection names (service_connection:stripe is your own).

values.title: Start a Stripe checkout that pays someone else
values.job: Make a Stripe hosted checkout whose money goes to a person I pay, with my fee kept back
values.description: Give offers (your offer rows), offer_id, price_option_id, payer_ref, payee_account (their Stripe account id), fee ({ percent }), success_url and cancel_url. The platform fee is worked out in whole cents and never above the amount. Uses the Stripe key of the seller connection that seller_connection names (service_connection:stripe is your own).

values.title: Start or resume the first setup
values.job: Say what starting or resuming a new person's first setup does next: the ordered owner calls, each with the read-back to make after it
values.description: Given the account's saved setup run, its access prerequisites and the Workshop tool ids the caller found, return what starting or resuming the setup does, as an ordered list of steps. Each step names its owner tool and the call the caller makes; a step whose owner is not in available_tools is marked unavailable and is never called. Each called step carries a read_back (tool:read-setup) to run after it; done_steps are the steps already read back. A stopped setup is not restarted unless restart is true; a failed or stuck run resumes with its run_id; a finished run has no steps. Writes nothing: the caller runs the calls. Port of old trillion setup-runtime ensure().

values.title: Move a person through a guided tour, quiz or spotlight
values.job: Work out where a person is in a guided tour, walkthrough, spotlight or branching quiz after they start, go on, answer, go back, jump to a step or restart
values.description: Give the tour (an ordered list of steps with an entry step; a step may route by the person's answer with a branch_map of by_answer routes and a default_next) and one action: start or restart, advance (with the person's answer when the step asks one), back, or jump (with step_id). The cursor from the last answer goes back in with every action but start and restart. The answer is the new cursor (current_step_id, the history of steps visited, and status active or complete), the whole current step exactly as the tour author wrote it (what it shows and where it points are the author's and pass through untouched) and whether the tour has finished. Going on from the last step, or along a route to a step the tour does not have, finishes the tour and the cursor stays on the last step shown. Going back undoes exactly, even across a branch. Nothing is kept between calls; the caller keeps the cursor.

values.title: Link records into people and stage each
values.job: Link records that share a key into one person and give each person the highest stage their records reach
values.description: Takes records and a config. Records that share a value at any key path are one person (the same value at two different paths never links). Each person gets the highest-ranked stage any of their records reaches by the stage rules (exists, equals or greater-than tests on a field), the first source by time, the sum of a value field, and a confidence word: the identified word when any strong key is present, the anonymous word otherwise. Answers the people best stage first. Key paths, stage rules, the base stage and the confidence words are all in the config.

values.title: Stop sending an email course to someone who unsubscribed
values.job: End a person's email course subscription from the token in their unsubscribe link, so no further lesson is sent
values.description: Give token (the unsubscribe token in the link the person was sent). Works out the subscription marked unsubscribed with the time and answers it in keep for the caller to write (records: the person's token and subscription rows); an unknown or already used token answers unsubscribed too. Answers { status: unsubscribed }.

values.title: Stop the programs left running
values.job: Ask each program chosen as left running to end, wait for it, and say what happened to each, with one notice for the sweep when any ended
values.description: Runs on the person's computer with the rights they granted it to see the programs running there and to stop one. Give programs (the picked list tool:choose-programs-left-running answered) and optionally grace_ms (how long to wait for each to end, 10000 when not given, at most 60000). Each program is asked to end (SIGTERM) only when the same program is still there (the same pid and start time); nothing is forced. Returns stops (one per program: address, pid, started_at_ms, name, command, rule, why, asked_at, ended_at and outcome: ended, still-running, already-gone, not-the-same-program or not-allowed) and notices (one notice for the sweep when any program ended, none otherwise).

values.title: Stop sharing a show type
values.job: Stop sharing one of my show-rule presets with someone
values.description: Takes one person or account out of a shared type's grant (sharing:show-types-shared:<id>), so their share key reads nothing any more; the others it is shared with keep reading it. Answers keep, the grant to write.

values.title: Put my finished cuts one after another into one reel to watch (runs on your computer)
values.job: Put all my finished cuts into one video to watch in a row, with a short card naming each one before it, and tell me where each starts
values.description: Strings the cuts the person lists, in their order, into one reel without re-encoding them, with a plain text card of the seconds and words the person gives between each two, made at the first cut's frame size and rate. Returns where each cut starts in the reel (and writes it as text when asked); a listed file that does not exist is named and left out.

values.title: Read the money on my Stripe account since a moment
values.job: List the money that moved on this Stripe account since a moment, newest first, at most 100 entries
values.description: Lists what moved this Stripe account's balance at or after `since` (seconds since 1970, UTC), newest first, at most 100 entries: Stripe's own answer ({ data: [balance transactions, each with amount, fee and net in the currency's smallest unit, currency and reporting_category], has_more }), read with the Stripe account `connection` names (the person may hold more than one). Business's read (tool:read-business) sums it. Reads only.

values.title: Check and decide form answers
values.job: Check a person's answers against a form kept in the database and, when they are all valid, keep them with the score and segment they earn and any follow-up the form hands to its owner
values.description: Give form_id, respondent_id and answers (questionId to value). The form is read from the table question_sequence (make it with save-a-form) and the rules that decide the segment from the tables score_rule, segment_rule and follow_up_sequence. Optionally submission_id (for a form answered again and again, so each time has its own rows) and answered_at. The answers are checked against the form as check-form-answers does. If any is invalid the first to fix is returned and nothing is kept. Otherwise one transaction keeps an answer fact for each answer the form asks about (table answer_fact), one segment assignment (segment_assignment) and one request row for each question whose afterSaved names an owner and action, with the answers filled into its input (owner_action_request), and the tool answers the decision (score and segment), the segment's follow-up sequence and the rows kept. It reaches no database: give the person's form rows it reads as rows, and keep the rows the answer lists in keep.

values.title: Suggest connections from links
values.job: Offer to connect a service when words I wrote link to one I have not connected
values.description: Give text (the words to read links from, with or without https://) and tools (the connection rows, each { id, invoke: { provider, connects: { domain } } }), and connected (providers already connected, left out of the answer). A link matches a domain when its host is that domain or a name under it; the longest matching domain wins, and services sharing it are all named. Returns hosts and suggestions [{ provider, host, reason }]. It only proposes: connecting stays the person's own step.

values.title: Suggest cuts from a recording's words
values.job: Propose cuts in a recording from its kept transcript (long silences or filler words), as typed lines a person can watch, with a typed ending when there is nothing to cut
values.description: Give identity (the recording's identity), mode (silent_pauses or filler_words) and transcript (segments with timed words). Returns lines (status, thinking, then complete with remove-span proposals in the recording's own seconds, or an error line NO_TRANSCRIPT, NO_PROPOSALS or FAILED), keep (the answer to keep under the recording, mode and algorithm version) and modes. Hand the kept answer back as kept and the tool answers from it until the algorithm version changes. Nothing is applied: proposals are data.

values.title: Suggest zooms for a screen recording
values.job: Turn the pointer moves and clicks noted beside a screen recording into zoom suggestions (where the pointer settled, for how long, how strong), as plain rows the person can edit before the video is exported
values.description: Give sidecar: { space: 'normalized-source', samples: [{ t (ms), type: move | click, x, y (0 to 1 of the captured source) }] }. Telemetry in another space or without one is refused. Answers zooms: [{ start_ms, end_ms, x, y, strength (light, medium, strong), zoom, clicks }], sorted, none overlapping, the same every time for the same samples. Thresholds: read-data/auto-zoom.json.

values.title: Sum a character's time in each video and set it against the video's views (runs on your computer)
values.job: Sum how much a character speaks in each video of a show, in the opening, the body and the close, and see how that goes with how the videos did
values.description: Per video with <data_folder>/voice/<id>.turns.json: turns, seconds, share, seconds in the opening (opening_seconds) and the close (closing_seconds), exchanges in the body (turns within 8 s) per ten minutes, median gap and turn, and whether it is one the character was stripped from (stripped_ids). Then, over the episodes: medians by year, the rank correlation of character seconds and share with views against the baseline per year and overall, the median against the baseline of the low, middle and high thirds by character seconds within each year, the stripped against the full episodes between compare_from_month and compare_to_month, and the episodes with the least character time from lowest_from_year. Writes <data_folder>/character-per-video.tsv.

values.title: Switch a kept show type
values.job: Switch one of my show-rule presets on or off
values.description: Switches a type you keep on or off (use: { type, on }, required); only types you keep can be on, and a type applies only while it is on. Answers in_use and keep, the record to write.

values.title: Tag a Stripe subscription
values.job: Add notes (metadata) to a buyer Stripe subscription without changing the ones already there
values.description: Give subscription_id and metadata (text values). Only keys you give are added or changed, and nothing is written when nothing changes. Uses the Stripe key of the seller connection that seller_connection names (service_connection:stripe is your own).

values.title: Take a request
values.job: Keep one request that arrived, as decided, and ask the owner who should act on it
values.description: request is what arrived: request_id, source_ref, atom_ref, text, origin_ref, optionally message_ref, content_revision and at. Its origin_ref must be one the person accepts (an intake-origins record with id intake-origins:accepted). decision is the caller's: disposition and reason, and hand_to_owner true with owner_ref (an active intake-owner record) and acceptance_criteria when an owner should act; hand_off, required when hand_to_owner is true, names what the owner is asked to run (action_ref or action_refs, optional id, input and copy rows). existing_task_ref is refused (current_task_executor_not_verified): a task reference says nothing about who runs it now. max_text_chars (default 65536) bounds the kept text: a longer text is kept cut to it, or, when it is being handed to an owner, held back. Returns { status, request_id, problems, owner_request, said }. status is handed, recorded, deferred (nothing is kept because the owner is not on file or the text is too long; take it again once fixed), already-taken (the same request again changes nothing) or refused (no accepted origins on file, incomplete, origin not accepted, a decision that names an existing task, or the same id from another source, message, place or version).

values.title: Take a show rule away
values.job: Take away one of my show rules
values.description: Takes one rule out of your show-rules record by its id (from see-when-things-show); a starting rule is switched off instead. Answers the rules after the change and keep, the record to write.

values.title: Take a show type away
values.job: Take away a preset of show rules I keep
values.description: Takes one type you keep out of your show-rules record (remove_type), and switches it off. A type another kept type inherits is refused, since its children would lose rules without saying. Answers keep, the record to write.

values.title: Take the next task waiting for me, or one task by its id
values.job: Take the next task that is waiting for me or for anyone, so no one else does it too
values.description: Without id, reads the tasks a take may move (waiting ones that name `as` or no one, and taken ones held longer than the stale-take time), sorts them by take_order (priority, then oldest first), and takes the first: one write of the whole task as taken by as at this time, conditioned on the value it read. When someone else took that task first the write is refused and changes nothing, and the next one is tried, at most take_tries. only_mine keeps only tasks that name as. With id, takes that task, or answers taken null with reason changed (and the task as it now is) when someone else won it. taken is null when there was nothing to take. The same request key gives back the same claim. The caller hands in every record it reads as input.records; this tool reads no store and names no store method. Each write it makes comes back as keep, for the caller to keep in the person's own store.

values.title: Take back a post
values.job: Work out taking back a post that is waiting for its time and that nothing was sent for, and answer it as a draft that goes nowhere
values.description: Give post_id of a scheduled post nothing was sent for. It becomes a draft again, so its time sends nothing. A post already on its way cannot be taken back. Give records: the post. Returns post, said and the draft post row to store under `keep`.

values.title: Take me to the thing that needs me
values.job: Take a person to the thing that needs them: give the screen to open on one waiting card, the arrangement that puts it beside what the caller names, the walkthrough that points at the card's own control and the notice that links to both, or say in plain words that nothing is waiting there or it opens outside their places
values.description: Give thing (a card id from the answer of tool:what-is-waiting-on-me, or a batch section's key, batch: and the section id), waiting (that answer: { sections: [{ cards }] } or { cards }, a card { id, source?, title?, action?, address?, points_at? }), screens (the caller's rows, { path_prefix, tool_id, route_input_from_query?: [names] }, one for each address path that opens a screen) and own_origins (the origins whose links open inside the person's own places). Answers { taken: false, said } when the thing is not waiting now or its link leads outside those origins or to no screen; otherwise { taken: true, screen: { tool_id, route_input }, arrangement (one pane, or a split with beside, its id the thing's key), tour (when steps are given: each step points at the card's own control, points_at filled with the item id, else a fallback selector; started by name, finished when the card's ids are completed), notice (when say is given), open (the address that opens the arrangement and tour), said }. It saves no arrangement or tour and sends no notice: whoever keeps those does that with what this returns.

values.title: Take over a space
values.job: Take over a space with a code someone handed you: you become its owner, and the owner before stays a member
values.description: The code works once. The answer marks its record:space-handover row used, and a later use is refused in the words for a lapsed link. A code past its 14 days is refused the same way. It replaces the old take_over.

values.title: Take the pictures out of a zip archive
values.job: Take the pictures out of a zip archive as files to import, without ever unpacking it to disk by entry name
values.description: Give zip_base64 (the archive's bytes), and when wanted profile (chat_export: the conversations*.json files of an account export) or limits (max_entries, max_entry_bytes, max_total_bytes, max_ratio, media_types, title_prefix). Only entries of an admitted extension are read; archive litter (__MACOSX, ._ files, .DS_Store, Thumbs.db) and folders never are. An entry's name is never a path: it gives only a title (its last segment without the extension). An archive over a limit is refused whole, naming the limit. Returns entries [{ title, media_type, byte_count, bytes_base64 }] in archive order and count.

values.title: Tally a community's match picks
values.job: Show how a community picked the winner of each match (the split by choice), what the result was, and how one person's own picks turned out
values.description: Give the records of the matches (pick-match: matchId, label, startsAt, choices of { choiceId, label }), the picks (match-pick: matchId, pickerId, choiceId, createdAt) and the results (match-pick-result: matchId, winningChoiceId, summary, resolvedAt). Each match comes back by start time with every choice's count and whole percent (rounded, so the percents may not add to 100), the winning choice once there is a result (the latest result record counts) and, with picker_id, that picker's own choice. A picker who changed their pick counts once, for the latest pick. With picker_id the answer also lists that picker's picks newest first with the match and choice in words, the result summary, whether the pick was right once the match has a result, and whether a later pick replaced it. Free picks only: this tool reads records and moves no money. To keep wording out of a prompt or a result summary (for example talk of money), check the text with tool:check-pick-copy and the list the person gives.

values.title: Tell if a tool changes anything
values.job: Tell whether a tool only reads or changes things, from its own operation name
values.description: Give tool (a tool descriptor: id, and optionally read_only and invoke.action). read_only: true is a read; otherwise the operation (invoke.action, or the id without tool:) is a read when it starts with a read verb such as read, list, find, show, check, search, get or view followed by -. Anything else, including an operation not understood, is a write. Returns write_class: 'read' or 'write'.

values.title: Tell a judge it was wrong, so it is tested on that case from now on (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn a verdict that was wrong into a known case in my rubrics file, so every model is tested against it from the next calibration on
values.description: Give rubrics_file, rubric_id, should_have_been (true, false, a number or one of the options), and either about (the text) or log_file (a verdict log written by tool:ask-a-small-model-for-a-verdict, the last verdict for that rubric is used), and optionally because. Adds one labelled case and stops: it does not change the question, the line or the model. The same text twice is not added twice (a different label corrects the earlier one). Adding cases makes a rubric harder to pass, which is the point: a model that cannot handle the new case stops being chosen for the question.

values.title: Tell our own spoken words from a heard request
values.job: Recognize recently spoken account notices in heard words and return evidence naming the notice, preserving generated words as labelled context.
values.description: Recognize recently spoken account notices in heard words and return evidence naming the notice, preserving generated words as labelled context. All opinion settings arrive as input rows; the tool reads no records. No old Worker store is imported.

values.title: Time how fast a small decider model loads and answers on my computer (runs on your computer)
values.job: Time how long a small decider model takes to load and to answer on my computer, and how much memory it holds
values.description: Give model (a decider snapshot in the Hugging Face cache) and optionally revision and device. Runs a made-up two-question case four times.

values.title: Get word-level timestamps for a recording on this computer
values.job: Give me timed words from a recording or a window of it
values.description: Runs the existing whisper_here.py provider with word timestamps, optionally on a source-time window, and writes source-time word bounds. Accepts JSON on stdin; model defaults to mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo.

values.title: Time each word of a voice take to where the voice starts (runs on your computer)
values.job: Move the word start times of a voice take to where the voice really begins, so graphics land on the word
values.description: Whisper puts part of a pause into the next word's start, so a graphic timed to it lands early. Each word's start moves to the first 10 ms window inside the word whose level is above -45 dBFS; its end stays. With the take's line.json ({"script": the words the take was made from}) each word takes the script's spelling when the script and the read have the same number of words. Writes {source, timing, words}. It runs on the person's own computer, never on Trillion.

values.title: Total the lines of a quote or invoice
values.job: Total the lines of a quote or invoice in order, where each percent line names the base it multiplies (the line above, the lines since the last subtotal, or all above) and a subtotal line resets that base
values.description: action totals takes lines { kind_field?, value_field?, base_field?, order_field? } and row_ids or every row. A line's kind is a row of read-data/list-settlements.json line_totals.kinds (amount, percent, subtotal); a percent line must name its base. Answers each line with its amount, the base it used and the running total, and the total. It reads only the `lists` handed in.

values.title: Follow one thing I point at through a video clip and outline it in every frame (runs on your computer)
values.job: Follow an object or a person I pointed at through a clip and get its outline in every frame
values.description: Takes a video, a stretch of up to 30 seconds, the second at which the person pointed, and one to 32 points on that frame, each marked as inside the object or outside it. It runs a point-prompted SAM 2 video model on the person's own computer and writes, in a new folder, a lossless grayscale mask video (mask.mkv), one mask picture and one transparent preview picture per frame, and result.json with how many pixels the object covers in each frame. A frame where the object is hidden has an empty mask: it is kept empty, not filled with a guess. If nothing is found at the pointed spot the run fails and says to choose another point. Frames never leave the computer, the model is read from the local cache and never downloaded, and the video is only read.

values.title: Trade a Facebook sign-in code for its short-lived token
values.job: Trade the code Facebook's sign-in page handed back for the connection's short-lived user token, kept sealed in the vault
values.description: One token request to Facebook (the facebook-messenger descriptor's acquire.token_url, client_auth form): the code and the callback address go in a form body with the Facebook login's app id and secret, placed from the vault only as the request leaves. The reply's access_token (a short-lived user token) is kept in the vault as the new connection's field short_lived_access_token before the reply is read; tool:trade-a-short-facebook-token-for-a-long-one then trades it for the 60-day user token (the descriptor's acquire.then). Run by tool:connect-an-account-by-signing-in-to-the-service at the sign-in callback.

values.title: Trade a Gmail sign-in code for its tokens
values.job: Trade the code Google's sign-in page handed back for the connection's access and refresh tokens, kept sealed in the vault
values.description: One token request to Google (the google-account descriptor's acquire.token_url, client_auth form, PKCE): the code, the callback address and the PKCE verifier go in a form body with the Google sign-in app's id and secret, placed from the vault only as the request leaves. The reply's access_token, refresh_token and id_token are kept in the vault as the new connection's own fields (reply_holds_values) before the reply is read, so no token is ever in a run's answer or journal; a field already held is never replaced and then nothing is sent. Run by tool:connect-an-account-by-signing-in-to-the-service at the sign-in callback.

values.title: Trade a short-lived Facebook token for a long-lived one
values.job: Trade the connection's short-lived Facebook user token for its 60-day user token, kept sealed in the vault
values.description: The facebook-messenger descriptor's acquire.then step: GET graph.facebook.com/v23.0/oauth/access_token with grant_type fb_exchange_token, the Facebook login's app id and secret and the connection's short-lived token, all placed from the vault only as the request leaves. The reply's access_token is kept in the vault as the connection's user_access_token field before the reply is read; tool:list-the-facebook-pages-a-sign-in-reaches then reads the Pages it reaches with it. Run by tool:connect-an-account-by-signing-in-to-the-service at the sign-in callback, right after tool:trade-a-facebook-sign-in-code-for-its-short-token.

values.title: Trade a short-lived Instagram token for a long-lived one
values.job: Trade the connection's short-lived Instagram token for its 60-day token, kept sealed in the vault
values.description: The instagram descriptor's acquire.then step: GET graph.instagram.com/access_token with grant_type ig_exchange_token, the Instagram login's app secret and the connection's short-lived token, both placed from the vault only as the request leaves. The reply's access_token is kept in the vault as the connection's access_token field before the reply is read. Run by tool:connect-an-account-by-signing-in-to-the-service at the sign-in callback, right after tool:trade-an-instagram-sign-in-code-for-its-short-token.

values.title: Trade a short-lived Threads token for a long-lived one
values.job: Trade the connection's short-lived Threads token for its 60-day token, kept sealed in the vault
values.description: The threads descriptor's acquire.then step: GET graph.threads.net/access_token with grant_type th_exchange_token, the Threads login's app secret and the connection's short-lived token, both placed from the vault only as the request leaves. The reply's access_token is kept in the vault as the connection's access_token field before the reply is read. Run by tool:connect-an-account-by-signing-in-to-the-service at the sign-in callback, right after tool:trade-a-threads-sign-in-code-for-its-short-token.

values.title: Trade a Threads sign-in code for its short-lived token
values.job: Trade the code Threads' sign-in page handed back for the connection's short-lived token, kept sealed in the vault
values.description: One token request to Threads (the threads descriptor's acquire.token_url, client_auth form): the code and the callback address go in a form body with the Threads login's app id and secret, placed from the vault only as the request leaves. The reply's access_token (Threads' short-lived token) is kept in the vault as the new connection's field short_lived_access_token before the reply is read; tool:trade-a-short-threads-token-for-a-long-one then trades it for the 60-day token (the descriptor's acquire.then). Run by tool:connect-an-account-by-signing-in-to-the-service at the sign-in callback.

values.title: Trade a tool server's sign-in code for its tokens
values.job: Trade the code a remote tool server's sign-in page handed back for its access and refresh tokens, kept sealed in the vault
values.description: One token request to the server's authorization server at the address its own sign-in documents gave (RFC 6749 section 4.1.3, a public client: the code, the callback address, the PKCE verifier and the client id go in a form body, the server named as the resource, RFC 8707). The reply's access_token is kept in the vault as the connection's access_token field, reaching only the resource's host (hosts_from_input: an OAuth token is for the resource it was issued for), and its refresh_token as refresh_token, reaching only the token address it came from; the token address and the client id are kept beside them from the input, so the engine can refresh the token when a tool of the server is called by its address (trillion-rust remote_mcp.rs at_address). Nothing else is kept. Run by the command line's connect (tools/use-your-tools-from-a-shell) when the person comes back from the sign-in page; the discovery and registration before it are do-work/sign-in-to-a-tool-server.mjs.

values.title: Trade a YouTube sign-in code for its tokens
values.job: Trade the code YouTube's sign-in page handed back for the connection's access and refresh tokens, kept sealed in the vault
values.description: One token request to Google (the youtube descriptor's acquire.token_url, client_auth form, PKCE): the code, the callback address and the PKCE verifier go in a form body with the Google sign-in app's id and secret, placed from the vault only as the request leaves. The reply's access_token, refresh_token and id_token are kept in the vault as the new connection's own fields (reply_holds_values) before the reply is read, so no token is ever in a run's answer or journal; a field already held is never replaced and then nothing is sent. Run by tool:connect-an-account-by-signing-in-to-the-service at the sign-in callback.

values.title: Trade an Instagram sign-in code for its short-lived token
values.job: Trade the code Instagram's sign-in page handed back for the connection's short-lived token, kept sealed in the vault
values.description: One token request to Instagram (the instagram descriptor's acquire.token_url, client_auth form): the code and the callback address go in a form body with the Instagram login's app id and secret, placed from the vault only as the request leaves. The reply's access_token (Instagram's short-lived token) is kept in the vault as the new connection's field short_lived_access_token before the reply is read; tool:trade-a-short-instagram-token-for-a-long-one then trades it for the 60-day token (the descriptor's acquire.then). Run by tool:connect-an-account-by-signing-in-to-the-service at the sign-in callback.

values.title: Trade an X sign-in code for its tokens
values.job: Trade the code X's sign-in page handed back for the connection's access and refresh tokens, kept sealed in the vault
values.description: One token request to X (the x descriptor's acquire.token_url, client_auth basic, PKCE): the code, the callback address, the PKCE verifier and the sign-in app's id go in a form body, and the app's Basic credentials (the held x-sign-in-client-secret-basic) in the Authorization header, each placed from the vault only as the request leaves. The reply's access_token and refresh_token are kept in the vault as the new connection's own fields (reply_holds_values) before the reply is read. Run by tool:connect-an-account-by-signing-in-to-the-service at the sign-in callback.

values.title: Teach a small decider model my rules by training a LoRA adapter (runs on your Mac or GPU)
values.job: Train a small local model to judge lines by my rules
values.description: LoRA-trains a decider-style multiple-choice model (a model folder that carries its own decider package and decider_config.json, such as decider-2b) on train.jsonl from tool:build-training-rows-from-a-persons-rules, with cross-entropy on the option letter, each line put in the person's frame. It runs at low priority with few CPU threads beside the person's work, projects the whole run after 20 steps and stops when the projection passes the time budget. It saves the adapter and train-info.json (settings, rows, minutes, final loss).

values.title: Train a writing-voice adapter on labelled rows
values.job: Train a small LoRA adapter that judges a writer's voice from labelled training rows bound to their source passages
values.description: Runs on the person's computer that holds the decider model snapshot and its frame (common.py, the folder decider_common_dir names, from the person's settings row for this tool). Only split train rows are taken; gold never enters the prompt; a provenance manifest binds every row to its source passage and criterion through the maintained request plan before the model loads. Writes the adapter and a receipt (BLAKE3 of the DATA, every setting) into a new folder; sends no request.

values.title: Transcribe a recording with a time for every word, and repair Whisper loops (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn a recording into a transcript with a time for every word, and fix the places where the transcription got stuck repeating one sentence
values.description: Runs the audio-transcription package's own transcribe-audio.py on the person's own computer: the recording (audio, or video with sound) is decoded to 16 kHz mono and read by whisper.cpp, and the answer is the package's result: language, full text, segments, and words with a start, an end and a timing_source that says whether the time came from the engine's token times, from the segment's bounds or from an even split of the segment. The seam adds the recording's length, its path, and when it was made (a camera's sidecar XML beside it, else the file's time). transcribe-many does a whole folder, skipping recordings already done, a few at once and waiting while the computer is busy. Whisper sometimes gets stuck and writes one sentence again and again over minutes of real speech or silence. find-loops finds those stretches (a sentence said four or more times that fills half a segment, or a segment that repeats the one before). repair merges the ones that are close, hears again only those windows with the earlier text not carried in (whisper.cpp -mc 0) and splices the new words in at their true seconds. A sentence that still loops is taken out and kept in removed_hallucinated, so nothing disappears silently; repair-many repairs a whole folder, each transcript from the recording it names. judge says whether a whole answer is to be trusted at all (one segment said over and over, one run of four words coming back again and again, too few different words, too few words a minute, mostly no speech) and why. index writes one line per transcript (length, words, segments, first thing said) with the totals, and text writes a transcript as [m:ss] paragraphs about thirty seconds long (with the title and header lines the person gives), refusing one judge rejects. When a transcript does not carry its recording's length, judge and text take it as --duration, or judge takes each recording's length from a tab-separated list (--durations). Nothing leaves the computer and no key is needed.

values.title: Move a conversation to the trash
values.job: Move every message of one conversation to the trash, where it can still be restored.
values.description: Move every message of one conversation to the trash, where it can still be restored. Takes provider (an id of read-data/mail-providers.json) and connection (the person's account of that provider, by its handle only: {connection_id}). Runs as that account with the key the person's vault holds for it; the engine hands the key to this run alone and it is placed only in the request to the provider's own host, never shown. Answers the provider-neutral rows of read-data/neutral.mjs, never the provider's own payload. A provider that does not offer it says so in words.

values.title: Move a message to the trash
values.job: Move one message to the trash, where it can still be restored.
values.description: Move one message to the trash, where it can still be restored. Takes provider (an id of read-data/mail-providers.json) and connection (the person's account of that provider, by its handle only: {connection_id}). Runs as that account with the key the person's vault holds for it; the engine hands the key to this run alone and it is placed only in the request to the provider's own host, never shown. Answers the provider-neutral rows of read-data/neutral.mjs, never the provider's own payload. A provider that does not offer it says so in words.

values.title: Turn a drawn stroke into a line, rectangle or polygon
values.job: Turn the points of a drawn stroke into the shape the chosen drawing tool makes: freehand ink, a straight line, a rectangle or a regular polygon or ellipse
values.description: Give the drawing tool's own row and the stroke's points in order. The tool's mapper picks the shape: passthrough keeps every point, segment keeps the first and last, polygon with corners gives the four corners of the rectangle between first and last point, polygon with sides N gives N points on the ellipse inscribed in that rectangle (3 to 18 reads as a regular polygon, many as an ellipse). A mapper of any other kind keeps the stroke as drawn. The answer also says whether the tool closes its figure and whether it is an eraser (an eraser appends a hide effect instead of ink). Points are [x, y] or { values: [x, y] }.

values.title: Turn a presentation plan into a teleprompter session
values.job: Turn a written video presentation plan into the recording session the camera screen runs: the teleprompter script sentence by sentence, the countdown, when to stop on silence, on the final word or on a stop phrase, and whether it may start by itself
values.description: Give plan (one compiled video presentation plan: id, title, medium video, execution.adapter capture.video, beats each with delivery speak and text, no open acquisitions, and the execution settings: countdown_seconds, auto_stop_seconds, silence_stop_seconds, silence_threshold_rms, minimum_speech_ms, stop_on_final_word, completion_grace_ms, completion_slack_words, script_end_quiet_seconds, stop_phrases, mirror_script, speech_language, follow_speech, allow_manual_nudge, completion_label), and optionally readiness (the setup pass's result for this plan), authorization (a grant: plan_id, authorized, authorized_at_ms, grant_until_ms) and nowMs (epoch milliseconds; the run's clock when left out). Answers the record-video.recording-session: session_id, title, subtitle, the stop and speech-follow settings with their defaults filled in, sentences (the teleprompter script), source_plan, requirements, plan_capabilities, readiness_state, authorization_state and auto_start, which is true only with a complete matching readiness and an unexpired grant for this plan. Refuses a plan that is not a video plan for capture.video, has open acquisitions (a gathering format), has no beats or a beat that is not spoken text, has a negative or non-numeric setting, and a grant that claims capture without fresh readiness or that does not match the plan and time. It reads only its input: it never opens a camera or microphone, never treats a plan as consent, records nothing and asks no AI to write a script. The screen's other work (the camera picture, countdown, live waveform, silence stop and speech-following teleprompter while recording, voice-only choice, and having the person's AI write the script for a format) needs a browser and is not done by this run.

values.title: Check the video quotes behind my device rows and write the rows as tables (runs on your computer)
values.job: Check that every quote my device rows cite is really said in the videos' captions, stamp each with the minute and second, and write the rows as tables grouped my way
values.description: A device row says what a creative technique (a device) does for a viewer, how it is built, and where it is seen, as exact quotes from videos ([video id, words]) or as unmeasured evidence (null, text). The script reads the person's settings row for this tool (list:settings, record:setting:turn-caption-quotes-into-analysis-device-rows~<scope_kind>~<scope_id>, one row per batch of rows, scope piece:<family>) through tools/settings: the family name, title and introduction, the channel and title of each video, the group order, the rows, the table columns as templates ({field} and {field|one|many}, a part kept only `when` its field is set), the head lines of the family file, the index marker, how a checked quote is written, and the fields kept in the checked-rows file. It finds each quote in the video's json3 caption file as exact words (ignoring case, white space and curly apostrophes), tells a wrong quote from a missing caption file, and counts the creators (channels) and items (videos) each row's checked quotes come from. Only when every quote holds does it write: the family file (head lines, then one table per group), the family's tables added once under its marker at the end of an index file, and the checked rows with [video, second, quote] for each quote. The tool holds no columns, wording or groups of its own.

values.title: Turn frames into slides
values.job: Turn a board's presentation frames into slides in story order, one page each, as SVG, printable HTML, a PDF and a picture of every page
values.description: Give a request file: board (its items: a presentation frame is an item with extra.presentationFrame.order, and every item centred inside it is on that slide), title, look_values and look_css (from tool:resolve-a-look, so any colour or font written as a variable name such as --accent-primary is the look's own), assets (name to file or https address; an item with src asset:<name> draws it, a file carried as its bytes), frames (the frame memberIds to make, in order; absent: every frame) and words_from (a filled word template from tool:fill-a-word-template: its tokens name the item they belong to, and that item's words become the filled ones). Text may show a look value as {{--name}} (a swatch label), so the value is never copied. An item may carry its own type: extra.fontSize, fontWeight, fontFamily, lineHeight, textInset and charWidth, and extra.imageFit contain for a logo. Every frame is one page of the frame's size. Writes slides/NN.svg and deck.html (which keeps the slide words as inert records a word template can be made from); with --pdf the PDF, with --pictures pages/NN.png. A variable the look lacks, an unknown asset or a frame of another size stops the run and says which.
