values.title: Turn my agent skills into workflows my AI can find and run
values.job: Take the agent skills I have installed (the rows of my agent-skills list) and make each one a workflow in my own account, leaving out any skill that names a secret key, a folder on my computer, an email address, a phone number or one of my private words
values.description: Takes the rows of the person's own agent-skills list (input.records, record:agent-skill; a long file is several rows, joined in order) and answers each clean skill as a workflow. A skill is a folder holding a SKILL.md with a name and a description. Each skill whose text is clean becomes one workflow: a row whose id is workflow: then skill- then the skill's name and one step whose instructions are the skill's, with its text files (smallest first, within a size budget) under files; the answer's workflows hold those rows (a record:workflow-recipe row and a record:workflow-step row each) for the caller's AI to write where the person keeps workflows. A skill whose SKILL.md or shipped files match a secret key, a computer path, an email address, a phone number, or a word in input.private_words stays home, and the answer names it and the kind of reason, never the text. Put the workflow rows already kept (record:workflow-recipe) in input.records too and a workflow made from a skill that is now gone or held back is named under stale. input.folder keeps only skills under that folder. This run reads only the records handed in and keeps nothing. What is screened and the size budget are data (data/skill-import-rules.json), not code.

values.title: Turn signed events into their effects, once each
values.job: Turn signed events into the effects their installed rules name, each effect once, from a verifier answer given in the input, and list a subject's effects from a reader answer given in the input, showing every call that would be sent
values.description: Runs the signed-event-effects targets with no transport. op admit (admitSignedEventEffects): descriptor_ref names an installed admission descriptor (records.json: signed-event-effects.owner-action-accepted.v1 or signed-event-effects.payment-provider-event-accepted.v1); each of events is sent to the descriptor's verifier target, whose answer must give the event's hash in evaluation.event_hashes; each fact of a verified event that matches an effect rule (relation, objects, required attributes) becomes one effect with an id made from its event, fact, relation, subject and object, so the same fact twice is one effect; each effect is then sent to the write path the dispatch policy declares. op list (listSignedEventEffects): descriptor_ref signed-event-effects.by-subject.v1 and subject; the descriptor's query is sent to its reader target and the rows it answers come back as effects. replies is DATA the caller makes up or brings: { <target>: reply | [reply, ...] }, the answers the verifier, writer and reader give (a list answers one call each, in order); this run does not check a signature itself, does not write or read any store and sends nothing anywhere: every call is answered from replies and written down in sent. Refuses a caller-given descriptor, a descriptor_ref that is not installed, a write path the dispatch policy does not declare, a verifier answer without the event's hash, a call to a target replies gives no answer for, and an op other than admit or list. The live screen sends these calls to the real verifier, workflow writer and current-items reader through its own send; this run does not.

values.title: Type dictated text at the cursor
values.job: Put dictated text where the person's cursor is as one clipboard transaction (save, write, paste, restore, verify), never pasting over a clipboard it cannot put back, and note the dictation in their bounded history
values.description: Give text (cleaned by tool:dictate) and entry_id and context.app when known. Returns entry_id, kind (inserted-verified, inserted-unverified, blocked or failed) and saved, wrote, pasted, restored, verified and error.

values.title: Unpair a sender
values.job: Stop letting a paired sender's messages through, so they are unknown again
values.description: Give source_id and sender. The sender is no longer paired for that source; their next message gets a new code. Returns source_id, sender and said. It reaches no database: give the pairing facts the person keeps as facts, and keep what the answer's keep lists.

values.title: Unpublish a tool
values.job: Take one of my published tools back out of the marketplace
values.description: Withdraws this maker's listing of one tool. The listing body is removed; the content-free evidence (maker, fingerprint, times) stays, so no other maker can take the id.

values.title: Take files out of the next commit
values.job: Take chosen files in a project on the person's computer out of the next commit, leaving the files as they are
values.description: Give folder (the full path of the project folder the person has let this tool use) and paths (the files to take out, relative to the folder). Returns the project's changes after it. The files keep every edit they have; only their place in the next commit changes.

values.title: Upload a file to a signed storage slot
values.job: Upload one file from a folder the person granted to a signed storage slot a page hands over, only to a destination the tool's own list allows, so the page never sees the file
values.description: Give file (its name inside the folder the person granted this tool, such as reports/diag.zip), content_type (the file's media type) and slot ({ url, fields }: the https address and the text form fields the storage service signed). The slot is checked as a whole before a byte leaves: https, a host equal to a destination row's, a path inside that row's folder, no query, fragment, credentials or port, text-only fields within the row's field cap, and a content type the row lists. The file is read from the granted folder only (a name that leaves it, or a link out of it, names nothing), held once, and posted as the form's last field. Storage redirects are refused, so the file is not forwarded to another address. Returns sent, size and said; the signed fields are never in an answer or an error. The shipped destination list is empty, so it uploads nowhere until a destination row is added to read-data/guarded-upload.json.

values.title: Use a snippet
values.job: Fill in one of my snippets with this time's names and give me its words to put in what I am writing
values.description: Give snippet_id (the snippet's id as the store keeps it) and values: { name: words } for each {name} blank. Returns snippet_id, title, text (the words with every given blank filled wherever it appears), left_blank (the blanks given no value, left exactly as written) and said naming them, so nothing is sent with a hole unseen. It counts and stores nothing and never changes the snippet's words. It sends nothing. Give records: the snippet's record. Refuses an unknown snippet_id.

values.title: Work in an app on your computer
values.job: On the person's own computer, edit a video timeline in DaVinci Resolve and do anything else its scripting allows (projects, media pool, clips, markers, colour, Fusion, Fairlight audio, rendering), or write DaVinci Resolve project, timeline and grade files that import into any edition, or reverse engineer an app or binary, decompile it and explain how a feature works under the hood (native computer, Linux and Windows programs, .NET, Android, Electron and JavaScript apps, firmware, websites), through the app's own tool server
values.description: Runs on the computer where the app is. Leave out operation to see every operation the app offers with the input each takes, then call again with one operation and its arguments. Which apps it can use are the rows of apps-here.json (app: davinci-resolve works in the open Resolve project in every edition, Studio through External scripting set to Local and the free edition through a helper this tool puts in Resolve's scripts folder, which Resolve runs when it opens; davinci-resolve-files writes and reads Resolve's .drp, .drt and .drx files without Resolve open; rea reverse engineers, inspects, decompiles and explains programs and files on this computer, using Hopper, Ghidra or IDA for native code where one is installed and a Chrome-family browser to watch a website or Electron app run). The app's own answer comes back as it said it. An app that must be running is opened in the background without taking focus; never file a Waiting on you row asking the person to open it.

values.title: Use your tools from any AI's shell: the site's own command (runs on your computer)
values.job: Let an AI that can run shell commands see my AIs and their jobs, hand and take work, and run my Workshop tools, with no MCP connection of its own
values.description: The `{cli}` command. Every command is ONE call of the engine's one MCP tool (do_one_thing_in_my_account) at the account's door: the brand's Mac app's local door when this computer has one, else the public origin. setup signs in once, puts `{cli}` on the PATH and writes the skill for each AI app here; whoami, who, send, work, take, finish, fail, stuck, release, withdraw, remove and serve move AI jobs through tools/hand-work-to-ais; publish answers this AI's own record as a keep row for the person's own store; tools and call list and run Workshop tools; op runs any engine operation; schedule lists and switches the wakes tool rows declare; records replay-from-transcripts lists the rows this computer's AIs wrote, from their own transcripts, for the person's own store (it writes nothing back). Nothing here reads or writes a row. The credential is the account's existing key or the sign-in login kept, read into memory only, never printed or put on a command line. Every call carries one request key reused on every retry. A copy an owner installed (its install-owner.json marker beside it) is never rewritten by a bare copy, and `{cli} update` names who updates it: the command never updates itself.

values.title: Verify a waiting completion
values.job: Read the same persisted target and verify the current effect of a waiting completion
values.description: Checks, on the waiting records handed in (read them again from the person's own store after the keep, each { id, type, value }), the saved completion key and BLAKE3 effect identity against the source's declared fields, and answers completed/next_round only when that same effect still holds. A hidden card, unavailable feed or historical command result proves nothing here. Hand in the person's record:waiting-sources records as sources when they added any. Reads and changes nothing in the person's records.

values.title: See a poker table as one player may see it
values.job: Show a poker table as one player may see it: the board, the pot, each seat, what that player may do now and only that player's own cards
values.description: Give a saved table (the room run-a-poker-table returned) and, optionally, the id of the player looking. Returns the phase and street, hand number, pot, current bet, minimum raise and blinds, the board as it is dealt so far, the label of the next street, every seat (chips, bet, dealer and blind marks, whose turn it is, folded, all in, out, connected), the four betting controls (fold, check or call with what a call costs, raise with its minimum, all in) switched on only for the player whose turn it is, that player's own two cards, every player's cards once the hand is over and never before, and the hand's result with the winners' names. With no player id it is the view of a spectator and holds no private cards. Refuses a room that is not a saved table and a player who is not at it.

values.title: Record a voice take of every line my plans have a voice read (runs on your computer)
values.job: Make a voice recording of every line in my plans that a voice reads aloud, with the voice I choose, and keep each one so it is made only once
values.description: Finds every segment whose piece is a voiced line in the person's piece table, and for each line with no take yet runs the person's speaker commands (voice.say: any text-to-speech and finishing chain, each command filled with the line, a file of it, a folder of its own and the take to write). Each take is kept as <name>.wav beside <name>.txt holding its exact words, named by the BLAKE3 of the words, so a line is found by what it says. Comes with a Kokoro speaker (do-work/say_line_kokoro.py: mlx-audio on Apple Silicon, trimmed to the words, a soft end and a little room tone).

values.title: Make my voice from a recording of me
values.job: Make the voice Trillion can speak to me in from a recording of me on this computer
values.description: Makes the person's own voice from `recording`, a recording of them on this computer: the speech model on this computer picks the stretch that ends where a sentence ends and makes a reference sound of it. The answer holds `voice` (the row { id, values } for their Voices list: label, engine, reference_text, made_from, made_at) and the reference sound as the run's declared output (`files`), the file the row's `reference` then names. This tool keeps nothing: the person's AI keeps the row in a store, chooses or removes voices there, and hands the rows to tool:say-with-a-voice-model.

values.title: Walk a sales funnel
values.job: Read a sales funnel's offers and see the price a buyer is shown and where an outcome such as buying or declining takes them next
values.description: Reads the funnel records a person keeps: the funnel graph, its offer nodes (each with an offer, a price and the outcomes that move a buyer on), and the price experiments run on them. Gives back the whole flow in the order a buyer meets it, the price shown on the entry offer (the winning version of a settled price experiment when one applies, else the offer's own price, with which record decided it), the step a buyer is on, and where a named outcome takes them (an outcome that leads to no node ends the flow). It can also order a page's call-to-action links, main one first. Outcomes and offers are the person's own words; nothing is built in.

values.title: Walk a new person through first setup
values.job: Walk a new person through first setup: the apps to install on their devices, the AIs to connect, and the one saved run that resumes where they stopped
values.description: Give the setup plan for one person's account from what the caller reads and hands over: the saved setup run and what it does next (its next calls, the workflow's steps), the access prerequisites still open, what the account already has (pursuits, connections, profile, devices), the computers it can reach and their tool cards, the person's pursuit lens and the entry point they came from. Returns the plan: the apps to install on their devices (with the public links or the honest not-yet words), the local harness installer's download, inspect, apply and remove commands per supported AI host, the MCP registration preview commands, the instructions the AI follows, and the setup policy. view 'state' returns the run and its next calls only; view 'full' adds the installs, the policy and the lens. Given database (or credential_name), it reads the toolkits and toolkit_swaps tables there and offers their rows, and a toolkit_choice (the toolkit picked, tool ids dropped from it, tool ids added) answers the tool ids to install. Nothing else is read from storage and nothing is written: starting or resuming the saved run is not yet ported, so next calls that name start_setup are not run by this tool.

values.title: Walk through an app like its users
values.job: Check that people can still do what they come to my app for after a change: walk each journey in a real browser, keep pictures, a log and a video, and tell my coding agent exactly what to fix, then check the fix
values.description: Opens the app at app_url in a headless Chromium on the person's own computer (so it reaches local, VPN and Tailscale addresses the computer reaches) and walks each journey in a browser context of its own. A journey is DATA: { id, goal, expect_every_step?, steps: [{ id, intent, do?, expect? }] }. `do` is one action a person takes: goto { url }, click { target }, fill { target, value }, press { key }, upload { target, files } (files relative to fixtures_folder) or wait { ms }; a target names a control as a person sees it: { role, name } or { role, name_contains }, with nth when several match. `expect` lists what must then be true: text_visible, text_absent, url_contains, title_contains { text }; control_present, control_absent { target }; field_value { target, equals }; checked { target, equals }; no_console_errors; no_failed_requests. A step with no `do` (or a learned action whose control has gone) stops as needs_decision with the actions the page offers, as `do` objects to copy back; the AI chooses one and runs again with it in `learned` or in the journey. Answers the report: verdict, each step with its pictures (the touched control boxed and numbered), console errors and failed requests, `fixes` (for each failed step: what was expected, what was there, the steps that reproduce it and the evidence), `decisions_needed`, `learned` (the actions that passed, to replay next time) and, given previous_report, `compared_with_previous` (fixed, still_failing, newly_failing, still_passing, now_passing). Every run walks every step again; nothing passes because it passed before. Evidence is written under evidence_folder (or a new folder in the computer's temporary folder) and report_file names the saved report.

values.title: Watch my sources
values.job: Watch the places I follow (any site's feed, a YouTube channel, a blog, a changelog, a page, a best-seller or trending list) and keep each new item as a row, weighed against what I am pursuing; only what moves a pursuit is handed to my AIs
values.description: Reads each source marked Yes in the person's list signal-sources (as handed in in records; a missing list is answered with its fields and its starter places turned off) and answers every item not kept before as a row of their list signals; a ranked-list source answers each item's rank in ranked-items and makes a signal of each entry, climb, fall or drop-out. The run reaches no store and keeps nothing: first read the person's lists from the store they keep them in (list:signal-sources, list:signals, list:ranked-items, their rows of types record:signal-sources, record:signals and record:ranked-items, and their pursuit records) and hand them in as records; the answer's keep is what the run found, each record { id, type, value, expected } expecting the value it was handed in with. Put keep in that store, refusing a record whose expected value moved, before the next run. A source's first read is a quiet baseline. A page is watched by whether its words changed; an X account needs a feed address; a YouTube channel is read from its feed or, when YouTube refuses that, its videos page; an address that answers 'not changed' costs nothing. Reads at most 25 sources and weighs at most 20 items a run; the rest wait. The run asks no model and hands nothing in itself: when new items wait it answers weigh_wanted, one question { purpose, identity, messages, max_tokens } for the oldest batch, the same until it is answered; put keep in the store, read the records again, answer the question and run again with weighed { identity, reply }. Each item that moves a pursuit comes back in arrivals, each exactly what the person's arrival door takes (route watch-sources, from_person false); the door keeps one arrival per route and source_id. Sends nothing outward and never writes to a source. Run it on a schedule (hourly) or when the person asks what is new in the places they follow. When the answer names weigh_wanted, answer that question yourself as the person's AI (reply with the JSON it asks for, nothing else) and run the tool again with weighed { identity, reply }. Hand each of arrivals to the person's arrival door as it is. Tell the person the moves; the rest is in their Signals list.

values.title: List what can do steps
values.job: List everything that can do a step for a person, with what each covers and what it costs, and the reasons a step may stay the person's
values.description: Give doers (the caller's own list) and optionally only_a_person. Answers each doer's id, label, the needs it covers, cost, and whether it spends money or reaches others, and the reasons. It is the list a caller chooses `needs` words from for tool:who-does-each-step.

values.title: Show everything waiting on me
values.job: Show everything waiting on this person that only they can do, gathered from every place it is kept: what their AIs asked them for, drafts to approve, work that is stuck, a sign-in, a decision
values.description: Give sources (the places that hold things up, the person's own list: { id, label, title, where?, detail?, opens?, at?, most? }) and found (the records of each source, { <source id>: [{ id, value }] }, read from the person's account by the caller). A record waits when every where test holds (equals, in, present or absent on a field). Answers one card per waiting record, newest first, with the title, detail and the address it opens read from the record by the source's templates, a count for each source, and a sentence. A source with no records handed in is told as unread, never as nothing waiting. The tool reads no records and names no source: a new place is a new row.

values.title: What would it do for my pursuit
values.job: Say what the platform would do for a pursuit in the person's own words: the closest tools and workflows, and where to start
values.description: Checks the pursuit's words (3 to 300 characters), then picks the Marketplace tools and workflows closest to it from the moves table, with each recording that shows it working. Give pursuit and pursuit_vector (the pursuit's own embedding, from the caller), moves (the moves table with its rows), rows (the Marketplace rows the answer may name) and recordings. Give person and database to keep the answer one day in the person's own database; without them nothing is kept. It changes nothing else.

values.title: Work out what is due and when to run next (schedules)
values.job: Scheduler: from recurring schedules (every day or week at a local time in a time zone, daylight saving handled) and one-off timed actions, work out what is due to run now and the next time to run
values.description: Give now plus schedules (schedule_id, timezone as an IANA name, start_local_date, cadence {unit: day | week, interval?, weekdays?: 0=Sunday..6}, local_window {start: HH:MM, duration_minutes}, dst {gap: skip | next-valid, fold: earlier | later | both}, action with its owner_dispatch) and their occurrence_states, and/or one-off time_windows, actions and receipts. Returns recurring_due, scheduled_due, the occurrences to record before running them, and next_wake_at: the next time anything is due, counting what is due now as done.

values.title: Who agreed to get which emails
values.job: Show who agreed to get which email list, in what words, when and from where, and whether they still do
values.description: Optional list (one list's id) and status (active, pending or unsubscribed). Works over every consent in the rows handed in as records: email courses and one-update interest lists. Returns people [{ email, list, kind: course or update, status, consented_at, consent_text, consent_version, source }], agreed (the addresses that can be sent to now, each once) and said. It changes and keeps nothing; hand agreed to a send tool as recipients.

values.title: Say who should do each step of a plan
values.job: For each step of my plan, protocol, checklist or workflow, say who should do it instead of me: a tool or my AIs, a tool after one tap, or only me for a reason only I can meet
values.description: Give steps (words, or { id, words, needs, only_a_person_because, given_in, past }) and doers (the caller's own list: { id, label, does: [words], tool_id?, cost?, spends?, reaches_others?, hand_off?, how? }), and optionally only_a_person (the reasons only the person can do a step), approved (doer ids the person already said yes to), past (outcomes { doer, result: met or failed }), words and ranking. For every step answers who (trillion, one-tap, you or nobody-yet), the doers that cover it with their cost and whether they need a tap, the needs nobody covers, and a sentence. A step is the person's only for a reason in only_a_person; a step nobody can do is nobody-yet, never a to-do; a reason the person gave once is not asked again when the step names the message that gave it; a reason with a first_try doer waits until that doer failed. Nothing is spent or sent. The doers and reasons are never built in.

values.title: Say who said each part of a recording
values.job: Name who said each stretch of a call or recording, from the voices of people who agreed to be known
values.description: Takes a recording and answers each turn with who said it. A supplied transcript is reused; otherwise tools/audio-transcription's existing Whisper engine chooser hears the bounded recording first. Its selected local provider may fetch public model weights; missing engines or models fail rather than inventing words. The person's name is given when one enrolled person is clearly the closest voice; every person it could be when two are too close to tell, so a guess is never made silently; otherwise an unknown voice with a number that stays the same for the whole listening, across every recording of it. Stretches of one voice are judged together, a stretch too short to measure takes its neighbour's voice, and turns of one voice a couple of seconds apart are joined. Thresholds, the wording of the labels and the gap that joins turns are inputs; the starting values are not yet calibrated on the person's own consented clips. The voice-print and listening-voices record kinds are stays_on_this_device: true: only the listening's listening-voices record is kept, with the numbers of the unknown voices heard, on this device. It names no one who has not enrolled.

values.title: Withdraw a referral code
values.job: Stop a referral code from earning, and give back the event to save
values.description: Gives back the event that, once saved, stops a referral code you made from earning. Only the account that made a code can withdraw it; a withdrawal from any other account is ignored when the events are read.

values.title: Turn words into a picture vector
values.job: Turn words into the vector a picture model (CLIP ViT-B-32, OpenAI weights) gives pictures that show them, to compare with picture vectors kept for recordings
values.description: Encodes 1 to 64 short texts with the CLIP ViT-B-32 text model (OpenAI weights, ONNX export pinned by BLAKE3) and returns one unit-length 512-number vector per text, with the model named, so it is compared only with picture vectors made by the same model. Runs sealed, without the network.

values.title: Work one piece through a bank of questions, with evidence for every answer (runs on your computer)
values.job: Ask a small set of the right questions about one thing I am making or reviewing, keep each answer with the files that show it, tell me when an answer's evidence has changed, and add what I learned to my library of findings
values.description: From a person's bank of questions and the run profile they name, picks a small routed set for one piece (a folder with a header listing its tags), writes the piece's investigation record, says which questions can be answered next, records each answer with the BLAKE3 identity of every evidence file (a missing file is refused, an unchanged file is not recorded twice), reports progress and which answers rest on evidence that has since changed or gone, and adds findings to the findings library. A recorded answer establishes structure and file identity, not that the answer is true. Everything about the bank, the profiles, the routes, the statuses and the finding kinds comes from the schema the person gives.

values.title: Work a session catalog
values.job: Offer my sessions in a catalog: publish an entry, read what is current, change it, withdraw it, replace it, or point it to a related offer
values.description: Works on catalog entries, each naming the groups that own it, the sessions it offers, a reference to the person's own visibility rule, a recommendation policy, related offers and where it is shown. An entry is current until it is superseded or retracted. Operations: publish (checks and tidies an entry), read (the current entries, optionally for given entry or session refs), update, retract (with a reason), supersede (an entry by a different one), cross_offer (point one entry at another, replacing an earlier pointer to the same target). Who may see an entry, and the order entries are recommended in, are the person's own rules and are not decided here. Nothing is saved.

values.title: Work out a recipe's nutrients from USDA FoodData Central
values.job: Work out the nutrients in my recipe, per batch and per 100 g, against the daily intakes an adult needs
values.description: Takes a recipe (each ingredient's FoodData Central food id and grams, or a count of a portion such as 2 tbsp) and the person's FoodData Central CSV downloads, and works out 33 nutrients for the whole batch and per 100 g of mix, each ingredient's share, and % of the adult 19-30 Dietary Reference Intake for men and women, with a flag: gap, low, meets a third or more, meets a full day, a limit (sodium), or unknown_lower_bound_only where a main ingredient has no value. Nutrient ids fall back in order (energy 1008 then 2047, sugars 2000 then 1063, and so on). An ingredient can be scaled so one nutrient matches its pack label. It answers the profile, the recipe with the person's own words kept, and a printed table; with write_to it also writes <id>.profile.json and <id>.recipe.json. It reads only the CSVs it is given and makes no calls. The recipe can come from the person's list:settings row (settings_record, read through tools/settings) instead of the request.

values.title: Work out values from a field's history
values.job: Work out, from the values a field of a row has held over time, the value it held at a moment, the value before the current one, since when it holds it, how long it spent holding a value and whether it ever held one
values.description: Send kept (the row, with _history: { <field id>: { cut, steps: [{ v, at, by?, via? }] } }, the steps a history-keeping field kept), fields ([{ id, history: { field, op, value?, at?, days_ago?, unit? } }], op one of value_at, previous_value, value_set_at, time_spent_in, has_been_in; unit seconds, minutes, hours or days) and now_ms. Answers values { <field id>: value }. An answer that needs history that was not kept (steps let go, or a first value whose start is not known) is null, never a guess. A field that is not finished (no op, no value for time_spent_in or has_been_in, no at or days_ago for value_at, an unknown unit) is refused with a sentence.

values.title: Work out measures from my records
values.job: Work out measures from my records: counts, totals, ratios, ranks, quantiles, the latest value, groups, or a ranked and packed list
values.description: Takes facts (a list of records) and measure definitions, or a pipeline of stages where a later stage reads the rows an earlier stage emitted. Each definition names an op (count, sum, distinct, ratio, bin, band, rank, latest, quantile, angle, rollup, formula, reduce-graph, weighted-rank, derive-spans, constrained-span-pack, relevance-rank, mutual-overlap), the fact windows it reads (a match on fields and a field path) and the op's params. Answers each measure with its value, confidence, the ids of the facts it read and ok. An op that is not known, or that fails, gives ok false and confidence 0, never a made-up number. Nothing is named by the tool: the fields, bands, weights and words are in the definitions.

values.title: Work out referral codes
values.job: See which referral codes are live, what a friend who types one gets, and what each sale earns under my referral reward rules
values.description: Reads the referral events a person saved (a code made, a code withdrawn, a signup that named a referrer) and works out the codes: who made each one, what it points at, and whether it is still live. The first account to make a code keeps it, in any order the events arrive; only the account that made a code can withdraw it. The rules are the person's own rows in their referral reward rules list (one row per rule: who earns, the kind of reward, its terms, which codes and sales it applies to), given in `rules`; nothing about a price, a product or an amount is in the tool. Give it the codes buyers typed and it says for each which live code that is and what the rules give the friend who typed it; give it sales too and it says for each pair whether the sale earns the code and what every rule gives: a whole-cent share, a discount (a checkout code that take-payments takes off a price) a customer credit for the referrer (given through take-payments' giveACustomerCredit), or access (a grant). It adds up only: it moves no money, reads nothing and keeps nothing. tool:give-referral-rewards gives the discount and access rows and names the customer credits.

values.title: Work out unit economics
values.job: Work out a business's unit economics (ARPU, gross margin, CAC, LTV, LTV to CAC, payback) from one period's revenue, costs, ad spend and customer counts
values.description: Takes one period's numbers in whole cents and counts and returns revenue per customer, gross margin, cost to win a customer, lifetime value, lifetime value to acquisition cost and months (periods) to earn back that cost. A figure these numbers cannot give (no cost, no spend, no churn, a zero count) comes back as null, never as a made-up zero.

values.title: Work out where a learner stands on a track
values.job: See how far a learner is along a course, lesson plan or learning path, which step comes next, and what they last showed
values.description: Give the tracks, their ordered steps and the learner's progress states, evaluation receipts, evidence and label rows, and (to look at one person) the learner. Returns, per track, the steps in order, the percent finished counted from the steps (a stored percent or a "mastered" label never counts), the step to do next, the latest evaluation the learner's state names, the three newest pieces of evidence, the label for the latest decision and the path: each step complete, active or locked.

values.title: Turn a document into a message body (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn a document I wrote (headings, paragraphs, images, a quoted reply) into the HTML and plain-text body of a message, ready to send
values.description: Takes a request file { document_nodes: [{ id, kind, props, children, visible }] or one root node, options? } and writes { body_html, body_text, inline_refs, degraded }. Text and heading kinds become paragraphs and headings with a plain-text line each; image and media blocks become inline_refs { cid, fetch_ref, mime } for the sender to attach; blocks marked as a quote become one blockquote with > lines; hidden subtrees are skipped; a block kind it does not know falls back to its text and is listed in degraded, never dropped silently. options.kind_renderers maps your own block kinds to paragraph, heading1 to heading3 or media. It names no mail provider.

values.title: Write a post for one place
values.job: Write one message for a pull request thread, a merge request note, a chat or a post from the same blocks, using only what that place can show
values.description: Give blocks (heading, paragraph, code, list, checklist, image with an optional dark_url, collapsible holding more blocks) and exactly one of surface (github_comment, gitlab_note, bitbucket_comment or plain_message), capability (a record with html, collapsibles, checkboxes, dialect 'markdown' or 'plain', max_chars or null, theme { strategy 'picture', 'suffix' or 'single' } and unproven) or place (a post place whose format may carry caption_max_characters and source). Optional marker is put first and kept through any cut. Returns body, degraded (the capabilities the place lacked, so the body did without them), unproven_used (capabilities relied on that nobody has confirmed for that place), truncated (a body over max_chars is cut at a block boundary and says so) and the capability record used. An unknown surface, more or fewer than one of surface, capability or place, or an unknown block type is refused. It posts nothing.

values.title: Prepare the request for a profile of a creator or a topic
values.job: Turn what was gathered about a creator or a topic (video words, page text) into the instruction the person's AI writes a profile from
values.description: Give subject_ref (who or what is profiled), instruction (the person's own words on what to look for; they come before the material) and either material (one text) or evidence ([{ id, text }], for example one video's words each). Optional profile_ref (profile:<subject_ref> when left out) and output_kind (profile). Returns one request per piece of material: { kind, status requested, request_id (subject_ref:id), profile_ref, subject_ref, output_kind, instruction_text }, and in skipped the ids whose text was empty (a video with no captions). It asks no model and stores nothing; the AI that called it writes the profile from instruction_text and keeps it in the person's own records.

values.title: Write a copy of a repository into my files, for citations to be checked against
values.job: Write the files of a repository, the dates of its commits and a stamp naming the commit into my own files under /source-copies/<root>/, so a check of what a finding cites can read them on any computer
values.description: Takes a root name, the ref and head the copy was made from, a list of files ({path, text}, at most 64, each at most 4 MiB), the commit dates ({<full hash>: <ISO date>}), whether the list is every tracked file, and stored.files: the files already under /source-copies/<root>/ that the caller read from where the person keeps them (a file not handed in is not there). It reads and writes no store: it answers keep, each file { file, identity, base64, expected } in order (expected is the identity of the file as handed in, null when it was not there, so a store refuses a keep whose file moved): each file, then .commit-dates.json, and the stamp .source-copy.json last, under /source-copies/<root>/, so a copy whose stamp is old never claims a new head. A file handed in that already holds the bytes sent is left out of keep. The stamp holds ref, head, copied_at and files: the sorted paths the copy holds (the earlier stamp's files plus these, or exactly these when complete is true; also_held paths, written by earlier runs of the same head, are added). A big copy can be sent in several runs: with final false a run keeps only its files (no dates, no stamp) and answers final:false; the last run (final true, the default) keeps the dates and the stamp. A path with .., ., an empty part, a leading / or a backslash is refused and nothing is kept. The tool never reads a repository: the caller reads git and hands in the text.

values.title: Write a web page from one record and a description of how to publish it (runs on your computer)
values.job: Turn one record and a publication descriptor into a finished web page: its words, its address, its search and sharing tags, its structured data and a proof of what it was made from
values.description: Takes an envelope file: publication_descriptor, source_record, optional materialized_values and correlation_id. The descriptor says which record fields become the title, description, language and page sections (heading, paragraph, prose, list, quote, code, image, group; any other operation still shows its text), where the page will live (scheme, domain and path pieces, each a literal or a value read from the record), the colours and font (tokens), extra sharing tags, and a list of structured-data nodes whose values are read from the record, with empty values dropped. Words from the record are escaped; a prose section is written as given, so its owner must have made it safe. The new page is written to the output path. The answer gives the address, tags, byte count and a proof naming the descriptor, record and revision it came from.

values.title: Write a word template by hand from the words I keep and the slots I leave open (runs on your computer)
values.job: Write a word template for a spoken line from the words that stay and the slots that change, when no reader can measure its file
values.description: Writes word-template@1 token tables from a request: for each template a name, a time span, where its words came from, parts (kept words, and slot words each naming a slot) and the slots (type and note). Each word becomes a token marked KEEP or SLOT in order, with its slot, slot type and note; only the slots a word uses are listed; every dimension other than the spoken words is left pending with the reason. The words, slots, sources and notes are the person's own and come in the request (one file, or several laid over each other key by key, so their settings can be a row of their records and the output folder stays with the run); the tool names no piece, speaker or film. The templates are the same shape make_template.py writes, so tool:fill-a-word-template and tool:check-words-against-a-word-template take them.

values.title: Write legal documents
values.job: Write a business's terms of service, privacy policy, refund policy or waiver from its facts
values.description: Assembles each document you ask for from a library of forty clauses, choosing the clauses the business's facts call for (accounts, paid offers, subscriptions, AI, physical activity, minors) and filling in its name, address, contact and policies. Each document comes back with its text, its identity, the clauses used, the facts still missing or to be confirmed, and whether it is ready to publish; nothing is ready to publish until a lawyer has reviewed it. facts_it_reads lists every fact each document uses, so a first call with a few facts shows what to ask for next.

values.title: Write the message models every app reads from one list (runs on your computer)
values.job: Write the Swift and TypeScript message models two apps and the web use to talk to each other, from one list of models
values.description: Reads one models file (models, each with its fields and types, and targets naming the type name, protocols and output file each app uses) and writes a Swift file per Swift target and one TypeScript declaration, so the apps cannot read the same message two ways. --check exits 1 and names each file that is behind its models file; --write (the default) brings them up to date. Nothing about any model is built in: the models are the person's rows.

values.title: Write the public files of my share links
values.job: Write the public files of every share link of mine that anyone may open, into the folder my public server serves, and remove the files of links I revoked or that expired
values.description: Takes the person's sharing rows (each link grant), the Lists those links share (a whole List, or one row of it) and the List's rows as input.records, read by the caller from the person's own store, reads the files its shown rows name from the files the caller hands in as input.stored.files, and writes into the folder the person granted: <code>.json (and <name>.json for a link with a readable address) in the shape { kind: "list", title, about, changed, fields, rows: [{ id, title, address, url, values }], files: [{ identity, name, url, media_type }] }, whole and never paged; <name>/index.html for the List and <name>/<row address>/index.html for each row; files/<identity> for each file a shown row names; sitemap.xml and llms.txt over every listed link; and manifest.json, every file with its BLAKE3 content identity and the files this run removed. A link has public files only while it is published, not revoked, not expired and open to anyone; a link for named people, an email, an audience or an access code has none. What leaves is the List's share rule less the fields the person left out, only the rows whose own rules hold and only the files they name. A link with its own condition, a match-only field, or a row rule that counts opens or reads the clock is left out with its reason, because a file on a public server cannot check it at each open. Runs on its own when a sharing row or a List changes, and again at the earliest expiry of a published link. Returns written, unchanged, removed, published, left_out, ended and next_change_at.

values.title: Write the icon shapes my motion film uses, from the real lucide icons (runs on your computer)
values.job: Put the real icons my film shows into the film, as shapes its page can draw
values.description: Reads each named icon from the lucide-react package on the person's computer (its dist/esm/icons folder) and writes the film's icons file: window.ICONS[name] = [[tag, attrs], ...] for a 24x24 viewBox, the React key dropped, with a first line naming where the shapes came from. Without out it answers the file's text instead of writing it. The icon names a film uses are its settings row.

values.title: Your files
values.job: Every name of the person's files, listed, followed as it changes, read by range, written, moved, shared and released, for an AI or a device's folder, through the engine's one door
values.description: The person's files (tools/live-namespace) as a session the engine keeps open and reaches only by calls: tools:run at @tools {tool: "tool:your-files", call: {name, arguments}} sends one MCP tools/call to the account's one session of this row, which the first call starts (trillion-rust src/tool_runs/tools/sessions.rs `call`); each call is answered on its own, so a list_changes that waits holds back no read. `name` is an operation of mcp-tools.json: list_files, list_changes, show_item, read_file_span, write_file, write_file_start, write_file_piece, write_file_finish, move_names, set_aside, put_back, make_folder, set_pin_rule, thumbnail, bounds, this_computer and the rest. The answer is {tool, result} with the operation's answer in result.structuredContent; a refusal is result.isError with {code, outcome}. read_file_span with raw: true answers the span's bytes themselves: {byte_slice: {total, offset, length, base64}}, or, to a request that accepts application/octet-stream, the raw bytes as the HTTP body with X-Total-Bytes and X-Offset (session.byte_result), so they cross the wire once, the first of them as soon as the store sends it. write_file_piece takes its piece raw the same way: a POST whose Content-Type is application/octet-stream, whose body is the piece and whose X-Call header is the base64url of the tools/call JSON; the engine names the body it kept as the call's content_file (session.byte_argument). The run opens no port. Its bytes are the person's own files-store connection, each field mounted on the descriptor settings.json `attached` names and never printed. Its names are rows a session of tool:your-files-names keeps (the one run that holds the person's database login), reached by calls through this run's door (invoke.records, descriptor 9): the engine lets one process reach only hosts every value it holds may go to, so a run holding the byte store's key and the database login could reach none. The program is the live-namespace this computer keeps among its program folders.

values.title: Your files' names
values.job: The names of the person's files (names, folders, chunks, shares), kept in the person's own database and answered by calls to the run of tool:your-files, so that run never holds the database login
values.description: The names rows of the person's files (tools/live-namespace `live-namespace rows`, src/serve/rows.rs), as a session the engine keeps open and reaches only by calls. Each call is one operation of the store's Rows (get, get_many, held_record_with_version, list_page, ids, mutate, stamp, totals, search, place, order, changes, minted, wait_for_order: src/store/by_calls.rs), each atomic alone, and is answered as a file of bytes (session.byte_result), so a page of rows is never held to one message. tool:your-files is its caller (its invoke.records.runs). It holds the person's database login alone (own-rows-postgres-connection on descriptor 3), so its reach is the database's host, and tool:your-files holds the byte store's key alone.
